local.name: FFTE
local.description: Discrete Fourier transforms in one, two and three dimensions, including serial and parallel variants.

classifications.notes: Documents complex FFTs and real/complex transforms; multidimensional coverage is recorded at J1 rather than treating every routine as one-dimensional.

The inspected ZFFT1D driver initializes twiddle tables with IOPT=0, factors supported lengths into powers of 2/3/5, and dispatches the complex FFT235 radix passes directly or through a blocked two-factor decomposition for larger vectors. IOPT=-1 selects the forward transform; IOPT=1 conjugates before the same FFT and conjugates/scales by 1/N afterward for the inverse. J1a2 records one-dimensional complex discrete Fourier transforms. The source requires N=2**p*3**q*5**r; FACTOR does not return an unsupported-factor error, so callers must validate the positive length themselves. B has 2*N complex entries and holds both scratch and coefficients. Large-path WX/WY tables are SAVE state: initialize again for the current length and do not assume independent large-length setups can be interleaved. Compiled param.h dimensions bound decomposition axes and no runtime bounds/status validation is supplied. Review covers the driver, factorization and radix dispatch, not every kernel, OpenMP behavior, MPI/GPU variants or numerical accuracy. No transform or round-trip was executed.

procedures.summary: External in-place complex-double FFT driver. A needs N entries, B needs 2*N entries; INTEGER N/IOPT must match the fixed-form build ABI. Initialize with IOPT=0, then use -1 forward or +1 inverse. Forward output is unscaled; inverse includes 1/N. Only positive 2/3/5-smooth lengths are supported, with additional compiled workspace-size constraints. There is no status dummy.
procedures.usage:
external :: zfft1d
integer, parameter :: n=8
complex(kind(0.0d0)) :: a(n), work(2*n)
a=cmplx(0.0d0,0.0d0,kind(0.0d0))
a(1)=cmplx(1.0d0,0.0d0,kind(0.0d0))
call zfft1d(a,n,0,work)
call zfft1d(a,n,-1,work)
! For this impulse the unscaled spectrum is all ones.
call zfft1d(a,n,1,work)
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled small-path fragment. No spectrum or round-trip comparison was performed. Build/link zfft1d.f, fft235.f, kernel.f and factor.f with a consistent param.h include and compatible COMPLEX*16/default INTEGER conventions; the upstream test Makefile shows that source set and OpenMP flags. Retain the coefficient part of work between calls, reinitialize when changing length, and do not assume shared large-path tables are reentrant. The sample avoids unsupported prime factors and large decomposition dimensions.

procedures.summary: Counts powers of 2, 3 and 5 without returning a validation status for remaining prime factors.
Radix dispatch only reviewed; individual arithmetic kernels remain outside this audit.

local.name: Expokit
local.description: Matrix exponentials and exponential actions using dense approximations and sparse Krylov methods.

classifications.notes: Documents exp(t*A), exp(t*A)v and phi-function actions for dense and sparse matrices. Linear algebra is supported; a more specific matrix-function mapping awaits procedure review.

The inspected real dense DGPADM routine scales t*H, evaluates the diagonal Pade rational approximation using matrix products and a linear solve, then repeatedly squares the result. It returns the full exp(t*H) through an offset into caller workspace. D8 follows the published NAG GAMS convention grouping matrix functions with other matrix equations (the NAG D8 index lists real matrix exponentials); this is not a claim of a general Sylvester-equation solver. Only this dense real path is reviewed: sparse Krylov exponential actions, complex variants and phi-functions are not certified here. Invalid sizes, zero norm of t*H (including t=0 or H=0), and linear-solve failure STOP rather than returning a recoverable error. The caller must handle identity cases and provide valid positive dimensions and workspace. No matrix exponential, conditioning or scaling-extreme test was run.

procedures.summary: External double-precision dense matrix exponential. Use positive m, ldh >= m, recommended ideg=6, ipiv(m) and wsp length >= 4*m*m+ideg+1. exp(t*H) occupies wsp(iexph:iexph+m*m-1) in column-major order; iexph is one-based relative to the passed workspace. ns reports squarings. Handle t=0 or H=0 outside the routine because its zero-norm branch STOPs. Link compatible BLAS/LAPACK.
procedures.signature: CALL DGPADM(ideg, m, t, H, ldh, wsp, lwsp, ipiv, iexph, ns, iflag)
procedures.usage:
external :: dgpadm
integer, parameter :: m=2, ideg=6, lwsp=4*m*m+ideg+1
integer :: ipiv(m), iexph, ns, iflag
double precision :: h(m,m), work(lwsp), exponential(m,m)
h = 0.0d0
h(1,1) = 0.1d0
h(2,2) = 0.2d0
call dgpadm(ideg,m,1.0d0,h,m,work,lwsp,ipiv,iexph,ns,iflag)
if (iflag /= 0) error stop "matrix exponential failed"
exponential = reshape(work(iexph:iexph+m*m-1),[m,m])
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled calling sketch. The analytic reference is diag(exp(0.1),exp(0.2)), but no comparison was run. The result is the full matrix exponential, not entrywise exponentiation or just its action on a vector. Link ABI-compatible BLAS/LAPACK; some failures terminate inside DGPADM before the iflag check can run. The chosen nonzero matrix/time avoids its identity-case STOP.

local.name: BLZPACK
local.description: Block Lanczos methods for sparse real symmetric standard and generalized eigenproblems.

classifications.notes: Documents both standard and generalized real sparse symmetric eigenproblems. A D4 mapping avoids implying that only the ordinary eigenproblem is supported.

DBLZDRV standard symmetric mode requests A*U by reverse communication, then orchestrates block-Lanczos recurrence, orthogonality control and projected-eigenproblem convergence dispatch. The inspected DBLZSTP controls recurrence/reorthogonalization helper calls, stores basis/projected coefficients and schedules Ritz evaluation/restarts; this is driver/step-control review, not a complete kernel or convergence proof. D4a1 covers real symmetric ordinary problems. The interface is matrix-free and can accept sparse products, but no particular sparse storage format is claimed. Initialize control/work arrays according to documented dimensions before LFLAG=0; service every positive request with NVOPU columns and reenter with the same flag. LFLAG=0 after a call is normal completion, negative is abnormal/early; partial eigenpairs and work-array warning/error reports require inspection. Workspace sizing includes control prefixes, and low memory can create temporary files. No eigenpairs, inertia or residuals were checked by execution.

procedures.summary: External double-precision block-Lanczos reverse-communication driver. ISTOR holds integer controls/work, RSTOR real controls/work, U/V blocks, EIG(LEIG,2) eigenvalue data and X(LNI,LEIG) vectors. SIGMA/NNEIG carry shift/inertia; LFLAG and NVOPU control caller operations.
procedures.signature: CALL DBLZDRV(ISTOR, RSTOR, SIGMA, NNEIG, U, V, LFLAG, NVOPU, EIG, X)
procedures.usage:
! Allocate and initialize controls/workspaces using the pinned DBLZDRV contract.
! Select ISTOR(9)=0 for standard symmetric mode.
lflag=0
do
  call dblzdrv(istor,rstor,sigma,nneig,u,v,lflag,nvopu,eig,x)
  if(lflag<=0) exit
  ! Implement the requested operation for all NVOPU columns, then reenter.
  ! Never reenter without filling V or completing the requested factorization.
end do
if(lflag<0) error stop "Lanczos terminated abnormally"

local.name: AMG4PSBLAS
local.description: Parallel algebraic multilevel preconditioners for sparse linear systems in the PSBLAS framework.

classifications.notes: Documents algebraic multilevel preconditioning used with PSBLAS Krylov solvers. This is a preconditioner component, not a standalone solver; MPI and PSBLAS are required.

The public real-double multilevel preconditioner type constructs an algebraic multilevel hierarchy and its level smoothers for a distributed PSBLAS sparse matrix. The build binding dispatches hierarchy_build followed by smoothers_build; init selects ML rather than the separate diagonal/block-Jacobi/Schwarz options. The associated apply implementation contains V/W/K cycle paths. This is a concrete associated linear-system operation, not a claim that build itself solves A*x=b or that a generic multigrid cycle is a particular Krylov method. MPI/PSBLAS context, assembled matrix/descriptor, level settings and optional coarse-solver configuration must already be consistent. INFO and the configured PSBLAS error policy govern failures; some policies terminate rather than returning. Review covers initialization, public binding/build dispatch and cycle entry documentation, not every smoother, coarse solver or parallel scaling claim.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound construction of a distributed multilevel preconditioner.
procedures.usage:
use psb_base_mod
use amg_d_prec_mod, only: amg_dprec_type
type(amg_dprec_type) :: p
integer(psb_ipk_) :: info
! After initializing CTXT and assembling distributed A and DESC_A:
call p%init(ctxt,"ML",info)
if(info/=0) error stop "AMG initialization failed"
call p%build(a,desc_a,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "AMG construction failed"
! Pass P to the matching PSBLAS iterative solver; BUILD is not a solve.
! After all applications of P have completed:
call p%free(info)
if(info/=0) error stop "AMG cleanup failed"
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-assembly fragment, requiring the matching PSBLAS/MPI build and configured coarse solvers. CTXT, A and DESC_A are caller-owned objects, not declared or initialized here. Retain compatible matrix/descriptor lifetime and inspect INFO/error policy. No hierarchy, cycle, residual or MPI test was run.

local.name: eiscor
local.description: Matrix eigenvalue algorithms based on small unitary core transformations.

classifications.notes: Documents Fortran 90 matrix eigensolvers and related unitary QR research. Build requirements and individual routine interfaces have not yet been reviewed.

d_symtrid_qr handles a real symmetric tridiagonal ordinary eigenproblem through a Cayley transformation, core-chasing reduction to unitary Hessenberg form, a unitary QR dispatch and inverse eigenvalue transformation. The inspected d_symtrid_factor stores core rotations and optionally accumulates Schur vectors; D4a5 is explicitly scoped here to symmetric tridiagonal inputs, not general nonsymmetric tridiagonals or the whole EISCOR API. D/E are overwritten and results are not explicitly sorted. Source findings require attention: the QR driver passes WORK(1:3*(N-3)) to a factor dummy Q(3*N-3), a shorter array section; factor code accepts N=1 but accesses E(1), so use a validated N>=2 path after repairing/checking workspace association. Schur vectors are COMPLEX(8) despite real input. Scaling is recommended; nonzero INFO means factorization/QR failure, and partial back-transformed output is not a success certificate. No eigensolver, author comparison or lower-level unitary QR audit was run.

procedures.summary: External REAL(8) diagonal D(N), subdiagonal E(N-1), WORK(5*N), INTEGER ITS(N-1), and COMPLEX(8) Z(M,N). VEC selects vectors, ID initializes Z, SCA controls scaling. Match literal kind 8 to the library build; inspect INFO.

real(8) :: d(n),e(n-1),work(5*n)
complex(8) :: z(n,n)
d=2d0; e=-1d0

call d_symtrid_qr(.true.,.true.,.true.,n,d,e,work,n,z,its,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "tridiagonal QR failed"

local.name: FFTLog-f90
local.description: Logarithmically sampled Fourier-Bessel transform code, currently restricted to the sine-transform case.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly limits this version to mu=0.5 (the sine-transform case). This mapping does not claim a general-order Hankel transform implementation.

The inspected FFTL entry reweights logarithmically spaced samples, dispatches FHTQ and postscales using logarithmic spacing, bias, kr and rk. FHTI initializes FFTPACK and complex-Gamma transform coefficients. With mu=+1/2 or -1/2 this is the logarithmically sampled sine/cosine transform subset J1a3, not a conventional equally spaced FFT or a certified infinite-domain quadrature. FHTI setup can be reused only while N/mu/q/spacing/kr stay fixed. Its OK flag is not a full validation certificate (N<=0 can still reach OK=true), so validate positive N, nonzero spacing and positive kr/rk. The command-line driver restricts mu to +1/2 despite a cosine hint in an error message, and applies its own physical normalization. Lower-level FHTQ, FFTPACK and complex-Gamma arithmetic are outside this review. No transform, ringing or round-trip check was run.

procedures.summary: External REAL*8 setup. N/KROPT default INTEGER; MU/Q/DLNR/KR real double; KR may be adjusted. KROPT=1 selects quiet low-ringing adjustment. WSAVE needs 2*N+2*(N/2)+18 for Q=0, or 2*N+3*(N/2)+19 otherwise. Check logical OK and validate inputs independently.

External in-place transform of A(N). DIR=+1/-1 forward/backward; initialize WSAVE with FHTI first, using MU=+0.5 for sine or -0.5 for cosine. RK is r_center/k_center, not the product KR. Output uses the logarithmic grid and sqrt(2/pi) sine/cosine normalization documented here, distinct from the command-line driver extra scaling.
procedures.usage:
external :: fhti, fftl
integer, parameter :: n=16
integer :: i
logical :: ok
double precision :: a(n), work(4*n+19), kr, rk, spacing, r
kr=1.0d0
spacing=0.1d0
call fhti(n,0.5d0,0.0d0,spacing,kr,1,work,ok)
if (.not.ok) error stop "FFTLog setup failed"
rk=1.0d0/kr
do i=1,n
  r=exp((i-0.5d0*(n+1))*spacing)
  a(i)=exp(-r*r)
end do
call fftl(n,a,rk,1,work)
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled interface fragment with r_center=1 and k_center=KR, so RK=1/KR after any setup adjustment. The short log range is illustrative, not an accuracy demonstration. Validate domain truncation, periodic-extension/ringing effects and grid/normalization before comparing transforms. Link FFTLOG plus bundled DRFFTI/DRFFTF/DRFFTB and CDGAMMA support. Never confuse RK ratio with KR product, or the library normalization with the CLI postprocessing.

local.name: adjac
local.description: Operator-overloaded automatic differentiation for sparse and dense real or complex Jacobians.

classifications.notes: The README documents AD types and Jacobian extraction. Its optional AD-aware FFT is not separately classified here.

The reviewed real adjac_double path records local first-derivative dependencies in module-wide tape arrays. Multiplication records the product rule through sum_taylor_a; get_dense_jacobian_a seeds dependent variables in blocks and traverses those dependencies backward to assemble Jacobian rows. adjac_set_independent seeds variable indices. This establishes operator-overloaded first differentiation, not higher derivatives or a numerical finite-difference method. The scoped review covers real variables and dense extraction; complex, sparse-COO, tapeless and FFT variants remain outside this source mapping. The shared storage and mode flag require coordinated lifecycle management and are not independently thread-local. Reset without product_mode preserves the previous mode. Fatal errors STOP rather than return status. No numerical derivative test was run.

procedures.summary: Reset shared tape indices before registering independent variables. Explicitly pass product_mode=.false. for the dense-Jacobian path; omitting it preserves the last mode. Existing AD values tied to an earlier tape must not be reused after resetting.

Public generic; inspected real vector overload takes type(adjac_double) x(:), double-precision xval(size(x)), and optional directional seeds dx. Dense mode numbers variables in x order. Scalar registration instead requires the variable index j.

declarations.text: double precision, dimension(size(x)), optional, intent(in) :: dx

procedures.summary: Public generic; inspected real overload takes dependent type(adjac_double) y(:) as INOUT and a caller-sized double-precision matrix. Allocate one row per dependent and one column per registered independent; extraction requires tape mode. Specific get_dense_jacobian_a is private.
procedures.usage:
use adjac
type(adjac_double) :: x(2), y(1)
double precision :: jac(1,2)
call adjac_reset(product_mode=.false.)
call adjac_set_independent(x, [2.0d0, 3.0d0])
y(1) = x(1)*x(2)
call adjac_get_dense_jacobian(y, jac)
call adjac_free()
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch for the inspected real dense path, not a checked driver. The analytic expected Jacobian is [3,2], but this was not compiled or compared. Complete all extraction before freeing or resetting shared tape storage. The supplied author example demonstrates a separate complex-analytic specialization, which is not certified by this real-path source review.

procedures.summary: Release the shared tape arrays after all values and derivatives have been extracted. Existing tape-dependent AD variables become unusable; this does not reset the product-mode flag.

local.name: autodiff
local.description: Automatic differentiation supporting derivatives through fourth order.

classifications.notes: The short README states the fourth-derivative scope and a Make-based test command. Supported operators and numerical behavior await source review.

The inspected src/avd.f90 implementation propagates derivatives through overloaded products and elementary-function composition. The avd_d4 inheritance chain stores a value and first through fourth raw derivatives with respect to one scalar parameter; the product and Q4_f chain rules contain the corresponding binomial/composition coefficients. This is forward differentiation, not finite differencing or symbolic expression manipulation. CALL init() must populate the module function-pointer table before elementary functions are used. H1 is the differentiation leaf; there is no finer automatic-differentiation child in this taxonomy. The review covers the fourth-order product/exponential path, not every overload or the older root autodiff.f90 implementation. Source requests an eight-byte default REAL build; module and caller settings must agree. No author tests or derivative comparisons were executed.

procedures.summary: Public no-argument generic that initializes the shared elementary-function derivative table. Call before exp and other table-based elementary functions.

Public exponential generic, scoped here to the avd_d4 overload. Input/output contain v and d1..d4 in REAL(8). Seed an independent scalar with d1=1 and higher derivatives zero; extract the same fields from the result. These are raw derivatives, not factorial-scaled Taylor coefficients.

use AVD, only: avd_d4, init, exp
type(avd_d4) :: x, y
call init()
x%v=0.5d0
x%d1=1.0d0
x%d2=0.0d0
x%d3=0.0d0
x%d4=0.0d0
y=exp(x)
! Read y%v and y%d1 through y%d4.

local.name: DNAD
local.description: Dual-number automatic differentiation for existing Fortran programs.

classifications.notes: Classification uses the documentation and quick-start guide embedded in dnad.F90. This is a review of that documentation, not a verification of every overloaded operation.

The dnadmod dual type carries a default-REAL value x and a derivative vector dx(ndv). Reviewed real assignment zeroes the vector, dual multiplication applies the product rule, and exp_d multiplies the seed vector by exp(x). The public entry is the exp generic; exp_d and mult_dd are private specifics. This is first-order forward automatic differentiation, with the derivative-vector length chosen at preprocessing time by ndv (default one), not a higher-order derivative or finite-difference implementation. Seed every derivative component explicitly for independent inputs and compile callers against the matching module. The header notes default single precision unless consistent compiler options promote default REAL. No derivative result was checked by execution.

procedures.summary: Public elemental exponential generic for type(dual). Read result%x for the value and result%dx for seeded first derivatives. Build dnad.F90 with preprocessing; -Dndv=N selects the number of stored directions. REAL assignment resets all derivative seeds to zero.

use dnadmod, only: dual, assignment(=), operator(*), exp
type(dual) :: x, y
x=0.5
x%dx=0.0
x%dx(1)=1.0

local.name: Fazang
local.description: Reverse-mode automatic differentiation with a forward-over-reverse Hessian interface.

classifications.notes: The README documents var/grad/adj and the fvar Hessian workflow. Example code is author-provided and has not been run here.

The current fz_var/fz_vari implementation records overloaded operations on shared byte-stack storage and per-node chain callbacks. grad(v) seeds the selected result adjoint to one and sweeps callbacks backward; primitive multiplication/addition and square/sine/exp chain rules visibly accumulate operand adjoints. H1 records reverse-mode automatic differentiation, not finite differences or validation of the advertised forward-over-reverse Hessian path. The public facade fazang reexports these interfaces. Repeated gradients require reset_adj because chain does not zero previous operand adjoints. reboot_chain reuses storage and invalidates old variable handles; module-global state is not per-thread/context. The convenience jac routine declares n but uses res(2:n) without assigning n, so the sketch avoids it. Storage exhaustion uses ERROR STOP; operation domains and alignment/kind assumptions remain caller/build concerns. No derivative, Hessian, performance test or complete operator set was compiled or run.

procedures.summary: Public generic grad(v) or grad() in fz_var, reexported by fazang. v is a recorded var handle; the no-argument form starts at the last recorded node. Obtain REAL(rk) values/adjoints via val/adj, not fields on var.

use fazang
type(var) :: x,y
real(rk) :: derivative
x=2.0_rk
y=x*x
call reset_adj(y)
call grad(y)
derivative=adj(x)
! Read all values/adjoints before reclaiming tape storage.
call reboot_chain()

local.name: Akima with Derivatives
local.description: One-dimensional Akima interpolation with derivatives with respect to arguments and input data.

classifications.notes: The README describes smoothing the absolute-value operation for data sensitivities. It explicitly cautions against substantial extrapolation.

setup forms segment slopes, extrapolated endpoint slopes and Akima weighted nodal slopes, then local cubic coefficients; interp selects an interval and evaluates its cubic. This establishes univariate piecewise-polynomial interpolation. abs_smooth rounds the absolute-value weights when delta_x is positive, so that variant differs from unsmoothed Akima. The source assumes ordered distinct nodes and at least three points without checking them. Queries outside the data range continue the nearest end polynomial; this is not a reliable general extrapolation method. No shape-preservation, monotonicity or accuracy guarantee is inferred from the README, and no spline was run.

local.name: fortran-rbf
local.description: Radial-basis-function interpolation and local derivative matrices.

classifications.notes: The rbf_mod source documentation identifies the RBF implementation, interpolation matrices and derivative matrices. Kept at interpolation class E pending a procedure-level review; no PDE solver claim is made.

The inspected rbf_type%build constructs a local RBF interpolation matrix for each caller-supplied neighbor stencil, obtains its inverse and forms derivative matrices from kernel evaluations. This is an interpolation service (E3), not a complete value-evaluation API: optional y is not referenced, and the routine neither fits data values nor returns values at arbitrary queries. The Gaussian unaugmented matrix path is identifiable in source; the derivative and polynomial branches need correction/checking. In particular, the Gaussian second derivative expression differs from the analytic derivative; polynomial-augmented B entries are not fully initialized before whole-matrix multiplication, and an active debug print indexes node ten without checking node count. Compile with USE_LAPACK: inverse_matrix has an empty alternative branch. Select a distance function first, validate indices and stencil nonsingularity, and use poly_order=-1 to avoid augmentation. No interpolant, derivative matrix or failure was checked by execution; no PDE-solver or general scattered-interpolator mapping is inferred.

Initialize distance_mod first. Reviewed unaugmented Gaussian use sets kernel_ga and poly_order=-1. Matrices are stored on the object; y is unused and no status is returned.

local.name: HiPPIS
local.description: High-order data-bounded and positivity-preserving interpolation on structured meshes.

classifications.notes: The README documents one-, two- and three-dimensional tensor-product mesh examples. This mapping is for interpolation, not every physical model in its demonstrations.

The public DIVDIFF builds the triangular table of Newton divided differences; NEWTONPOLYVAL evaluates supplied Newton coefficients by nested multiplication. These are univariate polynomial interpolation components, separate from adaptive positivity/boundedness selection. Require distinct finite abscissae, 0<=D<N and initialized coefficient entries: trailing unused triangular cells in TABLE are not assigned. No duplicate-node guard, condition estimate or numerical error bound is supplied. The sketch uses the fully defined first row of a degree-two divided-difference table.

procedures.summary: Public module scalar Newton-polynomial evaluator; U holds Newton coefficients, not sampled y values.
procedures.usage:
use mod_adaptiveInterpolation, only: dp,divdiff,newtonPolyVal
real(dp) :: x(3),y(3),table(3,3),estimate
x=[0.0_dp,1.0_dp,2.0_dp]; y=x*x
call divdiff(x,y,3,2,table)
call newtonPolyVal(x,table(1,:),2,0.5_dp,estimate)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Only valid triangular table entries may be read. The first row supplies all coefficients for this three-node polynomial. Noncontiguous TABLE(1,:) may require an array temporary. No interpolation residual or stability test was run.

procedures.summary: Public module divided-difference table builder. Trailing triangular storage is left undefined.

classifications.notes: ADAPTIVEINTERPOLATION1D constructs per-interval Newton polynomials using divided differences, expanding the stencil while the selected boundedness/positivity inequalities admit points, and evaluates at ordered output locations. INTERPOLATION_TYPE=1 selects data-bounded and 2 positivity-oriented constraints; DEG reports selected degrees. Require increasing distinct input/output coordinates, N>=3 (endpoint slopes read Y(3)), 1<=DEGREE<N and in-range queries for preservation claims. A header comment reverses input ordering, but source checks and interval comparisons require ascending order. Extrapolation explicitly loses the advertised preservation. The code may STOP on invalid coordinate ordering and does not return a success/status flag. This review covers stencil selection, interface and evaluation structure, not a proof that all bound conditions or floating-point corner cases preserve the advertised property.

local.name: SHEPPACK
local.description: Modified Shepard interpolation for scattered multivariate data, including robust variants.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes quadratic, cubic, linear, robust and RIPPLE variants and their dimensional restrictions. No single dimensional leaf is assigned to the entire suite.

QSHEP2 selects neighboring planar data, sets compact radii, forms local quadratic weighted least-squares models with Givens QR, enlarges neighborhoods/damps quadratic terms for conditioning, and returns cell-search/model data. QS2VAL blends those nodal polynomials by compact Shepard weights and returns exact nodal F on coincidence. E2b records bivariate scattered interpolation, not gridded-only or arbitrary-dimensional interpolation. N>=6, 5<=NQ<=MIN(40,N-1), 1<=NW<=MIN(40,N-1) and NR>=1 are required. Setup IER diagnoses ranges, duplicate nodes and degeneracy. QS2VAL returns zero both for some invalid input and for points outside all supports; use QS2GRD for a status-bearing evaluation. This review covers setup/evaluation control, not a complete audit of neighbor/rotation kernels or robustness in all geometries. No interpolant or author test was executed.

procedures.summary: Public module setup routine. REAL(R8) coordinate/value vectors have length N; output coefficients A(5,N), RSQ(N), LCELL(NR,NR), LNEXT(N) and geometry scalars must be retained together. Check IER before evaluation.
procedures.signature:
CALL QSHEP2(N, X, Y, F, NQ, NW, NR, LCELL, LNEXT, &
            XMIN, YMIN, DX, DY, RMAX, RSQ, A, IER)
procedures.usage:
use REAL_PRECISION, only: R8
use QSHEP2D_MOD, only: QSHEP2, QS2VAL
integer, parameter :: n=16, nr=2
integer :: i,j,k,ier,lcell(nr,nr),lnext(n)
real(R8) :: x(n),y(n),f(n),rsq(n),a(5,n),xmin,ymin,dx,dy,rmax,value
k=0
do j=0,3
  do i=0,3
    k=k+1; x(k)=real(i,R8); y(k)=real(j,R8); f(k)=x(k)**2+y(k)**2
  end do
end do
call QSHEP2(n,x,y,f,8,8,nr,lcell,lnext,xmin,ymin,dx,dy,rmax,rsq,a,ier)
if (ier /= 0) error stop "Shepard setup failed"
value=QS2VAL(1.5_R8,1.5_R8,n,x,y,f,nr,lcell,lnext,xmin,ymin,dx,dy,rmax,rsq,a)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Link the supplied blas_shep helper routines along with the precision and QSHEP2D modules. The grid-shaped sample is passed through the scattered-data API; no accuracy or polynomial-reproduction test was run. A zero QS2VAL return does not identify a successful zero value versus no support. Keep every setup array/scalar consistent with the original nodes.

classifications.notes: QS2GRD differentiates the compact Shepard quotient using nodal quadratic derivatives and derivatives of the weights. At a supplied node it returns F and the local linear coefficients A(4:5). E3a2 records derivatives of the fitted bivariate interpolant, not derivatives of an arbitrary callback or an automatic-differentiation service. Requires successful QSHEP2 data. local.name: BDDCML
local.description: Multilevel balancing domain decomposition solver library with subdomain matrix interfaces.

classifications.notes: The README documents the multilevel BDDC solver interface, matrix input modes and external numerical libraries. No working local installation is claimed.

The public bddcml_solve method selector 0 dispatches to preconditioned conjugate gradients for SPD systems using the multilevel BDDC preconditioner. The native Krylov module applies level preconditioning and distributed matrix/vector operations; this is not a classification inferred solely from an external sparse factorization dependency. Initialize MPI, upload the global or subdomain FEM problem and construct the preconditioner with a compatible matrix type first. A direct-only level configuration overrides the selected iterative method with a direct solve, so the mapping requires an iterative configuration. CONVERGED_REASON=0 means the relative-residual criterion was met, -1 means the iteration limit and -2 the nondecreasing-residual limit. Solution values remain in internal state until downloaded. The condition-number estimate belongs to the PCG path and is not an independent conditioning/accuracy guarantee. Shared level/Krylov state and MPI collectives require consistent calls across participating ranks. Review covers public dispatch and selected recurrence/preconditioner paths, not every mesh decomposition, singular problem or scalability case.

local.name: EigenExa
local.description: Parallel matrix eigensolver library with real and Hermitian solver variants.

classifications.notes: The README provides the build procedure; release notes discuss eigenmode algorithms and experimental Hermitian solver support. Kept at D4 rather than asserting every matrix-type specialization is verified.

EIGEN_S is the public module dispatcher for real symmetric distributed dense eigenproblems. It selects the configured EIGEN_S0 or EIGEN_FS implementation; inspected paths scale the matrix, reduce to real tridiagonal form, solve by divide-and-conquer/bisection and back-transform eigenvectors. MPI and EigenExa initialization precede the call, and EIGEN_GET_MATDIMS supplies required local storage for the configured two-dimensional cyclic distribution and work padding. A is overwritten, including implementation performance fields, so preserve the mathematical input for residuals. NVEC controls requested vectors and MODE selects values/vectors/refinement variants; the sketch selects A and all vectors. There is no public INFO dummy, and silent early returns/implementation error state must not be mistaken for a verified solution. Source review covers module dispatch and selected reduction/solve/backtransform calls, not all distributed kernels or every build configuration.

use mpi

local.name: Fortran Davidson
local.description: Davidson and generalized Jacobi-Davidson algorithms for selected eigenpairs.

classifications.notes: The README describes DPR/GJD correction methods and an optional second matrix for generalized problems. Its stated suitability for diagonally dominant symmetric matrices is retained; broader robustness is not established.

The inspected dense ordinary-problem path projects a real symmetric matrix into a basis, dispatches DSYEV on the projected matrix, forms Ritz vectors/residuals, appends diagonal-preconditioned corrections and reorthogonalizes/restarts the basis. This mapping is restricted to METHOD=DPR with SECOND_MATRIX absent; generalized and matrix-free paths remain outside this review. The convergence check uses residual norms, despite argument prose describing eigenvalue error. HAS_CONVERGED flags remain true across iterations, so ALL(HAS_CONVERGED) need not mean all current residuals satisfy tolerance. DPR divides by eigenvalue-minus-diagonal without a near-zero safeguard. Initial basis has 2*LOWEST columns and expansion can exceed limits without robust shape validation. No numerical convergence or complete LAPACK/helper audit was performed.

local.name: Interpolative Decomposition Library
local.description: Low-rank matrix approximation through interpolative decompositions.

classifications.notes: The README identifies the ID low-rank matrix approximation library and points to detailed documentation. It notes a transfer to GitLab; this entry describes the pinned GitHub snapshot, not the latest version elsewhere.

iddr_qrpiv selects columns by trailing norms, builds Householder transformations and updates/recomputes pivot norms for a fixed-rank real QR. iddr_id then composes the pivot swaps into selected-column indices and backsolves R11*proj=R12, packing interpolation coefficients into the start of overwritten A. D5 records the QR-based decomposition path; ID is not an SVD, and selected original columns must be retained from a copy. Require 1<=krank<=MIN(m,n): the QR helper clips loop count but the ID wrapper subsequently accesses the requested rank. rnorms receives signed diagonal entries despite absolute-value wording in its header. Large interpolation coefficients are zeroed at a fixed 2**20 comparison, not reported as a numerical-error status. No matrix approximation, reference QR or error bound was checked by execution.

local.name: chol-rev
local.description: Reverse-mode differentiation through a Cholesky factorization.

classifications.notes: The README documents the adjoint primitive that propagates factor sensitivities to the original positive-definite matrix. This is not classified as a general-purpose Cholesky solver or a complete automatic-differentiation system.

DPO2FT walks the lower Cholesky factor backward, propagating supplied factor adjoints through diagonal division, BLAS matrix/vector updates and diagonal halving. DPOFRT performs the corresponding blocked updates and delegates diagonal blocks to DPO2FT. This is a reverse first-derivative primitive for a scalar objective depending on an already-computed positive-definite Cholesky factor, not a factorization, solve or complete automatic-differentiation system. Only UPLO=L is implemented in the nonempty paths; the upper branches call XERBLA without reliably setting the advertised INFO=-8. Input checks omit LDC, so the caller must enforce it. The blocked path may overwrite entries above the selected triangle. Preserve the author triangular-adjoint convention when passing sensitivities onward. BLAS/LAPACK support routines and matching integer ABI are required. No adjoint identity or finite-difference comparison was run.

local.name: HOMPACK90

classifications.notes: The README documents dense and sparse Jacobian variants and ODE-based, normal-flow and augmented-Jacobian algorithms. Fixed-point and tracking support is recorded in the scope rather than asserting all specialized GAMS leaves.

HOMPACK90::FIXPNF initializes a homotopy path and controls dense normal-flow continuation with STEPNF, switching tolerances on curvature and dispatching ROOTNF when lambda reaches 1. With IFLAG=-1 it targets F(X)=0, using externally linked F and Jacobian-column FJAC callbacks specified by HOMOTOPY; IFLAG=0 instead solves a fixed-point problem and -2 selects a supplied homotopy. Source-visible input checks, adaptive tolerance updates, 1000-step continuation returns and cleanup are reviewed at driver level. IFLAG=1 is normal termination; 2/3 are resumable with saved state, and 4..8 record failures. Saved path arrays/scalars make interleaved solves unsafe without separate contexts. POLY_SWITCH is tested by presence, not logical value, so omit it for ordinary zero finding. No global-convergence guarantee, complete STEPNF/ROOTNF/kernel audit or numerical solve was established.

local.name: NITSOL

classifications.notes: The nitsol.f interface documentation describes backtracking, GMRES/BiCGSTAB/TFQMR and analytic or finite-difference Jacobian-vector products. Only interface documentation is reviewed, not convergence behavior.

The reviewed NITSOL path solves a square residual system with inexact Newton steps and residual-norm backtracking. The public driver validates option selections, partitions caller workspace and dispatches to nitdrv. The inspected GMRES path uses Jacobian-vector products, modified Gram-Schmidt and Krylov corrections; nitjv chooses supplied analytic products or directional finite differences and optional right preconditioning. nitbt evaluates trial residuals and reduces the step until its decrease condition holds. F2 is the system-of-equations leaf; the internal linear solves and residual norms do not make this a general nonlinear least-squares or optimization API. BiCGSTAB/TFQMR dispatch is present, but those implementations were not reviewed. Normal termination also permits a small-step criterion without the residual reaching ftol, so independently check the returned residual. local.name: ORTHPOL
local.description: Orthogonal-polynomial generation and Gauss-type quadrature rules.

classifications.notes: The brief README explicitly identifies orthogonal-polynomial and Gauss-type rule generation. No particular rule family, accuracy bound or integration API is inferred from the repository name.

The inspected DGAUSS routine constructs an n-point Gaussian rule from the monic orthogonal-polynomial recurrence coefficients. It builds the symmetric tridiagonal Jacobi matrix implicitly, iterates eigenvalues and first eigenvector components, sorts nodes and scales squared components by dbeta(1), the measure mass. It returns nodes and weights rather than invoking an integrand or returning an integral. H2c is therefore the precise quadrature-service mapping; an internal eigensolver does not make this a general eigensystem API. The caller must supply a valid positive integration measure and consistent recurrence coefficients. Negative beta entries and iteration exhaustion have error returns; eps is an eigensolver convergence parameter, not a requested integration-error bound. procedures.summary: External double-precision Gaussian-rule constructor. dalpha(n), dbeta(n), dzero(n), dweigh(n), and workspace de(n) are required. dbeta(1) is the total mass; later entries are recurrence coefficients. external :: dgauss
integer, parameter :: n=4
integer :: i, ierr
double precision :: alpha(n), beta(n), nodes(n), weights(n), work(n), q
alpha = 0.0d0
beta(1) = 2.0d0
do i=2,n
  beta(i) = dble(i-1)**2/(4.0d0*dble(i-1)**2-1.0d0)
end do
call dgauss(n,alpha,beta,epsilon(1.0d0),nodes,weights,ierr,work)
if (ierr /= 0) error stop "Gaussian rule failed"

classifications.notes: The README lists supported geometric domains, symmetry variants, rule files and driver programs. Mapping is multidimensional quadrature; author drivers have not been executed here.

The inspected triasymq entry retrieves tabulated reference-triangle nodes and weights, expands the D3 symmetry and maps them affinely to caller-supplied vertices. trianmap rescales weights to the absolute triangle area. adaptive_integrator%integrate wraps a procedure-pointer integrand, allocates work storage, obtains tolerances and subdivision limits, and dispatches the no-breakpoint finite-interval path to DQAGS. local.name: AUTO-07p
local.description: Continuation and bifurcation analysis for ordinary differential equations.

classifications.notes: The manual title and preface explicitly describe continuation and bifurcation of ODEs, including homoclinic-orbit analysis. This is not presented as an ordinary initial-value time-stepper.

AUTO is an initialized continuation application, not a drop-in stateless equation solver. Its framework supplies AUTOPARAMETERS, active parameter indices, weights, callbacks, restart/start data, output units and configured MPI state; prefer its supported run/CLUI workflow for ordinary use. Direct-call sketches below are post-framework-initialization contracts only. AE::AUTOAE controls continuation of real nonlinear algebraic systems through CNRLAE and SOLVAE. The corrector forms a bordered system from FUNI values/Jacobians and the continuation constraint, solves it with pivoted GEL, and tests relative parameter/state corrections against EPSL/EPSU within ITNW iterations. A failed corrector restores the old state and returns NIT=0 internally; AUTOAE itself has no scalar success dummy or returned solution array, since state and files are managed by the framework. The interface takes internal FUNI/STPNAEI/FNCI callbacks from interfaces.h, not the shorter user FUNC signature. Non-root ranks return immediately on this algebraic path. This mapping covers real nonlinear-system continuation and its Newton corrector, not a guarantee of finding every root, branch, bifurcation or global solution.

classifications.notes: MESH::ADAPT2 is a public service routine for retabulating AUTO solution/tangent data while changing the number of mesh intervals and/or collocation points. NEWMSH equidistributes a monitor based on differences of high-order derivative estimates; INTERP uses local Lagrange weights to transfer both UPSR and VPSR. If old and new counts agree it copies rather than adapts the mesh. Use positive strictly increasing interval meshes, at least two old intervals on the selected nonperiodic path, supported collocation orders 2..7, adequate zero-based sample storage and NDIM=NDOLD in the selected sketch. When dimensions differ only MIN(NDIM,NDOLD) components are assigned, so added components remain undefined. No status or verified error bound is returned; the monitor and interpolation do not prove ODE/BVP solution accuracy. classifications.notes: MESH::INTWTS forms Lagrange cardinal weights for nodes numbered 0..N. The caller evaluates the interpolating polynomial by a dot product of WTS with N+1 nodal samples; DT1DT is expressed in node-index units, not normalized physical coordinates. For an interval [a,a+h] sampled at a+j*h/N, pass N*(x-a)/h. The public GENWTS companion generates value/derivative weights at fixed collocation points, while private INTERP demonstrates actual piecewise sample transfer using INTWTS. Restrict N to the small supported AUTO collocation orders (2..7 in the sketch): the integer factorial/product denominators are not overflow guarded and arbitrary high degree is unsafe. There is no barycentric stabilization, shape preservation, conditioning estimate or status output. This mapping is polynomial interpolation of already sampled values, not fitting noisy data or selecting an adaptive degree.

classifications.notes: MESH::GENWTS constructs both value weights WT and first-derivative weights WP of the polynomial through NCOL+1 equally spaced samples on the normalized interval [0,1], evaluated at NCOL interior Gauss-Legendre collocation points. The caller obtains derivatives by DOT_PRODUCT(WP(:,IC),VALUES); physical interval width h requires division by h, as shown in SOLVBV. This is numerical differentiation of sampled data through the interpolating polynomial, not automatic/symbolic differentiation of a user routine. Use NCOL in 2..7 and arrays with first index 0:NCOL. Unsupported orders are not rejected: the private CPNTS SELECT CASE has no default and leaves collocation nodes undefined. No accuracy, noise sensitivity or error estimate is returned. local.name: CUTEst
local.description: Testing environment and problem interfaces for constrained and unconstrained optimization software.

classifications.notes: CUTEst supplies optimization test infrastructure and decoded problem interfaces. It is placed under software tools, not labeled as an optimization algorithm. Problem-specific SIF decoding may be required.

The external CUTEST_UOFG routine evaluates the objective and optionally its gradient for a previously decoded/setup unconstrained SIF problem. It dispatches through global CUTEST data/work state to element/group evaluation and derivative accumulation, updates work/counters and reports failures in STATUS. It does not minimize the objective, choose search directions or establish optimizer convergence, so the source mapping is a numerical problem-evaluation service rather than an optimization-solver leaf. GRAD=false leaves G unsuitable as a computed gradient. The default public names and kinds are selected by preprocessing: CUTEST_UOFG_R becomes CUTEST_UOFG, and the provided interface module becomes CUTEST_INTERFACE_DOUBLE in the normal double/32-bit build. A matching SIF-decoded OUTSDIF.d plus compiled ELFUN/GROUP/RANGE routines and a successful USETUP are prerequisites; the global wrapper is distinct from per-workspace threaded variants. No objective or derivative was numerically checked.

local.name: FilterSD
local.description: Filter-method nonlinear programming with sparse or dense matrix representations.

classifications.notes: The README describes original Fortran 77 algorithms and an ongoing modernization. Sparse and dense variants have distinct required source files; compiler readiness and individual problem-class claims remain unchecked.

filterSD solves local nonlinear programming with two-sided bounds on variables and nonlinear constraint values. It maps workspace and dispatches filter_SD, whose inspected phase-one/phase-two control uses GLCPD linearized subproblems, feasibility/objective filter tests and projection/step evaluations. External functions and gradients callbacks provide objective/constraints and their first derivatives; a reduced-Hessian/limited-memory mechanism is internal, not a required user Hessian. G2h3b1b records smooth nonlinear equality/inequality constrained optimization with supplied first derivatives. Supply matching dense or sparse derivative backends, invariant sparse structure and COMMON block settings including workspace capacities. X needs N+M storage; multipliers and final violation are distinct from a success certificate. IFAIL=3 means a locally infeasible point, not proof that the original feasible set is empty. IFAIL>=7 can return before workspace is scattered into X/AL. No NLP, derivative checks or GLCPD/kernel accuracy audit was executed.

 maxa,maxla,maxu,maxiu,kmax,maxg,rho,htol,rgtol,maxit,iprint,nout,ifail)

The cited generic driver uses CUTE data and is not a standalone sample problem. Check feasibility and stationarity independently.

classifications.notes: checkd perturbs one variable at a time by caller-supplied nonzero AL increments and compares each objective/constraint forward difference quotient with the supplied derivatives at both endpoints, using backend AIJ access. G4c records a first-derivative consistency diagnostic, not numerical certification of analytic derivatives. An inconsistency is printed and causes immediate RETURN without a machine-readable status or restoring the current perturbed X(i); preserve X before calling. Normal completion restores coordinates and prints an exit message. Insufficient workspaces STOP the process. A quotient between endpoint derivatives can pass despite an incorrect derivative, and cancellation/domain violations depend on the chosen increments/tolerance. No diagnostic was run.

local.name: Cedar
local.description: BoxMG variational multigrid library for parallel PDE-related solves.

classifications.notes: The README identifies variational multigrid and gives serial/MPI Poisson examples. No broader PDE equation families are assigned from the generic framework description.

The selected native BoxMG restriction and correction-prolongation entries are associated operations used inside a structured-grid multigrid linear solver. BMG2_SymStd_restrict accumulates a fine-grid vector to coarse interior points using transpose interpolation weights CI; periodic cases update input ghost cells in Q. BMG2_SymStd_interp_add adds coarse corrections to existing fine Q and also adds residual/diagonal terms at noninjection nodes: it is not pure interpolation of arbitrary data. It divides interior RES by the stencil diagonal in place, requiring nonzero diagonals and fresh residual storage before repeated calls. Provide matching BoxMG hierarchy extents/coarsening, initialized CI/stencil/boundary constants and ghost layers; these routines do not construct CI, solve a system, check convergence or return an error status. ModInterface defines len_t=C_INT and real_t=C_DOUBLE. Both external routines are BIND(C) with VALUE scalar dimensions/selectors, so Fortran callers need an exact explicit interface; USE ModInterface alone does not declare these external entries. The selected sketches cover serial 2-D transfer contracts, not MPI/3-D kernels or complete multigrid convergence.

local.name: mtprng
local.description: Fortran 95 Mersenne Twister pseudorandom-number generator library.

classifications.notes: The README identifies the generator family and Fortran interface/build instructions. This does not establish statistical quality, stream independence or suitability for cryptography.

The inspected stateful MT19937 path seeds 624 words, twists and tempers 32-bit outputs carried in INT64 storage, and scales them by 2^-32 in mtprng_rand_real2 for intended [0,1) uniform output. It is not a 64-bit-payload generator despite the rand64 function name. Explicit mtprng_init is essential: default mti=-1 bypasses the outer mti>=624 block that encloses the proposed lazy-seed test, then indexes mt(-1). The default-state path is therefore unsafe. This review covers explicit positive single-seed initialization and real2 dispatch, not array seeding, range conversion, normal sampling or statistical/bitwise validation. No generator was run.

local.name: BesselEval
local.description: Evaluation of real-order Bessel J and Y functions using precomputed expansions.

classifications.notes: The README restricts orders to nonnegative real values and arguments to positive reals, with phase/logarithmic variants. Required precomputed tables are documented; timing and accuracy statements have not been independently reproduced.

bessel_eval accepts nonnegative real order up to 1e9 and positive real argument, dispatching J_nu/Y_nu evaluation among tabulated expansions, small-argument series and asymptotic routines. In the inspected table path, bivariate Chebyshev coefficients represent phase/phase derivative in the oscillatory region or log magnitudes in the nonoscillatory region; values are recovered by trigonometric/exponential formulas. C10a3 is the real-argument, real-order cylindrical Bessel scope, not complex-argument or modified Bessel functions. Call bessel_eval_init first; it reads fixed relative binary filenames into shared module state using unit 20. Repeated init returns without assigning DSIZE. Missing tables or invalid parameter ranges STOP rather than return an error; binary layout, real-kind promotion and endianness must match. Auxiliary phase/log outputs are branch-dependent and initially zero, not universally valid derivatives/logarithms. No accuracy, binary-portability or advertised timing result was tested; series/asymptotic coefficient derivations were not fully audited.

local.description: Quadruple-precision evaluation of the real Gamma function in Fortran 77.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly implements real Gamma using reciprocal-series expansion, recurrence and reflection. The mathematical discussion of complex Gamma is not taken as evidence of a complex-argument implementation.

The inspected GAMMA_MOD::TGAMMA evaluates real Gamma by a 48-coefficient reciprocal-Gamma expansion in Horner form, recurrence products after reducing |X|, and reflection for negative noninteger arguments of magnitude above one. Positive integer arguments take a factorial-product branch. C7a records Gamma evaluation; no log-Gamma, reciprocal-Gamma output API, incomplete Gamma or complex extension is inferred. QP=selected_real_kind(32) requires compiler support for at least 32 decimal digits and sufficient range for the source literal 1e4000. At zero/negative integer poles the routine returns that finite sentinel rather than an IEEE infinity or status. Default-INTEGER conversions of X are not range-guarded; NaN, infinities, overflow and large recurrence products are not handled robustly. The last DATA coefficient lacks the _QP suffix used by the others, so coefficient rounding deserves checking before asserting a full precision guarantee. gamma.f also contains a main test program after the module; extract/build the module separately when linking a different main. No accuracy or pole/overflow case was executed.

classifications.notes: The public CONV generic computes finite linear convolution. The selected real64 and complex64-component overloads choose output length SIZE(X)+SIZE(Y)-1, pad to a power-of-two FFT length, multiply spectra, apply the inverse transform and trim. The complex operation does not conjugate Y; this is convolution, not cross-correlation or circular convolution. Real output discards the tiny imaginary FFT residue. A complete driver compares both double-precision overloads against independent nested finite sums for every pair of lengths 1 through 7, including unequal lengths and length-one inputs. All 98 vector comparisons passed with maximum normalized error 3.608225e-16. Single-precision variants take a different length path and were not checked. Use the public generic names, not their private specific functions. The checked GNU build maps real/complex KIND=8 to binary64 components and INTEGER(KIND=4) to 32-bit integers; these numeric kind values are not a portable kind-selection contract. Inputs and effective FFT lengths must be positive. Each FFT rebuilds factor/twiddle workspaces and discards backend IERR, so the caller receives no explicit numerical status or estimate. Wrapper work arrays are declared complex while the external FFTPACK routines expect real storage; the selected GNU ABI accepts this implicit-interface storage usage, which is not a portable interface guarantee. The old backend also has mismatched argument/storage conventions requiring -fallow-argument-mismatch; it was compiled without bounds instrumentation. procedures.summary: Public fftpack generic; selected double-precision finite convolution interface.
procedures.usage:
! GAMS J2: fftpack::conv checked against direct finite convolution.
program convolution
 use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
 use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
 use fftpack, only: conv
 implicit none
 integer :: nx,ny,i,j,count
 real(real64), allocatable :: x(:),y(:),r(:),reference(:)
 complex(real64), allocatable :: z(:),w(:),c(:),creference(:)
 real(real64) :: error,maximum
 maximum=0;count=0
 do nx=1,7
  do ny=1,7
   allocate(x(nx),y(ny),reference(nx+ny-1),z(nx),w(ny),creference(nx+ny-1))
   do i=1,nx
    x(i)=(-1._real64)**i*real(i,real64)/3
    z(i)=cmplx(x(i),0.1_real64*i,kind=real64)
   end do
   do j=1,ny
    y(j)=0.2_real64*j-0.7_real64
    w(j)=cmplx(y(j),-0.15_real64*j,kind=real64)
   end do
   reference=0;creference=0
   do i=1,nx
    do j=1,ny
     reference(i+j-1)=reference(i+j-1)+x(i)*y(j)
     creference(i+j-1)=creference(i+j-1)+z(i)*w(j)
    end do
   end do
   r=conv(x,y);c=conv(z,w)
   if(size(r)/=nx+ny-1 .or. size(c)/=nx+ny-1) error stop 'convolution size'
   if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(r))) error stop 'nonfinite real convolution'
   if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(real(c))) .or. .not.all(ieee_is_finite(aimag(c)))) error stop 'nonfinite complex convolution'
   error=maxval(abs(r-reference))/max(1._real64,maxval(abs(reference)))
   maximum=max(maximum,error)
   if(error>5.e-12_real64) error stop 'real convolution mismatch'
   error=maxval(abs(c-creference))/max(1._real64,maxval(abs(creference)))
   maximum=max(maximum,error)
   if(error>5.e-12_real64) error stop 'complex convolution mismatch'
   count=count+2
   deallocate(x,y,reference,z,w,creference,r,c)
  end do
 end do
 print '(a,i0)', 'Direct convolution comparisons: ',count
 print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized error: ',maximum
 print '(a)', 'PASS convolution'
end program

procedures.summary: Public fftpack generic; selected double-precision periodic analytic signal interface.
procedures.usage:
! GAMS J4: fftpack::hilbert for binary64 real input, analytic periodic signals.
program analytic
 use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
 use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
 use fftpack, only: hilbert
 implicit none
 integer,parameter :: sizes(*)=[1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9,10,16,17]
 integer :: k,n,j,m,count
 real(real64),allocatable :: x(:)
 complex(real64),allocatable :: z(:),want(:)
 real(real64) :: angle,nyquist,error,maximum,pi
 maximum=0;count=0;pi=acos(-1._real64)
 do k=1,size(sizes)
  n=sizes(k)
  allocate(x(n),want(n))
  do m=0,(n-1)/2
   do j=0,n-1
    angle=2*pi*m*j/n
    nyquist=0
    if(mod(n,2)==0) nyquist=0.3_real64*(-1._real64)**j
    if(m==0) then
     x(j+1)=1.25_real64+nyquist
     want(j+1)=cmplx(x(j+1),0._real64,kind=real64)
    else
     x(j+1)=1.25_real64+0.7_real64*cos(angle)+0.2_real64*sin(angle)+nyquist
     want(j+1)=cmplx(x(j+1),0.7_real64*sin(angle)-0.2_real64*cos(angle),kind=real64)
    end if
   end do
   z=hilbert(x)
   if(size(z)/=n) error stop 'analytic signal size'
   if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(real(z))) .or. .not.all(ieee_is_finite(aimag(z)))) error stop 'nonfinite analytic signal'
   error=maxval(abs(z-want))/max(1._real64,maxval(abs(want)))
   maximum=max(maximum,error)
   if(error>5.e-12_real64) error stop 'analytic signal mismatch'
   count=count+1
  end do
  deallocate(x,want,z)
 end do
 print '(a,i0)', 'Analytic periodic signal comparisons: ',count
 print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized error: ',maximum
 print '(a)', 'PASS analytic'
end program

Implicit external real/complex storage conventions remain an ABI limitation despite these passing finite checks.

classifications.notes: The public FFT generic accepts a real double-precision vector and returns the full complex spectrum through the complex-double backend. It does not use a packed-real output format or a specialized real FFT kernel. Optional positive N truncates the input or appends zeros. The normalization is the unscaled negative-exponent forward DFT; the wrapper compensates for the backend normalization by multiplying by N. The driver independently forms every spectral bin with a direct trigonometric sum for lengths 1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9,10,16,17, at the original length, N+3 padding and MAX(1,N-2) truncation. All 33 vector comparisons passed with maximum normalized error 4.540382e-15. This finite test set covers several mixed-radix/prime lengths, not every kernel or arbitrary transform size. Use the public generic names, not their private specific functions. The checked GNU build maps real/complex KIND=8 to binary64 components and INTEGER(KIND=4) to 32-bit integers; these numeric kind values are not a portable kind-selection contract. Inputs and effective FFT lengths must be positive. Each FFT rebuilds factor/twiddle workspaces and discards backend IERR, so the caller receives no explicit numerical status or estimate. Wrapper work arrays are declared complex while the external FFTPACK routines expect real storage; the selected GNU ABI accepts this implicit-interface storage usage, which is not a portable interface guarantee. The old backend also has mismatched argument/storage conventions requiring -fallow-argument-mismatch; it was compiled without bounds instrumentation. The wrapper and catalog mains were compiled with bounds checks and floating-point traps. These numerical checks do not establish standard conformance, full-backend memory safety, other compilers, large-array sizing or single-precision behavior. Existing GPL/version and wrapper-license scope findings remain; no upstream source is bundled here. The complete driver was compiled and run locally on Windows with GNU Fortran 17.0.0 20260510 (experimental). All results must be finite and normalized maximum error must not exceed 5e-12.

procedures.summary: Public fftpack generic; selected double-precision real-input full-spectrum Fourier transform interface.
procedures.usage:
! GAMS J1a1: fftpack::fft(real64) checked against an independent direct DFT.
program real_dft
 use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
 use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
 use fftpack, only: fft
 implicit none
 integer,parameter :: sizes(*)=[1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9,10,16,17]
 integer :: k,n,i,j,mode,dim,count
 real(real64),allocatable :: x(:)
 complex(real64),allocatable :: z(:),want(:)
 real(real64) :: angle,error,maximum,pi
 maximum=0;count=0;pi=acos(-1._real64)
 do k=1,size(sizes)
  n=sizes(k)
  allocate(x(n))
  do i=1,n
   x(i)=cos(0.4_real64*i)-0.1_real64*i
  end do
  do mode=1,3
   select case(mode)
   case(1);dim=n;z=fft(x)
   case(2);dim=n+3;z=fft(x,dim)
   case(3);dim=max(1,n-2);z=fft(x,dim)
   end select
   if(size(z)/=dim) error stop 'DFT output size'
   allocate(want(dim));want=0
   do j=0,dim-1
    do i=0,min(n,dim)-1
     angle=-2*pi*j*i/dim
     want(j+1)=want(j+1)+x(i+1)*cmplx(cos(angle),sin(angle),kind=real64)
    end do
   end do
   if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(real(z))) .or. .not.all(ieee_is_finite(aimag(z)))) error stop 'nonfinite DFT'
   error=maxval(abs(z-want))/max(1._real64,maxval(abs(want)))
   maximum=max(maximum,error)
   if(error>5.e-12_real64) error stop 'DFT mismatch'
   count=count+1
   deallocate(want,z)
  end do
  deallocate(x)
 end do
 print '(a,i0)', 'Direct real-input DFT comparisons: ',count
 print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized error: ',maximum
 print '(a)', 'PASS real_dft'
end program

The wrapper and main used -O0 -g -Wall -Wextra -ffree-line-length-none -fcheck=all -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow. procedures.procedure: real double to complex transform dispatch

classifications.notes: The public fftpack::xcorr generic implements finite zero-extended cross-correlation using inverse FFT of FFT(X)*CONJG(FFT(Y)). It pads to a power of two at least 2*MAX(NX,NY)-1 and rearranges the result to lags 1-MAX(NX,NY) through MAX(NX,NY)-1. At lag K the convention is SUM_J X(J+K)*CONJG(Y(J)) over valid indices. Unequal lengths still return the symmetric maximum-length lag range, including zero tails. This is an uncentered unnormalized cross-product sum: no mean subtraction, variance normalization or overlap-count division is performed. Real overloads discard the numerically negligible imaginary roundoff of the complex result; single overloads compute through the double-complex path then round the output. All four KIND=4/8 real/complex overloads are exercised by the complete driver for both lengths 1..7 and three patterns (dense trigonometric vectors, endpoint impulses, zero first signal): 588 direct-sum comparisons. Maximum normalized binary64 error was 3.717673e-16 and binary32 error 5.062557e-8, below tolerances 2e-12 and 2e-6. Single inputs are rounded before constructing independent references. GNU Fortran 17.0.0 20260510 (experimental), Windows, compiled and ran the main at O0 with bounds checks and invalid/zero/overflow traps. The unmodified FFTPACK backend was built with -fallow-argument-mismatch and without bounds instrumentation; implicit external real/complex storage conventions remain a portability and full-memory-safety limitation. The wrapper ignores IERR and rebuilds workspaces. Positive small lengths and ordinary finite data are the checked contract; empty arrays, large sizes, extreme amplitudes, optimized builds and other compilers were not checked. This mapping is for two-series cross-correlations (L10b2a), not correlation coefficients, spectral estimation or statistical significance.

procedures.summary: Public generic for raw finite cross-correlation of real or complex vectors, with single and double overloads. Output index K+MAX(NX,NY) represents lag K; complex Y is conjugated.
procedures.usage:
﻿program correlation
  use fftpack, only: xcorr
  use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
  implicit none
  integer :: nx, ny, n, pattern, i, j, lag, count
  complex(kind=8), allocatable :: x(:), y(:), reference(:), z(:)
  real(kind=8), allocatable :: r(:), real_reference(:)
  complex(kind=4), allocatable :: xs(:), ys(:), zs(:)
  real(kind=4), allocatable :: rs(:)
  real(kind=8) :: scale, error, max_double, max_single
  count=0; max_double=0; max_single=0
  do nx=1,7
    do ny=1,7
      n=max(nx,ny)
      allocate(x(nx),y(ny),reference(2*n-1),real_reference(2*n-1),xs(nx),ys(ny))
      do pattern=1,3
        do i=1,nx
          x(i)=cmplx(sin(real(2*i+nx,8)),cos(real(i+ny,8)),8)
        end do
        do i=1,ny
          y(i)=cmplx(cos(real(3*i+ny,8)),sin(real(i-nx,8)),8)
        end do
        if(pattern==2)then
          x=0; y=0
          x(nx)=cmplx(2.0_8,-1.0_8,8); y(1)=cmplx(-3.0_8,2.0_8,8)
        else if(pattern==3)then
          x=0
        end if
        reference=0; real_reference=0
        do lag=1-n,n-1
          do j=1,ny
            i=j+lag
            if(i>=1.and.i<=nx)then
              reference(lag+n)=reference(lag+n)+x(i)*conjg(y(j))
              real_reference(lag+n)=real_reference(lag+n)+real(x(i),8)*real(y(j),8)
            end if
          end do
        end do
        z=xcorr(x,y)
        call check_complex(z,reference,2e-12_8,.false.)
        r=xcorr(real(x,8),real(y,8))
        call check_complex(cmplx(r,0.0_8,8),cmplx(real_reference,0.0_8,8),2e-12_8,.false.)
        ! Round inputs before the single-kind reference comparisons.
        xs=cmplx(x,kind=4); ys=cmplx(y,kind=4)
        reference=0; real_reference=0
        do lag=1-n,n-1
          do j=1,ny
            i=j+lag
            if(i>=1.and.i<=nx)then
              reference(lag+n)=reference(lag+n)+cmplx(xs(i),kind=8)*conjg(cmplx(ys(j),kind=8))
              real_reference(lag+n)=real_reference(lag+n)+real(xs(i),8)*real(ys(j),8)
            end if
          end do
        end do
        zs=xcorr(xs,ys)
        call check_complex(cmplx(zs,kind=8),reference,2e-6_8,.true.)
        rs=xcorr(real(xs,4),real(ys,4))
        call check_complex(cmplx(rs,0.0_4,8),cmplx(real_reference,0.0_8,8),2e-6_8,.true.)
      end do
      deallocate(x,y,reference,real_reference,xs,ys)
    end do
  end do
  print '(a,i0)', 'Direct-sum cross-correlation comparisons: ',count
  print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized binary64 error: ',max_double
  print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized binary32 error: ',max_single
  print '(a)', 'PASS correlation'
contains
  subroutine check_complex(actual,expected,tolerance,single)
    complex(kind=8), intent(in) :: actual(:),expected(:)
    real(kind=8), intent(in) :: tolerance
    logical, intent(in) :: single
    if(size(actual)/=size(expected))error stop 'Wrong output size'
    if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(real(actual,8))))error stop 'Nonfinite real output'
    if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(aimag(actual))))error stop 'Nonfinite imaginary output'
    scale=max(1.0_8,maxval(abs(expected)))
    error=maxval(abs(actual-expected))/scale
    if(error>tolerance)then
      print *,nx,ny,pattern,error,tolerance
      error stop 'Cross-correlation differs from direct sums'
    end if
    if(single)then
      max_single=max(max_single,error)
    else
      max_double=max(max_double,error)
    end if
    count=count+1
  end subroutine
end program

local.name: fstpack
local.description: One-dimensional Stockwell and two-dimensional discrete orthonormal Stockwell transforms.

classifications.notes: The README documents Fortran/Python interfaces and inverse transforms. It cautions that independent negative-frequency content of complex input is not preserved; a generic complex FFT claim is not made.

cfst1f Fourier-transforms the input, doubles positive frequencies and clears negative bins through cht1f, then inverse-transforms Gaussian-weighted circularly shifted spectra into frequency voices. cfst1b sums the voices, restores conjugate negative-frequency content and transforms back. J records the one-dimensional Stockwell integral-transform service because this taxonomy has no Stockwell leaf; it is not classified as a plain Fourier transform merely because FFTs implement it. Default-kind COMPLEX input/output, allocated forward bounds (0:N/2,0:N-1), DC voice SUM(H)/N, and inverse voice/time layout are source-visible. Intended round trips assume real-valued data represented as complex; independent negative-frequency information is discarded. Require nonempty input and a correctly shaped inverse array; failures use ERROR STOP, not returned status. The 2D DOST and voice-extraction paths are outside the selected usage review. No transform/round trip was executed.

procedures.summary: Public pure module function returning allocatable default-kind COMPLEX voices. First dimension is frequency, second time; input is unchanged. Input lower bound is rebased to zero inside the routine.

h=cmplx([0.,1.,0.,-1.,0.,1.,0.,-1.],0.)
s=cfst1f(h)
restored=cfst1b(s)

This sketch uses real-valued samples stored as default COMPLEX; it does not establish invertibility for arbitrary complex signals. The lower bounds of an allocatable assignment result need not retain the function internal bounds, so use LBOUND/UBOUND when accessing coefficients. classifications.notes: The README documents transform types 1/2/3, F77/F90 workspace variants and direct evaluation routines for checks. This entry describes the pinned legacy distribution, not current FINUFFT or another successor.

The selected external nufft1d1f90 driver computes centered complex Fourier modes from nonuniform source locations using Gaussian spreading, an oversampled FFTPACK transform and modewise deconvolution. local.name: akima86
local.description: Akima 1986 univariate interpolation with a Python interface and Fortran implementation.

classifications.notes: The README cites the univariate interpolation algorithm and documents a gfortran-backed Python build. No assertion is made that the Python packaging exposes a standalone Fortran library interface.

The reviewed UVIPIA general path (ND>=5) locates successive intervals, estimates endpoint derivatives from weighted neighboring three-point slope estimates, forms cubic coefficients for NP<=3 or higher-degree basis factors, and evaluates the corresponding interval polynomial. This supports univariate piecewise-polynomial interpolation E1a, not a global polynomial, spline-system solve or smoothing fit. Ordered distinct XD is checked; invalid input prints a message and leaves YI at -9999 without a status argument. End extrapolation is linear, using endpoint slope estimates. The sketch uses NP=3 and ND=7; selecting larger NP does not establish higher-order derivative-estimate accuracy or shape preservation. Material findings: the general query loop unconditionally prints the OpenMP thread number and query index; the separate ND=4 cubic a3 formula repeats yuse(1) in its second term where the distinct second ordinate would be expected. That small-data branch requires checking/correction and is excluded from the sketch. No accuracy, small-data case or OpenMP execution was verified.

local.name: Interpolation in 2D and 3D
local.description: Modernized interfaces to Renka scattered-data interpolation on planar, spherical and three-dimensional domains.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes srfpak, sphpak, qshep2d and qshep3d and their geometries. Gradient estimation is documented; the suite is not assigned a single univariate interpolation class.

The inspected quadratic_shepard_2d wrapper creates local quadratic models for scattered planar points through alg660::qshep2. The reviewed core builds weighted least-squares systems, applies Givens rotations and solves for nodal quadratic coefficients. qs2val blends those local polynomials with compact-support modified Shepard weights, returning the stored value exactly at a node; qs2grd differentiates that weighted quotient. E2b is scattered multivariate interpolation, not gridded tensor-product interpolation. Only this 2D path is reviewed: the spherical, triangulation and 3D variants are not certified here. The wrapper fixes neighbor counts, uses default REAL and requires at least six equal-length samples. Duplicate/collinear configurations and unsupported query locations have status paths. Query methods assume successful construction and do not guard against unallocated data. No interpolation or gradient check was run.

local.name: NdSpline
local.description: Multidimensional B-spline interpolation.

classifications.notes: The brief README identifies multidimensional B-spline interpolation and cites its mathematical reference. Boundary conditions, supported dimensions and derivative interfaces require further review.

The inspected spline object constructs tensor-product B-spline coefficients on Cartesian-product axes by solving one-dimensional basis systems successively, then evaluates target grids via basis matrices and BLAS products. Cox-de Boor recursion implements the basis, and the author 2D example concatenates x/y axes and flattens f(i,j) in Fortran order. This establishes gridded multivariate interpolation E2a, not scattered-data fitting. The basis order k means degree k-1 (k=4 is cubic). Supply valid strictly increasing axes and compatible sizes/orders. DGESV info is ignored in set_coefs_1d, so singular/invalid interpolation systems are not reported to the caller. Extrapolation is a saved module-wide flag shared across objects, not an object-specific setting; omitted init arguments retain its previous value. Reinitialization requires cleanup, and fin assumes initialized allocations. This review excludes skip_solve-only workflows and does not establish interpolation accuracy, extrapolation safety or derivative APIs. No author test was run.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound generic initializer for type(spline). ks(:) gives B-spline orders and ns(:) gives axis sizes; xs concatenates axes with length SUM(ns), and fs flattens the source grid with length PRODUCT(ns), first axis varying fastest. Use real64 arrays, at least two axes for this mapped scope, 1 <= ks <= ns, and valid distinct increasing axis coordinates. Set extrapolation explicitly; keep skip_solve false when evaluating data. Failures may STOP and no status is returned.
procedures.signature: CALL sp%init(ks, ns, xs, fs, extrapolation, skip_solve)

procedures.summary: Public type binding for a Cartesian-product query grid. ns(:) gives target axis sizes and xs concatenates target axes. Results are stored as the flat allocatable component sp%fs, not returned as an argument; reshape to the target shape in Fortran order. Read/copy sp%fs before fin. Use an initialized, fully solved object and queries inside the source domain; shape mismatches are not a recoverable status interface.

use NdSpline, only: spline, dp
type(spline) :: sp
real(dp) :: axis(3), values(3,3), result(1,1)
integer :: i,j
axis = [0.0_dp,1.0_dp,2.0_dp]
do j=1,3
  do i=1,3
    values(i,j) = axis(i)+axis(j)
  end do
end do
call sp%init([2,2],[3,3],[axis,axis],reshape(values,[9]), &
             extrapolation=.false.)

local.name: mp-interp
local.description: Mean-preserving interpolation of averaged time series into finer intervals.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes four mean-preserving approaches and explains monthly-to-daily examples. This mapping concerns temporal interpolation, not statistical inference from the interpolated series.

The inspected public ainv_int path constructs a cyclic neighboring-interval mean matrix from interval lengths, explicitly inverts it with LAPACK DGETRF/DGETRI, adjusts the input means, then calls a midpoint-based piecewise-linear daily interpolator and computes discrete interval means. classifications.notes: The README describes lower/upper/percentage limits and a monthly-temperature example. Preservation and bound behavior have not been reproduced for this catalog.

local.name: PPR
local.description: Conservative piecewise polynomial reconstruction and remapping on one-dimensional structured grids.

classifications.notes: The README identifies ppr_1d, rcon1d and rmap1d with PCM/PLM/PPM/PQM and limiter variants. These are reconstruction/remapping components; their use inside transport examples is not treated as a general PDE solver.

The reviewed PCM path of ppr_1d reconstructs piecewise-constant cell profiles from cell means and remaps them by integrating profile/target-cell overlaps. rcon1d dispatches to pcm, which copies each cell mean as its constant coefficient; rmap1d/xmap1d selects that one-coefficient representation, and imap1d evaluates integral basis differences and divides the accumulated mass by target-cell width. A subsequent compensated-sum defect correction adjusts an extremal target mean. This establishes a degree-zero piecewise-polynomial reconstruction/remapping path in E1a; it is not point-sample interpolation or a standalone PDE integrator. Restrict this review to ndof=1, PCM, compatible monotone source/target edges over the same domain and positive cell widths. The higher-order PLM/PPM/PQM and limiter implementations were not fully reviewed. Workspaces and all option fields must be initialized; the init methods dereference opts even though declared optional. No conservation, positivity or remapping-accuracy test was run.

procedures.summary: Module routine reconstructing cell moments. For the reviewed PCM path, use ndof=1, opts%cell_meth=pcm_method and initialized work/options. fdat and fhat have shape (1,nvar,npos-1); delx is positive spacing, length one for uniform grids or npos-1 otherwise.
