local.name: diaglib
local.description: Matrix-free iterative eigensolvers including Davidson, LOBPCG and linear-response methods.

classifications.notes: The README documents distinct symmetric, generalized and nonsymmetric drivers with user-supplied matrix actions and preconditioners. Keeping the suite at D4 avoids extending one driver capability to every other driver.

DGL_DAVIDSON_DRIVER computes a few lowest eigenpairs of a real symmetric ordinary eigenproblem using caller block matrix-vector and preconditioner routines, subspace projection, Rayleigh-Ritz extraction, residual expansion and restart/locking. This mapping selects no METVEC argument, hence identity metric. Require 1<=N_TARG<=N_MAX with 2*N_MAX<N, a truly symmetric operator, compatible configured integer kind and suitable initial guesses. It checks both RMS and maximum residual components for targeted roots. OK reports convergence, whereas DGL_INFO reports API/numerical errors: budget exhaustion can leave INFO=0 with OK false and approximate eigenpairs. This is not a dense full-spectrum solver or a new eigenpair/orthogonality validation.

local.name: DLA-Future Fortran Interface

classifications.notes: The README explicitly identifies this repository as an interface to DLA-Future. It is not an independent self-contained eigensolver implementation; build details and backend requirements need further review.

DLAF_PDSYEVD is a public Fortran binding for ordinary real-symmetric distributed eigenproblems. Its native Fortran layer passes host array addresses, block-cyclic descriptors and scalar controls through BIND(C) to the separately linked DLA-Future implementation. local.name: Cyclic banded matrix solvers
local.description: Solvers for cyclic tridiagonal and general cyclic banded systems.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes dctsv and dcbsv and their LAPACK/BLAS dependencies. Documented dependency-removal alternatives are not assumed to be enabled in every build.

The inspected serial DCTSV solves real square cyclic tridiagonal systems with multiple right-hand sides by paired endpoint elimination, small determinant solves for the even/odd terminal cases, and back substitution. DL(1) stores the top-right corner and DU(N) the bottom-left corner. Those corners make this a general real system rather than an ordinary tridiagonal matrix in the displayed ordering; D2a1 is used without implying a dense factorization. D/DL/DU are read-only and B is overwritten by solutions. N>=4 and leading-dimension checks precede work. No pivoting is implemented; exact-zero intermediate determinant checks do not prove singularity of the entire matrix, and INFO=0 is not a conditioning or accuracy certificate. The README recommends diagonal dominance and warns that error grows faster with N than LU. This review excludes general wider-band and OpenMP variants. No solve, residual or timing comparison was executed.

procedures.summary: External double-precision cyclic tridiagonal solver. Supply N>=4, NRHS>=0, DL(N), D(N), DU(N), and B(LDB,NRHS), with LDB>=N. The wrapped corner elements are part of DL/DU. B becomes the solution; diagonals are preserved. Check INFO, but also assess residuals independently. Link XERBLA (normally supplied by LAPACK).

external :: dctsv
integer :: info
double precision :: dl(4), d(4), du(4), rhs(4,1)
dl=-1.0d0
d=4.0d0
du=-1.0d0
rhs(:,1)=2.0d0
call dctsv(4,1,dl,d,du,rhs,4,info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "cyclic elimination failed"

Retain a copy of the original RHS for that check. This routine does not return reusable LU factors. Default INTEGER and double precision must match the linked error-handler ABI; positive INFO is an elimination-breakdown indication, not proof that every possible solver would fail.

classifications.notes: The separate external thomas routine performs forward elimination and backward substitution for an ordinary real tridiagonal system with k right-hand sides. The lower diagonal a(i) is read for i=2..n, the upper c(i) for i=1..n-1; a(1) and c(n) are unused. It overwrites b and d while returning solutions in z. local.name: FORbID
local.description: Object-oriented definite-integral quadrature with Newton-Cotes, Gaussian and adaptive methods.

classifications.notes: The alpha-status README distinguishes implemented formulas from unchecked plans. Planned multidimensional Monte Carlo and acceleration methods are not classified as existing functionality.

The reviewed Newton-Cotes method evaluates a concrete integrand object at n+1 equally spaced nodes on a finite interval. init selects closed-rule weights for degrees 1..10, and integrate_1D performs a single fixed weighted sum without a tolerance or error estimate, supporting the nonautomatic callback quadrature leaf H2a1a2. Source finding: weights use the usual h=(b-a)/n normalization but the final multiplication uses (b-a)*k without dividing by n. Thus degrees above one appear scaled by n; the calling sketch is restricted to n=1 (trapezoidal rule). Unsupported degrees are not rejected and leave zero weights; no success status is returned. The inherited adaptive_integrate reads an INTENT(OUT) accumulator before defining it and is excluded from the calling sketch. 2D/3D bindings are empty result-returning stubs and receive no mapping. No quadrature output was run or checked.

DUALSIMPLEX maximizes C-transpose*X subject to A*X<=B by applying revised simplex to the asymmetric dual. local.name: FortRAND
local.description: Random sampling utilities built around the Fortran intrinsic pseudorandom generator.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes wrapping intrinsic uniform generation from algorithms for other distributions. It does not define an independent base generator family or establish stream independence.

The public random generic dispatches to intrinsic RANDOM_NUMBER for REAL(dp) scalar values and builds interval/list/integer variants from repeated scalar calls. L6a21 records intended uniform output. Every scalar draw first calls RANDOM_INIT(.false.,.false.), reinitializing the intrinsic generator rather than advancing an explicitly seeded local stream. This can defeat caller seeding, adds reseeding work and provides no guarantee of independent repeated values. Integer sampling scales a real draw with FLOOR; b<=a is rejected including a singleton interval, and b+1-a can overflow. No randomness, endpoint, stream-independence or compiler comparison was executed.

local.name: normal-deviates
local.description: Univariate and multivariate normal random generation from a mean and covariance matrix.

classifications.notes: The README documents the MultiNormalGenerator interface and rejects nonsymmetric or non-positive-definite covariance matrices. No behavior for singular covariance is claimed.

The public MultiNormalGenerator constructor builds 128 Ziggurat strips; get checks shapes/symmetry, factors the covariance in a private Cholesky helper, fills independent scalar normal proposals and applies mean + L*z to each sample row. This supports the multivariate normal generation intent (L6b14). Important implementation qualifications: strip indices use IAND(NINT(U*10000),127), which is not exactly uniform over 128 strips; the tail logs unguarded RANDOM_NUMBER results, which can be zero. Symmetry uses absolute tolerance 1e-6 and Cholesky rejects updated diagonal values below 1e-6, including some small positive-definite covariances. The intrinsic RNG is global rather than owned by each object. This source mapping does not certify exact distribution, randomness quality or empirical covariance; no samples were run.

local.name: spherical_bessel_fortran
local.description: Spherical Bessel functions of the first kind for real and complex arguments.

classifications.notes: The README documents sbessj and zsbessj and discusses reliability limits near zeros and parameter extremes. Its reported digits of accuracy and author comparisons have not been reproduced here.

The inspected real SBESSJ evaluates spherical j_n(x), choosing a power series for |x|<=0.78*n and upward recurrence from sin(x)/x and (sin(x)/x-cos(x))/x otherwise. At x=0 the series returns j_0=1 and j_n=0 for n>0. C10a3 (real argument, real order) is used for the half-integer cylindrical-Bessel subset: j_n(x)=sqrt(pi/(2*x))*J_(n+1/2)(x) for positive x (NIST DLMF 10.47.3, https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.47.E3). The procedure exposes only nonnegative integer spherical n, not arbitrary real cylindrical orders, Y/Hankel or modified I/K functions. Negative order, a flagged low-accuracy positive-x region for n>50, and series nonconvergence print diagnostics and STOP. The low-accuracy guard uses x rather than abs(x), so negative-x reliability is not established by that guard. Series stopping uses an absolute term threshold and a finite 20+2*n budget; it supplies neither a returned error estimate nor a status code. Precision/accuracy claims in comments/README were not reproduced. Complex and quad variants and the comparison implementation remain outside this source review. No Bessel value or recurrence residual was executed.

local.name: Elliptic K via AGM
local.description: Complete elliptic integral of the first kind using the arithmetic-geometric mean.

classifications.notes: The README defines K(k) with modulus k, lists supporting-module dependencies and describes precision variants. Optional real128 support depends on the compiler; parameter/modulus conventions must be respected in future drivers.

The inspected REAL64 elliptic_k overload evaluates the complete Legendre elliptic integral of the first kind with modulus k. It forms the complementary modulus as sqrt((1-k)*(1+k)); for k*k<0.5 it returns (pi/2)/AGM(1,k-prime), and otherwise uses an AGM/elliptic-nome logarithmic transformation. C14 is the elliptic-integrals leaf in this taxonomy; complete first-kind scope is recorded in the procedure rather than inventing a narrower code. IEEE branches return quiet NaN for NaN input or |k|>1 and positive infinity for |k|=1. Material limitation: although the interface advertises |k|<=1, the second branch calls arithmetic_geometric_mean_kernel(1,k), not AGM(1,abs(k)); negative k with k*k>=0.5 therefore reaches a signed-input dependency path and must not be assumed valid. The sketch uses nonnegative modulus and the simple direct branch. Dependencies are unpinned Git references in fpm.toml, and their full AGM/nome algorithms are outside this review. The committed module unconditionally imports/declares REAL128 as well as REAL32/64, so its build needs that kind despite README calling it optional. No integral or reference test was executed.

local.name: KFAS
local.description: R state-space modeling software with Fortran kernels for Kalman filtering and smoothing.

classifications.notes: The README and DESCRIPTION document Gaussian/non-Gaussian state-space inference, filtering and smoothing. This is an R package with compiled numerical components, not a ready-made standalone Fortran API.

KFILTER performs sequential-observation Kalman filtering for a linear Gaussian state-space model, including optional exact diffuse initialization via P1INF/RANKP. The inspected ordinary branch updates innovations, gain, mean/covariance and log likelihood, then propagates the state with T and R*Q*R^T. TIMEVAR has five 0/1 selectors controlling third-dimension lengths of Z,H,T,R,Q. YMISS=0 means observed; positive missing flags skip measurement updates. The scalar-observation sketch avoids the requirement to transform correlated multivariate measurement errors before sequential filtering: the core uses diagonal H entries. AT(:,t) and PT(:,:,t) are prediction states before observation t; the optional THETA output uses those predictions and is not a smoothed estimate. Likelihood accumulation and tolerance-based zero-innovation handling do not certify covariance positivity or model fit. Review covers driver and ordinary/diffuse one-step recurrences, not every R-facing data transformation or non-Gaussian smoother.

local.name: PDAF
local.description: Parallel data-assimilation framework with ensemble Kalman, nonlinear and variational methods.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes assimilation algorithms, model coupling, observation handling and ensemble infrastructure. Particular model integrations and MPI/OpenMP configurations remain unverified for this catalog.

The public PDAF_ASSIMILATE_ETKF entry schedules ensemble-transform Kalman analysis within an initialized multivariate state-space forecast workflow. It invokes forecast operations at each call, passes collected state/observation/error callbacks through PUT_STATE_ETKF when the forecast interval ends and redistributes the next ensemble forecast. OUTFLAG=0 can mean an ordinary forecast step with no analysis due, not proof that every call assimilated data; nonzero status must be handled. This is multivariate time-series/state-space analysis L10c, not a physical-domain PDE mapping or an independently validated forecast system. Review covers public scheduling/dispatch and selected native ETKF algebra, not the complete model/callback ecosystem.

local.name: Fortress
local.description: Modern Fortran components for Bayesian time-series estimation with Python bindings.

classifications.notes: The README describes Fortran-library and Python workflows with optional MPI/OpenMP. Specific posterior samplers and model families await procedure-level review.

KALMAN_FILTER evaluates per-observation Gaussian log-likelihood contributions for a linear state-space model. It initializes zero state mean and a stationary covariance using DLYAP, then forms innovations/covariances, performs the Kalman prediction update and accumulates contributions only for t>T0. The selected one-observation-channel use fits the univariate state-space class; the implementation also accepts multivariate observations, but this map does not infer a smoother or returned state trajectory from a likelihood-only function. Require stable transition dynamics and positive-definite innovation covariances. The basic path does not handle missing observations; separate missing-data functions exist. DLYAP and Cholesky/inversion status values are not propagated by this API, so finite likelihood output alone is not a convergence or factorization certificate. The reviewed non-SLICOT DLYAP branch uses covariance doubling; the SLICOT conditional branch has its solver call commented out and must not be assumed equivalent. Review covers the basic filter and initializer, not every alternate recursion or particle-filter method.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly calls this a toy/experimental project, notes gfortran-only availability and possible memory leaks, and points to Fazang as an alternative. It is not presented as a production-ready AD system.

The inspected scalar reverse-mode path builds pointer-linked nodes with local product/addition/exponential derivatives. tree_t%backward seeds the output adjoint to one, then recursively distributes local-derivative products; shared input nodes accumulate contributions. get_grad reads the stored scalar adjoint. local.name: FOLLIA
local.description: Object-oriented Lagrange interpolation on uniform and nonuniform one-dimensional grids.

classifications.notes: The README describes Lagrange coefficients and one-dimensional grid interpolation, with alpha status. No multidimensional API or independent accuracy verification is inferred.

The inspected type generates S separate degree-at-most-S-1 Lagrange polynomials on overlapping S-point stencils drawn from 2*S-1 nodes. compute_coefficients forms the product-form basis at one target, and compute_interpolations applies each stencil column to stored Y values, returning S estimates. E1b records single-polynomial interpolation within each stencil; the source does not choose or combine these estimates into one piecewise or WENO interpolant. Default coordinates are the integers -S+1..S-1; optional coordinates must provide the same 2*S-1 layout with distinct increasing values. S>=2 is required by the initializer accesses to x(-1), x(0) and x(1), but is not validated. The target must lie between the midpoints adjacent to x(0) and must not equal x(0); failure uses ERROR STOP. No duplicate-node, ordering or optional-array-size check is supplied, and no error estimate/status is returned. Recompute coefficients after changing coordinates/target. No polynomial reproduction or driver execution was checked.

local.name: FortranConsoleSpline
local.description: Cubic spline interpolation with natural or prescribed endpoint slopes and derivative evaluation.

classifications.notes: The README documents value, first/second derivative and extremum interfaces, plus linear behavior outside the data range. Endpoint and extrapolation behavior have not been independently checked.

The module constructs and evaluates a real64 univariate piecewise-cubic interpolant from ordered samples, with optional endpoint first derivatives and natural endpoint conditions when slopes are absent. The type-bound value, slope and slope2 methods evaluate the interpolant and its derivatives; outside the data range the implementation suppresses the cubic terms, giving linear value/slope extrapolation and zero second derivative. E1a is the supported polynomial-spline classification; this is not smoothing, multidimensional fitting or a generic global-extremum solver. Source inspection found a material construction discrepancy: the interior coefficient sig uses x(i)-(i-1), mixing an abscissa with an index, instead of the adjacent abscissa difference expected for the documented arbitrary-grid cubic-spline recurrence. The extrema helper continues bisection even after its same-sign endpoint branch, so no root/extremum enumeration claim is added. Neither the author example nor interpolation accuracy was tested.

classifications.notes: The README separates inverse-distance weighting, triangle barycentric interpolation and bilinear interpolation. Its example shows larger boundary deviations; these methods are not treated as interchangeable or uniformly accurate.

local.name: KernelyzeBase
local.description: Low-rank approximation of bivariate kernel functions.

classifications.notes: The README describes separable rank-reduced representations and sign-regular kernels. Optimality and comparative error claims are author statements; the entry is classified as approximation rather than a generic interpolation solver.

EIGEN_RANKN_PARAMS forms sqrt(Wx)*K*sqrt(Wy), computes a dense SVD and constructs Nystrom coefficients for separated singular-function kernel approximation, with X_FUNC_WTS sized (NY,RANK) and Y_FUNC_WTS (NX,RANK). This is a quadrature-discretized approximation for a supplied concrete two-variable kernel; it is not a uniform/global minimax error certificate. Although input guards allow nonnegative weights, later code divides by their square roots, so supply strictly positive finite weights; retained singular values must be nonzero before reciprocal scaling. Rank must be positive and no larger than either point count. No extra guard handles zero retained singular values, numerical rank deficiency or ill-conditioned kernels. The review covers this selected approximation path, not every numerically-optimal/rank-reduction algorithm in the larger library.

procedures.summary: Public pure module Nystrom/SVD coefficient generator. Always request ERR_STAT/ERR_MSG and also ensure positive weights and usable retained singular values.

use set_precision, only: wp

integer :: status
character(len=err_msg_len) :: message
x=[-1.0_wp,0.0_wp,1.0_wp]; y=x; w=1.0_wp/3.0_wp
call eigen_rankn_params(gaussian,2,x,y,w,w,xw,yw, &
     singular_values,status,message)
if(status/=0) error stop "Kernel approximation failure"

classifications.notes: BRENTZERO finds a scalar bracketed zero using bisection, secant and inverse-quadratic steps with finite iteration and function-evaluation tracking. Require a continuous finite-valued function on the bracket, a valid tolerance and positive iteration budget; the sign check multiplies endpoint values, so extreme scaling/overflow needs attention. The convenience ZEROIN function discards status, so the sketch selects the explicit-status service. local.name: polynomial_interpolation
local.description: Lagrange interpolation with derivative estimates and an interpolation-quality indicator.

classifications.notes: The README documents arbitrary data points and an auxiliary grid-to-grid interpolation routine. An error indicator is not described as a rigorously certified error bound.

poly_interp implements a Neville-style Lagrange correction recurrence for the polynomial through n+1 distinct samples, also propagating derivative corrections. It evaluates at zero, so callers shift their abscissae by the desired query. This is a single polynomial (E1b), distinct from the local moving-stencil grid wrapper. Output y(0) is the value and y(k) is derivative k, not divided Taylor coefficients. dy is the last signed interpolation correction, not a certified error bound. There is no input-validation/status interface; duplicate nodes divide by zero. Restrict this reviewed use to n >= 1 and 0 <= nd <= n: for n=0 or derivative orders beyond n, some dy entries need not be assigned. Accuracy, conditioning and behavior on closely spaced nodes were not checked by execution.

procedures.summary: External routine using selected_real_kind(12), named REAL64 locally. Pass xin(0:n), yin(0:n), output y(0:nd), dy(0:nd), degree n >= 1 and derivative limit 0 <= nd <= n. xin must contain distinct offsets from the target point, not absolute nodes unless querying zero. No error status is returned. dy entries are signed corrections, not guaranteed absolute errors.
procedures.signature: CALL poly_interp(y, dy, xin, yin, n, nd)
procedures.usage:
external :: poly_interp
integer, parameter :: rk=selected_real_kind(12)
real(rk) :: nodes(0:2), values(0:2), offsets(0:2), y(0:1), correction(0:1)
nodes = [0.0_rk,1.0_rk,2.0_rk]
values = nodes**2
offsets = nodes-0.5_rk
call poly_interp(y,correction,offsets,values,2,1)
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled calling sketch. The analytic value/first derivative at 0.5 are 0.25 and 1, but no comparison was run. Match selected_real_kind(12) consistently with the external routine. A small final correction does not certify interpolation error, and duplicate or nearly coincident input abscissae need independent validation.

classifications.notes: The inspected ordered-grid branch of grid_interp selects a local n+1-point stencil for each target, shifts its abscissae to that target and calls poly_interp. Stencil changes produce a piecewise-polynomial interpolation scheme (E1a), without an established spline smoothness condition at transitions. Both values and requested derivatives are copied into the target matrix. The wrapper checks some sizes and rejects extrapolation outside a scale-dependent tolerance. The unordered-grid sorting path is present but outside this source review. Its reported dymax is updated as a maximum of signed dy values starting from zero, rather than absolute corrections, so negative corrections can be hidden; it is not an absolute error estimate. Use distinct strictly ordered samples, in-range ordered targets and 0 <= nd <= n. No grid interpolation or derivative error check was executed.

local.name: SOSIE
local.description: Interpolation of scalar and vector fields between geophysical grids.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes scalar/vector interpolation and vector-component correction, with netCDF Fortran dependencies. The vector correction executable has a documented default ORCA-grid restriction.

The public AKIMA_1D generic selects a vector path which extends data by two synthetic samples at each end, computes local Akima slopes and evaluates cubic Hermite polynomials between increasing source abscissae. Require matching array sizes, at least three distinct ordered valid source points and finite values; extension construction reads a third point. REAL(8) source/query arguments feed REAL(4) extended arrays, slopes and output. Without persistence flags, unlocated/out-of-range queries retain -6666.0. The optional missing sentinel is designed for contiguous missing boundaries, not arbitrary internal gaps; its boundary-index logic should be independently checked before use. L_SURF_PERSIST and L_BOTM_PERSIST are copied into initialized local logical variables that have implicit SAVE; omitting them after another call can retain previous settings. Set both explicitly to obtain predictable call behavior. Size mismatches STOP and no recoverable solver status is returned. The separate 3-D overload is not covered here.

local.name: spharm-interp
local.description: Scattered-data fitting and interpolation on the sphere using spherical harmonic expansions.

classifications.notes: The README describes least-squares fitting followed by expansion evaluation. Drivers use MATLAB/Octave with Fortran MEX kernels; author demonstration errors are not catalog-verified results.

The selected ylgndr recurrence evaluates normalized associated Legendre functions for nonnegative degree/order, n<=nmax and 0<=m<=n, at finite x in [-1,1]. The normalization is sqrt(2*n+1)*sqrt((n-m)!/(n+m)!)*P_nm(x), with the negative diagonal square-root recurrence incorporating the Condon-Shortley sign. Only the lower triangle of y is assigned; other entries are undefined. There is no domain/status check or derivative output in this selected routine. This Fortran special-function mapping is separate from the MATLAB scattered-point fit and does not establish high-degree stability by execution.

procedures.summary: External REAL*8 associated-Legendre evaluator. Supply nmax>=0, finite -1<=x<=1 and y(0:nmax,0:nmax); read only entries with m<=n.

integer, parameter :: nmax=3
double precision :: y(0:nmax,0:nmax)
external :: ylgndr
call ylgndr(nmax,0.25d0,y)
! Read y(n,m) only for 0<=m<=n<=nmax.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The normalized functions differ from raw associated Legendre polynomials. This routine does not return derivatives or a numerical status. Match the implementation REAL*8 ABI; do not interpret the unassigned upper triangle.

classifications.notes: The selected sheval3d/ sheval3d0 pair evaluates an already supplied spherical-harmonic expansion at one point using ylgndr and exp(i*m*phi) recurrence, combining both positive and negative orders. Coefficients use mpole(0:nterms,-nterms:nterms) and only abs(m)<=n is read. The basis omits the usual 1/sqrt(4*pi) factor. The helper comment about scaling by 1/sqrt(2*l+1) is not reflected in an extra scaling operation after ylgndr. No output status, coefficient fit or approximation-error check was performed.

SPLIFT assembles/factors a tridiagonal system for nodal second derivatives with user endpoint relations, solves it and recovers first derivatives; SPLINT locates intervals by hunt/bisection and evaluates cubic values/first/second derivatives. ISX=1 reuses the factorization only when nodes, workspace and endpoint coefficients are unchanged; validation is skipped on that reuse path. Success is IERR/KERR=1, not zero. SPLINT extrapolates the end cubic and returns KERR=2; equal adjacent nodes can STOP. N<4 fitting returns zero derivatives and IERR=2 rather than the normal cubic result. No interpolation, derivative or extrapolation accuracy was run; integration through SPLIQ is outside this mapping.

local.name: SPRINT
local.description: Grid interpolation with bilinear interpolator interfaces and cached point weights.

classifications.notes: The inspected source interface identifies regular and curvilinear grids and cached weights. Periodic boundary handling is explicitly a TODO; source-interface inspection is not a full implementation or numerical review.

The inspected structured-grid path prepares four tensor-product bilinear weights from normalized x/y coordinates, caches them by a formatted coordinate key, and applies them to four supplied values. E2a records gridded bivariate interpolation; the type does not fetch a full field or perform three-/four-coordinate interpolation (higher-rank values carry extra fields). Important source defects prevent a general-use recommendation: REAL(8) regular-grid preparation uses FLOOR without the required one-based offset and leaves the fourth corner second index zero by writing corner 3 twice; REAL(4) uses CEILING but excludes the lower endpoint and accepts some cells past the final valid interval. apply calls prepare on a cache miss but computes its result only in the ELSE branch, leaving the first return undefined unless prepare is called explicitly. apply neither guards outside points nor checks value-array extents. Its corner order is (lower-left, lower-right, upper-right, upper-left) mapped to input positions (1,1),(2,1),(1,2),(2,2), not the usual rectangular-field order. The sketch is a restricted REAL(4), strictly interior, explicitly prepared interface illustration. Curvilinear location/inversion and dependencies are not audited. No interpolation or defect was reproduced by execution.

procedures.summary: Public generic type-bound initializer. Scope here is private REAL(4) one-dimensional-axis binding: x(nx), y(ny), optional default-INTEGER cache_size. It copies axes into REAL(8) storage and creates the cache. Regular axes must be increasing and equidistant, each with at least two points; no validation enforces this. Curvilinear overloads exist but are not the illustrated path.

Public generic for caching a point. The illustrated REAL(4) binding accepts scalar x/y and mutates the cache. Call explicitly before apply to avoid its unassigned first-return path. Boundary handling has documented defects, so the sketch uses a strictly interior point of a two-by-two grid.

Public generic, scoped to the REAL(4) scalar-field binding. Supply a two-by-two array in the source corner order: (1,1)=LL, (2,1)=LR, (1,2)=UR, (2,2)=UL, plus REAL(4) query coordinates. It mutates the cache; a prior prepare call is required for a defined return. Do not pass a conventional field slice without checking the swapped upper-corner ordering.

use bilinear_interpolator_mod, only: bilinear_interpolator_type
type(bilinear_interpolator_type) :: interp
real(4) :: x(2), y(2), corners(2,2), value
x=[0.0,1.0]
y=[0.0,1.0]
call interp%init(x,y)
call interp%prepare(0.25,0.5)
if (interp%is_outside(0.25,0.5)) error stop "point classified outside"
! Values of f=x+2*y in the SOURCE corner order, not normal field order.
corners(1,1)=0.0
corners(2,1)=1.0
corners(1,2)=3.0
corners(2,2)=2.0
value=interp%apply(corners,0.25,0.5)

The README identifies TRIPACK/STRIPACK triangulation and SRFPACK/SSRFPACK interpolation/derivatives. These are Python-facing interfaces with Fortran kernels, not a standalone Python-free Fortran API.

The selected fixed-form TRIPACK TRMESH routine incrementally constructs an unconstrained planar Delaunay triangulation in linked adjacency storage. It initializes a noncollinear triangle, inserts nodes and swaps edges using orientation/circumcircle tests and nearest-node search starts. Require distinct coordinates and a noncollinear first triple. LIST/LPTR need 6*N-12 storage, LEND/NEAR/NEXT/DIST need N. IER distinguishes invalid size, initial collinearity, duplicate nodes and internal swap failure; partial adjacency is not a completed mesh on failure. This is planar triangulation rather than spherical geometry or a PDE discretization. The selected fixed-form source uses default REAL and is included by SRFPACK; the separate tripack.f90 variant uses REAL(8) and must not be mixed blindly with these call declarations. Review covers construction and storage contracts, not robust exact predicates or every constrained-edge operation.

local.name: ttcross

classifications.notes: The README documents tensor cross interpolation and separate MC/QMC/cross-integration experiments. Approximation and integration are distinct capabilities; no universal convergence or accuracy claim is made.

The README documents tensor cross interpolation and separate MC/QMC/cross-integration experiments. Approximation and integration are distinct capabilities; no universal convergence or accuracy claim is made.

DMRGG_LIB::DTT_DMRGG adaptively samples a tensor-valued function at selected multi-indices, updates TT cross pivots/cores and increases bond ranks. It uses MPI distribution/communication and optional OpenMP callback evaluation; the callback has the positional convention FUN(M,IND,N,PAR). MAXRANK bounds growth and ACCURACY tests sampled pivot magnitude relative to a reference for three consecutive strikes, not a rigorous global residual bound over every tensor entry. The routine wipes an incoming nonempty TT state to rank-one initialization. Require initialized MPI with number of ranks strictly less than tensor dimension M, positive mode sizes, valid callback parameters, consistent precision and safe indices. Some diagnostics read ME before MPI_COMM_RANK initialization. This review covers the adaptive driver and inspected pivot/termination paths, not all lower-level max-volume/inversion kernels, every process partition or the optional quadrature application.

procedures.summary: Public module MPI TT cross-interpolation driver. Callback must remain safe under the configured threading/parallel call pattern.

use tt_lib, only: dtt,dealloc
use dmrgg_lib, only: dtt_dmrgg
type(dtt) :: approximation
double precision :: parameters(1)
double precision,external :: sampled_tensor
! MPI_INIT must precede this collective call on matching ranks.
! sampled_tensor(m,ind,n,parameters) returns a double precision value.
approximation%m=3; approximation%n(1:3)=[2,2,2]
parameters=1.0d0
call dtt_dmrgg(approximation,sampled_tensor,par=parameters, &
     accuracy=1.0d-6,maxrank=4)
call dealloc(approximation)
! MPI_FINALIZE follows after all collective work.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. This fragment omits callback definition and MPI setup intentionally; use fewer than three MPI ranks for these three modes. Pass PAR explicitly when the callback expects it, and use an exact matching callback signature/storage ABI. No tensor residual, function evaluation count, rank cap or MPI experiment was run.

local.name: Fortran Least Squares Problems
local.description: Lawson-Hanson least-squares routines including nonnegative and bounded-variable problems.

classifications.notes: The README documents HFTI, NNLS, BVLS and related routines and modern interfaces. Additional SVD/rotation utilities are noted but not all mapped to separate classes in this review.

The legacy NNLS routine initializes x=0, selects columns using the largest positive dual-gradient component, applies Householder transformations, solves the passive triangular system, and uses a feasibility interpolation/Givens update loop to move nonpositive coefficients back to the zero set. It returns a residual norm and mode, supporting constrained L2 linear least squares D9b1 with x>=0. A and b are overwritten by orthogonal transformations. Mode=1 succeeds, 2 rejects nonpositive M/N, and 3 reports the 3*N iteration limit. Leading dimensions/workspace extents remain caller obligations. This review follows active-set control and the included transformation helpers, not a numerical proof or a complete audit of all package solvers. The simplified module wrapper was inspected but shares a file with a test main; the calling sketch uses the independently linkable legacy routine. No fit or KKT/residual check was executed.

local.name: PyIntegral
local.description: Fortran numerical integration of tabulated arrays and functions with Python interfaces.

classifications.notes: The reviewed README lists trapezoidal, Simpson and Gaussian methods. The repository formerly listed as IntegralALL now resolves to PyIntegral; the catalog uses the current canonical repository identity.

The external GAUSSLEGENDREQUADRATURE routine generates successive n-point Gauss-Legendre rules with polynomial recurrence/Newton root refinement, linearly interpolates tabulated X/Y at those nodes and returns the last weighted sum. This is nonautomatic finite-interval quadrature of gridded data, not a callback integrator or accuracy-controlled algorithm. N_INT is the last quadrature order, not a tolerance. Source finding: an optional-argument fallback computes N_INTERATIONS, but the actual loop uses N_INT directly; omitting it references an absent optional argument. Orders below one leave Z undefined. LININTERPOL status is ignored and its indexing is unsafe even for in-range queries: resetting its saved index to -1 can start the upward search at -2. The calling sketch does not repair this. The rule generator caps Newton refinement at ten steps without reporting nonconvergence. This review does not promote the larger INTEGRALALL dispatcher or every branch to source-reviewed.

local.name: generic_rk
local.description: Modular Runge-Kutta ODE integration with adaptive-timestep examples.

classifications.notes: The brief README describes modular ODE solvers and a Brusselator initial-value example. Method inventory, stiffness handling and error-control guarantees need source review.

The active rk_wrapper path selects the explicit seven-stage Dormand-Prince embedded tableau, then uses two weighted stage estimates for adaptive one-step integration of a callback-defined initial-value system. Tolerances are hard-coded to sqrt(machine epsilon), the estimator uses an L2 difference and a global maximum component scale, and accepted states use the bstar estimate. This records intended one-step nonstiff scope, not verified order or accuracy. A material source finding is that calc_k initializes dummy_y only once before the stage loop and accumulates all successive stage sums into it, instead of rebuilding each stage from y; the implemented stages therefore need correction/checking before relying on the named method. The first adaptive trial is not clipped to the interval endpoint; clipping occurs after a step. Rejection exhaustion STOPs; there is no status output. The routine writes to unit 22. Implicit/nonlinear-solver branches and their stiff suitability are not reviewed or mapped.

local.name: RKSUITE
local.description: Runge-Kutta software for first-order ODE initial-value systems.

classifications.notes: The original RKSUITE README documents the intended initial-value problem class. This pinned distribution is not assumed to have every modernization or compiler adaptation found in other forks.

The reviewed Fortran 90 module provides setup plus range_integrate/step_integrate for a real first-order ODE vector. Setup validates shapes, tolerance/thresholds and direction, selects an explicit RK method and allocates state. The controller calls explicit stage combinations, estimates local error from an embedded pair with threshold-weighted max norm, rejects/shrinks or accepts/rescales steps, and returns requested output through interpolation when supported. I1a1a records one-step nonstiff IVP methods. Stiffness detection warns rather than turning this into an implicit stiff solver. This review covers the public stateful driver contract and selected stage/error-control paths, not all coefficient tables, interpolants or global-error assessment. Fatal errors stop by default and successful flag=1 is not a global-accuracy bound. Setup nullifies pointers, so collect_garbage before reinitializing allocated state; shallow copying communication objects is unsafe. No ODE or author template was run.

local.name: dae4py

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes Python implementations and Fortran wrappers. DASKR and DASPK wrappers are marked not implemented yet; they are not advertised as existing functionality.

The vendored DDASKR driver solves implicit differential/algebraic systems G(t,y,yprime)=0 with variable-order BDF integration, direct dense/band or preconditioned Krylov linear solves, and optional root-event detection. Its own category header identifies I1A2. The selected sketch uses direct dense finite-difference Jacobians, consistent supplied initial Y/YPRIME, scalar tolerances and no events. RES(T,Y,YPRIME,CJ,DELTA,IRES,RPAR,IPAR) has a CJ argument that older DASSL residual interfaces lack. Positive IDID distinguishes intermediate, endpoint, root and initialization returns; negative values require the documented recovery protocol, not blind resubmission. Continuation preserves workspace/state and changes INFO(1) as documented. This review covers driver controls, DDSTP BDF step dispatch/acceptance and residual contract, not every Newton/Krylov/preconditioner kernel, DAE index or consistent-initialization mode.

local.name: GALAHAD
local.description: Modern Fortran optimization packages for constrained/unconstrained, linear/quadratic and least-squares problems.

classifications.notes: The README documents a broad collection and several language interfaces. Individual algorithms, optional linear solvers and problem subclasses need their own procedure reviews; availability of a release binary is not catalog verification.

EQP solves equality-constrained quadratic subproblems through projected/preconditioned iterative work with dependency removal and sparse block factorizations. The concrete sketch has positive-definite H=2I, so its mapping is the convex quadratic-program class G2e1; this does not assert that all library EQP problems require positive-definite H on the full space. Public QPT data stores the constraint constant C in A*x+C=0, as the native example and feasibility RHS=-C show, despite the solve prologue shorthand A*x=c. H uses its lower triangle in coordinate storage. The sketch sets Hessian_kind=-1 to select the supplied Hessian explicitly. The source module name is precision-preprocessed; GALAHAD_EQP_double is the author-example public double-precision facade. Match its integer ABI and configured sparse/dense factorization backends. INITIALIZE/SOLVE/TERMINATE form the lifecycle; TERMINATE overwrites INFORM, so retain solve diagnostics first. Review covers the public solver, author data layout and selected native dispatch/stopping paths, not every linear algebra backend or a numerical verification.

procedures.summary: Public double-precision convex equality-constrained quadratic-program driver.
procedures.usage:
program quadratic_sketch
use GALAHAD_EQP_double
implicit none
integer,parameter :: wp=kind(1d0)
integer :: status
type(QPT_problem_type) :: p
type(EQP_data_type) :: data
type(EQP_control_type) :: control
type(EQP_inform_type) :: inform
p%n=2; p%m=1; p%f=0._wp; p%new_problem_structure=.true.
allocate(p%G(2),p%C(1),p%X(2),p%Y(1))
p%X=0._wp; p%Y=0._wp
p%Hessian_kind=-1; p%G=[-2._wp,-4._wp]; p%C=[-1._wp]
! EQP interprets the equality as A*X + C = 0.
call SMT_put(p%H%type,'COORDINATE',status)
if(status/=0) error stop "H storage allocation failed"
call SMT_put(p%A%type,'COORDINATE',status)
if(status/=0) error stop "A storage allocation failed"
allocate(p%H%val(2),p%H%row(2),p%H%col(2))
allocate(p%A%val(2),p%A%row(2),p%A%col(2))
p%H%ne=2; p%H%row=[1,2]; p%H%col=[1,2]
p%H%val=[2._wp,2._wp]
p%A%ne=2; p%A%row=[1,1]; p%A%col=[1,2]; p%A%val=1._wp
call EQP_initialize(data,control,inform)
control%SBLS_control%symmetric_linear_solver="sytr"
control%FDC_control%symmetric_linear_solver="sytr"
call EQP_solve(p,data,control,inform)
if(inform%status/=0) then
 print *,"solver status",inform%status
else
 print *,inform%obj,p%X
end if
! Preserve solve status before termination, which overwrites INFORM.
call EQP_terminate(data,control,inform)
end program

classifications.notes: QPB solves quadratic programs with simple variable bounds and two-sided linear constraints using a primal-dual interior/trust-region approach. local.name: DFO
local.description: Derivative-free nonlinear optimization for relatively small expensive black-box problems.

classifications.notes: The README targets fewer than roughly 100 variables and functions without efficiently available derivatives. This is the stated intended scale, not a tested hard limit or a claim of large-scale/global optimization capability.

The legacy external DFO driver minimizes an objective with simple, linear and nonlinear constraints using quadratic interpolation/trust-region modeling. The inspected driver validates/setup dimensions, scales inputs, evaluates linked FUN, initializes interpolation points and dispatches DFOSLV; the outer solver file shows model/subproblem dispatch rather than an independent full kernel audit here. local.name: GADfit
local.description: Joint nonlinear curve fitting with shared parameters and automatic differentiation.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly uses global fitting to mean fitting multiple datasets with shared parameters. It does not establish guaranteed global-minimum optimization; modified Levenberg-Marquardt is the documented fitting method.

GADF_FIT performs modified Levenberg-Marquardt nonlinear least squares on model functions defined with ADVAR arithmetic. It forms weighted residuals/Jacobians, sums normal-equation contributions across images, solves a damped system and optionally applies a directional second-derivative/geodesic correction. With USE_AD true, the user supplies the model expression rather than analytic derivative routines. Global fitting here means simultaneous datasets with shared parameters, not global optimization. The selected sketch follows the author single-dataset Gaussian setup with error mode NONE; other weighting modes change the objective. Call GADF_INIT, add datasets, mark active parameters and then fit. Data arrays are pointer-associated on input and need valid lifetime/targets. Coarray and preprocessing support plus compatible numerical libraries are required. The code repeatedly combines PRESENT with optional-argument access in logical expressions; strict evaluation/absent-option safety needs separate audit. No complete numerical fit or termination/covariance validation was run.

procedures.summary: Public module damped nonlinear-fit coordinator. Optional scalar tuning arguments such as LAMBDA are REAL32; internal model precision KP is configured separately.
procedures.usage:
use gadfit
! Define FITFUNC extension and initialized model/data as in the pinned Gaussian example.
call gadf_init(model)
call gadf_add_dataset(x_data,y_data)

local.name: Fast Critical Line Algorithm
local.description: Fortran implementation of Markowitz critical-line portfolio optimization.

classifications.notes: The README identifies historical MATLAB/Python bindings and explicitly warns that MEX tricks require adaptation for 64-bit systems. No modern MATLAB or compiler compatibility is implied.

calcturningpoints follows active-set changes along a Markowitz quadratic-program frontier, starting with the largest-mean single component. It updates a restricted covariance inverse when a component enters/leaves, forms affine weights satisfying sum(w)=1 and stores turning-point means, standard deviations, weights and multipliers. G2e1 is scoped to the convex positive-definite covariance case with nonnegative weights and a budget equality, not a generic QP API or the separate arbitrary-bound variant. NN>=2, distinct/nondegenerate means and adequate MAX_TPS are caller assumptions; covariance definiteness and denominator/pivot safety are not checked. Helpers use unpivoted elimination and inverse updates. Some degeneracies leave a zero candidate index, and turning-point output capacity is checked only after the initial stored point. On failure N_TPS can be undefined and early-return allocation cleanup is incomplete. Check ERROR_FLAG before reading valid output prefixes, then verify feasibility/frontier conditions independently. No frontier or QP residual was run.

local.name: BaM
local.description: Bayesian model estimation and prediction using MCMC posterior samples.

classifications.notes: The README documents a configuration-file-driven computational engine, optional R interface and dependencies on BMSL/miniDMSL. Configuration documentation is described as incomplete; no model-family or convergence guarantees are inferred.

BAM_FIT constructs a packed initial inference vector and proposal scales from already loaded model/data/prior state, then forwards the model posterior callback to the external ADAPTIVE_METRO_OAAT sampler. This is adaptive one-at-a-time Metropolis posterior simulation through a framework entry point, not a standalone arbitrary-density sampler or proof of posterior convergence. The reviewed wrapper validates top-level parameter/remnant-vector sizes against private INFER state, obtains headers/derived-parameter storage and passes adaptation/cycle/move-rate/scale controls and output/monitor file names through. Build and initialize the full BaM, BMSL and miniDMSL dependencies with matching MRK/MIK kinds and valid priors/likelihood/model configurations; INFER is module-global and independent concurrent contexts are not assumed. local.name: gfsolver
local.description: Hybrid Newton-bisection root finding for scalar functions.

classifications.notes: The brief README describes switching from basic Newton to a hybrid method after the iteration limit. Bracketing conditions, derivative callbacks and failure handling need further review.

The inspected module solves a scalar real equation through function-value and first-derivative subroutine callbacks; the dummy vectors have length one. sub_newton takes Newton steps and attempts a sign-changing bracket after its Newton iteration limit, then calls sub_hybrid_nb, which bisects when a Newton trial leaves its current interval. F1b describes general nonpolynomial scalar root finding; this is not polynomial root enumeration, a derivative-free interface or a square-system solver. The hybrid code updates the first endpoint when f(x)<0, so its input pair must have the matching sign orientation; it does not validate a bracket on entry. Failure paths print and STOP rather than returning a status, and the Newton path divides by df before testing for a small derivative. The optional fnorm on direct Newton success stores the residual computed before the final x update. The fallback call does not forward the optional tolerance or iteration controls, so the hybrid defaults apply there. Convergence, singular-derivative behavior and all bracket assumptions were not checked by execution.

local.name: Delaunay Density Diagnostic
local.description: Data-driven geometric-scale diagnostics based on Delaunay interpolation.

classifications.notes: The README documents geometric-scale detection and Python-driven examples requiring gfortran. It is a diagnostic workflow, not a general-purpose standalone Fortran interpolation API.

The bundled DELAUNAYSPARSES routine locates Delaunay simplices containing specified query points and returns vertex indices and barycentric weights. Its native serial path constructs a starting simplex, performs a budgeted visibility walk, and optionally projects out-of-hull queries. It does not construct/export an entire triangulation or certify arbitrary geometric predicates. PTS and Q are shifted/rescaled in place; shapes are D by N and D by M, with D+1 vertex/weight rows per query. Per-query IERR=0 means interpolation, 1 means permitted projected extrapolation, and larger codes report invalid data, degeneracy, budget or dependency failures. EXACT controls diameter/duplicate-check strategy, not exact arithmetic. This source review selects the bundled Fortran geometry, not the Python Delaunay-density diagnostic or an execution check of high-dimensional conditioning.

local.name: FLAPWxHZ
local.description: Hari-Zimmermann generalized hyperbolic singular-value and eigenvalue algorithms.

classifications.notes: The README identifies a specialized generalized hyperbolic SVD/EVD implementation and JACSD dependency. It explicitly says GNU Fortran 9 and newer are unsupported and documents GNU Fortran 8 support; modern compiler readiness is not assumed.

ZHZL1SA is a public module procedure included into HIF_HZ, not a standalone external routine or LAPACK-compatible driver. Match DWP, default INTEGER, SIMD/alignment parameters and the JACSD/VN/JSTRAT and BLAS/OpenMP build; the GNU make fragment uses -fdefault-integer-8. H(LDH,N) and S(LDS,N) are overwritten, Z(LDZ,N) is initialized internally to identity then accumulated, and JVEC(M) encodes the diagonal signature with entries +1/-1. Selected usage requires M>=N>=2, even N, aligned leading dimensions/storage, a valid noncolliding JS/JSPAIR schedule generated through JSTRAT, NSWP>=1, valid CPR/TPC and enough stack storage for vector/thread scratch. The actual OpenMP team size must not exceed CPR because thread IDs index CPR-wide scratch arrays; disable dynamic team sizing and configure the matching team explicitly. Preserve original factors for residual checks. INFO<0 is an input rejection; for nonempty valid work INFO is the sweep index, so positive INFO<=NSWP can be normal and NSWP+1 means the sweep budget was exhausted. Internal STOPs and floating-point failures are not fully represented by INFO. The selected positive-signature JVEC=+1 case is a complex generalized singular-value decomposition of the factor pair (H0,S0), with S0 full column rank and suitable regularity. One-sided Hari-Zimmermann pair transformations act on H, S and the accumulated Z; final column normalization returns SY/SW and scales Z, giving factor relations H0*Z=H_out*diag(SY) and S0*Z=S_out*diag(SW). These generalized values/vectors use project conventions rather than ordinary singular values of one matrix. EY/EW are pre-normalization squared factor-column norms, EE=EY/EW, and SY/SW are normalized together with SS. This mapping remains at GAMS D6 because that hierarchy does not distinguish this generalized factor-pair decomposition cleanly. Review covers public contract, selected Gram accumulation, transformation application and final normalization; not every pair formula, hyperbolic degeneracy, rank-deficient case or convergence proof.

procedures.procedure: sweep stopping count and final signed/ordinary norms

classifications.notes: ZHZL1SA is a public module procedure included into HIF_HZ, not a standalone external routine or LAPACK-compatible driver. Match DWP, default INTEGER, SIMD/alignment parameters and the JACSD/VN/JSTRAT and BLAS/OpenMP build; the GNU make fragment uses -fdefault-integer-8. H(LDH,N) and S(LDS,N) are overwritten, Z(LDZ,N) is initialized internally to identity then accumulated, and JVEC(M) encodes the diagonal signature with entries +1/-1. Selected usage requires M>=N>=2, even N, aligned leading dimensions/storage, a valid noncolliding JS/JSPAIR schedule generated through JSTRAT, NSWP>=1, valid CPR/TPC and enough stack storage for vector/thread scratch. The actual OpenMP team size must not exceed CPR because thread IDs index CPR-wide scratch arrays; disable dynamic team sizing and configure the matching team explicitly. Preserve original factors for residual checks. INFO<0 is an input rejection; for nonempty valid work INFO is the sweep index, so positive INFO<=NSWP can be normal and NSWP+1 means the sweep budget was exhausted. Internal STOPs and floating-point failures are not fully represented by INFO. The signature-weighted factor representation defines a complex Hermitian pencil A=H0^H*diag(JVEC)*H0 and B=S0^H*S0. With S0 full column rank, B is positive definite, and simultaneous diagonalization produces generalized eigenvalues EE=EY/EW and right directions in Z. EY is accumulated with JVEC and may be signed; EW is a nonnegative ordinary factor norm. This is a factor-based Hermitian-definite generalized eigenproblem, not a driver accepting arbitrary A/B arrays or general nonsymmetric pencils. The procedure normalizes H/S and scales Z after the sweep; original-pencil residuals must use original factors, not overwritten arrays. Require valid signature and regular/well-conditioned factors consistent with the method; unverified isotropic/degenerate pairs are outside the selected contract. Review covers signature Gram accumulation, common right transformations, ratio extraction and status/normalization, not all pair kernels or numerical eigenpair accuracy.

procedures.summary: Public module Hari-Zimmermann complex factorized Hermitian generalized-eigenvalue procedure.

use hif_hz, only: zhzl1sa
use omp_lib, only: omp_set_dynamic,omp_set_num_threads, &
                   omp_get_dynamic,omp_get_max_threads
! After compatible aligned allocation, initialized H/S/JVEC, and valid
! JSTRAT JS/JSPAIR schedule; M>=N>=2, even N, NSWP>=1:
call omp_set_dynamic(logical(.false.,kind(omp_get_dynamic())))
call omp_set_num_threads(int(cpr,kind(omp_get_max_threads())))
call zhzl1sa(m,n,h,ldh,jvec,s,lds,z,ldz,js,jspair, &
 nswp,cpr,tpc,ee,ey,ew,sy,sw,ss,nrot,info)
if(info<0.or.info>nswp) error stop "invalid input or sweep limit"
! Check original-factor residuals independently; INFO is not an error bound.

local.name: PDHGEQZ
local.description: Parallel QZ iteration for generalized eigenvalues and generalized Schur forms.

classifications.notes: The driver documentation describes generalized eigenvalues and optional Schur reductions of the input pair. This is a QZ-stage implementation, not an asserted end-to-end solver for every arbitrary matrix-pair representation.

PDHGEQZ computes generalized eigenvalue pairs of a distributed real nonsymmetric Hessenberg/upper-triangular pencil, optionally overwriting it with generalized real Schur form and accumulating left/right orthogonal Schur factors. The native driver dispatches small/large QZ kernels, with shift/deflation work in the distributed implementation. This entry assumes H already upper Hessenberg and T upper triangular; it is not a complete arbitrary dense-pencil reduction in one call. Eigenvalues are represented by (ALPHAR+i*ALPHAI,BETA); retain that representation for zero/tiny BETA instead of blindly dividing. Schur vectors are not individual generalized eigenvectors. MPI/BLACS context, block-cyclic descriptors and local storage must match on all ranks. Query both real and integer workspace after setup; nonzero INFO can mean invalid input or algorithmic failure and no residual/conditioning guarantee follows from zero alone. Review covers public dispatch, workspace contract and selected QZ/deflation paths, not every tuning variant or backend.

procedures.summary: External distributed generalized real QZ driver for a prepared Hessenberg-triangular pencil.
procedures.usage:
external :: pdhgeqz
integer :: info,ldwork,liwork,integer_query(1)
integer,allocatable :: iwork(:)
double precision :: real_query(1)
double precision,allocatable :: dwork(:)
! After MPI/BLACS setup: H Hessenberg, T triangular, matching descriptors,
! allocated Q/Z storage and replicated ALPHAR/ALPHAI/BETA vectors of length N.
call pdhgeqz("S","I","I",n,1,n,h,desch,t,desct,alphar,alphai,beta, &
 q,descq,z,descz,real_query,-1,integer_query,-1,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "QZ workspace query failed"
ldwork=max(1,ceiling(real_query(1))); liwork=max(1,integer_query(1))
allocate(dwork(ldwork),iwork(liwork))
call pdhgeqz("S","I","I",n,1,n,h,desch,t,desct,alphar,alphai,beta, &
 q,descq,z,descz,dwork,ldwork,iwork,liwork,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "inspect QZ diagnostics"
! Preserve homogeneous eigenvalue pairs when BETA is zero or tiny.

The reviewed CGL path generates Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto nodes mapped to [a,b], produces alternating barycentric weights with half endpoint weights, and evaluates a single univariate global Lagrange polynomial by the barycentric quotient. A near-node isclose test returns the stored sample rather than dividing by a small node difference. E1b records a single polynomial, not a piecewise interpolant or noisy-data fit. n is polynomial degree and arrays need n+1 elements despite some abbreviated shape comments. bary_weights only implements CGL weights, so the sketch does not combine it with CG/CGR nodes. Explicitly pass is_descending=.false.: the node generator default flag has declaration initialization and therefore retains a prior supplied value between calls. Positive n, distinct endpoints and adequate array extents are caller responsibilities; no error estimate/status is returned. Module imports require MKL BLAS95/F95_PRECISION even though this reviewed scalar interpolation path uses no BLAS operation. No interpolation result, extrapolation behavior or alternate node family was verified by execution.

local.name: ecTrans
local.description: Distributed spectral transforms on the sphere and limited-area grids.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes global spherical-harmonic and limited-area bifourier transforms and describes CPU/GPU backends. Numerical stability, scaling and accelerator maturity are not independently checked.

Selected CPU scalar-field interface of ecTrans. Initialize the matching FIAT/MPI/OpenMP environment and SETUP_TRANS0, then geometry/truncation/resolution setup, and query the local grid/spectral sizes before allocation. Match PARKIND1 JPIM/JPRB and all linked BLAS/FFTW/FIAT interfaces; these are assumed-shape OPTIONAL-argument external procedures requiring explicit generated interfaces. The author benchmark includes the build-provided dir_trans.h/inv_trans.h headers, not merely EXTERNAL declarations. Use one spectral field-set partition for the selected no-KVSETSC fragment; general field-set splitting requires a consistent KVSETSC map. Calls participating in distributed transforms must agree across the initialized communicator; setup/distribution state is shared and unrestricted concurrent use is not established. No scalar INFO is returned: validation can invoke ABORT_TRANS rather than report a recoverable status. DIR_TRANS maps real gridpoint samples on the initialized spherical geometry to packed real spherical-harmonic coefficients; INV_TRANS synthesizes samples from that storage. The selected PSPSCALAR layout is (local_fields,NSPEC2), with NSPEC2 counting the library real/imaginary spectral storage, not a portable complex triangular alm array. PGP uses (NPROMA,global_scalar_fields,NGPBLKS), and blocked padding is not additional physical data. Driver checks select resolution, field counts and mutually exclusive array layouts. The CPU controller dispatches longitude Fourier work then Legendre work for analysis, reversing that order for synthesis. GAMS J records a spherical integral transform rather than a Cartesian FFT. Wind/vorticity/divergence, derivative flags, regular-lat/lon alternatives, adjoints, GPU residency and individual numerical kernels are outside this selected scalar contract. Review covers driver checks, layout, setup/dispatch and author usage; no transform normalization or reconstruction accuracy was verified.

local.name: GetRootsF
local.description: Scalar root bracketing and hybrid bisection/Newton or bisection/secant methods.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes methods with and without supplied derivatives. Its exhaustive range search does not establish that every root can be found for an arbitrary function and step size.

The public real32 scalar solvers hybridD and hybridSA implement Newton/bisection and accelerated-secant/quadratic-candidate/bisection branches respectively. Their callbacks are pure scalar functions; hybridD also requires a derivative. Source findings prevent treating these as checked solvers: hybridD updates the bracket using fx0*fx1 rather than the newly evaluated midpoint value; hybridSA tests f0*f2 when accepting x3 rather than f0*f3. Both use relative step tests that divide by the candidate root, print on bracket failure without returning a status, and expose no explicit convergence flag. The separate range-scan routine root_searchD skips the first scanning segment and refers to optional max_iters without consistently using its local default. No all-roots or correctness guarantee is recorded, and no program was run.

classifications.notes: The README describes a simplification of Jacob Williams DOP853 interfaces. Users cannot set tolerances and other parameters through this simplified interface; complete configurability of the original is not claimed.

The inspected easydop853 wrapper initializes a DOP853 object and integrates a callback-defined initial-value system. The reviewed core evaluates explicit Runge-Kutta stages, scales embedded error estimates by absolute/relative tolerances, accepts or rejects steps and clips the last step to the requested endpoint. local.name: RKAdaptiveMethods
local.description: Adaptive explicit Runge-Kutta methods with Pleiades test problems.

classifications.notes: The README lists several explicit embedded Runge-Kutta schemes and reference outputs. Printed high-precision reference values are not evidence that every implemented method attains that accuracy.

The selected rk54DormandEachStep forms seven explicit stages and two embedded endpoint estimates, scales their difference with global rtol/atol and proposes/rejects a step. The inspected stage calls all pass t unchanged rather than t+c_i*h, so this mapping is restricted to autonomous systems such as the bundled Pleiades RHS; general time-dependent ODEs require correction. DyDtMod::dev is a compiled dependency to replace, not a callback argument. Global atol has only 50 slots, controls/counters need initialization, and the IEEE_IS_NORMAL endpoint check rejects exact zero and subnormals as well as NaNs/infinities. Zero estimated error also enters err**(-1/6) without a separate guard. No claimed order, trajectory accuracy or success was verified by execution.

local.name: L-BFGS
local.description: Limited-memory quasi-Newton unconstrained optimization with a CMake build.

classifications.notes: The README identifies Nocedal limited-memory unconstrained optimization and repackaging with a C/C++ header. No bound-constrained capability or global-minimum guarantee is inferred.

The inspected LBFGS path constructs a limited-memory inverse-Hessian action from stored step/gradient-difference pairs, uses a More-Thuente-style MCSRCH line search and requests function/gradient values through reverse communication. The user supplies first derivatives, not a Hessian; G1b1b records smooth multivariate unconstrained minimization. DIAGCO optionally requests a positive diagonal scaling through IFLAG=2. The normal stopping test is ||G||/max(1,||X||)<=EPS after a completed line search; no global-optimality or local-minimum certificate is implied. The initial step is 1/||G|| before that test, so an exactly stationary starting point is not safely handled by this path. LBFGS and MCSRCH retain SAVE state and shared LB3 parameters; do not interleave independent solves as though this interface were reentrant. Preserve workspace and re-enter with the returned IFLAG. No minimization, gradient comparison or full audit of MCSTEP/BLAS dependencies was executed.

procedures.summary: External double-precision reverse-communication minimizer. N/M are positive default INTEGER; W needs N*(2*M+1)+2*M elements. Initially evaluate F/G and set IFLAG=0. Return 1 requests fresh F/G at X, 2 requests positive DIAG when DIAGCO is true, 0 reports normal completion and negative values report errors. Link the LB2 block-data defaults and keep the state/workspace intact between calls.
procedures.signature: CALL LBFGS(N, M, X, F, G, DIAGCO, DIAG, IPRINT, EPS, XTOL, W, IFLAG)
procedures.usage:
external :: lbfgs, lb2
integer, parameter :: n=2, m=3
integer :: iprint(2), iflag, calls
double precision :: x(n), g(n), diag(n), w(n*(2*m+1)+2*m)
double precision :: f, eps, xtol
logical :: diagco
x=[2.0d0,-1.0d0]
diagco=.false.
iprint=[-1,0]
eps=1.0d-8
xtol=epsilon(1.0d0)
iflag=0
do calls=1,1000
  f=0.5d0*sum(x*x)
  g=x
  call lbfgs(n,m,x,f,g,diagco,diag,iprint,eps,xtol,w,iflag)
  if (iflag <= 0) exit
  if (iflag /= 1) error stop "unexpected reverse-communication request"
end do
if (iflag /= 0) error stop "L-BFGS did not finish normally"
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled fragment minimizing a quadratic from an explicitly nonstationary initial point. It uses DIAGCO=false, so no diagonal-request branch is needed. The 1000-call guard is a caller limit, not a library convergence claim. Check an initially stationary point before entering this implementation. Link the complete lbfgs.f object, including LB2 and bundled support routines, with compatible default INTEGER/double precision; archive/block-data retention may require toolchain-specific handling. Saved/shared state prevents safe interleaving of solves.

classifications.notes: The README describes a doctoral-assignment origin and an ifort-oriented Makefile needing adjustments for other environments. Compiler portability and each algorithm interface remain unchecked.

GOLDENSECTION performs derivative-free univariate interval reduction using golden-ratio interior points, evaluating a named external EVALFUNC1 rather than accepting a procedure argument. The user supplies ordered distinct endpoints and a fixed NITER; the routine returns four bracket/interior coordinates and function values, not a scalar minimizer or a status/accuracy estimate. GOLDENINT is a separate interactive file-writing wrapper that derives NITER from a requested relative interval contraction and chooses the smallest returned value. A unimodal finite objective over the supplied interval is required for usual interval-search interpretation; no multimodal global search guarantee is inferred. local.name: Jacobi theta functions
local.description: Jacobi theta functions, generalized theta functions and logarithmic variants.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly uses a z convention with period one for theta3, unlike the NIST convention with period pi. Future comparisons must convert arguments consistently; no convention-independent identity is asserted.

THETA3 dispatches to a logarithmic implementation that shifts/inverts tau, reduces z, sums paired exponential terms and finally exponentiates the result. Source uses exp(i*pi*n*(tau*n+2*z)), so z has real period one, unlike conventions with period pi. Require Im(tau)>0. Invalid tau, excessive transformation/shift recursion and detected NaNs call EXIT(-1), terminating the process rather than returning status. MAXITER limits transformations/shifts, not the final series loop, whose stopping test uses floating-point stagnation. Only THETA3 and the inspected shared helper path are mapped here; the other advertised theta/log/generalized interfaces are not independently certified.

classifications.notes: The associated-function FORWARD/BACKWARD C-binding entries perform discrete associated-Legendre analysis/synthesis of longitude-Fourier coefficient columns. local.name: Butterworth Filter
local.description: Butterworth IIR filtering with forward/reverse zero-phase application.

classifications.notes: The brief README identifies arbitrary-order Butterworth filtering. Boundary treatment, numerical conditioning at high order and phase behavior have not been independently checked.

The inspected low-pass design prewarps the cutoff with cot(pi*f*dt), assembles first/second-order Butterworth factors and expands their polynomials into coefficient vectors. buttfilt applies a causal recursive linear difference equation with input numerator coefficients b and feedback denominator coefficients a, overwriting samples 0:nt after zero-state initialization. L10a1c3 records this autoregressive-linear filtering path, not statistical AR-model parameter estimation. The forward routine omits division by a(0), so it requires a(0)=1; the separate filtfilt implementation divides by a(0) and uses forward/reverse zero-state passes, which is not an equivalent endpoint-transient policy to every other library filtfilt. Positive order/dt and cutoff below Nyquist are caller checks; only near-zero cutoff is rejected in buttlp. High-order direct-form conditioning, stability and frequency response were not measured. No signal or author driver was run.

procedures.summary: External low-pass coefficient designer. INTEGER(4) order and REAL(8) sample spacing dt/cutoff f; a and b have bounds 0:order. Cutoff uses cycles per unit time consistent with dt. Arrays are filled through polynomial expansion; no error status is returned.
procedures.signature: CALL buttlp(order, dt, f, a, b)
procedures.usage:
integer, parameter :: order=3, last=99
real(8) :: a(0:order), b(0:order), signal(0:last)
integer :: i
external :: buttlp, buttfilt
signal = [(sin(0.1d0*dble(i)), i=0,last)]
call buttlp(order, 0.01d0, 5.0d0, a, b)
! buttfilt requires a(0)=1; normalize the coefficients explicitly.
b = b/a(0)
a = a/a(0)
call buttfilt(order, last, a, b, signal)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. last is the highest zero-based sample index, so this sketch filters 100 samples. Validate nonzero a(0) and design order/dt/cutoff before normalization. Match default INTEGER/REAL kinds to the external INTEGER(4)/REAL(8) implementation. The forward filter starts with zero history and returns no streaming state; restarting it on chunks changes transients. No spectral-response or sample check was performed.

local.name: GARCH
local.description: Simulation and estimation of ARCH, GARCH and GJR-GARCH volatility models.

classifications.notes: The README documents simulation, Nelder-Mead estimation and return/volatility diagnostics. The examples are not a general guarantee of estimator consistency, identification or optimizer convergence.

garch_mod::simulate_garch generates a GARCH(1,1) return path using Gaussian innovations, starting conditional variance at omega/(1-alpha-beta), emitting optional conditional STANDARD DEVIATIONS and updating variance with alpha*noise**2+beta*sigma2+omega. Supply preallocated caller arrays; despite a source comment, the dummy is assumed-shape and not allocated inside. Require finite mu, omega>0, alpha/beta>=0 and alpha+beta<1 for this initialization. No parameter guard enforces those constraints. The normal helper caches a Box-Muller draw and replaces a zero uniform by 1e-10, so random state is not simply reset by reseeding the intrinsic stream after cached draws. This mapping is stochastic time-series generation, not estimation accuracy or a financial recommendation. No stochastic/variance test was run.

local.name: Nonstationary AR(1) Markov approximations
local.description: Markov-chain approximations of nonstationary AR(1) processes.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes extensions of Rouwenhorst and Tauchen discretizations. This is transition/state approximation of a stochastic process, not a parameter-estimation routine for arbitrary Markov models.

lcrouwenhorst propagates unconditional standard deviations of a supplied time-varying AR(1), creates a finite symmetric state grid, and recursively constructs Rouwenhorst transition matrices. lctauchen instead forms time-varying grids and Gaussian bin probabilities using ERF. M1a records finite-state discrete stochastic-model construction for simulation, not random path generation or fitted AR parameters. Both assume y(0)=0; rho(1) does not set a stationary initial variance. Output trans(i,j,t) is row-oriented from period t-1 to t, with identical first-period rows. Caller must provide compatible T vectors, N>=2 states, nonzero innovations/variance and valid positive grid scales; no status, input validation or probability/moment check is returned. No chain or approximation-error test was run.

local.name: acepack
local.description: R interfaces to Fortran ACE and AVAS regression-transformation algorithms.

classifications.notes: The README identifies the original Fortran kernels and modifications for double-precision R use. The relative advantages described for ACE/AVAS are not independently reproduced here.

The selected SUPSMU entry smooths ordered weighted observations with running local linear fits. Positive module SPAN selects the fixed-span path; zero invokes candidate spans, cross-validation residual smoothing and interpolated locally selected spans. It is an EDA smoother, not the complete ACE/AVAS transformation estimator. The sketch explicitly uses IPER=1 and fixed SPAN=0.5: the periodic branch in SMOOTH reads X(J) before correcting a negative wrapped index and needs repair/bounds checking before use. SUPSMU has no status output, divides by total weight for constant x and accesses quartile indices, so supply sufficiently many finite sorted data and positive total weights. Module control state is shared; no accuracy or smoothing-selection experiment was performed. SMOOTH also combines J<N with X(J+1)<=X(J) in a logical expression: Fortran does not guarantee short-circuit evaluation, so tied terminal abscissae can expose X(N+1). The sketch uses strictly increasing x; this is not a fix or bounds-safety proof.

local.name: ASURV
local.description: Survival-analysis methods for censored data with a Fortran backend and Python interfaces.

classifications.notes: The README lists Kaplan-Meier estimation, two-sample tests, correlations and censored regressions. The broad mapping does not validate assumptions or every method/configuration in the suite.

PLESTM forms a product-limit survival estimator from sorted uncensored/censored arrays, accumulates pointwise standard-error terms, and computes a mean and its error. The implementation first converts largest censored observations to detections until the tail is uncensored, mutating U, NU and NC and reporting ICHANGE/NCHANGE. This is an explicit tail convention, not an assumption-free estimate of an unidentified unrestricted mean. NTOT-sized arrays need spare space for moved observations; all-censored input is unsafe because U(NU) is read before NU is checked. Tied/small samples also expose loops reading U(I+K) before a bound test, and Fortran does not guarantee short-circuit evaluation. No recoverable status output certifies valid inputs. Higher-level ASURV wrappers handle censoring direction/data transformation separately. Review covers the product-limit implementation and tail conventions, not the complete interactive package or validation of survival inference.

local.name: SplitMix64 Fortran
local.description: Fortran 2008 implementation of the SplitMix64 generator.

classifications.notes: The brief README identifies the generator and reference C implementation. Arithmetic portability, seeding and stream properties have not been checked for this translation.

splitmix64_next adds the fixed golden-ratio increment to a local copy of its INTENT(IN) seed, applies two XOR-shift/multiply mixers and a final XOR shift, returning an INT64 bit-pattern harvest. The caller seed is unchanged: calling repeatedly with the same seed repeats the same output. Assigning harvest back as the next seed instead iterates a different map from the usual SplitMix counter progression. L6a21 records the generator mixing step rather than claiming an automatically advancing stream or a real-valued uniform API. The BOZ constants are passed through TRANSFER, and signed integer addition/multiplication still assumes intended wrapping. No bitstream/reference or portability test was run.

procedures.summary: Public pure elemental INT64 function of an INTENT(IN) seed. Despite the name next, the input seed is not advanced. This sketch demonstrates one mixing call only, not a complete repeated-draw driver.

use iso_fortran_env, only: int64
use pkg_splitmix64, only: splitmix64_next
