seed = 123_int64
harvest = splitmix64_next(seed)
! seed remains 123; repeated calls with it repeat harvest.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Compile the parent module before its submodule. For a standard successive SplitMix sequence, manage the additive counter progression separately with explicitly supported modular arithmetic; do not assume this function updates it or that seed=harvest reproduces that progression. local.description: Fortran implementation of xorshift64* using signed-integer representation workarounds.

classifications.notes: The README describes a multiword signed-integer workaround for unsigned arithmetic. Correct equivalence to the reference algorithm and behavior across compilers remain unverified.

RandomNumberGenerator%random_uniform dispatches to a xorshift64star state update using shifts 12,25,27 and an explicit base-2**16 multiplication modulo 2**64. It then assembles a floating-point fraction from the four words. L6a21 records uniform-output sampling; state must be seeded to a nonzero C_INT64_T bit pattern, since zero is absorbing. Scalar and rank-one through rank-three wrappers share this state. Conversion to C_DOUBLE can round a high unsigned fraction to 1, despite the intended [0,1) range; callers must not assume a strict upper bound. The OpenMP critical region serializes scalar draws but does not establish independent parallel streams. No sequence, endpoint or reference comparison was run.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound generic returning a scalar or array of C_DOUBLE values. The sketch selects a scalar and constructs a nonzero explicit seed. Scalar generation updates state inside an OpenMP critical region when enabled.

use precision, only: dp, di

Floating-point conversion does not enforce u<1; range-sensitive consumers need endpoint handling. The private kernel uses limb multiplication rather than signed 64-bit multiply overflow, but no integer/reference equivalence or parallel reproducibility test was executed.

classifications.notes: The public random_normal generic uses the Box-Muller transform of two uniform draws, returning one sine component and saving the cosine component. A SAVE cache/has_cache belongs to the procedure, not each RandomNumberGenerator; interleaving two objects can return a cached value derived from the other object, and reseeding an object does not clear it. OpenMP marks the cache threadprivate, not per object. LOG(u(1)) is unguarded for a zero uniform output. This source mapping records the implemented transform and lifecycle limits, not independent streams or a verified normal law. No sample was run.

The inspected DGESV driver solves a general real dense square system with one or more right-hand sides. It checks dimensions, dispatches LU factorization with partial pivoting to DGETRF and solves through DGETRS only if factorization reports success. It does not establish conditioning, error bounds, inverse formation, sparse support or numerical accuracy by execution.

local.name: HSSPACK
local.description: HSS-based algorithms for tridiagonal eigenproblems, bidiagonal SVD and divide-and-conquer problems.

classifications.notes: The short README specifies specialized matrix forms and hierarchically semiseparable techniques. These component algorithms are not advertised as unrestricted dense eigensolver/SVD replacements.
The short README specifies specialized matrix forms and hierarchically semiseparable techniques. These component algorithms are not advertised as unrestricted dense eigensolver/SVD replacements.

HSSCHOLSOLVER solves a real dense symmetric positive-definite system through an approximate hierarchical semiseparable Cholesky representation, optionally refined by preconditioned CG. The caller supplies a dense matrix, block/rank/compression controls and one RHS vector, despite comments mentioning multiple RHSs. RS=S selects deterministic SVD compression and RS=R randomized compression; WPCG=N uses the approximate direct solve, Y the iterative refinement path. Selected construction code compresses tree blocks and applies local Cholesky/orthogonal transformations; SOLVECHOLSVD traverses the factor tree and applies triangular solves. INFO validates option flags but is not propagated from lower-level factorization/convergence/allocation failures (some allocation exits retain INFO=0). Thus INFO=0 is not a numerical solve certificate. Input A is copied internally and B overwritten; preserve original RHS and check a residual. Review covers the driver and selected construction/solve tree paths, not all low-rank kernels or an accuracy/scaling guarantee.

procedures.summary: External dense SPD hierarchical approximate Cholesky/optional-PCG driver with one RHS.

external :: HssCholSolver
integer :: n,ni,rank_cap,oversampling,maxit,info
double precision :: tol,tau
! Allocate/initialize DOUBLE PRECISION A(N,N), RHS(N), and preserve copies.
! Use a sufficiently sized SPD matrix with compressible off-diagonal blocks.
ni=20; rank_cap=10; oversampling=5; maxit=30; tol=1d-8; tau=1d-12
call HssCholSolver("S","N",a,n,rhs,ni,tol,rank_cap,oversampling,tau,maxit,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "invalid HSS options"
! Independently validate the returned solution residual against original A/RHS.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-allocation fragment using author-style block/rank controls. Link the complete HSSPACK/BLAS/LAPACK build; adapt controls to actual matrix size and structure. INFO does not carry all numerical failures or establish residual accuracy. No SPD solve, compression, randomized or PCG case was run.

classifications.notes: DHSSMM compresses a dense square real A into a hierarchical semiseparable representation, then traverses its low-rank factor tree to overwrite dense B with approximate A*B in column panels. FASTHSSMM applies upward/downward tree products with dense block multiplications. The wrapper assumes LDA=M=N and needs valid block/rank and panel sizes; this is not a general rectangular matrix product. The selected wrapper has concrete limitations: INFO is never assigned, the remainder-panel branch slices B rows instead of columns, and multiplication TIME(2) subtracts clocks in reverse order. The sketch therefore restricts K to a positive multiple of NCOL and does not interpret INFO or timing as validation. Compression tolerance controls internal approximations, not an independently measured product error. Review covers construction/product dispatch and selected tree multiply paths; it does not certify every compression kernel or OpenMP variant.

procedures.summary: External panel-wise approximate dense product through HSS compression, with restricted safe panel shape.

external :: DHSSMM
integer :: n,k,panel,ni,rank_cap,info

! Allocate/initialize A(N,N), B(N,K), preserve copies, and choose N/block sizes.
panel=20; k=40; ni=20; rank_cap=10; tol=1d-8; info=-999
! B must already be allocated with K=40 columns; K is a multiple of PANEL.
call DHSSMM(a,n,n,n,b,n,k,tol,rank_cap,ni,panel,times,info)
! INFO is not assigned, and TIMES(2) is reversed; validate A*B independently.

Use a square matrix and a positive panel size dividing K to avoid the reviewed remainder-slice defect. Build all HSSPACK dependencies; do not rely on unassigned INFO or the reversed timing. local.name: Lanczos Iterator
local.description: Matrix-free Lanczos methods for low-lying real-symmetric or complex-Hermitian eigenpairs.

classifications.notes: The README requires a user-supplied matrix-vector product and describes residual-based polishing. Its maximal-precision and robustness claims have not been independently reproduced.

rs_lanczos creates real vector views over output columns and invokes the iterator sequentially for the lowest requested eigenpairs of a matrix supplied by callback. The inspected core performs a three-term Lanczos update with orthogonalization, reduces to a tridiagonal problem and dispatches Ritz extraction/polishing. D4a1 records real-symmetric ordinary eigenproblems, not nonsymmetric/generalized solvers. Callback ADD controls overwrite versus accumulation and must be honored. The output named variance is filled by residual using vector_norm, so it is a residual norm rather than a squared variance. There is no public success flag; maxstep does not bound all later polishing work. Saved RNG/recurrence state prevents assuming reentrancy. The wrapper seed packing is normalized to a valid odd final seed by vector_random_fill before LAPACK use. Restart/range mode and complex variants are outside the usage sketch. No eigenpair or independent residual was computed.

local.name: JKogb
local.description: J-Kogbetliantz algorithm for the hyperbolic singular value decomposition.

classifications.notes: The README describes the specialized hyperbolic SVD, libpvn dependency and compiler-specific build adjustments. General SVD conventions and modern GNU compiler behavior are not assumed interchangeable with this algorithm.

The public DHSVD2 module procedure performs a two-by-two real hyperbolic singular-value transformation, using a signature J with entries +/-1. It scales the input, triangularizes/pivots it, dispatches the specialized KHSVD2 transformation if needed, accumulates left/right transforms and handles signature-dependent sorting. This is a small signature-metric decomposition building block, not an ordinary Euclidean SVD for arbitrary matrix dimensions; broad D is retained. A is overwritten, U/Z are outputs, and positive INFO values encode transformation/exceptional-case bits rather than failure under a simple INFO/=0 rule. Negative INFO reports invalid signature/nonfinite/error paths; signature checks can be compiled out with NDEBUG. TH1 controls an exceptional near-unit-hyperbolic-parameter path that may retain off-diagonals. Preserve original A and use author transformation conventions for reconstruction and signature checks. Review covers the small dispatcher/triangularization/sorting and selected hyperbolic recurrence, not the complete parallel J-Kogbetliantz sweep driver.

procedures.summary: Public pure module two-by-two signature-metric decomposition kernel with bit-encoded nonnegative status.

use params, only: DWP,TH1FIX
use dtransf, only: DHSVD2
real(DWP) :: a(2,2),u(2,2),z(2,2)
integer :: signature(2),info
a=reshape([2._DWP,0.1_DWP,0.2_DWP,1._DWP],[2,2])
signature=[1,-1]
call DHSVD2(a,signature,u,z,TH1FIX,info)
if(info<0) error stop "hyperbolic transformation failed"
! Decode nonnegative INFO bits before assuming A has become diagonal.

The public JACV0_EXECUTE generic performs the one-sided Jacobi column-orthogonalization core of an SVD through a Fortran interface to AVX2/FMA or AVX-512 native kernels. It initializes V to identity, applies column rotations/swaps to G and V and returns packed transformation/sweep counters. It does not itself return a normalized U and singular-value vector, so a complete validated SVD needs postprocessing and residual/orthogonality checks. The inspected parameter/preparation predicates require M=N and vector-multiple dimensions; they must not be generalized to arbitrary rectangular matrices. Matrices and integer strategy workspace require matching alignment, prepared pivot offsets and supported CPU instructions. The reviewed C bridge expects 64-bit pointer-offset workspace and packed integer storage, so select a matching 64-bit-integer build rather than assuming default INTEGER works. QUERY/PREPARE use positive strategy counts on successful paths and EXECUTE INFO holds counters, not an INFO=0 success convention. Review covers the concrete Fortran bridge and AVX2 rotation/sweep paths, not the unrelated full LAPACK comparison executables or all platforms.

local.description: Integer/string conversion, numeric-string validation and numeric-string comparisons.

classifications.notes: The README describes parsing and error reporting rather than numerical equation solving. Performance and security wording in the original description is not treated as a benchmark or security assessment.

DECTOINT32 converts a signed decimal character representation to the selected integer kind using character tests, shifts/additions and explicit magnitude/range logic. INT32TOBINARYASU formats the stored integer bit pattern as a 32-character binary string: negative inputs use the unsigned bit representation rather than a leading minus, and positive outputs are right-justified with blanks. The implementation hard-codes ASCII digit/sign/space codes and 32-bit limits, while K_INT32=SELECTED_INT_KIND(9) only guarantees a minimum decimal range; verify actual bit size on the target compiler. Only ordinary spaces are trimmed, not all whitespace. Optional substring positions are clipped/normalized in some cases rather than uniformly rejected as the prose implies. ERROR must be inspected; OUTPUT can hold a partial accumulation on failure. This mapping records selected base/representation conversion, not arbitrary precision or a verified boundary/encoding implementation.

procedures.summary: Public module decimal parser with logical error output; optional inclusive positions have kind K_INT32.
procedures.usage:
use fnConsts, only: k_int32
use fnDecimalUtil, only: decToInt32
use fnInt32Util, only: int32ToBinaryAsU
integer(k_int32) :: value
logical :: failed
character(32) :: bits
call decToInt32(" 12345 ",value,failed)
if(failed) error stop "invalid or out-of-range decimal"
bits=int32ToBinaryAsU(value)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use ASCII-compatible encoding and confirm a 32-bit selected integer kind before relying on the fixed limits/bit layout. Do not use partial OUTPUT after ERROR. This sketch deliberately uses an in-range positive decimal without substring options. No round-trip, negative minimum, overflow or malformed-character case was tested.

classifications.notes: The source interface includes differentiation of a supplied Jacobian and explicitly selects real128. Interface inspection does not establish supported platforms, stencil accuracy or successful compilation; real128 availability is compiler-dependent.

local.name: lcmin
local.description: Interior-point linearly constrained minimization solver.

classifications.notes: The README lists Algencan, HSL MA48/MA57, MeTIS and supporting module/source requirements. Inclusion does not imply that those dependencies are supplied or that the solver builds without additional setup.

The current lcmin module exposes typed setup and lcmin_optimize. It copies sparse linear equalities/bounds, installs objective/gradient/Hessian callbacks into global procedure pointers, preprocesses fixed/dependent constraints and dispatches a primal-dual interior-point barrier solver. The inspected barrier driver updates the barrier parameter and calls Newton/KKT, line-search and objective-derivative routines. G2h2a3 records smooth optimization with linear constraints and supplied first/second derivatives, scoped to A*x=b plus simple bounds; generic linear inequalities need a suitable reformulation rather than an invented inequality-row API. Coordinate A arrays and sparse Hessian callbacks are caller-supplied. Globals, unconditional output files and external HSL/ALGENCAN dependencies prevent treating this as a standalone or reentrant routine. The old f90wrapper calls an obsolete external lcmin signature; use the reviewed module API. Several multiplier-copy blocks are commented out, so do not assume every vars dual field is populated. No KKT, feasibility, dependency build or optimization test was run.

procedures.summary: Public module subroutine using lcmin_params, lcmin_constraints and lcmin_variables. Initialize parameters via lcmin_load; allocate/populate constraints and primal X before calling. Objective, gradient and coordinate-Hessian procedure arguments must match user_subs interfaces. FLAG distinguishes optimal, acceptable-feasible, infeasible and failure outcomes.
procedures.usage:
use lcmin, only: lcmin_params,lcmin_constraints,lcmin_variables,lcmin_load,lcmin_optimize
type(lcmin_params) :: param
type(lcmin_constraints) :: cons
type(lcmin_variables) :: vars
integer :: flag
call lcmin_load(param)
! Allocate/populate cons%arow/acol/aval, cons%b/l/u and vars%x for N,M.
! Implement explicit-interface EVALF, EVALG and EVALH callbacks.
call lcmin_optimize(n,m,param,cons,vars,evalf,evalg,evalh,flag)
if(flag/=0) error stop "LCMIN did not report KKT convergence"
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Setup fragment, not a complete optimization driver. The row relation is A*x=b, with variable lower/upper bounds. Build the current modules and separately obtain compatible HSL MA48/MA57, ALGENCAN and other documented dependencies. FLAG=1 is an acceptable feasible return rather than the FLAG=0 KKT-tolerance result; FLAG=2 is infeasible. Set capacities/scaling deliberately and independently verify primal feasibility and returned solution. Full dual return coverage and concurrency are not certified.

local.name: libdlfind
local.description: C and Python interfaces to Fortran DL-FIND geometry optimization.

classifications.notes: The README documents a callback-driven geometry-optimization backend and examples with external electronic-structure code. Its interface is distinct from a standalone implementation of every DL-FIND optimization method.

The external DLF_LBFGS_STEP procedure supplies a limited-memory BFGS search step for smooth unconstrained multivariate optimization using caller positions and first derivatives. DLF_LBFGS_INIT allocates a selected shared instance/history; the step routine forms position/gradient differences and applies the two-loop inverse-Hessian recursion. The first step is normalized to length 0.02 and divides by the gradient norm without a zero-gradient guard. Later updates divide by y-transpose-s and y-transpose-y without safeguarding zero/invalid curvature, and a positive gradient-dot-step triggers direction inversion. This is a direction/update component, not a complete minimizer: the caller must evaluate energy/gradient, test convergence before the first/each call, choose acceptable new points and manage line/step control. Module LBFGS_MODULE stores history but the callable procedures are external, after END MODULE, so do not label the step as a module binding. Review covers step/init/destroy lifecycle and selected-instance state, not all DL-FIND coordinates, transition-state or chemistry workflows.

procedures.summary: External RK-kind L-BFGS step generator with shared history and caller-supplied gradients.
procedures.signature:
CALL dlf_lbfgs_init(NVAR,NMEM)
CALL dlf_lbfgs_step(X,G,STEP)
CALL dlf_lbfgs_destroy()
procedures.usage:
use dlf_parameter_module, only: rk
use dlf_global, only: printl
external :: dlf_lbfgs_init,dlf_lbfgs_step,dlf_lbfgs_destroy
real(rk) :: x(2),g(2),step(2)
printl=0; x=[1._rk,2._rk]; g=2._rk*x
! Initialize the author DL-FIND allocation/runtime support before this fragment.
call dlf_lbfgs_init(2,5)
if(sqrt(sum(g*g))>1.e-8_rk) call dlf_lbfgs_step(x,g,step)
! A full optimizer must accept a new X, recompute G and guard curvature before
! later calls; this fragment deliberately shows only the first direction.
call dlf_lbfgs_destroy()
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Link the full matching DL-FIND module/support graph and BLAS ABI; LBFGS_MODULE holds state but these routines are external. Do not call at zero gradient, reuse unchanged points/gradients, or assume the returned step is a converged solution. No direction, line search, curvature or convergence case was tested.

local.name: libga
local.description: Fortran genetic-algorithm optimization modules with organism and fitness interfaces.

classifications.notes: The Evolution source header and interfaces identify genetic optimization, generations and a user fitness callback, with companion module dependencies. The documentation section files inspected were empty; numerical behavior and build setup remain unverified.

Evolution::Next_Generation sorts fitness values for minimization, transforms them into selection weights, retains elites, permutes selected organisms, crosses pairs and mutates non-elites. Changed organisms alone have fitness recomputed through the externally linked Feval callback. G2i records genetic global-search generation steps, scoped to the inspected real-valued genotype path rather than a complete stopping-controlled optimizer or all complex/integer/string variants. Caller must initialize/evaluate every member and drive the generations. Equal fitness gives FSUM=0 before MOD-based selection and needs caller/source handling. Real mutation multiplies genes by 1+normal, so an exactly zero real gene is unchanged by that mutation; no box-bound enforcement is present. Crossover lengths use the first organism twice in MIN, so use compatible genotype lengths. Public mutation/elite/crossover parameters are module-global. Required NumTypes/Statistics/etc. come from an external f90 utility library. No generations or fitness/selection properties were tested by execution.

procedures.summary: Public module function accepting an evaluated Generation and returning the next Generation. Member(:) contains Genetics::Organism with genotype arrays and a scalar fitness; smaller fitness is favored. FEVAL is externally linked with an INOUT Organism, not passed as an argument.
procedures.usage:
use NumTypes, only: dp
use Genetics
use Evolution
type(Generation) :: current,next
integer :: i
call Init_Generation(current,20)
do i=1,20
  call Init_Organism(current%Member(i),[0,2,0,0],.true.)
  call Feval(current%Member(i))
end do
! Guard equal/invalid fitness and ensure a suitable initialized population.
next=Next_Generation(current)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Supply the matching external FEVAL and build the external f90 utility modules required by Makefile. This performs one generation and has no convergence/status output. Keep all members structurally compatible and avoid equal-fitness division/modulo degeneracy; the sketch does not repair that source path. Bounds, reproducible seeding, stopping budgets and final-best extraction belong to the caller. Only the real-gene path is selected.

local.name: octree-mg
local.description: Parallel geometric multigrid on adaptive quadtree and octree grids.

classifications.notes: The README identifies elliptic/Poisson solves and explicitly restricts stencils without diagonal elements and strongly unequal grid spacing. The solver is not represented as handling arbitrary AMR stencils or anisotropy.

The public FAS full-multigrid/V-cycle entries solve discretized elliptic problems on an initialized MPI tree/grid. The selected Cartesian constant-Laplacian path installs native centered box operators and Gauss-Seidel or red-black smoothers; the supplied uniform-grid driver creates a rectangular domain and a manufactured Poisson problem. A cycle restricts data/coarse RHS, relaxes the coarse grid, prolongs corrections and smooths upward. One call performs a cycle, not an automatic globally tolerance-driven solve. MAX_RES optionally reduces maximum residual magnitudes across ranks; callers must repeat/check cycles and assess discretization error separately. Fully periodic constant-Laplacian setup removes mean RHS/solution to address compatibility/gauge. The coarse level must reside on one rank in the reviewed cycle implementation; unsupported geometries/smoothers/configurations can ERROR STOP. Review covers selected native dispatch, cycles and constant operator, not every AMR refinement or boundary case.

procedures.summary: Public FAS full-multigrid cycle on an initialized distributed Poisson problem.

! First initialize MPI, tree storage/distribution, operator/smoother methods,
! physical boundaries, RHS and ghost-cell data as in the supplied uniform-grid driver.
call mg_fas_fmg(mg,.false.,residual)
! Repeat cycles with HAVE_GUESS=.true. as required and inspect residual/error.

The source is preprocessed for the selected dimension and requires the full matching MPI/module graph. One cycle or a small residual alone does not certify PDE solution accuracy. No grid, cycle, MPI reduction or convergence order was run.

procedures.summary: Public single FAS V-cycle with optional level selection and maximum residual output.

comments.text: Whether the V-cycle is called by itself (default: true)

classifications.notes: The native variable-Laplacian methods implement a Cartesian divergence-form elliptic operator with a smoothly varying cell-centered coefficient. Neighbor coupling uses harmonic face coefficients 2*a0*a_neighbor/(a0+a_neighbor) divided by squared grid spacings, supporting a nonseparable second-order linear elliptic mapping. VLAPLACIAN_SET_METHODS reserves coefficient storage, configures coefficient ghost boundaries and installs the native box operator/smoother for FAS cycles. Supply finite positive coefficients and valid initialized ghost values; zero/opposite-sign neighboring coefficients can make harmonic denominators singular and ellipticity is not checked. The method explicitly disables the constant-Laplacian mean-subtraction flag, so periodic/nullspace compatibility must not be assumed to be handled identically. Geometry/smoother restrictions and collective cycle prerequisites remain. This review records the selected smooth variable-coefficient implementation, not discontinuous-material accuracy, a general anisotropic tensor operator or automatic convergence.

local.name: PDECHEB
local.description: Chebyshev PDE semidiscretization with coupled ODE residuals and DASSL time integration.

classifications.notes: The README architecture diagrams separate user equations/boundaries, semidiscretization and DASSL integration. The entry does not imply that arbitrary PDEs are solved without user callbacks or an appropriate time integrator.

PDECHEB semidiscretizes mixed one-space-dimensional parabolic PDE/ODE systems by C0 Chebyshev generalized collocation. INICHB initializes element/grid/workspace COMMON state and initial values through CSET/UVINIT. PDECHB builds the implicit ODE residual by element differentiation, flux/boundary assembly through CRES/DRES and optional coupling through SODEFN. Time integration is delegated to DASSL; PDECHB alone does not advance time. User routines SPDEFN, SBNDR, UVINIT and compatible optional coupled-ODE definitions are required. NPTS=NEL*NPOLY+1 and NEQN=NPDE*NPTS+NV; workspace lengths depend on polynomial degree/elements/coupling. ITIME=-1 signals setup failure and IRES communicates residual rejection/termination to DASSL. Shared saved COMMON blocks preclude assuming independent concurrent contexts. Review covers initialization, residual assembly and an author call sequence, not spatial convergence, temporal integration or every supported coordinate/coupling variant.

procedures.summary: External collocation setup driver; IWK here is the scalar real-workspace length.
procedures.usage:
external :: INICHB,PDECHB
! Supply user PDE/boundary/initial-condition callbacks and sized arrays.
! XBK(IBK), IBK=NEL+1; NPTS=NEL*NPOLY+1; U has NPDE*NPTS+NV entries.
itime=1
call INICHB(neqn,npde,npts,x,u,wk,lwk,m,t,iband,itime,xbk,ibk,nel,npoly,nv,nxi,xi,6)
if(itime==-1) error stop "PDECHEB setup failed"
! A compatible DASSL call uses PDECHB as its residual callback.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-allocation setup fragment. Follow the author example for problem-specific workspace formulas, consistent initial derivatives and DASSL controls; this does not include a time integrator or PDE callback bodies. No mesh, residual or trajectory was tested.

local.name: Fortran Parallel Sort
local.description: OpenMP parallel sorting interfaces that return an ordering permutation.

classifications.notes: The documented integer-array interface returns indices ordering the input. Stability, scaling and support for other element types are not inferred from the generic library name.

The inspected REAL(8) overload initializes an index permutation, ranks OpenMP chunks through the bundled REAL64 ORDERPACK-derived merge-ranker, offsets local indices, and repeatedly merges adjacent ranked chunks. A is INTENT(IN); A(order) is the intended ascending sequence. N6a1b records passive internal real sorting, not in-place value mutation. Review covers the REAL(8) wrapper, REAL64 ranker and outer merge, not the other overloads or a parallel scaling/stability proof. Kind 8 must match REAL64 on the compiler. Chunking uses omp_get_max_threads rather than an actual-team-size query, and tiny/empty inputs, large index arithmetic and oversubscribed chunk layouts have not been checked. No OpenMP build, permutation or timing was run.

procedures.summary: Public generic, shown for REAL(8) values and default-integer order(SIZE(A)). The input values are retained; use A(order) to obtain the sorted values and apply the same order to associated data. Compile m_mrgrnk before mod_sort and link the OpenMP runtime.
procedures.usage:
use omp_lib, only: omp_set_dynamic, omp_set_num_threads
use mod_sort, only: parallel_sort
real(8) :: values(4), sorted(4)
integer :: order(4)
values = [3.0d0, 1.0d0, 4.0d0, 2.0d0]
call omp_set_dynamic(.false.)
call omp_set_num_threads(2)
call parallel_sort(values, order)
sorted = values(order)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The sketch uses a nonempty input evenly divisible into two chunks; it does not validate arbitrary team/chunk configurations. Ensure REAL(8) matches the bundled REAL64 ranker. Use finite, non-NaN values and validate the returned permutation before applying it. No throughput, thread-safety or stable-tie claim is established.

local.name: Fortran Timsort
local.description: Fortran implementation of Timsort with CMake build presets.

classifications.notes: The README identifies the algorithm and compiler presets. Stability, worst-case behavior and supported types require source/driver checks rather than relying solely on the algorithm name.

The committed generated INTEGER(INT32) no-history overload dispatches small arrays to binary insertion sort, detects ascending/descending runs, extends short runs, maintains a run stack and merges it. The default OPTMLVL=1 merge copies the shorter run and merges forwards/backwards; OPTMLVL=0 is the simple merge. This supports active internal integer sorting N6a2a. Private tsort_int32 is reached through public sort. Source findings qualify the implementation: run discovery reads array(start_+1) without guarding a final singleton run; descending runs admit equal keys before reversal, so stable tie ordering is not established. Module-wide gallop variables are reset on calls, so do not assume reentrancy. History, real overloads, optimization-level 2 and asymptotic/performance claims were not verified, and no sort was executed.

local.name: Heapsort
local.description: In-place real-array heapsort with an index permutation.

classifications.notes: The README documents the permutation convention and an author ordering/permutation test. Those tests have not been run for this catalog; stability and arbitrary-type support are not asserted.

heap_sort builds a maximum heap by downward sifting, repeatedly swaps the root with the shrinking last element and sifts again. Data values are overwritten in ascending order, supporting active real sorting N6a2b. Optional permutation labels start as 1:N and follow the same swaps, so sorted(i)=original(perm(i)); this is also the relation tested in the author driver and is the inverse convention to the header formula sorted(perm(n))=unsorted(n). The size argument and permutation must match storage, C_SIZE_T/C_DOUBLE kinds must be respected, and index/size overflow and NaN ordering are not checked. No stability, performance or executed correctness claim is made.

DRAW_JU generates correlation-matrix draws using sequential beta-distributed partial correlations and the Joe construction. The output stores the strict lower-triangle correlations in row-by-row order (2,1),(3,1),(3,2),(4,1),(4,2),(4,3),..., with unit diagonal implicit; NUMCORRGROUP must equal P*(P-1)/2. Invalid NB/frequency controls can STOP the process. There is no explicit returned convergence/error flag, weighting or missing-data handling. The public FMZM GAMMA generic dispatches the real FM derived type to FMGAM, using configurable multiprecision arithmetic rather than machine-real GAMMA. The inspected core checks special/pole cases, caches nearby arguments, shifts to a larger argument, evaluates log-gamma/exponential and reverses the shift; negative noninteger arguments use reflection. Precision increases and retry logic respond to cancellation, subject to configured storage/exponent limits and global KFLAG diagnostics. The sketch restricts the domain to a positive real value, avoiding pole/reflection subtleties. FM_SET determines requested decimal precision; decimal strings avoid importing machine-precision literal rounding. Shared FMVALS scratch/caches and state mean ordinary concurrent calls need isolation. This is the pinned historical TOMS814 distribution, not a review of newer FM releases. Review covers the real generic and selected gamma paths, not every elementary or complex special function.

local.name: BayesFM
local.description: R/Fortran Bayesian factor-model inference with stochastic factor-structure search.

classifications.notes: DESCRIPTION documents Bayesian exploratory factor analysis and MCMC-based inference of factor counts/loading allocations. This is an R package requiring compiled Fortran, not a general standalone matrix-factorization library.

The public update_factor_normal component draws latent Gaussian factor scores conditional on the supplied loadings, dedicated-factor assignments, idiosyncratic precisions and factor covariance distribution. It adds loading-weighted diagonal contributions to the factor precision, inverts this precision, forms the conditional mean and adds a Cholesky-transformed normal draw. This is a factor-analysis component, not a complete Bayesian fit or evidence that one draw constitutes a converged posterior analysis. DEDIC values must lie in 0..NFAC, with zero denoting an inactive measurement; precisions and covariance must be valid. The module uses the package MT19937-64-based probability generator, while matrix failures call R error helpers and inversion uses LAPACK. Consequently this is not a standalone standard-library routine or a routine governed by R RNG state alone. Review covers this conditional update and its constructors/numerical dependencies; it does not assert that this particular type is the full BEFA driver path.

dgersvd1 orthogonalizes a caller-provided column sketch, optionally alternates matrix/transpose products and QR/LQ power steps, forms Q-transpose*A through a callback, computes its small SVD, and lifts left singular vectors by GEMM. classifications.notes: The README explicitly distinguishes nonnegative low-rank approximation from nonnegative matrix factorization. MARIA-related build dependencies and algorithmic results are not independently checked.

nn_lrma_svd forms A=U*VT, applies an entrywise nonnegativity transformation and takes a truncated SVD, returning factors with singular values absorbed into U. METHOD=1 clips at zero; other methods reflect, clip at a positive shift or add a shift derived from the largest negative entry. K records the selected constrained low-rank approximation step. This routine performs one projection/truncation step, not an internally converged optimizer or a least-squares fit against a preserved original target; no narrower global-best approximation claim is inferred. METHOD=1 may regain negative entries after rank truncation, so repeat/control convergence at application level. Both real/integer workspace queries are supported via either length=-1, but zero-size/rank early returns precede query outputs. DGESDD error is not checked before copying factors and a following DDGMM call can overwrite IERR. Flat column-major buffers and actual capacities are caller obligations. No approximation, singular values or convergence test was run.

gauss_legendre builds nodes/weights by Newton iterations on the Legendre three-term recurrence and mirrors the half-rule. gauss_legendre_ab applies affine node/weight scaling; gauss_lobatto_legendre includes both endpoints and iterates on the derivative roots. Repair guards/copy bounds against actual returned sizes before treating the sketch as an executable driver. local.name: Fortran Rationals
local.description: Rational-number arithmetic with checked finite-width integer representation.

classifications.notes: The README specifies int64 numerators/denominators and stopping on invalid arithmetic or overflow. Exact arithmetic within representable limits is not arbitrary-precision unbounded arithmetic.

The rational type stores reduced INT64 numerator/denominator pairs with positive denominator. The selected integer constructors simplify with Euclidean GCF, reject zero denominators and the most-negative integer, and normalize signs. Rational addition cancels denominator common factors before checked integer products/sums; multiplication cancels cross factors before multiplying. These are exact finite-width rational operations, not arbitrary precision. Error paths use ERROR STOP and some representable final results can still encounter finite intermediate limits; this review does not prove completeness of overflow handling across every operator. Other intrinsic overloads, matrices, random rational generation and formatted I/O are outside this selected arithmetic review.

procedures.summary: Public generic integer-pair constructor; the selected overload takes two INT64 arguments. Private components are exposed through get_num/get_den queries.
procedures.usage:
use iso_fortran_env, only: int64
use rationals, only: rational, operator(+), operator(*)
type(rational) :: a,b,c
integer(int64) :: numerator, denominator
a=rational(1_int64,3_int64)
b=rational(1_int64,6_int64)
c=a+b
numerator=c%get_num()
denominator=c%get_den()
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The sketch selects the INT64 constructor and public generic operators. Arithmetic is bounded by finite integer representation; zero denominators and checked overflows terminate the process. No exact-result or overflow-boundary tests were run.

classifications.notes: The REAL64 rational constructor iterates continued-fraction convergents until conversion back to REAL64 equals the original absolute input, the fractional remainder vanishes, or the next convergent/reciprocal exceeds the finite INT64 bounds. It then restores the sign. Consequently this is a real-to-fraction conversion/approximation, not a promise of representing the exact binary rational or the originally intended decimal. If no round-tripping convergent fits, the last fitting convergent is retained. Nonfinite/out-of-range input reaches ERROR STOP. The reverse REAL overload divides the stored integer components in REAL64 and rounds normally. No round-trip or best-approximation experiment was performed.

procedures.summary: Public generic REAL64-to-rational constructor, backed by a continued-fraction loop with finite-size checks.

Finite continued-fraction limits can produce a fallback approximation; do not infer an exact decimal interpretation or arbitrary-size rational result.

procedures.summary: Public REAL overload returning REAL64 from the stored numerator/denominator ratio.

classifications.notes: The public integer gcf and lcm generics expose Euclidean greatest-common-factor calculation and divide-before-checked-multiply least-common-multiple calculation. GCF normalizes with ABS and defines zero cases, including gcf(0,0)=0; LCM returns zero if either input is zero. INT32 overloads compute via INT64 and reject results exceeding INT32. The direct INT64 GCF/LCM path applies ABS without guarding the most-negative representable INT64 input, which is excluded from this mapping usage. B is the available GAMS number-theory leaf; this is not primality or factorization software. No integer-result or boundary tests were run.

local.name: HDMod
local.description: Fortran hyper-dual-number arithmetic and calculations.

classifications.notes: The brief README identifies hyper-dual-number calculations. Individual derivative interfaces, supported operations and numerical behavior need further source review; no complete automatic-differentiation framework is inferred.

The hyperdual type stores value, two first-direction components and a mixed component. The selected hdual constructor copies all four seeds. hdexp and hdsin propagate first derivatives and the mixed second derivative by chain-rule formulas, including the incoming mixed seed. For a univariate x seeded as (x,1,1,0), dx1 and dx2 represent the first derivative and dx1x2 the second derivative of the selected smooth expression. This is operator/function-based automatic differentiation, not a finite-difference step-size method or a full Hessian driver. Only the scalar constructor, exponential and sine paths were inspected; thousands of other overloads, branch logic and nonsmooth/domain behavior are outside this review. Floating-point errors/overflow remain and no derivative check was run.

y=hdexp(hdsin(x))

local.name: compare
local.description: Tolerance-based comparisons of real and complex numbers.

classifications.notes: The README describes absolute differences and an optional/default tolerance. Its approximate relations are not assumed to have all equivalence/order properties of exact arithmetic.

The selected eq generic compares absolute differences with a tolerance, including default-real scalars, REAL64 scalars, default complex scalars and real arrays. local.name: fortran-approx
local.description: Absolute and absolute-plus-relative floating-point comparison interfaces.

classifications.notes: The README documents elemental comparisons, precision variants and default tolerances. Choosing a tolerance remains application-dependent; approximate equality is not a certified error bound.

The public elemental aeq and haeq generics implement absolute tolerance abs(a-b)<=tol and hybrid tolerance abs(a-b)<=atol+rtol*max(abs(a),abs(b)). Defaults are 1e-10 in each supported real kind. Array calls return elementwise logical masks, unlike the scalar array-reduction behavior of tcanich/compare. Explicit tolerances must match the argument kind; haeq exposes two-argument default or four-argument explicit forms. Negative tolerances, NaNs/infinities and subtraction/scaled-threshold overflow are not specially handled, so the mapping/sketch is limited to finite ordinary-range values and nonnegative tolerances. REAL128 overload declarations affect compiler support even for a REAL64-only user. No accuracy/equivalence test was performed.

local.name: Powell optimization archive
local.description: Archive of M. J. D. Powell Fortran 77 optimization software.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly says these implementations are no longer maintained and directs users to PRIMA for modernized reference implementations. This entry describes the archive without asserting current compiler readiness.

BOBYQA performs local derivative-free minimization of a smooth objective subject to simple bounds, using interpolating quadratic models and bounded trust-region subproblems. The reviewed wrapper partitions workspace, checks interpolation-count/bound-spacing restrictions and adjusts the starting point near bounds; BOBYQB dispatches model steps and objective evaluations. The model gradient is internal and does not mean the caller supplies derivatives. Require N>=2, N+2<=NPT<=(N+1)(N+2)/2, positive ordered radii and each bound interval at least twice RHOBEG. This original interface returns the best sampled variables but no explicit convergence flag or objective output argument. Printed termination reasons, independent objective/feasibility checks and evaluation-budget exhaustion must be distinguished; RHOEND is a radius target, not a solution-error certificate. This is a local constrained method, not global optimization.

call bobyqa(n,npt,x,xl,xu,0.5d0,1d-6,1,500,w)
! Re-evaluate the objective and bound feasibility; no status code is returned.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Build the complete BOBYQA folder with a matching custom CALFUN instead of its supplied problem callback. Do not combine unrelated solver-folder callbacks/symbols blindly. No minimum, termination reason, budget or bound residual was tested.

classifications.notes: COBYLA minimizes an objective subject to nonlinear inequalities using simplex interpolation of objective/constraint values and native linearized trust-region subproblems. The caller supplies CALCFC values with feasible constraints CON>=0; it supplies neither objective nor constraint derivatives. G2h3b1a records the smooth general nonlinear-constraint/no-derivative scope, with zero equality constraints in this selected interface. Equalities are not separate inputs and tight paired inequalities need independent care. Unlike the other reviewed Powell folders, this copy has no IMPLICIT REAL*8 declaration and its Makefile does not promote REAL, so the reviewed default build uses default-real arrays and radii. MAXFUN is an input evaluation limit overwritten with evaluations used. There is no returned convergence code, and small final simplex radius does not guarantee feasibility or an accurate optimum.

procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Match the actual build precision in the driver, all solver files and CALCFC. Do not pass DOUBLE PRECISION solely because other Powell folders use it. No constrained optimum, precision-promoted build or feasibility tolerance was run.

classifications.notes: LINCOA performs local derivative-free minimization of a smooth objective with linear inequalities, building quadratic interpolation models and solving linearly constrained model trust subproblems. Columns A(:,J) are constraint normals for A(:,J) dot X<=B(J). The wrapper normalizes constraints and, if the initial point violates one, increases its internal normalized right-hand side to admit that point; the input B array itself is not overwritten by this adjustment. A feasible initial point is therefore important if the original feasible region must be preserved. Model-improvement objective calls may be infeasible; the incoming sign of F is a feasibility indicator before CALFUN overwrites it. Require nonzero constraint normals, valid N/NPT/radii and sufficient budget/workspace. W(1) and W(2) return objective and evaluation-count information after the normal algorithm; invalid-input early returns need separate handling and there is no explicit status code. It is neither linear programming nor a global optimum certificate.

classifications.notes: NEWUOA minimizes a smooth unconstrained multivariate function from a supplied initial point without user derivatives. It forms quadratic interpolation models with least-change Hessian updates and calls a truncated-CG trust-region model solver. N must be at least two, NPT must lie in the documented interpolation range, and both radii must be positive with RHOEND<=RHOBEG. This original entry uses a globally linked CALFUN symbol and a caller-sized double-precision workspace, changes X and reports progress through printing rather than a returned convergence status. The callback must be defined on trial points outside any intended box because no bounds are enforced. This mapping records the native local search/dispatch and model step, not a guarantee that RHOEND measures actual solution error or that a global minimum is found.

classifications.notes: GETMIN is the documented TOLMIN entry for a differentiable objective with linear equalities/inequalities and simple bounds. The caller supplies FGCALC objective and first derivatives; the solver maintains active constraints, seeks feasibility, uses line searches and tests the projected first-order/KKT residual against ACC. Constraint normals occupy columns; the first MEQ constraints are equalities and subsequent constraints use A(:,J) dot X<=B(J). Fixed variables can use equal lower/upper bounds. INFO is an input evaluation limit (zero means no imposed limit) and an output reason: 1 is the normal feasibility/first-order stop, while 2/3 indicate stalled feasible progress and 4 through 8 report invalid/inconsistent constraints or budget exhaustion. Return is not a second-order or global optimality certificate. Review covers the public contract, feasibility/minimization dispatch and native first-order stopping path, not every degeneracy/line-search dependency.

classifications.notes: The README lists distinct Martello-Toth algorithms and problem variants. Python wrapper availability does not establish uniform exactness, supported bounds or numerical behavior for every variant.

The external MT1 routine solves a binary single-capacity profit-maximizing knapsack through greedy initialization, integer upper bounds, branching and backtracking. CHMT1 checks selected admissibility conditions when JCK=1: at least two items, positive integer profits/weights/capacity, every weight <= capacity, total weight > capacity and nonincreasing profit/weight ratios. It is not a wrapper that sorts arbitrary inputs or handles the all-items-fit case. All eight arrays need N+1 elements; sentinel slots P(N+1),W(N+1) are overwritten despite a blanket unchanged-input comment. Integer products/sums and default-REAL ratio/bound arithmetic can overflow or lose precision; no large-instance robustness or optimality experiment was run. This mapping is the selected MT1 path, not every MT2/generalized/multiple knapsack algorithm.

classifications.notes: MTP minimizes the number of equal-capacity bins through a packing heuristic, lower bounds, reduction and ENUMER branch-and-bound, then reconstructs original item assignments. local.name: Clawpack Riemann solvers
local.description: Fortran and Python Riemann-solver components for Clawpack-compatible PDE schemes.

classifications.notes: The README describes a repository of solver components and normal/transverse interfaces. These components are not full time-dependent PDE applications by themselves.

The selected pointwise routines solve scalar interface Riemann problems used in wave-propagation finite-volume methods for one-dimensional hyperbolic conservation laws. rp1_advection_ptwise uses constant velocity from REAL(KIND=8) COMMON /cparam/ u, returns the state jump, speed and signed flux fluctuations. rp1_burgers_ptwise uses the Roe average speed for flux q**2/2 and applies an always-enabled entropy fix to transonic rarefactions. Require NUM_EQN=1 and NUM_WAVES=1; the checked drivers use NUM_AUX=1 with unused auxiliary arrays. All numerical arrays are REAL(KIND=8), integers use the matching default ABI, and the pointwise declarations are INOUT even for quantities only read by these implementations. There is no status/dimension validation; larger arbitrary systems are not implied by dimension arguments. The two files export the same external symbol and are alternative link selections. Source review covers the full selected small kernels. Two complete catalog-owned main programs were compiled and run with bounds/FPE checks: nine advection cases and eight Burgers cases verify exact interface fluxes, fluctuation conservation, jumps and reported speeds. The results establish those cases, not a complete Clawpack time integrator, boundary treatment, convergence order or all solvers in the repository.

procedures.summary: Pointwise scalar advection Riemann-solver component; link this source variant separately.
procedures.usage:
! GAMS I2a2; scalar advection interface checks.
! Upstream pin: 008d4921ea46878a97a96c8b8daa399a2e7b9078
program check_advection
  implicit none
  interface
    subroutine rp1_ptwise(ne,na,nw,ql,qr,al,ar,w,s,am,ap)
      integer, intent(in) :: ne,na,nw
      real(kind=8), intent(inout) :: ql(ne),qr(ne),al(na),ar(na)
      real(kind=8), intent(inout) :: w(ne,nw),s(nw),am(ne),ap(ne)
    end subroutine
  end interface
  real(kind=8) :: u
  common /cparam/ u
  real(kind=8) :: ql(1),qr(1),al(1),ar(1),w(1,1),s(1),am(1),ap(1)
  real(kind=8), parameter :: speeds(3)=[-2d0,0d0,3d0]
  real(kind=8), parameter :: left(3)=[1d0,-1d0,2d0],right(3)=[4d0,2d0,2d0]
  real(kind=8) :: flux,err,maxerr,tol
  integer :: i,j
  maxerr=0d0; al=0d0; ar=0d0
  do i=1,size(speeds)
    u=speeds(i)
    do j=1,size(left)
      ql=left(j); qr=right(j); w=0d0; s=0d0; am=0d0; ap=0d0
      call rp1_ptwise(1,1,1,ql,qr,al,ar,w,s,am,ap)
      if(u>=0d0)then
        flux=u*left(j)
      else
        flux=u*right(j)
      endif
      err=max(abs(u*left(j)+am(1)-flux),abs(u*right(j)-ap(1)-flux), &
              abs(am(1)+ap(1)-u*(right(j)-left(j))), &
              abs(w(1,1)-(right(j)-left(j))),abs(s(1)-u))
      tol=2d-13*max(1d0,abs(flux),abs(u*left(j)),abs(u*right(j)))
      if(.not.(err<=tol))error stop 'advection flux/speed/jump check failed'
      maxerr=max(maxerr,err)
    enddo
  enddo
  print '(a,es12.4)','Maximum absolute error: ',maxerr
  print '(a)','PASS advection: 9 positive/negative/zero-speed and state cases'
end program check_advection

Nine cases check positive/negative/zero velocities, jump/speed and upwind Godunov flux from both sides. Maximum absolute discrepancy was zero for these finite test cases. procedures.summary: Pointwise scalar burgers Riemann-solver component; link this source variant separately.
procedures.usage:
! GAMS I2a2; scalar burgers interface checks.
! Upstream pin: 008d4921ea46878a97a96c8b8daa399a2e7b9078
program check_burgers
  implicit none
  interface
    subroutine rp1_ptwise(ne,na,nw,ql,qr,al,ar,w,s,am,ap)
      integer, intent(in) :: ne,na,nw
      real(kind=8), intent(inout) :: ql(ne),qr(ne),al(na),ar(na)
      real(kind=8), intent(inout) :: w(ne,nw),s(nw),am(ne),ap(ne)
    end subroutine
  end interface
  real(kind=8) :: ql(1),qr(1),al(1),ar(1),w(1,1),s(1),am(1),ap(1)
  real(kind=8), parameter :: left(8) =[1d0,-3d0,-2d0,1d0,2d0,1d0,2d0,0d0]
  real(kind=8), parameter :: right(8)=[3d0,-1d0,1d0,-1d0,-1d0,-2d0,2d0,0d0]
  real(kind=8) :: fl,fr,flux,err,maxerr,tol
  integer :: i
  maxerr=0d0; al=0d0; ar=0d0
  do i=1,size(left)
    ql=left(i); qr=right(i); w=0d0; s=0d0; am=0d0; ap=0d0
    call rp1_ptwise(1,1,1,ql,qr,al,ar,w,s,am,ap)
    fl=0.5d0*left(i)**2; fr=0.5d0*right(i)**2
    ! Independent exact Godunov flux from the scalar Riemann solution.
    if(left(i)>right(i))then
      flux=max(fl,fr)
    elseif(left(i)>=0d0)then
      flux=fl
    elseif(right(i)<=0d0)then
      flux=fr
    else
      flux=0d0
    endif
    err=max(abs(fl+am(1)-flux),abs(fr-ap(1)-flux), &
            abs(am(1)+ap(1)-(fr-fl)), &
            abs(w(1,1)-(right(i)-left(i))), &
            abs(s(1)-0.5d0*(left(i)+right(i))))
    tol=2d-13*max(1d0,abs(fl),abs(fr),abs(flux))
    if(.not.(err<=tol))error stop 'Burgers Godunov flux/entropy check failed'
    maxerr=max(maxerr,err)
  enddo
  print '(a,es12.4)','Maximum absolute error: ',maxerr
  print '(a)','PASS Burgers: 8 shock, rarefaction, transonic and constant-state cases'
end program check_burgers

local.name: Singular surface operators
local.description: Nystrom discretization of weakly singular integral operators on surfaces.

classifications.notes: The README identifies single/double-layer potentials and the associated discretization paper. Operator discretization is not taken as evidence of a complete general integral-equation solver.

CADAPTRI adaptively integrates a complex-valued callback over a planar triangle. It compares a parent integral against the sum over four midpoint subtriangles, accepts the parent when the absolute difference is below EPS, otherwise recursively processes children through an explicit stack. The one-triangle kernel maps a hardcoded 82-node rule by an affine transformation and absolute Jacobian determinant. Header claims of a 60-point rule and approximately 30 digits are not accepted as precision evidence; the implementation uses double precision. EPS is a local parent/children comparison, not an apportioned bound on accumulated global error. NQUAD adds 79 per accepted parent and is inconsistent with the 82-node kernel and refinement evaluations, so it is not an actual function-evaluation counter. IER=4/16 report stack/depth exhaustion and partial VAL must not be treated as a complete integral. The source file begins with a debugging main; extract the documented library section to avoid duplicate main programs. Review covers this planar adaptive kernel, not the full singular surface-operator solver.

local.name: Unstructured finite volume
local.description: Unstructured field-calculus and finite-volume PDE code with a Poisson demonstration.

classifications.notes: The author Poisson example documents a unit-square manufactured solution, mesh inputs and GMRES assembly/solve. It has not been run here; source-interface inspection does not verify its reported convergence or sign conventions.

The public CONJUGATE_GRADIENT%SOLVE binding implements unpreconditioned CG for an attached real linear operator, including the sparse stencil operators used by this finite-volume framework. The native recurrence updates residual, search direction and the iterate using inherited matrix actions and scalar products. The operator must be symmetric positive definite in the actual pairing; the code does not verify symmetry/positivity, and its tiny-PAP guard checks magnitude rather than positive curvature. The stopping threshold is TOLERANCE*(1+NORM(RHS)); ACHIEVED reports a residual norm, but return can also follow a tiny denominator or exhausted iteration budget. There is no separate reason/status output. Affine constants from an attached operation must be moved to the RHS consistently. This mapping records sparse symmetric solver usage, not a sparse storage-format API or a guarantee for nonsymmetric/indefinite systems.

procedures.summary: Public operator-attached CG binding with residual-norm output and no separate convergence code.
procedures.usage:
use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
use operation_conjugate_gradient, only: conjugate_gradient
type(conjugate_gradient) :: solver
real(real64) :: achieved
! After constructing/attaching a symmetric-positive sparse linear action and
! consistent execution/unknown domains: RHS and initial X have matching sizes.
solver%tolerance=1.e-10_real64; solver%max_iterations=1000
call solver%solve(rhs,x,achieved)
! Independently form RHS-A*X and distinguish a tolerance exit from breakdown.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-attach context fragment requiring the complete field/graph/operator framework. CG assumes the chosen attached linear system has the needed symmetry/definiteness. No stencil solve, residual or breakdown was run.

classifications.notes: The public GMRES%SOLVE binding implements restarted real GMRES for attached general linear actions, including sparse finite-volume stencils. It uses native Arnoldi orthogonalization, Givens rotations, triangular back substitution and correction updates. RESTART is the Krylov dimension, while MAX_ITERATIONS bounds outer restart cycles rather than the total number of matrix actions. On an estimated-tolerance exit the true residual norm is recomputed before returning, but an exhausted final cycle can leave an estimate as ACHIEVED. Zero MAX_ITERATIONS can leave that output undefined. The radius/breakdown branch can still reach division by a zero triangular diagonal; return has no dedicated failure/status code. Require positive tolerances, sensible dimensions, initialized attachment and explicit affine-RHS handling. This is a general sparse/operator solver mapping, not a rank-deficient least-squares solver or automatically preconditioned algorithm.

procedures.summary: Public restarted GMRES operator binding; restart cycles and residual-output limitations are explicit.
procedures.usage:
use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
use operation_gmres, only: gmres
type(gmres) :: solver
real(real64) :: achieved
! Attach the initialized linear action/domain and prepare RHS/initial X first.

local.name: FERRE
local.description: Parameter fitting by interpolation in tabulated model grids and chi-squared matching.

classifications.notes: The README requires model predictions supplied as an array and describes covariance outputs. Validity of inferred parameter errors and coverage outside the supplied model grid are not established.

LIN performs multilinear interpolation of vector-valued responses on a tensor-product parameter grid. It converts normalized parameter coordinates into grid indices, loads 2**NDIM neighboring response vectors from the shared in-memory array or direct-access file and repeatedly interpolates along configured parameter axes. This supports multivariate gridded interpolation, not scattered interpolation or a fit of model parameters. The short routine depends on fully initialized SHARE dimensions, strides, axis/order maps and grid/file data. It has no local clipping or endpoint correction: at p=1 its corner indexing can request a neighbor past the final grid cell, so callers must follow the enclosing package coordinate conventions and verify boundaries. The scratch response array grows exponentially with dimension. SHARE sets DP=SELECTED_REAL_KIND(6) in this pin, despite historical double-precision comments elsewhere; use the actual module kind. No shape/range/status validation is returned by LIN.

classifications.notes: The README identifies a translation of the Weinert smoothing algorithm. Smoothing is not exact interpolation, and claimed speed improvement is not independently benchmarked.

CSPLINE forms second differences of equally spaced observations, factors a structured smoothing system using an untruncated or truncated recurrence, reconstructs the fitted values, evaluates a GCV-style score and fills intermediate/end samples. K5 records smoothing rather than exact interpolation through the supplied data. The user supplies LAM; returning SCORE does not mean the routine automatically minimizes GCV or chooses LAM. T enters through LAM*T**3, R selects subdivision/output layout and JJ controls recurrence truncation. There are no argument checks or status output. Small N and truncated recurrence sizes can cause invalid indexing; divisions/logarithms and score trace need valid nondegenerate inputs. The source review does not establish a general admissible parameter region or numerical stability.

local.name: Fortran GMM EM
local.description: Expectation-maximization for Gaussian mixtures using BLAS and optional OpenMP.

classifications.notes: The README documents mixture components, covariance data and parallel build options. Convergence, initialization sensitivity and statistical model selection are not verified by this documentation review.

The selected fit routine estimates a multivariate Gaussian mixture by alternating E-step log-density/log-sum-exp responsibilities and M-step weighted means/covariances, with BLAS products and Cholesky-derived precisions. This supports parametric analysis of independent multidimensional observations. It is not K-means or a proof of finding the global likelihood maximum. Components must be allocated and initialized before fit; empty-component responsibility sums can divide by zero and covariance factorization failures STOP. regCovar is a module variable initially zero. The stopping condition is a signed likelihood improvement per sample, with no iteration cap or returned convergence status, so a decreasing/nonfinite objective can also end iteration. No fit or statistical validation was run.

The external HYG0F1 evaluates the confluent hypergeometric limit series 0F1(;A;Z), accumulating positive terms through logarithms of the rising factorial and ordinary factorial. The actual log formulation requires A>0 and Z>0 on the selected real branch; it does not implement general negative/complex arguments, analytic continuation or poles. It stops on an absolute term threshold 1e-15 or before iteration 1000, without returning a convergence flag or rigorous tail bound. Overflow, finite-precision loss and truncation are not diagnosed. This scoped mapping records the positive-real confluent limit function, not the separate Gauss 2F1 implementation or all special-function regimes in the package.

local.name: TISEAN
local.description: Legacy nonlinear time-series analysis software with Fortran programs.

classifications.notes: The original distribution README identifies the nonlinear time-series project and installation workflow. Individual estimators, dependencies and current compiler/platform compatibility need separate review.

The supplied AUTOCOR executable estimates a univariate autocorrelation sequence using the squared Fourier amplitudes and an inverse transform. Its default path demeans/normalizes nonconstant data, zero-pads and divides lag values by the decreasing overlap count before normalizing lag zero. The -v path requests unnormalized autocovariance and bypasses the normalizing helper, so callers needing centered covariance should center input explicitly. The -p/-P periodic paths have different continuation/length conventions. The CLI reads files/columns and writes lag/value pairs; it is not a reusable Fortran module function. Constant-series normalization stops and the helper uses fixed one-million-point work arrays; default padding can make the helper limit smaller than the advertised input length. Review covers the command driver and Fourier-power/backtransform helper, not every file parser or a bias/uncertainty guarantee.

procedures.summary: Supplied command-line FFT autocorrelation program with file/column controls.
procedures.usage:
! After building TISEAN, create a finite nonconstant single-column series.dat.
! Shell command, writing lag/value pairs to standard output:
!   autocor -c1 series.dat
! Default behavior uses nonperiodic continuation and normalized autocorrelation.
! Keep input and padded FFT lengths within the STORE_SPEC work-array limit.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. This is the supplied executable, not a callable module API or a newly validated driver. Build the complete matching CLI/FFTPACK support. Input centering and periodic flags change the statistic; no autocorrelation, boundary correction or command execution was tested.

classifications.notes: The supplied SPECTRUM executable forms a Fourier periodogram of a univariate sample sequence and prints frequency/power pairs. STORE_SPEC scales the real FFT, stores squared amplitudes and optional phase slots; the driver emits powers and can sum neighboring frequency bins when -w requests coarser resolution. It does not automatically remove the sample mean, taper the sequence or supply confidence intervals, and summed bins are not an automatic spectral-density normalization. NLENGTH may be reduced to a supported transform length; the driver reports this truncation. The selected unsmoothed CLI use belongs to periodogram analysis L10a3a2, not an autoregressive spectrum or an arbitrary continuous Fourier transform. Review covers driver frequency/bin layout and the shared periodogram helper. Finite positive sampling rate, sufficiently long finite samples and interpretation of DC/Nyquist units remain caller responsibilities.

procedures.summary: Supplied command-line Fourier periodogram program with sampling-rate and bin-width controls.
procedures.usage:
! After building TISEAN, prepare finite samples in column one of series.dat.
! Shell command, using a sampling rate of one sample per time unit:
!   spectrum -f1 -c1 series.dat
! Center/taper the input beforehand if needed; retain any length-truncation notice.
! Output is frequency/power data, not a checked spectral-density estimate.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use the supplied CLI and complete FFT/file support, within its fixed-array limits. Frequency units follow the sampling-rate option. No periodogram, normalization, binning or command run was tested.

local.name: TSSS
local.description: R interfaces to compiled time-series analysis, simulation and state-space modeling routines.

classifications.notes: DESCRIPTION identifies Kitagawa-methodology state-space analysis. It does not establish coverage of every time-series model or a standalone Fortran user interface.

UNICORF dispatches univariate autocovariance, normalized autocorrelation and estimated error-bound calculations. The underlying AUTCOV centers using observations strictly between OUTMIN/OUTMAX and divides each lag sum by the total accepted-observation count, not the number of accepted pairs at that lag. Missing/out-of-bound pairs are skipped; zero accepted count or zero lag-zero variance causes unguarded divisions in mean/correlation calculations. Output COV(0:LAG,1:4) holds covariance, correlation and two error-bound arrays. Choose nonconstant finite accepted data and 0<=LAG<N. Review covers wrapper dispatch and mean/autocovariance/correlation calculations; error-bound coverage is not statistically validated.

procedures.summary: External double-precision univariate lag-summary driver with a four-column output array.
procedures.usage:
external :: UNICORF
double precision :: y(8),cov(0:2,4),average
y=[1d0,2d0,1d0,3d0,2d0,4d0,3d0,5d0]
call UNICORF(y,8,2,-1d30,1d30,cov,average)
! COV(:,1:2) contain covariance/correlation; columns 3:4 are estimated error bounds.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Link the package support routines and match double/default-integer kinds. Boundaries are exclusive; a successful return is not protection against empty selections or constant-series division by zero. No lag estimate or confidence/error coverage was tested.

classifications.notes: CRSCORF computes lagged covariance/correlation between channels; the selected sketch uses two time series. Means are formed separately from values strictly within each channel bounds. C(L,I,J) pairs channel I at time t with channel J at t-L, dividing by sqrt(NSUM(I)*NSUM(J)); it is not recomputed with a pairwise-complete denominator per lag. R normalizes by lag-zero channel variances. Output includes both channel orders for nonnegative lags, so cross-lag orientation must be retained when comparing implementations. All-rejected/constant channels and large integer count products need validation because no error status guards their divisions. Review covers the two-channel wrapper and core normalization/lag loops, not every multivariate statistical model.

procedures.summary: External double-precision channel cross-covariance/correlation driver.
procedures.usage:
external :: CRSCORF
double precision :: y(8,2),lower(2),upper(2),c(0:2,2,2),r(0:2,2,2),average(2)
y(:,1)=[1d0,2d0,1d0,3d0,2d0,4d0,3d0,5d0]
y(:,2)=[2d0,1d0,3d0,2d0,4d0,3d0,5d0,4d0]
lower=-1d30; upper=1d30
call CRSCORF(y,8,2,2,lower,upper,c,r,average)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The lag dimension starts at zero and observations occupy array rows. Preserve C(L,I,J) orientation and do not assume lag-specific pair-count normalization. No cross-correlation, missing-value or error case was executed.

local.name: urca
local.description: R unit-root and cointegration testing with compiled Fortran components.

classifications.notes: DESCRIPTION documents applied econometric tests. Critical-value approximations, test assumptions and behavior under particular data-generating processes remain unchecked here.

The external DDNOR routine evaluates the standard normal cumulative distribution via Cody-style piecewise rational error/complementary-error approximations. It uses symmetry and separate small/intermediate/large transformed-argument branches. The input is clipped internally to [-16,16], and positive-tail probabilities can round to one; this is not a survival-function API preserving arbitrary extreme-tail relative accuracy. No input argument is overwritten and no error/status output is supplied. Accuracy claims in inherited comments were not adopted as verified results. This selected distribution-function mapping does not imply every urca test or response-surface coefficient table was source reviewed.

procedures.summary: External REAL(8) standard-normal CDF subroutine with one scalar output.
procedures.usage:
external :: ddnor
real(8) :: x,p
x=1.0d0
call ddnor(x,p)
! P approximates Pr(Z<=X) for standard normal Z; no separate upper-tail result.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Compile/link the containing source with its required R print/exit support or provide a properly scoped standalone extraction consistent with licensing. Match REAL(8) to the expected double kind. No CDF values, tails or accuracy claim were tested.

classifications.notes: INNORZ estimates a standard normal quantile using an Abramowitz-Stegun-style initial approximation, a second approximation-based correction, then a CDF/density Newton correction through DDNOR. Use strictly interior probabilities: the input check rejects values outside [0,1] but permits endpoints whose later 1/PR**2 and logarithms are singular. Extreme interior probabilities can still overflow or lose accuracy through complementary-CDF cancellation and density division. Invalid input uses R REALPR/REXIT rather than a recoverable Fortran status. The result is a scalar quantile, not a random draw or normal order-statistic sample. Review covers approximation/correction flow and domain hazards, not validated tail accuracy.

procedures.summary: External REAL(8) normal inverse-CDF subroutine with R error-path dependencies.
procedures.usage:
external :: innorz
real(8) :: p,z
p=0.975d0
if(p<=0d0.or.p>=1d0) error stop "probability must be strictly interior"
call innorz(p,z)
! Compare Z and its independently evaluated normal CDF with the requested P.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use moderate interior probabilities and resolve R error-support linkage. Endpoints are unsafe despite passing the routine range check, and no INFO output reports numerical failure. No quantile, round trip or extreme-tail behavior was tested.

local.name: Vector fitting Fortran
local.description: Fortran vector-fitting software with a documented test/plot workflow.

classifications.notes: The README identifies vector fitting, source/build files and a gnuplot-based test script. Model order, pole constraints and stability preservation require more detailed documentation/source review.

calculate_residues builds fixed-pole rational basis columns 1/(s-a), adds optional constant/linear terms, stacks real/imaginary sample equations and solves for real coefficients, coupling complex-conjugate poles so residues form conjugate pairs. K1a1a3 records this unconstrained linear least-squares fit in specified nonpolynomial basis functions with poles held fixed. It is not a mapping of the separate iterative pole-relocation optimization. The default morse_penrose_solve explicitly forms A-transpose*A and inverts it; the alternative pads the matrix and dispatches EISPACK SVD. Neither returns solver status to the caller. Adjacent complex conjugate poles are required and invalid pairing STOPs; sampling at poles is unguarded. NEW_A and C_HAT dummy arrays are not assigned by this routine, despite appearing in its signature. Require 2*NF>=number of real unknowns and adequate rank; normal equations worsen conditioning. No fit, conditioning or SVD/back-end accuracy was checked by execution.

procedures.summary: External fixed-pole residue fit using nonstandard COMPLEX*16/REAL*8 declarations and default INTEGER/LOGICAL controls. C receives residues; D/H receive real optional polynomial terms or zero. NEW_A/C_HAT are unused, not returned pole updates. There is no INFO output.
procedures.signature:
CALL calculate_residues(order, a, new_a, c, c_hat, d, h, nf, f, s, &
 include_const_term, include_s_term, use_SVD_invert, verbose)
procedures.usage:
integer,parameter :: order=1,nf=3
complex*16 :: a(order),unused_a(order),c(order),unused_c(order),f(nf),s(nf)
real*8 :: d,h
a(1)=(-1d0,0d0)
s=[(0d0,1d0),(0d0,2d0),(0d0,3d0)]
f=2d0/(s-a(1))
call calculate_residues(order,a,unused_a,c,unused_c,d,h,nf,f,s,.false.,.false.,.false.,.false.)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Compile/link the external matrix helpers and required dependencies. This sketch chooses a single fixed real pole and the normal-equation path; it does not endorse that path for ill-conditioned fitting. Never read the unused NEW_A/C_HAT arrays as results. Check fitted responses and residuals independently because no returned solver status or uncertainty estimate is provided. Full Vfit pole iteration and passivity/stability guarantees are outside this mapping.

classifications.notes: calculate_fit_function initializes each response as d+s*h and adds c(i)/(s-a(i)) for every supplied pole/residue. K6a1 records evaluation of an existing rational fit; it does not estimate coefficients, relocate poles, enforce passivity or validate stability. The external routine accepts explicit-size COMPLEX*16 vectors, REAL*8 d/h and no status. Caller must supply finite compatible arrays and avoid s=a denominators; no cancellation/overflow or singular-evaluation guard is present. No response values or checked driver were executed.

procedures.summary: External scalar-response rational evaluator over NF sample points. A/C have ORDER poles/residues, S/F_FIT have NF complex entries. Output F_FIT is fully assigned; there are no module/global-state dependencies in this selected body.

procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. This call needs only the selected evaluator body, but its legacy COMPLEX*16/REAL*8 declarations require compatible compiler support. Avoid sample/pole coincidences and verify values/residuals against the intended model. No fitted-pole quality, physical realization or extrapolation accuracy is certified.
