local.name: Timeseries Tools
local.description: Weighted spectra, filtering and frequency extraction for unevenly sampled time series.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes site-specific prebuilt installations from local source compilation. Performance claims and suitable OpenMP settings are not independently verified.

The external CalcAlphaBeta routine forms weighted sine/cosine normal-equation sums at a requested frequency and solves the two-by-two system for alpha and beta. The spec program uses alpha**2+beta**2 as its raw power before output transformations. t is in seconds and nu in microhertz; twopi_micro incorporates 1e-6. The routine reads timeseries::sumWeights rather than computing SUM(w), so callers bypassing ImportData must set that global consistently. Equal array lengths, positive effective weight sum, finite nonnegative weights and a nonsingular sine/cosine design are preconditions; determinant division has no check/status. There is no fitted floating mean/intercept in this routine and no automatic significance test. This is a source-reviewed least-squares periodogram path, not an FFT or a new spectral accuracy/timing check.

procedures.summary: External assumed-shape spectral-fit subroutine whose explicit interface is reexported by the timeseries module. Shared sumWeights must match the supplied weights.
procedures.usage:
use kind_defs, only: dbl,twopi_micro
use timeseries, only: CalcAlphaBeta,sumWeights
real(dbl) :: t(4),f(4),w(4),nu,alpha,beta,power
t=[0.0_dbl,250.0_dbl,500.0_dbl,750.0_dbl]
nu=1000.0_dbl
f=sin(twopi_micro*nu*t); w=1.0_dbl
sumWeights=sum(w)
call CalcAlphaBeta(t,f,w,nu,alpha,beta)
power=alpha**2+beta**2
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. USE timeseries supplies an interface to an external routine, not a type-bound/module implementation. The example has no offset; preprocess a mean as appropriate rather than assuming an intercept is fitted. Link the repository dependencies used by the full source. No spectral peak or normalization was checked.

local.name: TOMS Algorithm 675
local.description: Square-root covariance and information filtering in dense or Hessenberg forms.

classifications.notes: The README identifies the original ACM algorithm and source/licensing reference. These are specialized filtering routines, not a general covariance-estimation or arbitrary-state-space package.

SRCF forms a square-root covariance pre-array from R, C*S, A*S and B*Q (or a pre-multiplied B), triangularizes it with Householder helpers, and copies the updated lower factor S and optional combined-update gain K. SRIF constructs the corresponding information pre-array, triangularizes it and optionally solves for state X. L10a2e is scoped to scalar-observation (P=1) state-space filtering; the interfaces can also accept multiple observations, but no multivariate mapping is added here. SRCF updates covariance/gain only, not a complete observed-state trajectory. WITHK/WITHX are input requests that may be cleared by a condition estimate, leaving optional outputs unavailable. Inputs are triangular square-root/inverse-factor forms, not arbitrary covariance matrices; leading dimensions/workspace are caller responsibilities. No Kalman recursion, covariance identity or author driver was run.

procedures.summary: External double-precision combined covariance update. S lower factor is overwritten; WITHK requests K and can be set false. MULTBQ=true means B already supplies the required B*Q product. For positive dimensions, WRK needs at least (P+N) rows and (P+N+M) columns.
procedures.signature:
CALL SRCF(S, LDS, A, LDA, B, LDB, Q, LDQ, C, LDC, R, LDR, &
          N, M, P, K, LDK, WRK, LDW, MULTBQ, WITHK, TOL)
procedures.usage:
external :: srcf
double precision :: s(1,1),a(1,1),b(1,1),q(1,1),c(1,1),r(1,1),k(1,1),work(2,3)
logical :: withk,multbq
s=1.0d0; a=0.9d0; b=0.1d0; q=0.3d0; c=1.0d0; r=0.2d0
withk=.true.; multbq=.false.
call srcf(s,1,a,1,b,1,q,1,c,1,r,1,1,1,1,k,1,work,2,multbq,withk,1.0d-12)
! Inspect withk before using k; s is an updated factor, not a state estimate.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Scalar interface sketch using square-root factors. Link the supplied NAG-style helpers, DTRCO and compatible BLAS. With P=1 this is a univariate observation stream even if a larger application uses a vector state. There is no INFO/output-accuracy flag; inspect WITHK and independently verify factor/gain conventions. Larger triangular factors require correct stored triangles and sufficient workspace.

local.name: tidybench
local.description: Time-series causal-structure learning baselines with compiled Fortran components.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes SLARAC, QRBS, LASAR and SELVAR. Competition rankings and causal interpretations are author results, not proof of correct causal recovery for arbitrary observational data.

SLVAR performs selective multivariate autoregressive structure/lag search: each directed variable pair has one selected lag or no edge, candidate changes are scored in contiguous data batches and a greedy hill-climb retains improving changes. The final B matrix is batch-averaged absolute coefficients, not the full signed VAR lag tensor; A stores selected lags. BS, ML and MXITR can be rewritten, and MXITR=0 skips search so it requires an already initialized graph. The PRESS-like score helper calls DORGQR using workspace left by DGELS, which does not expose a reflector-TAU output contract; the validity of these leverage corrections is therefore not established and needs validation/repair. Too-small batches, singular designs and leverage denominators near zero also need checks. INFO is reused through candidate fits/final coefficient calculations and does not certify the global optimum or every intermediate fit. Review covers the native selection/control flow and concrete returned quantities, not a causal-identification guarantee or a validated scoring implementation.

procedures.summary: External selective VAR lag-graph search returning selected lags and absolute coefficient scores.

external :: slvar
integer :: batch_size,max_lag,max_iterations,info

! Allocate DOUBLE PRECISION B(N,N) and default-INTEGER A(N,N).
! Choose T sufficiently larger than N+maximum lag, and full-rank batches.
batch_size=t-2; max_lag=2; max_iterations=20
call slvar(t,n,x,batch_size,max_lag,max_iterations,b,a,info,0)
! A(i,j) is a selected lag; B(i,j) is an average ABSOLUTE coefficient.
! Validate/repair the PRESS QR-workspace handoff before relying on the scores.

local.name: twdtw
local.description: Time-weighted dynamic time warping for multidimensional seasonal time series.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes an R interface and Fortran kernels with flexible weighting. A similarity score is not a statistical proof of equivalence or a complete time-series forecasting model.

The selected legacy external twdtwf90gt routine aligns two multichannel time series by dynamic programming over Euclidean feature distances plus a logistic penalty on cyclic time differences. It takes the minimum cumulative cost from diagonal/horizontal/vertical predecessors, tracks start indices and reports best endpoint candidates. The first matrix column is accumulated separately without the LB exclusion used in later columns. XM is (M,D), YM is (N,D), with time in column 1. Callers must initialize CM first-row boundary costs and output buffers before the legacy call. JB is declared length N although as many as M endpoint groups may be written; this sketch restricts M<=N. Times must share a cycle representation with differences within CL. This is alignment/cost calculation, not automatic classification or an accuracy certificate. The separate callback BIND(C) routine marks CM INTENT(OUT) while reading boundary entries; that interface needs correction and is not the sketch path.

local.name: Fortran Iterative Quicksort
local.description: Iterative quicksort with explicit-stack and caller-buffer interfaces.

classifications.notes: The README documents nonrecursive integer/real procedures and an allocation-free design. Its safety-critical and deterministic-resource claims are not treated as independent certification or a bound proved for every input.

The public quicksort generic dispatches the INTEGER overload to iterative range-stack processing and last-element Lomuto partitioning with <= comparisons. Values are sorted in place in ascending order. The stack is supplied by the caller, avoiding recursive calls and allocations in the core. push_pair silently ignores a range when two more stack slots do not fit, so an undersized stack can return partially unsorted data without a status flag; use the documented 2*N default-integer workspace. Last-element pivots retain quadratic worst cases for ordered/equal data; nonrecursive does not mean bounded linearithmic work. The other kind has its own mapping; no upstream sort/test or timing was run.

procedures.summary: Public generic, shown for default INTEGER values and a default-INTEGER work_stack. Both dummies are INTENT(INOUT); stack contents are scratch. For N>=2 use workspace of at least 2*N entries. Empty/singleton arrays return before stack use; there is no success/error output.

use sorting_module, only: quicksort
integer :: values(4)
integer :: stack(8)
values = [3, 1, 4, 2]
call quicksort(values, stack)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Provide enough workspace: overflow is silently skipped rather than reported. The sketch uses the generic, not its private specific. Large 2*N allocation arithmetic needs caller checking; last-pivot degeneration can take quadratic time. local.name: FAS
local.description: Factor-augmented sparse-regression testing and bootstrap tuning/inference with Fortran components.

classifications.notes: DESCRIPTION restricts the documented tests to linear and factor-augmented sparse regressions. Tuning-free wording does not establish universally valid inference outside the model assumptions.

FITNOISEF fits a lasso regression path and evaluates multiplier-bootstrap effective-noise quantiles/tuning thresholds along that path. The native loop multiplies fitted residuals by caller-supplied ESIM draws, computes 2*abs(X-transpose*residual_draw)/NOBS and the maximum over predictors, then obtains type-7 empirical quantiles. Random multipliers are generated by the R wrapper, not inside this Fortran kernel. This is a tuning/inference component of penalized multiple-linear regression, not ordinary-least-squares inference or an end-to-end factor-estimation routine. X/PF/ULAM and work/output arrays can be changed; initialize JERR=0 because allocation statuses are accumulated onto its incoming value. Require valid quantile levels, positive bootstrap count, adequate nonconstant design/path sizes and compatible multipliers. HATLAM=-1 can remain when no threshold crossing is found; negative path statuses and NALAM limit usable outputs. Review covers native path/bootstrap/quantile logic, not the asymptotic validity of the test or every R wrapper.

procedures.summary: External lasso effective-noise bootstrap/tuning kernel with externally supplied multipliers.

! After allocating inputs/outputs with the linked declarations:

! Set a valid descending ULAM path or the documented automatic-path sentinel.
jerr=0
call fitnoiseF(qlev,nquant,esim,numboot,nobs,nvars,x,y,pf,dfmax,pmax, &
 nlam,flmin,ulam,eps,isd,intr,maxit,nalam,b0,beta,ibeta,nbeta, &
 alam,npass,jerr,quant,hatlam)
if(jerr/=0) error stop "inspect bootstrap regression path diagnostics"

local.name: fOptimize
local.description: Educational one- and multidimensional continuous-optimization methods.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly limits the routines to academic use without further improvements. Its local search, derivative-free and quasi-Newton methods are not treated as globally convergent production solvers.

biss_1d compares objective values at two interior points separated by 20 percent of the current interval, then discards one side until interval width falls below tolerance. G1a1a records a derivative-free scalar minimization search on a suitable unimodal bracket, not a root bisection despite its name. imode=1 minimizes; other values maximize. The routine prints the estimate and optionally writes iteration data, but returns neither a minimizer argument nor a success flag. Initialized local tol/kmax/mode variables have implicit SAVE, so omitted optional settings can inherit previous calls. Iteration exhaustion uses STOP; no bracket/unimodality/NaN validation is supplied. The similarly named golden routine has an unguarded optional-unit write and is not the recommended entry here. No objective or bracket reduction was executed.

classifications.notes: The README documents changes to NITSOL, including Gram-Schmidt choices, finite-difference precision and removal of COMMON blocks. BLAS/LAPACK must be supplied externally; detailed solver behavior and convergence remain unchecked.

local.name: polyhomocont
local.description: Homotopy continuation for isolated solutions of square complex polynomial systems.

classifications.notes: The README describes total-degree projective paths, predictor/corrector tracking and a Cauchy endgame. Positive-dimensional components are not specially handled, and completeness or singular-endpoint behavior has not been independently verified.

SOLVE builds a randomized total-degree homotopy with product(degrees) start paths, tracks in projective coordinates using an RK4 predictor and Newton corrector with adaptive step rejection, and optionally applies a Cauchy end game. The driver classifies finite/infinite and regular/singular endpoints, refines regular solutions and clusters duplicates. STATUS reports setup errors separately from RES%NFAILED, path statuses and end-game status: STATUS_OK alone does not mean all roots were obtained. Numerical residuals, condition estimates, winding/multiplicity counts and real-root tolerances are diagnostic approximations, not certified algebraic counts or proof of completeness. A custom POLY_SYSTEM must supply exact total degrees, evaluations and Jacobians; the default homogeneous evaluator loses accuracy near infinity, so sparse/direct homogeneous evaluation is preferable there. Source review covers construction/driver dispatch, selected tracker and endpoint classification, not every continuation/end-game kernel or a numerical root test.

procedures.summary: Public module driver re-exported by POLYHOMOCONT; output result contains per-path classifications and approximate solutions.

use polyhomocont, only: wp,sparse_system,solve,solve_result,status_ok
type(sparse_system) :: sys
type(solve_result) :: res
integer :: status
call sys%init(2)
call sys%add_equation([1.0_wp,1.0_wp,-5.0_wp], &
     reshape([2,0,0,2,0,0],[2,3]),status)
if(status/=status_ok) error stop "first polynomial invalid"
call sys%add_equation([1.0_wp,-2.0_wp], &
     reshape([1,1,0,0],[2,2]),status)
if(status/=status_ok) error stop "second polynomial invalid"
call solve(sys,res,status)
! Check STATUS, RES%NFAILED, duplicates, path/endgame status and residuals.

Total-degree path counts can grow rapidly with dimension/degree. A small residual or no failed paths alone is not a completeness certificate. Review singular/infinite paths and independent affine residuals before interpreting the output.

local.name: pypolsys
local.description: Python interface to Fortran POLSYS_PLP polynomial-system homotopy solvers.

classifications.notes: The README limits the main interface to square complex polynomial systems and discusses BLAS/LAPACK packaging. Advertised convergence and solution-completeness properties have not been independently reproduced.

The wrapper initializes complex polynomial term coefficients/exponents and a partitioned linear-product start system, then calls POLSYS_PLP to track homotopy paths, returning candidate roots, per-path statuses and evaluation counts in module arrays. This is a square complex polynomial-system solver, not a general nonpolynomial system API or a new proof that every path succeeds. INIT_POLY expects concatenated equation terms; INIT_PARTITION defines variable groups for each equation. Always pass DENSE explicitly: the omitted-optional branch in SOLVE attempts to assign the absent dummy. The wrapper also fixes SCALE_FACTORS length at 30, so do not exceed 30 variables without correcting that bound; COMPLEX(KIND=8) coefficients must match core R8. Shared polynomial/partition/output state is not reentrant. Inspect SOLVE_STATUS/PATH_STATUS before interpreting roots; the wrapper assumes core output pointers are associated when copying them, so abnormal-error paths need additional protection. This review covers setup/driver dispatch and inspected core path tracking, not every singular/multiple/infinite-root case.

local.name: dfsaneacc
local.description: R package for secant-accelerated derivative-free spectral-residual nonlinear-system methods.

classifications.notes: DESCRIPTION identifies large-scale nonlinear systems and the published secant-acceleration method. The R interface and compiled components are not assumed to be a separately documented standalone Fortran solver.

The Fortran bmqrf module supplies column-pivoted Householder QR support, not the nonlinear DFSANE algorithm implemented in R. bmqr overwrites A with a compact factorization, stores reflector factors in gam and column permutation in p, and estimates rank using a scaled threshold of about 100 machine epsilons. extractQ/extractR expose the rank-sized factors. Restrict this reviewed interface to n>=m>=1, lda>=n and mlim>=m; it is not a reviewed wide-matrix routine. Failure hooks call REXIT and need the R runtime or a deliberately compatible replacement. No standalone compilation or factorization residual was checked.

local.name: L-BFGS-B CMake distribution
local.description: CMake distribution of limited-memory bound-constrained optimization software.

classifications.notes: The top-level README documents CMake; the bundled original Readme describes version 2.3, objective/gradient callbacks and reverse communication. The repository title modernized is not taken to establish equivalence to current L-BFGS-B releases.

solver_lbfgsb::setulb partitions workspaces and dispatches mainlb, whose selected path computes a generalized Cauchy point, limited-memory bound-subspace steps and a line search using caller-provided objective/gradient evaluations. G2h1a2 records smooth box-constrained optimization with first derivatives, not unconstrained-only optimization or global minimization. This distribution exposes the version-2.3 implementation through a module; its workspace formula and argument list must not be replaced with those from newer forks. TASK is a reverse-communication protocol: START first, FG requests F/G at returned X, NEW_X marks an accepted iterate, and terminal text distinguishes convergence, abnormal termination and input errors. Stopping uses projected-gradient norm or relative objective reduction scaled by FACTR*machine precision; small objective reduction need not imply small gradient. Caller controls evaluation/iteration limits. No optimization, line-search or bounds test was executed.

procedures.summary: Public solver_lbfgsb module subroutine. DOUBLE PRECISION X/L/U/G(N), default-INTEGER NBD(N), IWA(3*N), ISAVE(44), LOGICAL LSAVE(4), CHARACTER(60) TASK/CSAVE and DSAVE(29). WA length is 2*M*N+4*N+11*M*M+8*M for this pin. Preserve work/state arrays across calls.

use solver_lbfgsb, only: setulb
integer,parameter :: n=2,m=5
integer :: nbd(n),iwa(3*n),isave(44),request
logical :: lsave(4)
character(60) :: task,csave
real(8) :: x(n),l(n),u(n),f,g(n),wa(2*m*n+4*n+11*m*m+8*m),dsave(29)
x=[1d0,-1d0]; l=-2d0; u=2d0; nbd=2; f=0d0; g=0d0; task="START"
do request=1,1000
 call setulb(n,m,x,l,u,nbd,f,g,1d7,1d-6,wa,iwa,task,-1,csave,lsave,isave,dsave)
 if(task(1:2)=="FG") then
  f=sum(x*x); g=2d0*x
 else if(task(1:5)=="NEW_X") then
  cycle
 else
  exit
 end if
end do
if(task(1:4)/="CONV") error stop "L-BFGS-B did not report convergence"
! Independently verify projected gradient, bounds and objective.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Illustrative bounded quadratic using this pin-specific workspace. The loop caps reverse-communication requests, not accepted iterations. Read full terminal TASK, not just the absence of FG. Nonnegative FACTR/PGTOL select distinct stopping tests. classifications.notes: The setulb interface comments identify limited-memory bound-constrained optimization; the signature contains additional parameters relative to the original algorithm. No nonsmooth-convergence guarantee is inferred from the repository suffix or inherited original documentation.

SETULB exposes an extended reverse-communication limited-memory BFGS bound-constrained optimizer. TASK requests F and G at X, returns accepted iterates and eventually reports convergence, stop or error strings. NBD selects no/lower/both/upper bounds; The inherited FACTR/PGTOL documentation does not match this fork: both projected-gradient stopping checks are commented out and the relative-objective test is guarded by IF(.FALSE.). Callers must supply their own convergence and work-budget logic. The actual interface adds TAUX,NFG,JMAX,TAUD,NBISECT, uses ISAVE(47), DSAVE(30) and WA length 2*M*N+5*N+11*M*M+8*M+2*JMAX*N: the inherited shorter workspace comments are obsolete. The selected smooth path keeps NFG=0 to bypass the added stored-gradient convex-hull test; it still uses this fork's modified line search. Enabling that extension requires caller-managed gradient/point history as in the supplied driver and separate investigation: FREEX=1/INDCLOSE uses integer division before real assignment. This mapping does not establish nonsmooth convergence, global optimality or correctness of that extension. Driver/workspace partition, Cauchy/subspace and line-search dispatch were inspected, not every BLAS/LINPACK kernel.

local.name: OpenFSAM
local.description: Simulated-annealing objects for combinatorial, continuous and discrete optimization.

classifications.notes: The README describes three public optimizer types and user-supplied state and objective definitions. Annealing schedules and results depend on problem-specific configuration; global optimality is not certified.

The continuous sa_cont_type path initializes energies/state, clips uniform neighbor perturbations to one shared scalar bound interval, accepts moves using a Boltzmann probability, cools and returns the best state found. G2i records simulated-annealing global search, scoped to the continuous path with linear-additive cooling and monotonic temperature. It does not establish global optimality, a stationary sampling distribution or the discrete/combinatorial paths. state_curr is a pointer to caller-owned writable target storage and energy is a required associated type-bound callback. Bounds/damping defaults depend on the initial state and can collapse exploration; set them explicitly. max_step counts accepted moves plus a 1 percent random increment for rejected moves, while total_steps counts trials, so max_step is not an evaluation budget. prog_bar uses a MOD divisor rounded from max_step/91, which can be zero for small limits; the sketch disables it. No optimization or acceptance/cooling test was run.

procedures.summary: Inherited public type-bound method on OpenFSAM::sa_cont_type. REAL(8) state_curr pointer, state_best allocatable array and e_best/total_steps expose results. energy callback takes CLASS(sa_cont_type),INTENT(INOUT) and REAL(8) state(:), returns REAL(8). No status output.
procedures.usage:
use OpenFSAM, only: sa_cont_type
type(sa_cont_type) :: solver
real(8),target :: x(2)=[1d0,-1d0]
! Supply a matching explicit-interface ENERGY(thisSA,state_val) function.
solver%state_curr=>x
solver%energy=>energy
solver%smin=-2d0; solver%smax=2d0; solver%damping=0.5d0
solver%t_max=10d0; solver%t_min=0.01d0; solver%max_step=100
solver%cool_opt="LinAdd"; solver%mon_cool=.true.; solver%prog_bar=.false.
call solver%optimize()
! x is overwritten by the best state; inspect solver%e_best and total_steps.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Callback fragment requiring ENERGY; keep its target state alive and associated for the entire call. The same scalar interval bounds every coordinate, rather than separate bounds per parameter. Use nonempty state, positive damping and t_max>t_min>0 for this sketch. max_step does not bound objective calls or wall time; repeated rejected trials can take longer. local.name: LIBPARABOL / sippp
local.description: One-dimensional parabolic PDE solvers with layer-adapted meshes and implicit Runge-Kutta methods.

classifications.notes: The README restricts the documented operator to one spatial dimension and describes preconditioned GMRES for implicit-stage systems. It is not classified as an arbitrary multidimensional PDE framework.

The public GMRES routine solves a general real linear system represented by a matrix-action callback, stored as an N by S block-shaped vector. The native restarted Arnoldi process uses modified Gram-Schmidt, Givens rotations and right preconditioning. S is part of one flattened system, not a collection of independent right-hand sides. D2a4 records use with sparse/operator-defined general systems; no sparse matrix format is required by the callback. Restart length 30, absolute tolerance 1e-15 and iteration cap 100000 are hardcoded. The module preconditioner must be selected before calling, otherwise it terminates through the error handler. There is no returned convergence flag or residual history; estimated residual exits, breakdown divisions and restart behavior need independent validation. Review covers this implementation, not a guarantee of robustness or the whole parabolic solver.

classifications.notes: RUNGE_KUTTA_STEP advances a spatially discretized one-dimensional linear parabolic problem on the current mesh. The fully implicit route forms an operator-defined coupled stage system and calls native right-preconditioned GMRES. The selected G2 tableau is two-stage Gauss; the source header mentioning only Crank-Nicolson understates the actual method dispatch. Users supply the complete parameter, boundary and spatial operator interfaces. Mesh state and RK tableau must be initialized, U and ROUNDOFF must match the interior mesh size, and ROUNDOFF initially must be zero. local.name: copa
local.description: Serial and OpenMP ensemble Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling in Fortran.

classifications.notes: The README documents affine-invariant sampling, red-black and independent ensemble parallelism and chain storage. Despite Optimization in the expanded name, the reviewed interfaces establish sampling rather than a certified optimization solver.

The serial RUN_SAMPLER implements an affine-invariant ensemble stretch proposal with a companion walker, stretch density proportional to 1/sqrt(z) on [1/2,2], and acceptance factor z**(NDIM-1)*exp(delta log posterior). LOG_PRIOR and LOG_LIKE callbacks supply scalar logs. RANGES initializes walkers only; the callbacks must enforce posterior support thereafter. CHAINS has shape (NDIM,NWALKERS,NSTEPS), LOG_PROBS (NWALKERS,NSTEPS). Require NWALKERS>=2 to avoid the distinct-partner loop hanging and NSTEPS>=10 because progress MOD uses integer NSTEPS/10. The inspected range-shape guard combines tests incorrectly, so the caller must enforce shape (2,NDIM). EVORTRAN supplies the RNG and must be initialized consistently with WP. The routine allocates the whole chain even if output is omitted; no burn-in, autocorrelation or effective-sample-size calculation is performed. This mapping covers the serial implementation, not the separate OpenMP samplers or a verified posterior sample.

Review covers this lasso/median branch, not every SCAD/MCP variant, a statistical selection guarantee or nonsmoothed quantile accuracy. classifications.notes: The README describes Gaussian resampling and NL2SOL-based fitting, with the model supplied by editing routines. It assumes the provided observation errors and resampling model; uncertainty estimates have not been independently validated.

The public BOOTSTRAP workflow reads (x,y,sigma_y) observations, forms residuals (y-model)/sigma_y and invokes NL2SNO twice per fit, using finite-difference Jacobians rather than supplied derivatives. SPARSE_FOUR implements a dense Gaussian sparse-group-lasso path using block updates, separate group/L1 penalties, strong-rule screening and subsequent KKT rechecks. Groups are contiguous intervals described by BS/IX/IY; GAM supplies positive group curvature/step controls and LB/UB bound group coefficients. ALSPARSE splits lambda into L1 and group parts. Unlike a compressed scalar-coefficient path, BETA is dimensioned NVARS by NLAM but only active-group blocks are assigned, so inactive entries must not be interpreted as defined zeros. The native interface also declares JERR INTENT(OUT) and assigns it only on error paths, leaving the success status undefined; initializing a caller variable does not repair that contract. This needs a source fix before trustworthy success-status handling. NALAM/NBETA/ACTIVEGROUP delimit populated path blocks, and nonzero iteration/active-size errors can leave partial results. Review covers the concrete Gaussian update/screening implementation, not logistic/mixed-frequency preprocessing, inference or an assertion that the current native entry is production-ready.

local.name: Timeslab
local.description: Fortran 77 time-series analysis code accompanying H. Joseph Newton's Timeslab book.

classifications.notes: The brief README identifies the author, book and extracted original distribution. Individual estimators, build requirements and modern compiler compatibility need further review; no specific model coverage is inferred solely from the title.

ARCV computes the theoretical autocovariance sequence of a stationary autoregressive model from its coefficients and innovation variance. It converts coefficients to partials to determine lag-zero variance, then rebuilds lower-order coefficient/covariance relations and extends the sequence recursively. These are model-implied covariances, not empirical estimates from observations or a fitted AR model. Timeslab uses X(t)+sum(ALPHA(j)*X(t-j))=innovation; consequently an AR(1) coefficient phi=0.5 is supplied as ALPHA=-0.5. ALPHA is overwritten by the intermediate conversion/reconstruction and should be copied if needed later. IER is nonzero when the partial-recursion stationarity check fails; unit-modulus partials are rejected in code as well as values beyond one. Require positive model order, nonnegative requested lag count, positive innovation variance and adequate output storage. Review covers the covariance recursion and its stationarity helper, not every interactive Timeslab command.

procedures.summary: External default-real theoretical AR autocovariance calculation with overwritten coefficient workspace.
procedures.usage:
external :: arcv
real :: alpha(1),covariances(5),variance
integer :: ier
! Model x(t)=0.5*x(t-1)+innovation, innovation variance one.
alpha=[-0.5]
call arcv(alpha,1,1.0,5,covariances,variance,ier)
if(ier/=0) error stop "stationarity recursion failed"
print *,variance,covariances
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use the pinned default-REAL legacy ABI, not DOUBLE PRECISION arguments. ARCV calls ARPRT; linking the entire interactive ar.F object can also require unrelated Timeslab support symbols, so isolate the reviewed kernels or link the complete package. No covariance sequence, stationarity or accuracy case was run.

classifications.notes: ARPRT implements the backward recursion converting stationary AR coefficients to signed reflection/partial-autocorrelation coefficients. It overwrites ALPHA and checks abs(c)>=1 at each stage before division by 1-c*c. The raw kernel returns Timeslab-signed partials; the public ARPART command negates its output before labeling it partial autocorrelations. The calling sketch includes that same negation and preserves no original coefficients. This computes partials implied by a supplied model, not sample PACF estimation or model-order selection. Near-unit partials can make the recursion ill-conditioned even without a nonzero IER, and invalid model orders are not checked in this kernel. Review covers the transformation and the caller-established sign convention.

The adapted local ZNAUPD implements implicitly restarted Arnoldi reverse communication for a few eigenpairs of a general complex operator. The selected standard mode uses OP=A and B=identity; requests for operator products are returned through IDO and WORKD offsets, followed by ZNEUPD Ritz-value/vector extraction. Saved locals/debug/stat modules also prevent assuming independent concurrent solves. Review covers the adapted driver/state dispatch and extraction interface, not upstream ARPACK validation or the parallel variant. ZNEUPD also declares IPNTR INTENT(OUT) while consuming saved pointer offsets; its extraction contract needs the same persistence review.

CHOLESKY forms a real lower-triangular Cholesky factor by diagonal square roots and column updates, supporting the positive-definite real-symmetric decomposition part of D2b1b. Only the lower triangle of output L is assigned; the upper triangle remains undefined and the optional internal CHECK path nevertheless reads the full array through multiplication. It reads upper-triangle input entries as lower-factor data and assumes symmetry. No factorization or residual was executed.

The public CUTHILL_MCKEE wrapper dispatches supported tetrahedral mesh connectivity to a private reverse Cuthill-McKee bandwidth-reduction path. GENRCM is explicitly PRIVATE, so it is implementation evidence rather than a callable public graph interface. GENRCM visits connected components, chooses pseudo-peripheral roots through ROOT_FIND and reverses degree-ordered breadth-first traversals through RCM. The wrapper overwrites NN or MM connectivity depending on mesh type; the private reduction builds one-based adjacency and applies an inverse permutation. A source-interface defect remains: CUTHILL_MCKEE_REDUCE declares ZN INTENT(IN) but passes it to R8COL_PERMUTE, whose A dummy has no INTENT and is modified in place; the public wrapper also declares Z input-only. Coordinate permutation/discard behavior and intent contracts need correction before use. Review records this implemented path and public interface without certifying a usable mesh-conversion build. For the higher-order/edge/face paths, the local ZNOD scratch array is passed without initialization; its role and coordinate consistency require investigation.

local.name: meshf
local.description: Development-stage basic two-dimensional Delaunay triangulation.

classifications.notes: The README limits current coverage to basic 2D triangulation and partial VTK/Triangle/TetGen format support. Three-dimensional, constrained, refinement and structured-mesh capabilities are explicitly planned rather than implemented.

BOWYER_WATSON2 implements an incremental planar triangulation path: initialize a first triangle plus dummy exterior triangles, locate conflicts, recursively remove cavity triangles, insert new triangles and remove exterior cells. Conflict tests use orientation and circumcircle predicates evaluated in a requested quad-precision kind after converting default-real input coordinates. This is broad computational geometry P because the GAMS taxonomy provides no finer general Delaunay leaf; it is not constrained Delaunay, refinement, 3D meshing or an elliptic-solver-specific domain triangulation claim. The README labels the project as development-stage. INITIALISE_MESH loops until the first three points are positively oriented, but its permutation calls are commented and the loop does not change them: clockwise or collinear initial triples can hang. Require at least three distinct points, a positive first-triangle orientation, initialized mesh counters and sufficient precision-kind support. Fixed absolute predicate tolerance is not exact arithmetic or a scale-invariant degeneracy guarantee.

m%points(:,3)=[0.,1.]; m%points(:,4)=[0.2,0.3]

classifications.notes: The README requires a level-restricted tree and tensor-product Chebyshev samples. It explicitly warns that more complicated periodic and boundary-condition options in legacy poisson8.f are not thoroughly tested in the wrapped environment; timing/accuracy claims were not reproduced.

LBFMM2D wraps the legacy eighth-order adaptive box-code volume-potential solver for a two-dimensional free-space Poisson problem. This is a volume-potential tool with the library kernel normalization, not an arbitrary prescribed-boundary-value interface; the mapping stays at the Poisson/Laplace class without selecting a rectangular Dirichlet/Neumann subclass. Input is a level-restricted quadtree and density values on each leaf box 8-by-8 Chebyshev grid; the active wrapper loops over ND density components and dispatches FMMSTART8_WRAP. The latter hardcodes IPERIOD=0 and allocates/maps legacy FMM tables/workspace. Require NORDER=8, NPBOX=64, IPERIOD=0, positive box counts and a valid tree. The wrapper does not enforce its apparent NORDER/IPERIOD parameters, and TIMEINFO is never assigned; do not infer timing/status outputs from its dummy list. Source-declared IPTR(8) is default INTEGER despite the header calling it INTEGER(8); the converter also contains explicit INTEGER*4 data, so use the compatible default-four-byte integer build rather than blindly promoting all integers. FVALS/POT actually have rank three (ND,NPBOX,NBOXES), unlike the rank-two prose summary. Centers/sizes are normalized by BOXSize(0) without a visible final physical potential rescaling: the selected fragment requires a unit-side root and leaves general physical scaling to separate verification. Only leaf potential entries are within the documented output scope. Review covers wrapper shapes, tree conversion and core dispatch; the author legacy core test is linked as usage context but has not been compiled or run for this catalog, nor has the modern wrapper, near-field behavior or all FMM kernels. The legacy core wrapper reserves 64000*NBOXES entries in each real and integer workspace; check memory capacity and default-integer size arithmetic before using large trees.

classifications.notes: CHEBEXPS with ITYPE=1 constructs Chebyshev-root nodes in ascending order on [-1,1] and weights for unweighted interpolatory quadrature. The degree recurrence accumulates even-Chebyshev moments into the weights, which the caller applies to sampled integrand values. This is fixed-order quadrature for grid data (H2a1b2), not an adaptive callback integrator or the weighted Gauss-Chebyshev measure dx/sqrt(1-x**2). procedures.summary: External legacy Chebyshev-root node and unweighted quadrature-weight construction.
procedures.usage:
! GAMS H2a1b2. Unweighted polynomial quadrature on [-1,1].
program check_cheb_quadrature
  implicit none
  interface
    subroutine chebexps(itype,n,x,u,v,w)
      integer :: itype,n
      real(kind=8) :: x(*),u(n,n),v(n,n),w(*)
    end subroutine
  end interface
  integer,parameter :: orders(4)=[2,4,8,16]
  real(kind=8),allocatable :: x(:),w(:),u(:,:),v(:,:)
  real(kind=8) :: exact,error,maxerr
  integer :: n,i,k,cases
  cases=0; maxerr=0d0
  do i=1,size(orders)
    n=orders(i)
    allocate(x(n),w(n),u(n,n),v(n,n))
    call chebexps(1,n,x,u,v,w)
    if(.not.all(x(2:n)>x(1:n-1)))error stop 'nodes not ascending'
    if(.not.all(abs(x)<1d0))error stop 'nodes outside open interval'
    if(.not.all(w>0d0))error stop 'weights not positive'
    do k=0,n-1
      exact=0d0
      if(mod(k,2)==0)exact=2d0/real(k+1,8)
      error=abs(sum(w*x**k)-exact)
      if(.not.(error<2d-13))error stop 'unweighted polynomial moment failed'
      maxerr=max(maxerr,error); cases=cases+1
    enddo
    deallocate(x,w,u,v)
  enddo
  print '(a,i0)','Polynomial moments checked: ',cases
  print '(a,es12.4)','Maximum absolute moment error: ',maxerr
  print '(a)','PASS Chebyshev-node quadrature: 30 moments and node/weight checks'
end program check_cheb_quadrature

procedures.summary: External legacy Chebyshev nodal/coefficient basis conversion.
procedures.usage:
! Catalog-owned analytic checks of GAMS E3c using CHEBEXPS.
! Upstream source is downloaded at a pinned revision; it is not bundled here.
program basis
 use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
 use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
 implicit none
 integer :: n,k,j,count
 real(real64), allocatable :: x(:),weights(:),u(:,:),v(:,:),a(:,:),d(:,:),w(:),ending(:),values(:),want(:),got(:)
 real(real64) :: error,maximum,endpoint
 real(real64), parameter :: tolerance=2.e-11_real64
 external :: chebexps,chebinmt
 maximum=0
 count=0
 do j=1,4
   n=2**j
   allocate(x(n),weights(n),u(n,n),v(n,n),a(n,n),d(n,n),w(3*n*n+2*n+50), &
      ending(n),values(n),want(n),got(n))
   call chebexps(2,n,x,u,v,weights)
   do k=0,n-1
     values=cos(real(k,real64)*acos(x))
     got=matmul(u,values)
     want=0;want(k+1)=1
     call verify()
     got=matmul(v,want)
     want=values
     call verify()
   end do
   deallocate(x,weights,u,v,a,d,w,ending,values,want,got)
 end do
 print '(a,i0)', 'Checked polynomial cases: ',count
 print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized error: ',maximum
 print '(a)', 'PASS basis'
contains
 subroutine verify()
   if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(got))) error stop 'nonfinite result'
   error=maxval(abs(got-want))/max(1._real64,maxval(abs(want)))
   maximum=max(maximum,error)
   if(error>tolerance) error stop 'analytic polynomial mismatch'
   count=count+1
 end subroutine
end program

classifications.notes: The brief README identifies the currently implemented WENO variant. Reconstruction is a numerical component; no complete time-dependent PDE solver, arbitrary-dimensional WENO family or convergence test is inferred.

The two-dimensional square-stencil path constructs tensor-polynomial reconstruction matrices from cell integrals, solves for ideal sub-stencil coefficients and blends reconstructed point values with WENO-Z smoothness weights and positive/negative coefficient splitting. E2a records reconstruction on a gridded bivariate stencil, scoped to cell-average inputs rather than scattered point interpolation or a complete PDE solver. Initialize the stencil, add evaluation points and compute ideal coefficients before rank-two reconstruct. The inspected inversion helper has INTENT(OUT) IERR but assigns it only on failure; its success return is undefined and is then checked by setup. This must be resolved/validated before relying on the setup status. REAL(16) setup arithmetic and preprocessing limit portability. NDEBUG removes size checks; reconstruction does not return an accuracy estimate or enforce positivity. Other widths/masks, rhombus and one-dimensional paths are excluded. No reconstruction or formal-order test was run.

It warns that poor convergence can violate the intended potential field and boundary values; accuracy is not certified by the nominal discretization order.

NDSM_POISSON::solve_poisson_bvp applies multigrid V cycles to finite-difference Poisson problems on Cartesian rectangular grids. This mapping and local check select two dimensions, uniform equal spacing in both directions and homogeneous Neumann conditions. NDSM_ROOT sets FP to double precision and IT=C_INT64_T; do not pass default-width integers where the interface requires IT. Create MG_HANDLE through new_mg_handle with coordinate vectors and valid hierarchy sizes, set smoothing count, coarse tolerance, boundary selectors and the module DEBUG flag. The constructor floors coarser sizes and can reach one point; choose levels so every active dimension retains at least two points, since setup divides by NQ-1 and stencils read adjacent coordinates. Select zero-mean compatible Neumann data; the generic smoother subtracts the arithmetic solution mean to fix its additive constant. SOLVE_POISSON_BVP returns IERR=0 on its chosen maximum/mean iterate-change tolerance, 1 when the outer cycle budget is exhausted, and DU_LAST is that change metric rather than a PDE residual. Coarse relaxation may print nonconvergence without propagating a distinct outer status; independently check residual and gauge. The selected generic 2-D path uses red/black relaxation, restriction/interpolation and coarse correction; optimized 3-D paths and OpenMP behavior were not checked. A complete serial main program adapted from the BSD-licensed author setup was compiled and run on 17x25 and 33x49 grids. Maximum solution errors were 8.78906e-4 and 2.19727e-4 (ratio 0.25), independently calculated interior residuals below 3.4e-12, and solution means below 1.5e-19. ! GAMS I2b1a1a. Manufactured Neumann problem, following the author test setup.
program check_poisson
  use ndsm_root
  use ndsm_poisson
  implicit none
  real(fp) :: errors(2),residuals(2),gauges(2)
  debug=.false.
  call solve_case(17_it,25_it,3_it,errors(1),residuals(1),gauges(1))
  call solve_case(33_it,49_it,4_it,errors(2),residuals(2),gauges(2))
  if(.not.(errors(2)<0.35_fp*errors(1)))error stop 'refinement did not reduce error by expected order'
  print '(a,es12.4)','Fine/coarse error ratio: ',errors(2)/errors(1)
  print '(a)','PASS Poisson: two grids, analytic error, interior residual and zero-mean gauge'
contains
  subroutine solve_case(nx,ny,ng,error,residual,gauge)
    integer(it),intent(in) :: nx,ny,ng
    real(fp),intent(out) :: error,residual,gauge
    type(mg_ptr) :: mesh(2)
    type(mg_handle) :: bvp
    real(fp),allocatable :: u(:,:),exact(:,:),rhs(:,:)
    real(fp) :: h,x,y,lx,ly,du,stencil
    real(fp),parameter :: a=0.75_fp,b=-0.4_fp
    integer(it) :: nshape(2),nsize,ierr
    integer :: i,j
    nshape=[nx,ny]; nsize=nx*ny; h=1.0_fp/real(nx-1,fp)
    lx=1.0_fp; ly=real(ny-1,fp)*h
    allocate(mesh(1)%val(nx),mesh(2)%val(ny),u(nx,ny),exact(nx,ny),rhs(nx,ny))
    mesh(1)%val=[(real(i-1,fp)*h,i=1,int(nx))]
    mesh(2)%val=[(real(j-1,fp)*h,j=1,int(ny))]
    do j=1,int(ny)
      y=mesh(2)%val(j)
      do i=1,int(nx)
        x=mesh(1)%val(i)
        rhs(i,j)=a*(2*x-lx)+b*(2*y-ly)
        exact(i,j)=a*x*x*(x/3-lx/2)+b*y*y*(y/3-ly/2)
      enddo
    enddo
    exact=exact-sum(exact)/real(nsize,fp)
    call new_mg_handle(bvp,2_it,nshape,ng,mesh,.true.,100000_it)
    bvp%ms=5_it; bvp%ex_tol=1e-13_fp; bvp%copt='N'
    u=0.0_fp
    call solve_poisson_bvp(bvp,nsize,1e-12_fp,256_it,u,rhs,du,ierr)
    if(ierr/=IERR_POISSON_SUCCESS)error stop 'Poisson solver did not report convergence'
    error=maxval(abs(u-exact)); gauge=abs(sum(u)/real(nsize,fp)); residual=0.0_fp
    do j=2,int(ny)-1
      do i=2,int(nx)-1
        stencil=(u(i-1,j)+u(i+1,j)+u(i,j-1)+u(i,j+1)-4*u(i,j))/(h*h)
        residual=max(residual,abs(stencil-rhs(i,j)))
      enddo
    enddo
    if(.not.(error<0.5_fp*h*h))error stop 'analytic solution error too large'
    if(.not.(residual<5e-8_fp))error stop 'independent interior residual too large'
    if(.not.(gauge<1e-11_fp))error stop 'Neumann solution gauge not removed'
    print '(a,2i5,a,3es13.5)','Grid ',nx,ny,' error/residual/mean: ',error,residual,gauge
    call delete_mg_handle(bvp)
  end subroutine
end program check_poisson

classifications.notes: With NDIM=1 this is univariate piecewise-linear interpolation, a degree-one polynomial spline, not a single global high-degree polynomial fit. Seven independent known-value checks cover an affine function at endpoints, a node, an interior point and below the interval, plus a non-affine nodal table with explicitly calculated interpolation and extrapolation values. Maximum error was 1.655814e-16. NDSM_INTERP::ninterp uses adjacent nodes in each coordinate and successively reduces the 2**NDIM corner values with linear weights. Supply strictly increasing coordinates with at least two nodes and uniform spacing within each axis; different axes may have different spacing. FP is the module double-precision kind and IT=C_INT64_T, so all size/shape arguments must use IT. F contains PRODUCT(NSHAPE) samples flattened in Fortran order, with the first coordinate varying fastest. MG_PTR%VAL stores each coordinate vector and may have nondefault bounds. Set NDSM_ROOT DEBUG explicitly. The bracketing helper selects the first/last interval for endpoint or exterior queries; NINTERP discards its IERR and applies the weights without clipping or returning status. Exterior values therefore extrapolate the end cell rather than reporting failure. Assertions can stop on inconsistent dimensions or indexing; no accuracy estimate is returned. High dimension requires exponentially many corner samples. Nonuniform or decreasing coordinates, repeated nodes, and high-dimensional behavior are outside the checked contract. The complete catalog main program and both original module sources were compiled and run locally with GNU Fortran 17.0.0 20260510 (experimental) on Windows, with bounds checks and floating-point traps; tolerance was 5e-13. These finite known-value cases do not establish arbitrary-data accuracy or every extrapolation regime.

procedures.usage:
! Catalog-owned numerical checks; upstream numerical sources are downloaded separately.
program check_linear
  use ndsm_root, only: fp, it, mg_ptr, debug
  use ndsm_interp, only: ninterp
  use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
  implicit none
  integer(it) :: ndim, shape(3), nsize, k, j, index, rem, axis
  integer :: trial, checked
  type(mg_ptr) :: mesh(3)
  real(fp), allocatable :: f(:)
  real(fp) :: q(3), x(3), want, got, err, maximum
  real(fp), parameter :: tol=5.e-13_fp
  debug=.false.
  checked=0
  maximum=0
  do ndim=1_it,1_it
    shape=[4_it,5_it,3_it]
    nsize=product(shape(:ndim))
    do axis=1,ndim
      ! Different spacing per axis; nondefault mesh bounds exercise internal remapping.
      allocate(mesh(axis)%val(-2:shape(axis)-3))
      do j=0,shape(axis)-1
        mesh(axis)%val(j-2)=-0.5_fp*axis+0.25_fp*axis*j
      end do
    end do
    allocate(f(nsize))
    do k=1,nsize
      rem=k-1
      x=0
      do axis=1,ndim
        index=mod(rem,shape(axis)); rem=rem/shape(axis)
        x(axis)=mesh(axis)%val(index-2)
      end do
      f(k)=known(ndim,x)
    end do
    ! Tensor product of endpoint, node, interior and exterior coordinates.
    do trial=0,5**int(ndim)-1
      rem=trial
      q=0
      do axis=1,ndim
        j=mod(rem,5_it); rem=rem/5
        select case(j)
        case(0); q(axis)=mesh(axis)%val(-2)
        case(1); q(axis)=mesh(axis)%val(shape(axis)-3)
        case(2); q(axis)=mesh(axis)%val(-1)
        case(3); q(axis)=mesh(axis)%val(-2)+0.37_fp*axis
        case(4); q(axis)=mesh(axis)%val(-2)-0.1_fp*axis
        end select
      end do
      want=known(ndim,q)
      got=ninterp(ndim,nsize,shape(:ndim),mesh(:ndim),q(:ndim),f)
      if (.not.ieee_is_finite(got)) error stop 'nonfinite interpolation'
      err=abs(got-want)/max(1._fp,abs(want))
      maximum=max(maximum,err)
      if (err>tol) error stop 'interpolation mismatch'
      checked=checked+1
    end do
    ! A non-affine nodal table distinguishes piecewise-linear evaluation from a global fit.
    f=[0.25_fp,0.0625_fp,0._fp,0.0625_fp]
    do trial=1,2
      if(trial==1) then
        q(1)=-0.375_fp; want=0.15625_fp
      else
        q(1)=-0.6_fp; want=0.325_fp
      end if
      got=ninterp(ndim,nsize,shape(:ndim),mesh(:ndim),q(:ndim),f)
      if (.not.ieee_is_finite(got)) error stop 'nonfinite tabular interpolation'
      err=abs(got-want)
      maximum=max(maximum,err)
      if(err>tol) error stop 'piecewise tabular mismatch'
      checked=checked+1
    end do
    deallocate(f)
    do axis=1,ndim
      deallocate(mesh(axis)%val)
    end do
  end do
  print '(a,i0)', 'Known-value checks: ',checked
  print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized error: ',maximum
  print '(a)', 'PASS linear'
contains
  pure function known(n,x) result(y)
    integer(it), intent(in) :: n
    real(fp), intent(in) :: x(3)
    real(fp) :: y
    y=1.25_fp-0.7_fp*x(1)
    if(n>=2) y=y+0.4_fp*x(2)+0.6_fp*x(1)*x(2)
    if(n>=3) y=y-0.3_fp*x(3)+0.2_fp*x(1)*x(3)-0.5_fp*x(2)*x(3)+0.8_fp*x(1)*x(2)*x(3)
  end function
end program

classifications.notes: The brief README identifies a Fortran 90 signal-transform program and these two wavelet families. Normalization conventions, boundary treatment and numerical accuracy need source/example review; other wavelet families are not inferred.

The inspected program evaluates Morlet or Mexican-hat kernels at each integer scale and translation, multiplies by sampled signal and applies a trapezoidal weighted sum before writing coefficient magnitudes. This is a direct demonstrative continuous-wavelet-transform implementation, kept in the verified broad integral-transform class J rather than inventing a finer wavelet code. Quadrature omits time-step factors, translations use sample indices rather than input times, and the Morlet path uses default COMPLEX even though times are real(kind=8). File/allocation controls are not robustly validated; a malformed input can STOP the process.

classifications.notes: The short README is supplemented by Runge-Kutta interface comments describing caller-supplied right-hand sides and time stepping. Detailed assimilation algorithms, order claims and numerical results have not been independently verified.

The public RK4 routine implements one classical explicit four-stage Runge-Kutta step for a vector initial-value problem. It calls RHS at the standard starting, midpoint and endpoint stages and forms the weighted increment in a separate output vector. The actual callback signature is RHS(N,T,X,DXDT), including N, despite comments omitting that leading argument. DP is KIND(0D0) from TYPES. The caller owns the time loop, step choice, output scheduling and stability/error assessment; no adaptive control, embedded estimate, rejection, event location or convergence status is provided. This review selects the RK4 implementation rather than endorsing all other order-named routines or a particular dynamical-system model.

classifications.notes: The public AKIMA generic computes regularized Akima slopes and evaluates piecewise cubic Hermite interpolation for scalar or vector queries. EVLAK locates an interval and evaluates the native Hermite formula; outside the data interval it continues the nearest interval polynomial. Supply matching arrays with at least three distinct strictly increasing abscissae: DAKIMA reads the third sample before its later N=2 return, so two-point input is unsafe. The slope rule includes an epsilon proportional to the abscissa span; it is not an unconditional monotonicity/shape-preserving guarantee. EVLAK saves its interval index between calls and clamps it to N rather than N-1, which can leave an invalid last interval when changing datasets/lengths. Concurrent calls and reuse with varying grids need review. This is univariate piecewise-polynomial interpolation, not a global polynomial fit or quadrature.

classifications.notes: Location mapping: arithmetic and weighted means; AVEVAR also supplies a mean. The shared driver additionally checks sample variance under the separate L1a1b mapping. The public math::mean and avevar compute descriptive location/dispersion statistics. Unweighted mean uses SUM(A)/N; optional weights select DOT_PRODUCT(W,A)/SUM(W), despite a comment suggesting division by N. AVEVAR first computes the mean, accumulates squared deviations and their residual sum, and returns (SUM((A-AVE)**2)-SUM(A-AVE)**2/N)/(N-1), a corrected sample variance. DP=KIND(0D0). Empty input returns the module NaN; singleton AVEVAR divides by zero. Weight sizes, finite values and nonzero weight sum are not validated; signed weights are accepted mechanically. There is no missing-data policy, error estimate or negative-variance clamp. The checked contract is N>=2, ordinary finite arithmetic progressions and positive conforming weights. A complete main checks N=2..20, offsets 0 and 10, steps .25, 1 and 4 (114 cases), using closed-form mean, sample variance and weighted mean for W(I)=I. All outputs were finite and normalized errors <=2e-12; maximum 2.197555e-16. Huge offsets, cancellation, signed/zero-total weights, singleton/empty paths and overflow remain unchecked. Complete main compiled and run locally on Windows with GNU Fortran 17.0.0 20260510 (experimental), 2026-11-06. Unmodified types/constants/utils/math modules use -fno-range-check -O0 -g -Wall -Wextra -ffree-line-length-none -fcheck=all -ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow; main uses the same flags except -fno-range-check. The extra module flag accommodates constants.f90 zero-division NaN/infinity parameter initializers and is not a portability claim. Hashes, flags, warnings and successful results are under drivers/system-dynamics-math/. Only the named routines were executed; previous RK4/Akima source reviews are unchanged. Numerical Recipes notices in AVEVAR and eigen helpers leave component licensing unresolved; no upstream numerical source is bundled.

program statistics
  use types, only: dp
  use math, only: mean,avevar
  use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
  implicit none
  integer :: n,i,io,is,count
  real(dp) :: offset,step,a,v,m,wmean,expected_mean,expected_var,expected_weighted,e,maximum
  real(dp), allocatable :: x(:),w(:)
  maximum=0;count=0

procedures.summary: Public covariance eigensystem with descending eigenvalues. Negative eigenvalues are clipped and RANK uses exact-zero counting; no convergence status is returned. Intended for positive-semidefinite inputs only.
procedures.usage:
program covariance_eigen
  use types, only: dp
  use math, only: eigencov
  use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_is_finite
  implicit none
  integer :: n,i,j,k,family,iscale,rank,cases
  real(dp) :: scale,norma,residual,orthogonality,trace_error,maxres,maxorth,maxtrace
  real(dp), allocatable :: a(:,:),p(:,:),u(:,:),d(:),gram(:,:),v(:)
  maxres=0;maxorth=0;maxtrace=0;cases=0
  do n=1,8
    allocate(a(n,n),p(n,n),u(n,n),d(n),gram(n,n),v(n))
    do family=1,4
      a=0
      select case(family)
      case(1)
        do i=1,n
          a(i,i)=real(i,dp)
        end do
      case(2)
        v=[(real(i,dp)/n,i=1,n)]
        do i=1,n
          a(:,i)=v*v(i)
        end do
      case(3)
        do i=1,n
          do j=1,n
            a(i,j)=0.5_dp**abs(i-j)
          end do
        end do
      case(4)
        do i=1,n
          do j=1,n
            gram(i,j)=sin(real(i+2*j,dp))
          end do
        end do
        a=matmul(transpose(gram),gram)
        do i=1,n
          a(i,i)=a(i,i)+0.25_dp
        end do
      end select
      do iscale=-1,1
        scale=10.0_dp**(8*iscale);p=scale*a
        call eigencov(n,p,u,d,rank,.false.)
        if(.not.all(ieee_is_finite(u)).or..not.all(ieee_is_finite(d)))error stop 'Nonfinite eigensystem'
        if(any(p/=scale*a))error stop 'Input covariance changed'
        if(any(d<0).or.rank/=count(d/=0))error stop 'Rank/nonnegative convention mismatch'
        if(any(d(1:n-1)<d(2:n)))error stop 'Eigenvalues not descending'
        norma=maxval(sum(abs(scale*a),dim=2))
        residual=0
        do k=1,n
          residual=max(residual,maxval(abs(matmul(scale*a,u(:,k))-d(k)*u(:,k)))/norma)
        end do
        gram=matmul(transpose(u),u)
        do i=1,n
          gram(i,i)=gram(i,i)-1
        end do
        orthogonality=maxval(abs(gram))
        trace_error=abs(sum(d)-sum([(scale*a(i,i),i=1,n)]))/norma
        if(max(residual,orthogonality,trace_error)>2e-11_dp)error stop 'Eigensystem invariant failed'
        if(family==1)then
          if(maxval(abs(d-[(scale*real(n-i+1,dp),i=1,n)]))/norma>2e-11_dp)error stop 'Diagonal spectrum mismatch'
        end if
        maxres=max(maxres,residual);maxorth=max(maxorth,orthogonality);maxtrace=max(maxtrace,trace_error)
        cases=cases+1
      end do
    end do
    deallocate(a,p,u,d,gram,v)
  end do
  print '(a,i0)', 'Positive-semidefinite eigensystem cases: ',cases
  print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized eigenpair residual: ',maxres
  print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum orthogonality error: ',maxorth
  print '(a,es14.6)', 'Maximum normalized trace error: ',maxtrace
  print '(a)', 'PASS covariance_eigen'
end program

local.name: Fortran Variable Transformation
local.description: Yeo-Johnson and Box-Cox variable transformations with parameter fitting.

classifications.notes: The README identifies pure transformation functions and golden-section maximum-likelihood parameter estimation. Valid input domains, likelihood assumptions and handling of degenerate data are not independently checked.

The module provides fixed-lambda Yeo-Johnson and Box-Cox transformations plus lambda selectors using golden-section maximization on [-3,3] with tolerance 0.001. This supports transformation selection, but it is not a validated maximum-likelihood estimator: both internal objectives compute sqrt(sample variance) into var_z. In the Yeo-Johnson objective, -0.5*n*log(var_z) therefore weights log standard deviation by half the usual coefficient relative to the unchanged Jacobian term, changing the optimization criterion. In the Box-Cox selector the geometric-mean scaling absorbs the Jacobian and the same factor is an overall positive likelihood scaling, which by itself leaves the maximizing lambda unchanged. The Box-Cox selector also computes log(x) before any positivity shift, unlike box_cox_lambda which shifts a nonpositive dataset by 1-min(x). Constant/short data, nonpositive selector inputs, overflow, near-zero cancellation and convergence/global optimality are not guarded. The sketch deliberately uses fixed lambdas and does not recommend the Yeo-Johnson selector without objective correction and validation; the Box-Cox selector still requires strictly positive data.

The reviewed Fortran type-bound PREDICT_ONE entries evaluate previously trained nonlinear regression models: a neural network uses dense affine layers and activation callbacks, a decision tree follows feature-threshold comparisons, and a random forest averages tree outputs. Restrict regression sketches to compatible validated models/activations (e.g. identity output); do not infer classification probabilities or current scikit-learn compatibility. local.name: Differential Evolution F95

classifications.notes: The README identifies DE/rand/1/bin with dithering and reports early grid locking for the example. Suggested larger populations or ad hoc perturbations are upstream workarounds, not independently established reliability or global convergence.

DIFF_EVOL implements a stochastic differential-evolution search using mutation, binomial-style crossover, greedy selection and optional population perturbation. It calls the module-specific Griewank OBJ_FTN directly rather than accepting an objective callback. Lower/upper bounds initialize/reinitialize the population but do not constrain later mutation trials. Source findings: donor rejection uses AND rather than OR, so indices need not be distinct/exclude the target; the forced crossover coordinate can be NOP+1; BH_BEST is assigned only after improvement over the initial minimum and can remain undefined. G2i records the intended global-search method, not a guarantee of a global solution, correct bounded DE, or fitness for production use. The fixed generation/progress logic prints each generation and exposes no status or evaluation count.

local.name: Minimization course program
local.description: Educational multivariate minimization using steepest descent and conjugate gradients.

classifications.notes: The README describes configurable test functions, finite-difference derivatives and optional gnuplot output. Its suggestion that ever-smaller derivative steps improve accuracy is not treated as a floating-point guarantee; convergence and default example behavior were not checked.

Steep repeatedly estimates a gradient by central differences of the selected source-defined objective and takes a negative-gradient step. A fixed config gamma is used when nonzero; zero selects a secant-based step update. G1b1a records smooth unconstrained minimization without user-supplied derivatives: the internal finite differences do not make it a derivative-supplied API. The objective is edited in MatFunction or RastriginFunction rather than passed as a callback. Source findings include copying uninitialized gradient into gradientOld on the first iteration, pointer targets repeatedly allocated without release in CalculateGradient, and an unguarded denominator in adaptive gamma. It stops on coordinate change/iteration limit but prints the same convergence message in either case, with no returned optimizer/status. The conjugate module freezes one Hessian and is outside this nonlinear-minimizer claim. No minimization was run.

procedures.summary: Public module subroutine consuming ConfigType. Prints the final vector and overwrites Vectors.txt; no solution/status argument. The sketch uses the two-variable default objective and fixed positive gamma, but does not repair the recorded initialization/allocation findings.

use ConfigHandler, only: ConfigType
use SteepestDescent, only: Steep
type(ConfigType) :: config
config%order=2; config%x1=[0.0d0,0.0d0]
config%mode="default"; config%direction="min"; config%list="off"
config%gamma=0.01d0; config%convergeLimit=1.0d-6; config%iterationmax=100
call Steep(config)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Build ConfigHandler, objective modules and GradientCalculator before SteepestDescent. Resolve the first-iteration undefined gradient copy and pointer lifecycle before treating this as a checked driver. Fixed gamma avoids the adaptive-step division but does not certify descent/convergence. Output says convergence even at the limit; verify results independently.

classifications.notes: CalculateGradient perturbs each component by a fixed h=0.0000001 and forms (f(x+h e_i)-f(x-h e_i))/(2h), using a source-defined default or Rastrigin objective. H1 records first numerical derivatives, not automatic differentiation or user-provided gradients. The separate config h does not control this routine; it is used by the Hessian routine instead. Inputs and outputs are POINTER arrays, and the routine allocates a new gradient and scratch x without releasing their previous targets. The default objective accesses two components, so use two-dimensional input for the sketch. Unknown modes leave gradient unassigned. No truncation/roundoff error estimate or step-size study was executed.

local.description: Arbitrary-precision FC-Gram tables for periodic continuation of sampled data.

classifications.notes: The README documents MPFUN-Fort or MPFUN-MPFR, configurable precision and optional blend-to-zero operators. This constructs continuation tables/operators rather than a standalone general FFT implementation; timings and accuracy remain unverified.

The public MPRQR routine computes a square real arbitrary-precision QR factorization using classical Gram-Schmidt: projection coefficients are formed against the original current column, then the combined projection is subtracted and the result normalized. There is no reorthogonalization, pivoting, numerical-rank test or status output; a zero/dependent column can cause division by zero. Nonsquare input terminates with STOP. MPFUN MP_REAL arithmetic is used throughout. This maps the inspected table-generation support kernel to QR factorization, not all of FC-Gram continuation or a rank-revealing least-squares solver. Review covers the full small QR kernel and its matrix-vector helper.

use mpmodule

type(mp_real) :: a(2,2),q(2,2),r(2,2)
a(1,1)=mpreal("1."); a(2,1)=mpreal("1.")
a(1,2)=mpreal("0."); a(2,2)=mpreal("1.")
call mprqr(a,q,r)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Build MPFUN and the module with one consistent configured precision/backend. Supply a nonempty full-rank square matrix and inspect orthogonality/reconstruction independently. Arbitrary precision does not remove rank failure or classical Gram-Schmidt sensitivity. No factorization or numerical-rank case was run.

classifications.notes: The public MPRSVDPLAN type exposes initialization, a fixed number of one-sided Jacobi sweeps, normalization into singular values/vectors, and cleanup. Pairwise column inner products determine rotations that update U and V; TO_SVD takes column norms, normalizes retained columns and zeros singular values below EIGENMIN. Singular values are not explicitly sorted. The stored V is accumulated as right-vector columns, with A=U*diag(sigma)*transpose(V) after sufficient orthogonalization. Sweep topology requires an even column count; this sketch uses four columns and a tall/full-rank matrix. ITERATE performs the requested sweep count without a convergence flag; its first progress-rate print divides by the initial zero step count and needs repair before use with invalid/divide-by-zero traps. Rank truncation, fixed precision and fixed sweeps are user controls rather than accuracy certification. Review covers initialization, rotation/normalization and cleanup, not all continuation operators or least-squares solve modes.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound fixed-sweep one-sided Jacobi iteration; initialize and normalize through the same plan.
procedures.signature:
CALL plan%init_plan(A,EIGENMIN,EPS)
CALL plan%iterate(ITERS)
CALL plan%to_svd()
CALL plan%destroy_plan()
procedures.usage:
use mpmodule
use mprlinalg, only: MPRSVDPLAN
type(MPRSVDPLAN) :: plan
type(mp_real) :: a(4,4)
integer :: i
a=mpreal("0.")
do i=1,4
 a(i,i)=i*mpreal("1.")
end do
call plan%init_plan(a,eigenmin=mpreal("1.e-40"),eps=mpreal("1.e-30"))
call plan%iterate(20)
call plan%to_svd()
! Inspect PLAN%U, PLAN%SIGMA and PLAN%V; preserve A for residual checks.
call plan%destroy_plan()
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use an even column count and compatible MPFUN precision; fix the first progress-print division before enabling arithmetic traps. Fixed sweeps are not proof of convergence, singular values are unsorted, and discarded columns are zeroed rather than completed to an orthogonal basis. No SVD, rank-truncation or residual result was tested.

classifications.notes: The README gives only broad space-application scope and a build.sh entry point. The interpolation module comments identify linear, Hermite, Lagrange and Chebyshev methods; this review does not establish complete orbit propagation or validate astronomical conventions.

LAGRANGE_INTERPOLATION evaluates a global degree-at-most-N-1 polynomial through explicit products of cardinal basis factors and a weighted sum. It is not piecewise interpolation, a spline or an adaptive stencil. Require N>=1, finite data and distinct abscissae; no denominator/duplicate-node or conditioning checks protect the O(N**2) product formula. Module-global error control can return early with Y unassigned when an earlier error is pending. This mapping is the scalar interpolation component, not orbital/ephemeris modeling or a numerical stability guarantee for high-degree/equispaced grids.

classifications.notes: TRIGONOMETRIC_INTERPOLATION sums cardinal products sin((x-xk)/2)/sin((xi-xk)/2). For an odd number N of distinct nodes modulo 2*pi, these products lie in an integer-frequency trigonometric polynomial space. The comments advertise arbitrary N, but even N gives N-1 odd half-angle factors and anti-periodic rather than generally 2*pi-periodic basis functions; this review does not certify that path as a conventional periodic interpolant. Duplicate nodes modulo 2*pi cause zero denominators. The sketch selects three radian nodes. local.name: MEPACK
local.description: Dense Sylvester, Lyapunov, Stein and related matrix-equation solvers.

classifications.notes: The README enumerates standard, generalized and coupled equations, triangular substitution variants and iterative refinement. Hardware-dependent block tuning and perturbed Schur decompositions affect use; no accuracy or performance results were reproduced.

DLA_GELYAP reduces a real coefficient matrix to Schur form when needed, transforms a symmetric right-hand side, dispatches a triangular Lyapunov solver and transforms the solution back. DLA_GESYLV performs the two-matrix Schur/transformation analogue for op(A)*X +/- X*op(B)=SCALE*Y. D8 is the GAMS matrix-equation leaf, covering these standard Lyapunov/Sylvester drivers, not generalized/Stein/refinement variants. FACT selectors distinguish general, Hessenberg and already-factored matrices; Schur factors overwrite A/B. Workspace query uses LDWORK=-1 and returns the required integer length in LDWORK itself, not WORK(1). Initialize INFO before calling because it is read on entry. Preserve and interpret SCALE and inspect INFO before treating X as a solution; internal failure can return before the back transformation. Library-global solver/blocksize options are consulted; lower-level kernels and all solver modes are not fully audited. No matrix equation or residual was run.

procedures.summary: External DOUBLE PRECISION standard Lyapunov driver. FACT/TRANS are one-character selectors, X contains symmetric RHS on input and solution on successful output, A/Q store the Schur form/vectors. Query/reuse LDWORK as an INTEGER INOUT length.
procedures.signature:
CALL DLA_GELYAP(FACT, TRANS, M, A, LDA, Q, LDQ, X, LDX, &
                SCALE, WORK, LDWORK, INFO)
procedures.usage:
integer, parameter :: n=2
integer :: ldwork,info
double precision :: a(n,n),q(n,n),x(n,n),scale,query(1)
double precision,allocatable :: work(:)
a=0d0; a(1,1)=-1d0; a(2,2)=-2d0
q=0d0; q(1,1)=1d0; q(2,2)=1d0
x=0d0; x(1,1)=1d0; x(2,2)=1d0
info=0; ldwork=-1
call dla_gelyap("F","N",n,a,n,q,n,x,n,scale,query,ldwork,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "workspace query failed"
allocate(work(ldwork)); info=0
call dla_gelyap("F","N",n,a,n,q,n,x,n,scale,work,ldwork,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "Lyapunov solve failed"
! Check A0*X + X*transpose(A0) - SCALE*Y0 independently.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use a configured/initialized complete MEPACK build with compatible BLAS/LAPACK and its options modules. local.name: monolis
local.description: Real and complex iterative linear-system solver interfaces.

classifications.notes: The brief README is supplemented by the solver module interface and comments, including real/complex right-hand sides, solution vectors and method dispatch. This supports a broad linear-system mapping, not independent verification of every solver, preconditioner or accelerator path.

The public MONOLIS_SOLVE_R wrapper copies the RHS and initial guess into assembled matrix storage, dispatches preconditioned conjugate gradients for a real sparse symmetric positive-definite system through the configured method selector, then retrieves X and updates halo values. The inspected recurrence uses sparse products, preconditioner applications and communicator-aware inner products, with periodic explicit residual recomputation. The caller must prepare the sparse/block pattern, values, DOF layout, communication tables, preconditioner/control state and compatible vector extents. CG requires an SPD operator and appropriate SPD preconditioner; BiCGSTAB has possible recurrence breakdowns and is not a universal nonsymmetric convergence guarantee. Query the parameter error/convergence records rather than treating return of X as success. This review covers the selected real CPU algorithm path, not all accelerator, variable-block, distributed partition, factorization or complex branches.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes backend libraries, matrix formats and analysis/factorization reuse. Its configuration is motivated by shared-memory lubrication applications and uses sequential MUMPS; a wrapper does not independently implement or validate each backend algorithm.

SOLVE_SYST dispatches initialization, analysis, numerical factorization, solution and cleanup for real sparse general systems through MA48, SuperLU, MUMPS or UMFPACK wrappers. The selected UMFP path passes compressed-column pointers/row indices/values to symbolic and numeric factorization and solves A*x=b, with iterative refinement explicitly disabled. local.name: PaScaL TDMA
local.description: Batched distributed tridiagonal solves with CUDA Fortran and CUDA C++ implementations.

classifications.notes: The README documents rank-local reduction, reduced-system exchange/solve and reconstruction, with a single-rank Thomas path. It distinguishes the published Fortran implementation from later C++ extensions; performance is hardware/problem dependent and was not measured here.

PASCAL_SOLVER solves batches of real tridiagonal systems using CUDA Fortran device arrays, with one system per GPU thread in the single-rank Thomas path. The multi-rank dispatcher reduces each local row segment to two interface rows, redistributes and solves reduced systems using CUDA-aware MPI, then reconstructs each local solution. A/B/C are lower/main/upper diagonals and D is overwritten by solutions; C is destroyed even on the single-rank path, and A is also changed on the distributed path. No pivoting or caller-visible numerical INFO is supplied, so matrices must avoid zero/unstable elimination pivots. Public plan creation and cleanup bracket repeated solves. Distributed calls require compatible system counts/decomposition and at least two local rows, with CUDA-aware MPI rather than a host-staging fallback. The sketch uses only one rank, while the evidence records distributed dispatch without claiming a tested parallel solve. This is a general real tridiagonal mapping, not an SPD-only or cyclic solver claim.

procedures.summary: Public CUDA Fortran batch tridiagonal solver using reusable MPI/GPU plan state.
procedures.usage:
use mpi
use cudafor
use PaScaL_TDMA_cuda, only: ptdma_plan_cuda,pascal_plan_create,pascal_solver,pascal_plan_clean
type(ptdma_plan_cuda) :: plan
integer :: rank,nranks,ierr,istat
real(8),device :: a(0:1,0:3),b(0:1,0:3),c(0:1,0:3),d(0:1,0:3)
real(8) :: solution(0:1,0:3)
call MPI_Init(ierr)
call MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD,rank,ierr)
call MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD,nranks,ierr)
! Launch this sketch with one MPI rank and a visible GPU.
if(nranks/=1) error stop "single-rank sketch"
istat=cudaSetDevice(0)
if(istat/=0) error stop "device selection failed"
a=-1d0; b=4d0; c=-1d0; d=2d0
a(:,0)=0d0; c(:,3)=0d0; d(:,0)=3d0; d(:,3)=3d0
call pascal_plan_create(plan,2,MPI_COMM_WORLD,rank,nranks,32,32)
call pascal_solver(plan,a,b,c,d,2,4)
istat=cudaDeviceSynchronize()
if(istat/=0) error stop "GPU solve failed"
solution=d
call pascal_plan_clean(plan)
call MPI_Finalize(ierr)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Requires NVIDIA CUDA Fortran, compatible GPU/runtime and MPI modules. A/B/C/D follow the exact zero-based system-first layout. Preserve coefficients/RHS and check a residual independently; the solver has no pivot/status guarantee. Restore destroyed coefficients before reusing a plan. No serial or distributed solve, pivot case or timing was tested.
