local.name: PCG Coarray
local.description: Coarray Fortran Chebyshev, CG, preconditioned CG and flexible PCG solvers.

classifications.notes: The README documents object-based matrix/preconditioner interfaces, CRS and matrix-free examples, libsparse and MKL dependencies. Historical compiler tests are upstream reports; current coarray runtime compatibility and numerical convergence were not checked.

The cg binding computes a real conjugate-gradient recurrence with distributed row products, global dot-product reductions and gathered search directions for an assumed symmetric positive-definite operator. D2b1b records that ordinary CG system-solve scope; no nonsymmetric or indefinite support is inferred. Matrix input can be a compatible crssparse object or gen_coeff extension. x is a replicated global-length coarray; only owned rows are updated and the full solution is assembled on image 1 at the end. Initial x is required zero, but the source tests SUM(x)==0 rather than every entry. RHS is read from a binary stream file with integer header. Stopping adds image-local Euclidean norms, not the square root of globally summed squares; zero RHS and curvature breakdown are unguarded. getlargeeigenvalue receives MINVAL, and last-image scratch is O(maxit**2). No coarray solve, speed or convergence check was run.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound CG solve. Constructor cg(neq) takes global INT32 equation count. startrow/endrow are scalar INT32 coarrays; x is REAL64(:)[*]; crhs is a filename. gen_coeff%multbyv supplies the row-restricted product for a user-defined matrix operator.

use iso_fortran_env, only: int32,real64

solver=cg(neq)
call solver%setmaxiterations(100_int32)
call solver%setthreshold(1.0e-8_real64)
x=0.0_real64
call solver%solve(matrix,x,rhs_filename,startrow,endrow)

local.name: PFLARE
local.description: PETSc extensions for parallel asymmetric linear systems and reduction multigrid.

classifications.notes: GitHub resolves the listed address to PFLAREProject/PFLARE. The README documents approximate inverses, AIR-family multigrids, splittings and Fortran/C/Python interfaces; scalability and GPU capabilities are upstream claims, not catalog benchmarks.

PFLARE supplies approximate-ideal-restriction multigrid and related preconditioners for PETSc sparse-system solves; it is not a complete replacement for the outer PETSc KSP solver. The public Fortran PCRegister_PFLARE entry registers air and pflareinv types. Selecting air on a PETSc KSP PC constructs a Fortran shell, builds the hierarchy through setup_air_pcmg and applies its underlying PETSc PCMG object. The selected usage assumes an initialized compatible real-scalar PETSc/MPI build, an assembled square host AIJ nonsymmetric A, compatible distributed vectors and a separately chosen outer Krylov method. Call registration before selecting the type when using this explicit path, check each PETSc ierr and KSP converged reason, then independently evaluate the unpreconditioned residual. Registration has no ierr dummy. Options choose strength splitting, transfer operators, approximate inverses, smoothers and coarse solves; this review traces registration/setup/application dispatch and does not certify every numerical method, GPU path, convergence rate, complex-scalar build or preconditioner reuse policy.

local.name: PROPACK
local.description: Lanczos bidiagonalization for singular values and vectors of large sparse or structured matrices.

classifications.notes: The distribution README documents partial reorthogonalization and restarted/nonrestarted variants. Their memory/convergence tradeoffs and dated platform configurations are recorded as documentation, not verified current compiler or performance results.

The nonrestarted real DLANSVD driver dispatches Lanczos bidiagonalization with partial reorthogonalization, solves the projected bidiagonal SVD, refines Ritz error estimates and extends the Krylov space until requested singular triplets converge or the space is exhausted. APROD must supply both A*x and A-transpose*x. Singular-vector reconstruction is dispatched only on the driver completion conditions. K is overwritten with the number obtained, and INFO distinguishes ordinary completion, smaller invariant subspace and failed convergence. Caller workspace, callback correctness and options are essential; the few scalar guards are not a complete input validator. LAPINFO from the bidiagonal solver is not propagated as a checked caller status in the inspected path. No callback, singular triplet or numerical error bound was verified by execution; restarted/complex variants remain unreviewed.

local.name: PSFUN
local.description: Distributed sparse matrix-function vector products built around PSBLAS.

classifications.notes: The README describes products f(A)x for large sparse matrices and explicitly warns that the library is under active development with no releases. Individual supported functions, algorithms and numerical behavior need further review.

PSFUN_D_ARNOLDI approximates a distributed sparse matrix-function action y=f(alpha*A)*x by building an Arnoldi Krylov basis, evaluating the small Hessenberg matrix function through PSFUN_D_SERIAL, and projecting back. The default serial function object selects EXP/EXPOKIT. This is broader matrix-function linear algebra, not merely ordinary matrix-vector multiplication or an explicitly supplied matrix polynomial; the retained class D avoids an unsupported narrower leaf. EPS/ISTOP select estimated stopping behavior, not a certified normwise error bound. The implementation normalizes by the input norm and Arnoldi subdiagonal without a visible zero-input/happy-breakdown guard; projected dimensions and final accumulation require numerical validation. The routine temporarily changes FUN scaling and has a shared error-handler path. Review covers the Arnoldi path, public interface and serial dispatch, not every serial function or rational/Lanczos variant.

PSMMA_TOEPLITZ computes a distributed dense-by-Toeplitz product Q=alpha*A*H+beta*Q from replicated Toeplitz generators and block-cyclic matrix data. The native core circulates local panels with BLACS, constructs needed Toeplitz blocks and uses dense products or RRQR-compressed block products. Despite an older wrapper comment saying low-rank work is not implemented, the inspected core does call ConstToeplitzlowrank and Compress_RRQR. This can therefore be an approximate product, not an exact-structure FFT convolution or an eigensolver. The sketch restricts N=K, full generators LDB=2*K-1, equal descriptor row/column block sizes, origin submatrices and REDIST=false. These avoid extrapolating from unverified symmetric-short-generator, submatrix-offset or redistribution layouts. No INFO is returned; allocation/backend failures can print and return, and internal compression tolerance is not a user-requested product error bound. Review covers wrapper, panel multiplication and low-rank construction/compression dispatch, not parallel scaling or all descriptor combinations.

procedures.summary: External MPI/BLACS block-cyclic matrix product with a replicated Toeplitz generator.
procedures.usage:
external :: psmma_toeplitz
! After MPI/BLACS setup: square N-by-N distributed A and Q, compatible
! DESCA/DESCQ with equal row/column blocks and source process (0,0).
! B(1:2*N-1) is replicated; H(i,j)=B(N+j-i).
! WORK is DOUBLE PRECISION and sized for the local-panel algorithm;
! follow the author driver for the actual grid, block sizes and local extents.
call psmma_toeplitz(n,n,1d0,a,1,1,desca,b,2*n-1, &
 0d0,q,1,1,descq,work,.false.)
! No status is returned; compare with an independently formed A*H.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Restricted post-allocation collective fragment, requiring the complete package and MPI/BLACS/ScaLAPACK/BLAS/RRQR dependencies. Retain full generators even for a symmetric Toeplitz matrix. The author local workspace allocation is an example, not a universal size query. No product, compression tolerance or distributed run was tested.

local.name: qrupdate-ng
local.description: Fast QR, Cholesky and LU factorization updates and downdates.

classifications.notes: The README lists rank-one updates and row/column insertion/deletion/shift operations, with different restrictions by factorization. It explicitly distinguishes pivoted and unpivoted LU stability; not every update operation applies to every stored factorization.

DQR1UP updates an existing real QR factorization after A -> A+u*v-transpose. It forms Q-transpose*u, applies Givens rotations to factors, updates the leading row and retriangularizes; the economy branch additionally handles the component orthogonal to the basis and dispatches a Cholesky update. This is decomposition updating, not a fresh QR factorizer or a linear solver. Inputs must already form a valid full/economy factorization. Q/R and V are overwritten, U can be destroyed in economy form, and WORK needs 2*K elements. Invalid scalar dimensions go through QRUPDATE_XERROR; no status dummy is returned. Review covers this driver/rotation dispatch, not every helper, downdate or complex variant.

procedures.summary: External real64 subroutine. Q is M-by-K, R K-by-N, with K=M (full) or K=N<M (economy). LDQ>=M and LDR>=K; U(M), V(N), W(2*K). Match the library default-integer/BLAS ABI. Configure error handling if process termination by the default handler is unsuitable.

real(real64) :: q(2,2),r(2,2),u(2),v(2),work(4)

u=[1.0_real64,0.5_real64]; v=[0.25_real64,1.0_real64]

The fragment uses the full-factor branch; economy completion was inspected only at dispatch level. Check reconstruction and Q orthogonality independently; no error bound or runtime result is asserted.

These are collective ScaLAPACK Fortran drivers, not serial LAPACK calls with larger arrays. Initialize MPI/BLACS, put all participating ranks in the same valid process grid, construct consistent nine-integer type-1 block-cyclic descriptors and distribute the local column-major arrays with adequate local leading dimensions. Global indices are one-based; descriptors include global sizes, block sizes, source ranks and BLACS context, not a global matrix replicated at every rank. Match DOUBLE PRECISION/COMPLEX*16 and INTEGER ABI across ScaLAPACK, BLACS, PBLAS, BLAS/LAPACK and the caller, including any ILP64 choice. Selected sketches use full matrices at global origin (1,1), square blocks and compatible layouts; they omit the required distribution/setup and are not runnable standalone drivers. Negative INFO can encode a descriptor entry as -(argument*100+entry), and PXERBLA handling may abort rather than just return. The selected real general square-system driver factors A with partial-pivoted LU, then calls the corresponding GETRS only after successful factorization. Local A stores factors, B is overwritten by the distributed solution, and local IPIV must accommodate LOCr(M_A)+MB_A entries and remain tied to A. Require block-aligned origin, square A blocks, matching A/B row block size and owning process row, and a common context. Positive INFO identifies an exactly zero U diagonal in the global submatrix, not a condition estimate or forward-error bound. The review covers driver checks and factor/solve dispatch rather than every distributed LU/communication kernel.

Negative INFO can encode a descriptor entry as -(argument*100+entry), and PXERBLA handling may abort rather than just return. PDTRTRS applies a distributed triangular solve through PDTRSM, selecting upper/lower, transpose and unit/nonunit diagonal conventions. The selected sketch uses lower, nontransposed, unit-diagonal input; diagonal entries are then implicit ones. A remains a triangular coefficient matrix and B is overwritten. Require matching block-aligned origins, square A blocks and compatible B row distribution. Important nonunit-path finding: the diagonal scan sets LL=IOFFA+LDA+1 repeatedly instead of advancing LL, so for blocks longer than two it can miss later zero diagonals. Do not rely on that scan as a complete nonsingularity check; repair it or validate diagonals independently before nonunit use. The unit-diagonal sketch bypasses the defective scan and does not establish numerical conditioning.

classifications.notes: These are collective ScaLAPACK Fortran drivers, not serial LAPACK calls with larger arrays. Initialize MPI/BLACS, put all participating ranks in the same valid process grid, construct consistent nine-integer type-1 block-cyclic descriptors and distribute the local column-major arrays with adequate local leading dimensions. Global indices are one-based; descriptors include global sizes, block sizes, source ranks and BLACS context, not a global matrix replicated at every rank. Match DOUBLE PRECISION/COMPLEX*16 and INTEGER ABI across ScaLAPACK, BLACS, PBLAS, BLAS/LAPACK and the caller, including any ILP64 choice. Selected sketches use full matrices at global origin (1,1), square blocks and compatible layouts; they omit the required distribution/setup and are not runnable standalone drivers. Negative INFO can encode a descriptor entry as -(argument*100+entry), and PXERBLA handling may abort rather than just return. PDGESVD reduces a distributed real rectangular matrix to bidiagonal form, calls DBDSQR and optionally back-transforms thin left/right singular vectors. JOBU/JOBVT accept V or N rather than serial DGESVD A/S conventions. A is destroyed; S(MIN(M,N)) is replicated in decreasing order, U has global shape (M,MIN(M,N)) and VT has (MIN(M,N),N), containing rows of V-transpose rather than columns of V. The selected sketch uses positive dimensions, matching block layouts and origins (1,1) for all arrays. Query local WORK collectively; even the query creates and releases temporary BLACS grids. Positive INFO can report bidiagonal nonconvergence or MIN(M,N)+1 for detected interprocess singular-value mismatch, so interpret the final status and check reconstruction/orthogonality independently. A further status-propagation limit is visible: DBDSQR failure is not checked before the optional back-transform calls reuse INFO, so a later successful call can overwrite that earlier failure status. Review covers driver workspace, reduction and dispatch, not every distributed/kernel path or arbitrary submatrix offset.

classifications.notes: PDGBSV is a distributed real general-banded solver using pivoted divide-and-conquer factorization through PDGBTRF and solve through PDGBTRS. Unlike the selected 2-D dense drivers, use its documented blocked one-dimensional matrix layout: A descriptor type 501 and B type 502 (or compatible documented type-1 descriptors). Initialize MPI/BLACS and compatible scalar/integer ABI; packed A needs LLD_A>=2*BWL+2*BWU+1, B needs its NB-based local row capacity, and IPIV at least NB entries. Require JA=IB and the noncyclic constraint P*NB>=MOD(JA-1,NB)+N; if spanning ranks, NB>=BWL+BWU+1. A factors differ from serial LAPACK band factors because of reordering; A/B are overwritten and pivot/work storage must follow this interface. Allocate the full documented WORK formula before entry: the driver forms WORK(1+WS_FACTOR) before lower-level calls and has no top-level LWORK=-1 query path. Positive INFO identifies a singular local/reduced partition, not necessarily the global diagonal-pivot convention used by GESV. Review covers driver layout, workspace slicing and factor/solve dispatch, not every banded kernel, arbitrary grid layout or condition estimate.

local.name: PDHSEQR Algorithm 953
local.description: Parallel Hessenberg QR with aggressive early deflation for nonsymmetric eigenproblems.

classifications.notes: The README restricts current coverage to double-precision real matrices and identifies complex support as planned. The principal operation is a real Schur form of an upper Hessenberg matrix, with MPI/BLAS/LAPACK/ScaLAPACK dependencies.

PDHSEQR computes the ordinary eigenvalues of a distributed real upper Hessenberg matrix and optionally its real Schur form/factors. The native multishift QR path invokes aggressive early deflation and bulge-chasing kernels, with alternative/recovery paths for small or unconverged blocks. This is specifically the compact Hessenberg eigenvalue leaf D4c2b; a general dense matrix must first be reduced, and Schur vectors must not be labeled individual eigenvectors. WR/WI contain replicated real/imaginary eigenvalue components. The query requires valid distributed descriptors and returns real/integer workspace sizes; H is overwritten on computation. Nonzero INFO needs interpretation for invalid controls or incomplete convergence, and balancing/reduction transforms must be retained if original-matrix factors are desired. Review covers public driver, workspace/dispatch and selected AED/multishift calls, not every tuning/kernel or numerical accuracy claim.

 real_query,-1,integer_query,-1,info)

 work,lwork,iwork,liwork,info)

classifications.notes: PDGEBAL balances a distributed general real matrix by optional permutation and diagonal similarity scaling. It isolates rows/columns, communicates norms and applies power-of-two scaling with underflow/overflow guards. JOB=B performs both stages; JOB=P or S selects one, and SCALE combines permutation records outside the active interval with scale factors inside it. This is an associated eigenproblem transformation, not an eigenvalue computation or a promise that balancing improves every problem. A is overwritten and ILO/IHI identify the remaining active block. The caller must retain SCALE/permutation information and apply matching backtransformation conventions when using original-matrix vectors. NaN/invalid inputs can invoke PXERBLA. Review covers the native distributed permutation/scaling path and public contract, not the original LAPACK implementation or arbitrary exceptional floating-point behavior.

local.name: PSBLAS
local.description: Distributed sparse linear-algebra kernels and iterative-solver infrastructure.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes sparse matrix/dense operations, triangular block solves and solver infrastructure from optional external preconditioner packages. It documents integer-size choices and a CUDA incompatibility with 8-byte local indices; not every configuration is interchangeable.

The public PSB_KRYLOV generic dispatches its distributed real-double CG selection to a native preconditioned conjugate-gradient iteration. The implementation forms b-A*x, applies the supplied preconditioner, computes global dot products and updates search directions, solution and recursive residual. This selection requires an SPD system and compatible fixed SPD preconditioning, not an arbitrary nonsymmetric matrix. The caller must initialize a PSBLAS/MPI context, assemble the distributed sparse matrix/vectors/descriptor and build the preconditioner. ISTOP=2 selects relative residual scaling and iteration/error outputs are explicit; zero denominators and breakdown exits have internal conventions, so INFO plus a fresh independently computed residual should be checked. Unknown method strings otherwise fall back to BiCGStab, making the exact CG selector significant. Review covers public dispatch, CG recurrence and convergence cleanup, not every backend/precision or Krylov variant.

spral_lsmr::lsmr_solve performs Golub-Kahan bidiagonalization through reverse-communication A and transpose-A products, applies plane rotations and updates the least-squares iterate and norm/conditioning estimates. D9a1 records unconstrained real L2 linear least squares, scoped to no preconditioner and no damping. The caller supplies matrix actions, so dense/sparse/matrix-free storage is a caller choice, not a mandatory stored matrix input. Initialize ACTION=0 and U=B. ACTION=1 requires V=V+TRANSPOSE(A)*U; ACTION=2 requires U=U+A*V, preserving the other vector. Overwriting with a bare product loses the recurrence contribution. ACTION=0 means termination, including errors; inspect INFORM%FLAG and independently verify residual/normal residual. Default CTEST=3 uses built-in stopping; custom tests/preconditioning/damping require their documented protocols. No solve, numerical monotonicity or dependency build was run.

procedures.summary: Public generic for the double implementation, with default-INTEGER dimensions/actions and DOUBLE PRECISION U(M),V(N),Y(N). KEEP preserves private state; OPTIONS and INFORM are mutable derived types. Without preconditioning Y is X. Preserve all state across calls.
procedures.usage:
use spral_lsmr, only: lsmr_keep,lsmr_options,lsmr_inform,lsmr_solve,lsmr_free
type(lsmr_keep) :: keep
type(lsmr_options) :: options
type(lsmr_inform) :: inform
real(8) :: a(3,2),b(3),u(3),v(2),x(2)
integer :: action,stat
a=reshape([1d0,0d0,1d0,0d0,1d0,1d0],[3,2]); b=1d0
options%ctest=3; options%unit_diagnostics=-1
action=0; u=b
do
 call lsmr_solve(action,3,2,u,v,x,keep,options,inform)
 if(action==0) exit
 select case(action)
 case(1)
  v=v+matmul(transpose(a),u)
 case(2)
  u=u+matmul(a,v)
 case default
  error stop "unexpected LSMR action"
 end select
end do
call lsmr_free(keep,stat)
! Inspect inform%flag, cleanup stat and independently check A*x-b.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. No-preconditioning, no-damping reverse-communication sketch. ACTION=0 is not a success code; flags distinguish compatibility, least-squares accuracy, conditioning, iteration and allocation failures. Keep U/V accumulation exactly as documented. Caller must interpret and check final norms, and check cleanup status. Link the SPRAL build and its configured BLAS/dependencies.

local.name: SpLLT
local.description: Sparse symmetric-positive-definite systems solved by task-based Cholesky factorization.

classifications.notes: The README restricts the solver to symmetric positive-definite systems. It documents a sequential default and selectable OpenMP, StarPU or PaRSEC runtimes, with SPRAL/METIS analysis dependencies; indefinite-system support is not inferred.

SpLLT provides sparse real-SPD Cholesky factorization and triangular solves through analysis/factor/solve phases. The native factor wrapper selects task-based STF/PTG work; local diagonal kernels use Cholesky and block triangular updates, while solves traverse forward/backward work. Symbolic analysis uses SPRAL and requires the lower-triangular CSC pattern, consistent values and permutation storage. The selected usage is an initialized OpenMP/STF configuration after successful analysis. SOLVE JOB=0 or omission means both phases, JOB=1 forward and JOB=2 backward in the actual worker, despite a conflicting earlier prologue description. Task completion is explicit through SPLLT_WAIT where required. INFO%FLAG reports framework diagnostics, but the reviewed local diagonal kernel returns on nonzero DPOTRF status without exposing that status as a public argument; do not treat the wrapper flag as sufficient numerical certification. Review covers public phase dispatch, selected factor kernel and solve-job dispatch, not all runtimes, GPUs or indefinite systems.

procedures.summary: Public sparse SPD task-based factorization phase, followed by a complete solve through SPLLT_SOLVE.

use spllt_mod
use spllt_solve_mod, only: spllt_solve
! After SPLLT_INIT and successful SPLLT_ANALYSE of an SPD lower-triangle CSC matrix:
! AKEEP/FKEEP/OPTIONS/INFO are matching SpLLT objects; VAL follows the analysed pattern.
! X is REAL(WP), length FKEEP%N, initialized to the original-order right-hand side.
! This fragment assumes the configured OpenMP/STF runtime.
call spllt_factor(akeep,fkeep,options,val,info)
call spllt_wait()
if(info%flag/=0) error stop "inspect SpLLT factorization diagnostics"
call spllt_solve(fkeep,options,x,info=info)
if(info%flag/=0) error stop "inspect SpLLT solve diagnostics"
! Independently validate the residual, then release matrix data and finalize the runtime.

classifications.notes: The README describes MATLAB-facing CUR code backed by Fortran LUSOL and random sketches. Claimed speedups over svds are upstream results; the CUR algorithm is not presented as entirely Fortran, and documented old MATLAB build environments may need adaptation.

The external CARRQR routine computes a blocked column-pivoted QR representation: REDUCEQRCP selects/reduces candidate panels, the driver stores reflector coefficients and triangular factors, and UPDATEA applies the block update. JPVT maps the permuted columns; A is overwritten with factor/reflector storage, not an explicit Q. The current source hardcodes NTHD=1 and disables intended OpenMP paths, so no parallel communication-avoidance timing claim is made. Its LDA guard uses MIN(M,1) instead of MAX(1,M); callers must enforce LDA>=MAX(1,M) themselves. Require positive nonempty sizes and 1<=BLKMAX<=MIN(M,N); zero-sized cases are rejected by the block-size guard before the nominal quick return. This is the inspected Fortran QR component, not the full spectrum-revealing CUR workflow implemented elsewhere in the repository, a numerical rank certificate or an audit of all LUSOL/BLAS kernels.

local.name: TT Fortran core
local.description: Fortran computing core of TT-Toolbox with tensor-train and local solver support.

classifications.notes: The README warns that standalone use is not easy and includes customized PRIMME/Expokit libraries. It distinguishes four-byte-integer standalone builds from eight-byte MATLAB MEX builds; neither interoperability nor example eigenvalues were tested here.

The selected real-valued SVD(N,A,TT,TOL,RMAX) overload converts a dense flattened tensor into tensor-train cores by successive right-to-left matricization SVDs, singular-value truncation and propagation of scaled left factors. The optional rank cap can force more truncation than the tolerance request. This is a separated tensor approximation, not proof of a best global TT approximation or a complete review of all matrix/DMRG/complex operations. Positive mode sizes, consistent Fortran-order input length, safe integer dimension/workspace products and compatible BLAS/LAPACK are caller requirements. The DTT type holds pointer-backed cores and has no active finalizer; release with DEALLOC and do not assume intrinsic pointer copying provides independent ownership. Zero-norm input has a special zero-rank/deallocation return.

procedures.summary: Public module generic; this card selects the dense real tensor-to-TT overload, not the in-place rounding overload. N is a vector of mode sizes and A is flattened dense storage.
procedures.usage:
use tt_lib, only: dtt,svd,dealloc
type(dtt) :: tensor
double precision :: dense(8)
dense=[1.0d0,2.0d0,3.0d0,4.0d0,5.0d0,6.0d0,7.0d0,8.0d0]
call svd([2,2,2],dense,tensor,1.0d-8,rmax=8)
! Use tensor cores, then release their pointer-owned storage.
call dealloc(tensor)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. This uses three two-point modes and real cores. Link the complete module dependency set, select matching floating/integer kinds and retain input for an independent reconstruction/error check. No tolerance, rank or compression benchmark was run.

classifications.notes: The real DOT(TT1,TT2) overload contracts compatible TT cores through successive DGEMM and transpose operations instead of expanding both tensors. Its result is a rank-one REAL(8) ARRAY, with length equal to the product of the four outer bond ranks; ordinary closed rank-one boundaries give a one-element array holding the scalar inner product. Matching core ranges, mode sizes, associated core storage and consistent bond dimensions are caller obligations; there is no comprehensive shape validation in the inspected routine. The selected real operation is not a review of conjugation conventions in the complex overload or a claim that arbitrary open-boundary contractions are scalars.

procedures.summary: Public TT generic returning a rank-one array for the real DTT pair, including the scalar-boundary case.
procedures.usage:
use tt_lib, only: dtt,svd,dot,dealloc
type(dtt) :: a,b
double precision :: dense(4),inner(1)
dense=[1.0d0,2.0d0,3.0d0,4.0d0]
call svd([2,2],dense,a,1.0d-8)
call svd([2,2],dense,b,1.0d-8)
inner=dot(a,b)
call dealloc(a); call dealloc(b)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The two tensors here have unit outer ranks, so INNER(1) is the intended scalar contraction. This is not valid scalar assignment syntax for arbitrary boundary ranks. No dense inner-product or roundoff comparison was performed.

local.name: Zolo SVD
local.description: QDWH and Zolotarev-based polar decomposition and singular-value algorithms.

classifications.notes: The README identifies QDWH-PD/QDWH-SVD and Zolo-PD/Zolo-SVD and an ELPA 2016 dependency, plus modified ScaLAPACK QR routines. Its comparative performance claim and compatibility with newer ELPA releases were not independently checked.

The external routine named ZOLOPD in zolopd.f90 actually implements QR-based dynamically weighted Halley polar iteration, with a Cholesky/positive solve branch once the iterate is sufficiently conditioned. It is distinct from PZOLOPD1, which dispatches Zolotarev coefficients and communicator-split rational work. This mapping records matrix polar decomposition under broad linear algebra D, not QR as an end product or a singular-value decomposition inferred from the repository name. Although the header permits M>=N, important operations use N-by-N dimensions, so the sketch is deliberately square. POLAR=T additionally forms the symmetrized Q-transpose*A factor in WORK2. Descriptor layouts, local leading dimensions, two workspace buffers and BLACS/MPI initialization are prerequisites. Error state is overwritten across dependency calls and the main loop has no visible hard iteration cap. Source review is not a polar residual or distributed convergence check.

procedures.summary: External distributed real square polar-factor driver in this inspected QDWH implementation.
procedures.usage:
external :: ZOLOPD
! Initialize MPI/BLACS, square full-rank real A, Q and compatible descriptors.
! Allocate/query both workspaces and TAU according to the defining routine.
! DESCW describes the stacked 2*N-by-N QR workspace.
call ZOLOPD(n,n,0d0,a,1,1,desca,q,1,1,descq,work,lwork,descw,tau,work2,lwork2,info,"T")
! Inspect INFO and independently check A_original-Q*H and Q-transpose*Q.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-setup collective-call fragment with zero shift and square storage. H is in WORK2 on the POLAR=T path; workspace-query semantics and all descriptors need validation against this prototype. No distributed factorization, iteration or accuracy was tested.

classifications.notes: ZOLOEIG computes a partial real symmetric eigendecomposition given a polar factor of A-sigma*I. PQDWHSUBIT subtracts I and halves Q, estimates the projector rank from its squared Frobenius norm, forms a randomized invariant subspace and compressed matrix, then ZOLOEIG calls PDSYEVD and back-transforms selected vectors. The executable projector is (Q-I)/2 despite a nearby comment saying (Q+I)/2, so do not infer a selected side from the comment alone. The computed RK is local and printed rather than returned by ZOLOEIG; callers cannot safely infer the number of valid returned eigenpairs from INFO alone. Q/AS/work buffers are overwritten. Subspace iteration has a two-step limit, and downstream INFO overwrites require review. This is prototype subset-symmetric functionality, not full-spectrum, nonsymmetric or generalized eigensolving.

call ZoloEig(n,nblk,q,a,context,comm,work,lwork,work2,lwork2,tau,info)

local.name: mclust
local.description: Gaussian finite-mixture models for clustering, classification and density estimation.

classifications.notes: DESCRIPTION documents EM fitting, Bayesian regularization, visualization and resampling inference. The repository contains compiled Fortran components, but package-level functions may combine R and Fortran; model-selection and classification performance are not independently established.

ME1E alternates Gaussian-mixture M and E steps for one-dimensional observations with a variance shared by all G components. It begins from caller membership weights Z, computes means/variance/proportions, forms log densities, normalizes posterior weights with a log-sum-exp style shift and stops on relative log-likelihood change or iteration budget. VINv<=0 selects no uniform noise component; EQPRO=.FALSE. estimates component proportions. Z, MAXI, TOL and EPS are input/output: normal return writes iterations, achieved change and log likelihood; exceptional EPS sentinels represent insufficient membership or collapsed variance. This is one fixed-component mixture fit, not automated model-number/covariance-model selection, supervised classification or a guarantee of global likelihood maximum. BLAS is required and default LOGICAL/integer/double ABI must match.

procedures.summary: External common-variance univariate Gaussian-mixture EM core. Initialize nonnegative row-normalized memberships with nonempty components.
procedures.usage:
double precision :: x(6),z(6,2),tol,eps,mu(2),sigsq,pro(2)
integer :: iterations
external :: me1e
x=[-2.0d0,-1.8d0,-1.5d0,1.5d0,1.8d0,2.0d0]
z=0.0d0; z(1:3,1)=1.0d0; z(4:6,2)=1.0d0
iterations=100; tol=1.0d-6; eps=1.0d-10
call me1e(.false.,x,6,2,0.0d0,z,iterations,tol,eps,mu,sigsq,pro)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The sketch selects two common-variance components, no noise and estimated proportions. Interpret returned EPS sentinels/TOL/MAXI before accepting a fit; iteration exhaustion is not convergence. No likelihood, partition or label-stability comparison was run.

classifications.notes: DMVNORM evaluates multivariate Gaussian LOG densities by upper Cholesky factorization of Sigma, triangular solves of centered data and a squared-norm/log-determinant formula. Sigma is overwritten by its factor. The interface name does not imply exponentiated density or CDF output. W(P) is scratch; W(1) receives factorization INFO on failure, but range-rejection sets W(1)=0 and HOOD=FLMAX too, so W(1)=0 alone is insufficient. HOOD is not assigned on successful completion and is not a joint log likelihood: initialize it to a nonsentinel before calling and check the failure sentinel before reading LOGDENS. This source review covers the driver and selected helper, not all linked BLAS/LAPACK kernels or an independent distribution test.

procedures.summary: External double-precision Gaussian log-density driver. X has observations in rows; Sigma is overwritten, LOGDENS is undefined on early failure.
procedures.usage:
double precision :: x(2,2),mu(2),sigma(2,2),w(2),hood,logdens(2)
external :: dmvnorm
x(1,:)=[0.0d0,0.0d0]; x(2,:)=[1.0d0,1.0d0]
mu=0.0d0; sigma=reshape([1.0d0,0.0d0,0.0d0,1.0d0],[2,2])
hood=0.0d0
call dmvnorm(x,mu,sigma,2,2,w,hood,logdens)
if(w(1)/=0.0d0.or.hood==huge(1.0d0)) error stop "Density failure"
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use finite observations and a symmetric positive-definite covariance with a compatible LAPACK/BLAS ABI. HOOD remains its initialized value on success. Only LOGDENS holds the per-observation results; no density integration or Mahalanobis residual was checked.

local.name: leaps
local.description: Regression subset selection using branch-and-bound and faster search alternatives.

classifications.notes: The README identifies Alan Miller Fortran 77 routines and describes subset-size restrictions and rank-deficient predictor support. Exhaustive subset search is a documented option, not a claim that every available search heuristic returns the same optimum.

The selected AS274 pipeline CLEAR -> repeated INCLUD -> TOLSET -> REGCF accumulates weighted raw design rows into an orthogonal reduction and back-substitutes regression coefficients for the first NREQ variables. Intercepts must be supplied as a design column. INCLUD overwrites XROW; REGCF may zero D entries judged below tolerance. TOLSET uses a fixed 5e-10 threshold in this revision. IER checks dimensions but does not certify rank, finite inputs or fit quality. This is parameter estimation from raw rows, not a review of every exhaustive/forward/backward subset-selection path in the R package, inference or residual validation. Use nonnegative finite weights and adequate rank; preserve raw data for independent checks.

procedures.summary: External double-precision coefficient extraction from the AS274 orthogonal state. Initialize and update state first; inspect IER after every stage.
procedures.usage:
integer :: ier,i
double precision :: d(2),rbar(1),theta(2),sse,tol(2),work(2),beta(2),row(2)
external :: clear,includ,tolset,regcf
call clear(2,1,d,rbar,theta,sse,ier)
if(ier/=0) error stop "CLEAR"
do i=1,4
  row=[1.0d0,dble(i)]
  call includ(2,1,1.0d0,row,1.0d0+2.0d0*i,d,rbar,theta,sse,ier)
  if(ier/=0) error stop "INCLUD"
enddo
call tolset(2,1,d,rbar,tol,work,ier)
if(ier/=0) error stop "TOLSET"
call regcf(2,1,d,rbar,theta,tol,beta,2,ier)
if(ier/=0) error stop "REGCF"
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. This is a full-rank coefficient pipeline fragment, not a checked regression driver. NRBAR needs NP*(NP-1)/2 entries. No subset search, residual or rank-deficient case was run. Link/build the relevant AS274 routine set; package-wide R entry points require their runtime.

local.name: Induced Smoothed Lasso
local.description: R/Fortran smoothed-lasso inference for linear and generalized linear models.

classifications.notes: The README lists Gaussian, binomial, Poisson and Gamma families and a Fortran backend. Hypothesis-test validity, smoothing behavior and high-dimensional performance depend on statistical assumptions and were not checked for this catalog.

The selected ISLASSO entry estimates a weighted Gaussian multiple-linear regression with induced-smoothed lasso/elastic-net-style penalty terms. It precomputes X-transpose W X and X-transpose W(y-offset), alternates damped penalized coefficient solves and covariance/standard-error updates, and optionally adapts penalties/mixture parameters. This is penalized regression, not ordinary unpenalized least squares or a robust-loss mapping inferred from the lasso name. Starting coefficient/SE/covariance inputs and positive observation weights are part of the workflow. X, lambda, limits/tolerance and output arrays can be overwritten; STAND=0 avoids standardization in the sketch. CONV reports outer limit or numerical failure, but the initial DPOTRF status is overwritten by DPOTRS before inspection, so a failed factorization can be obscured; additional factorization validation is required. R interrupt/normal-density/CDF and trace helpers mean this is R-hosted code, not a standalone Fortran library. Review covers the Gaussian entry and penalty derivative routines, not the separate generalized-linear family/link paths or inferential coverage.

procedures.summary: External R-hosted penalized Gaussian regression kernel with explicit-array work/output arguments.
procedures.usage:
external :: islasso
integer,parameter :: n=6,p=2
integer :: i,itmax,itmaxse,conv
double precision :: x(n,p),y(n),theta(p),se(p),cov(p,p),lambda(p),alpha,pi(p)
double precision :: tol,sigma2,offset(n),eta(n),mu(n),varmu(n),mueta(n),w(n),res(n)
double precision :: dev,weights(n),hi(p),edf,xtw(p,n),xtx(p,p),grad(p),hess(p,p),invh(p,p),pen(p)
! Execute inside an initialized R process with all package numerical helpers linked.
x(:,1)=1d0
do i=1,n
 x(i,2)=dble(i-1)
end do
y=1d0+2d0*x(:,2); theta=0d0; se=1d0; cov=0d0
cov(1,1)=1d0; cov(2,2)=1d0; lambda=[0d0,0.1d0]
alpha=1d0; pi=0.5d0; itmax=100; itmaxse=50; tol=1d-6
sigma2=1d0; offset=0d0; weights=1d0
call islasso(x,y,n,p,theta,se,cov,lambda,alpha,pi,0, &
 itmax,itmaxse,tol,sigma2,0,0,offset,conv,0,1, &
 eta,mu,varmu,mueta,w,res,dev,weights,hi,edf,xtw,xtx,grad,hess,invh,pen)
if(conv/=0) error stop "penalized fit did not report success"

The unpenalized first column is specified by LAMBDA(1)=0. Factorization status handling needs repair/validation before treating CONV=0 as sufficient; no coefficients, covariance or significance results were tested.

local.name: mix
local.description: Estimation and multiple imputation for mixed categorical and continuous data.

classifications.notes: DESCRIPTION gives the mixed-data estimation/imputation scope, and the repository contains a Fortran core. Individual distributional assumptions, missingness mechanisms and convergence diagnostics require further method/source review.

The external CTRSC routine centers and rescales each observed column while preserving entries exactly equal to MVCODE. It computes mean and standard deviation using sums and sums of squares and divisor COUNT, not COUNT-1; this can suffer cancellation. Zero-variance columns are centered and SDV is set to one. For all-missing columns SDV is one but XBAR is not assigned. No observation-mask tolerance, NaN handling, overflow protection or stable online recurrence is provided. This mapping covers the descriptive-statistics/standardization component, not EM, imputation or the entire mixed-data model.

procedures.summary: External in-place double-precision column standardization, with exact missing-value sentinel matching. Avoid reading XBAR for an all-missing column.
procedures.usage:
double precision :: x(3,1),average(1),scale(1)
external :: ctrsc

SIMTHOM simulates a Thomas/Neyman-Scott clustered spatial point pattern: Poisson parent count, uniform parents in a width-one/height-TY rectangle, Poisson offspring counts, and Box-Muller Gaussian offspring offsets. Offspring coordinates are wrapped periodically into the rectangle. The class records joint spatial sampling rather than independent univariate draws or an unbounded-window model. AMU is overwritten by AMU*TY; use a fresh density value on each call. NPTS counts parents, and NCL(i) counts offspring of parent i. IER=-1 reports parent-capacity overflow; IER=-2 reports an offspring row exceeding NMAX, leaving only partial outputs. Only initialized rows/columns are meaningful. The external RNG INIT/RANDOM and POIS support are required. Review covers the simulation path, not parameter estimation, reproducibility across R builds or goodness of fit.

classifications.notes: The README documents a standalone LAPACK-based Fortran utility, fitted-function evaluation and intersections. Its resampling uncertainties depend on the data/error model; the example values were not reproduced and do not certify arbitrary extrapolations.

The PROGRAM contains its fitting helpers; they are not externally callable public library routines. In the independent-coefficient path, the code builds sums of weighted powers of shifted abscissae, factors and inverts the symmetric normal matrix via DSYTRF/DSYTRI, multiplies by the weighted data vector, and accumulates weighted squared residuals. The external GAMV kernel computes directional lag-binned spatial continuity statistics from irregular multidimensional coordinates and observed variables. It enumerates accepted data pairs, filters lag/direction/bandwidth and trimming conditions, accumulates products/differences and normalizes per-bin means. The selected IVTYPE=3 branch returns lag covariance after subtracting the head/tail means. The adopted GAMS tree has no dedicated spatial-variogram leaf, so this spatial statistical analysis remains in multidimensional elementary data analysis L4c rather than being called temporal autocovariance or kriging interpolation. NP reports floating-point pair counts; empty bins remain zero and need masking. The semivariogram cloud branch has an off-by-one capacity guard and stores cumulative bin values rather than a clearly isolated pair statistic; the sketch selects covariance, for which that cloud branch writes no points. No general success status is returned. Review covers covariance accumulation/normalization and related public declarations, not every variogram type or the separate kriging solver.

The external rlRWAGm2 kernel implements the W-algorithm for robust/bounded-influence multiple-linear regression. The selected ITYPE=1, ISIGMA=0 branch performs a fixed-scale M-estimation update with residual-dependent weights, rank-revealing QR and coefficient increments. IPS=3 selects Huber psi; PSP0=1 is its derivative at zero. This scoped use does not include a high-breakdown initial fit or the complete MM regression workflow exposed by higher-level R wrappers. COV supplies the packed coefficient convergence metric and WGT is not an arbitrary precision-weight interface for all ITYPE branches. NIT is an iteration count, not a general numerical-success code; small-scale/rank exits can bypass final output assignment, so SIGMAF and coefficients need inspection. Source review covers the selected fixed-scale update and psi selector, not all scale estimators, leverage corrections or inferential covariance calculations. The full package includes R trace/error helpers.

local.name: rrcov
local.description: Robust multivariate location, covariance, PCA and discriminant-analysis methods.

classifications.notes: The README enumerates MCD/MVE/S/MM/SD and regularized/projection-pursuit variants. This is mixed R and compiled-code software; not every advertised estimator is necessarily implemented in the repository Fortran components or valid under the same assumptions.

RLDS computes a nonparametric robust multivariate location/scatter estimate from projection outlyingness. RLWEIGHTS samples subsets defining projection directions, standardizes projected distances using medians and robust scale, retains maximal outlyingness and forms redescending weights. RLDONOSTAH then computes weighted location using W and scatter using W squared, normalized by their respective sums; this is not the ordinary sample covariance. The GAMS nonparametric multidimensional-data-analysis class is retained because the adopted taxonomy has no specific Stahel-Donoho leaf. Positive NRESAMP bounds requested valid random subsets and MAXRES bounds attempted subsets; NRESAMP=0 instead enumerates all subsets and is not bounded by MAXRES. NRESPER reports valid subsets, not a success or accuracy certificate. Degenerate data or vanishing weight sums need caller-side checks because the location/scatter divisions have no general error status. The routine brackets its own R RNG state and requires the package R/native helpers. Review covers the estimator paths, not breakdown guarantees, covariance calibration or exhaustive runtime complexity.

local.name: SmoothHazard
local.description: Smooth hazard models for interval-censored survival and illness-death data.

classifications.notes: The README identifies an R interface to Pierre Joly Fortran functions. This supports the specialized statistical scope without claiming a general survival-analysis toolkit; censoring assumptions, model options and numerical estimation need deeper review.

The external SURVWEIB entry fits a parametric Weibull proportional-hazards survival model by maximizing a likelihood with exact/right/interval-censored observations and optional left truncation. The likelihood contains exp(X*beta), Weibull baseline cumulative hazard and the selected censoring/truncation contributions; the baseline parameters are squared internally to keep them nonnegative. The baseline formula is S(t)=exp(-(b2*t)**b1), so B2 is an inverse-scale/rate rather than the usual direct Weibull scale. A baseline-only optimization precedes the covariate fit. For P>0, CONVERGED(1:2)=1 denotes success of both optimizer stages; zero is not the success convention. EPS holds integer accuracy exponents. Confidence-band arrays should only be used if requested and successfully computed. Saved module work arrays and unconditional R RNG enter/exit calls mean this is R-hosted shared-state code even with bands disabled. The interval branch subtracts survival terms and invalid likelihoods use a sentinel, so tail cancellation and invalid data need independent validation. Review covers the parametric likelihood/driver, not the separate spline model, confidence-band coverage or arbitrary survival workflows.

The selected utilclc routines compute a column Gram product S-transpose*S and its weighted analogue S-transpose*diag(w**2)*S using DOT_PRODUCT. Despite the names mkcov/mkcovweight, the routines neither subtract means nor divide by a sample-count denominator: raw input is not automatically converted to statistical covariance. Weights are applied to BOTH vectors and hence squared, not used once. Shapes are partly checked through printerror2; callers should supply full ncols-by-ncols outputs and matching row weights. Precision is the preprocessed SESAM BIGREAL/kr setting, with repository module/configuration and error-hook dependencies. This maps elementary matrix multiplication, not the full data-assimilation system or an automatic covariance estimator.

classifications.notes: DESCRIPTION identifies a deliberately restricted sparse storage format and MCMC-oriented design; the README records provenance of Fortran Cholesky code. Large-index scaling uses an extension package and is not assumed to be available in every configuration.

ROWMEANS traverses compressed sparse rows and accumulates their stored values into the caller output. FLAG=1 divides by the number of stored entries in a nonempty row; other flags divide by NCL, including implicit zeros. RS MUST be initialized to zero by the caller. Stored explicit zeros count in the FLAG=1 denominator. Empty stored-only rows leave their initialized result unchanged; no size, column-count or pointer validation is performed. classifications.notes: CSRMSR converts a square 1-based CSR matrix to modified sparse-row storage with the diagonal in AO(1:N), AO(N+1) unused, and off-diagonal row pointers and columns sharing JAO. local.name: KronLinInv
local.description: Kronecker-structured Bayesian linear inversion with Gaussian separable covariance models.

classifications.notes: The README limits the method to Gaussian/separability assumptions, with serial/OpenMP/MPI Fortran variants and LAPACK. It explicitly says the non-Julia implementations are unmaintained; the catalog preserves that scope/status rather than implying active Fortran development.

The selected shared-memory Fortran pipeline computes the posterior mean of a linear Gaussian inverse problem with three-factor Kronecker-separable forward/covariance structure. CALCFACTORS solves component systems, constructs generalized symmetric eigenvectors and diagonal 1/(1+lambda1*lambda2*lambda3) factors; POSTERIORMEAN contracts the observed-minus-prior-predicted data through these factors and adds the correction to MPRIOR. This is conditional multivariate Gaussian analysis, not general non-Gaussian Bayesian sampling, arbitrary covariance structure or a new inverse-problem validation. Caller arrays must have consistent tensor-product dimensions/order and positive-definite covariance factors. The mean routine uses integer progress divisors EVERYNIT/NTHR: small models or many threads can make this zero, and initial ETA calculations divide by a zero count. Repair/validate that reporting path before relying on it. OpenMP runtime symbols are used even outside directives. The README marks the non-Julia implementations unmaintained.

local.name: PDFO
local.description: Python and MATLAB interfaces to Powell derivative-free optimization solvers.

classifications.notes: The README identifies modified Fortran UOBYQA, NEWUOA, BOBYQA, LINCOA and COBYLA sources. Interfaces and underlying solvers are distinguished; individual constraint classes and numerical results are deferred to deeper review.

The selected modified BOBYQA entry minimizes a real smooth objective with bound constraints through interpolation-based quadratic trust-region models, without user derivatives. It partitions workspace, adjusts an initial point/radii against bounds and dispatches BOBYQB, which evaluates named external CALFUN and computes constrained model steps through TRSBOX. Unlike the original Powell interface, this variant adds F, INFO and FTARGET; callers must use the pinned signature and matching modified dependency set. N>=2, N+2<=NPT<=(N+1)*(N+2)/2, adequate workspace and positive ordered radii are required; RHOBEG/RHOEND can be overwritten. INFO distinguishes radius/target termination, evaluation cap, invalid inputs and numerical failures. Radius/target success does not establish a global optimum or objective error bound. Review covers public workspace/adjustment dispatch and selected evaluation/trust-step/status paths, not a complete trust-region proof or every PDFO front end.

local.name: PRIMA
local.description: Modern Fortran reference implementations of Powell derivative-free optimization methods.

classifications.notes: The README identifies COBYLA, UOBYQA, NEWUOA, BOBYQA and LINCOA, with bindings in other languages. Broad optimization coverage is recorded without independently endorsing every performance, bug-fix or convergence claim.

The modern BOBYQA module driver minimizes a real objective under simple bounds without user derivatives, constructing quadratic interpolation models and bounded trust-region steps through BOBYQB. It preprocesses dimensions, bounds, radius/budget controls and optional histories before dispatch. X is both starting point and returned approximate minimizer; CALFUN has the modern assumed-shape (X,F) interface and must match configured RP. Bounds and interpolation geometry matter: this is local smooth-model optimization, not a global minimum certificate or a claim of nonsmooth convergence. INFO reports the specific termination reason, NF the evaluation count; radius and target/budget terminations have different meanings. This review covers driver/core trust-region dispatch, not all geometry/rescue/update kernels or fresh optimization results.

classifications.notes: The README documents a scalar loss callback, parameter bounds and topology controls; additional optimizers are future plans. It refers to opti in installation examples, while this reviewed repository identity remains Konrad1991/pso.

The public OPTIMIZER initializes random particles, evaluates a scalar callback, updates velocity from inertial/personal/social terms and clamps coordinates to bounds. local.name: pyOpt
local.description: Object-oriented Python optimization framework with compiled Fortran solver components.

classifications.notes: The README documents problem/solver separation and interfaces to open and industrial optimizers. An interface framework does not imply that every backend is bundled, licensed identically or independently verified here.

Native Fortran routines bundled with pyOpt, distinct from its Python API. Match default INTEGER and DOUBLE PRECISION ABI with the bundled helpers/BLAS; these files alone are not a complete solver build. The unconstrained path minimizes or maximizes general locally Lipschitz objectives using a modified Shor r-algorithm with space dilation and supplied gradients/subgradients or finite differences. The selected fragment minimizes with an analytic subgradient; it does not establish smooth Newton convergence or global optimality. The patched interface adds explicit B(N,N), twelve real N-vectors and IDX(N) work storage, plus output unit/file controls. The executable calls FUN(N,X,F), GRAD(N,X,G), FUNC(N,X,FC) and GRADC(N,X,GC); the header synopsis omits N and must not be copied literally. N must be at least two. OPTIONS has thirteen DOUBLE PRECISION entries: call SOPTIONS then set entry 5 to -1 for quiet operation without opening a file. Entry 9 is an iteration count or negative abnormal-stop code; the N<2 branch actually sets -1 despite the header listing -2. Output is not an optimality certificate.

procedures.procedure: BFGS update, line search and least-squares subproblem dispatch

classifications.notes: Native Fortran routines bundled with pyOpt, distinct from its Python API. Match default INTEGER and DOUBLE PRECISION ABI with the bundled helpers/BLAS; these files alone are not a complete solver build. COBYLA minimizes an objective under nonlinear inequalities CON>=0 by simplex interpolation and a decreasing trust-region radius without user derivatives. The mapping selects smooth objective/constraints without supplied derivatives; the routine does not enforce smoothness itself. Its pyOpt signature adds CALCFC first and status/count/unit/file/FF/GG arguments. CALCFC(N,M,X,F,CON) supplies values; encode bounds as constraints. Allocate W>=N*(3*N+2*M+11)+4*M+6 and IACT>=M+1, choose positive RHOBEG>=RHOEND and an evaluation budget. IFAIL=0 is normal radius termination, 1 evaluation limit and 2 damaging roundoff. FF/GG are set on each callback evaluation, but final selection can restore X from the best simplex vertex without refreshing those outputs; reevaluate F/CON at returned X. RHOEND does not guarantee accuracy or feasibility. This review covers the driver, interpolation/trust-region dispatch and output bookkeeping, not every TRSTLP numerical branch.

procedures.summary: Patched native derivative-free inequality-constrained minimizer.
procedures.usage:
! Initialized DOUBLE PRECISION X(N), FF, GG(M); N>=1, M>=1.
allocate(w(n*(3*n+2*m+11)+4*m+6),iact(m+1))
maxfun=2000
call COBYLA(calcfc,n,m,x,0.5d0,1d-7,0,maxfun, &
 w,iact,ifail,nfvals,6,"unused.log",ff,gg)
if(ifail/=0) error stop "COBYLA did not terminate normally"
call calcfc(n,m,x,ff,gg)
! Check GG>=-chosen_feasibility_tolerance independently.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Provide an external CALCFC with DOUBLE PRECISION values and matching integers. MAXFUN is overwritten with evaluation count. Reevaluate FF/GG after return; no trust-region solve, tolerance or output consistency was tested.

classifications.notes: Native Fortran routines bundled with pyOpt, distinct from its Python API. Match default INTEGER and DOUBLE PRECISION ABI with the bundled helpers/BLAS; these files alone are not a complete solver build. NNLS solves nonnegative linear L2 least squares by an active/passive-set method, Householder updates and Givens rotations. A(MDA,N) and B(M) are overwritten, X(N)>=0 is the selected variable constraint, and W(N), Z(M), INDEX(N) are scratch. MODE=1 success, 2 invalid dimensions, 3 iteration count above 3*N. The same class also covers LSEI below, but NNLS has no equality/general inequality inputs. Preserve originals for residual and KKT checks; supplied legacy BLAS calls include zero-increment broadcasts. LSEI uses Householder null-space reduction for min ||E X-F|| with C X=D and G X>=H. Its selected contract requires 0<MC<N, ME>=N-MC, MG>=1, full row rank C and the reduced design assumptions; inputs are overwritten. Avoid the MC=N shortcut if inequalities need validation: it bypasses the inequality solve. The returned XNRM is combined with the equality-space solution norm in the constrained branch and should not be assumed to equal the original residual norm; compute that from saved E/F. MODE=1 is the native success code, with rank, compatibility and NNLS-limit failures otherwise. Workspace follows the source formula with L=N-MC; JW>=MAX(MG,L).

double precision :: a(3,2),b(3),x(2),rnorm,w(2),z(3)
integer :: ind(2),mode
a(:,1)=[1d0,0d0,1d0]; a(:,2)=[0d0,1d0,1d0]
b=[1d0,2d0,3d0]
call NNLS(a,3,3,2,b,x,rnorm,w,z,ind,mode)
if(mode/=1) error stop "NNLS failed"
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. No nonnegativity, residual or KKT check was executed.

integer :: jw(2),mode

classifications.notes: Native Fortran routines bundled with pyOpt, distinct from its Python API. Match default INTEGER and DOUBLE PRECISION ABI with the bundled helpers/BLAS; these files alone are not a complete solver build. HFTI handles rank-deficient unconstrained linear L2 least squares through column-pivoted Householder reduction and a retained-rank minimum-norm completion. TAU is an absolute diagonal threshold, not a relative singular-value tolerance; KRANK is a computed pseudorank. A and B are overwritten; B first N rows hold solutions and RNORM(NB) residual norms. Require positive M/N, MDA>=M, MDB>=MAX(M,N), H/G/IP length N. There is no MODE or conditioning estimate. The sketch gives B an extra row to keep zero-length tail references within storage; choose TAU based on problem scaling, preserve originals and independently assess numerical rank/residuals.

integer :: ip(2),krank
a(:,1)=[1d0,2d0,3d0]; a(:,2)=2d0*a(:,1)
b=0d0; b(1:3,1)=[1d0,2d0,3d0]
call HFTI(a,3,3,2,b,4,1,1d-10,krank,rn,h,g,ip)
! B(1:2,1) holds the retained-rank solution; inspect KRANK and saved-input residual.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The rank-one example, pseudorank and minimum-norm result were not tested.

classifications.notes: Native Fortran routines bundled with pyOpt, distinct from its Python API. Match default INTEGER and DOUBLE PRECISION ABI with the bundled helpers/BLAS; these files alone are not a complete solver build. LDP solves the minimum-distance problem min 0.5*X^T X subject to G X>=H by forming a dual NNLS problem. This is a strictly convex quadratic objective with identity Hessian, not an arbitrary quadratic-programming interface. G(MG,N), H(M) are preserved; X(N), XNORM and first M workspace entries return the solution, norm and multipliers on MODE=1. W length is at least (M+2)*(N+1)+2*M, INDEX at least M; require N>=1, M>=1, MG>=M. MODE=2 is invalid N, 3 NNLS iteration limit, 4 incompatible constraints. Near degeneracy and floating-point feasibility must be assessed independently; no original residual or KKT certificate is returned.

classifications.notes: Native Fortran routines bundled with pyOpt, distinct from its Python API. Match default INTEGER and DOUBLE PRECISION ABI with the bundled helpers/BLAS; these files alone are not a complete solver build. H12 constructs (MODE=1) and/or applies (MODE=2) an elementary Householder reflection, represented by modified U and separate UP. LPIVOT<L1<=M with LPIVOT>=1 defines the pivot and tail. IUE strides U; ICE strides C elements; ICV strides vectors; NCV counts transformed vectors. No explicit dense Q is returned. Invalid/degenerate indices can return silently; a zero construction vector can leave UP undefined, so do not apply that undefined state. Selected sketch uses a nonzero vector and contiguous column-major C. Preserve U/UP when applying the same reflection again; there is no status output.

call H12(1,1,2,3,u,1,up,c,1,3,2)
! U/UP now encode the reflection; C contains its application to two columns.

local.name: qap
local.description: R package for quadratic-assignment heuristics with reference problem instances.

classifications.notes: The README identifies a simulated-annealing heuristic and QAPLIB examples. Known solutions supplied for benchmarks do not imply that the heuristic always returns a global optimum; individual Fortran procedures need later review.

QAPH4 searches permutations to minimize SUM(A(i,j)*B(perm(i),perm(j))) using random transpositions, a Metropolis acceptance probability and a decreasing temperature with increasing trials per stage. The O(N) swap delta explicitly assumes symmetric A and B; it is not a general asymmetric QAP implementation or a continuous quadratic-programming solver. The R wrapper validates symmetric nonnegative matrices and schedules independent restarts. The Fortran core has no equivalent validation and calls R RNG/interrupt services via a C wrapper; it is not standalone Fortran. Require N>=2, valid permutation, positive trial count, FITER>=1 and 0<FT<1, finite well-scaled data and representable iteration counts. OPE/OL are best-found heuristic output, not a proof of global optimality.

procedures.summary: External double-precision/integer QAP heuristic embedded in R. Use the R package interface for runtime setup and matrix validation.
procedures.usage:
! Interface fragment inside a correctly initialized R-linked caller.
! Supply symmetric finite nonnegative A/B and a valid initial permutation.
! Use qap::qapSA(A,B) in R for the supported validation/restart wrapper.
call qaph4(n,a,b,miter,fiter,ft,ope,ol,perm,maxsteps)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The fragment requires the R runtime, RNG wrapper and interrupt support; an ordinary standalone link is insufficient. PERM is overwritten. A zero/degenerate temperature, integer trial growth and failed input assumptions need explicit handling/verification. No QAPLIB case or optimality gap was computed.

local.name: QuadProg Solver interface
local.description: C and Fortran quadratic-programming interface adapted from R quadprog sources.

classifications.notes: The README documents equality/inequality constraints, bounds and error codes and a BLAS dependency. Interface examples and memory-leak claims were not reproduced; the exact admissible Hessian class needs source-level review.

The quadprog generic copies the Hessian, changes signs/transposes row-oriented constraints, appends bound inequalities when requested, allocates workspace, and dispatches to Goldfarb/Idnani qpgen2 with Cholesky-based positive-definite setup. G2e1 records strictly convex QP with linear equality/inequality constraints, not indefinite or general nonlinear optimization. H_check changes every near-zero diagonal to 1e-10; this is not a valid general positive-definiteness test and can change the problem. constrain_check misses some positive equality residuals because its two-sided test uses AND incorrectly. res is qpgen2 criterion/objective output, not an independently computed feasibility residual despite wrapper wording. The C adapter copies only qeq constraint rows and is outside the shown Fortran API. This review covers wrapper and core setup/dispatch rather than every active-set update. No QP or feasibility/KKT check was run.

procedures.summary: Public module generic for double-precision QP. Aeq(q,n) stores equality rows first then <= inequality rows; beq(q) matches them. Optional bound-vector overload takes lb/ub together before x. Use a genuinely symmetric positive-definite H, and independently inspect constraints after err=0.

use quad_prog, only: quadprog
integer :: err
double precision :: h(2,2), f(2), aeq(1,2), beq(1), x(2), criterion
h=reshape([2.0d0,0.0d0,0.0d0,2.0d0],[2,2])
f=[-2.0d0,-4.0d0]; aeq(1,:)=[1.0d0,1.0d0]; beq=[2.0d0]
err=0
call quadprog(2,1,0,h,f,aeq,beq,[0.0d0,0.0d0], &
              [3.0d0,3.0d0],x,1.0d-8,criterion,err)
if (err /= 0) error stop "quadprog failed"
! Independently verify Aeq*x<=beq, bounds and optimality.

The sketch starts with a positive-definite diagonal Hessian so it avoids the diagonal patch, but it does not repair the wrapper equality checker. local.name: RALFit
local.description: Modern Fortran nonlinear least-squares solver with other-language interfaces.

classifications.notes: The README identifies a Fortran/C toolchain and BLAS/LAPACK requirements and points to separate build documentation. No particular trust-region variant or problem subclass is assigned from this overview alone.

nlls_solve drives repeated nlls_iterate calls for a local first-order critical point of 0.5*SUM(F(X)**2). The inspected unconstrained first-order model evaluates residuals and an analytic Jacobian, sets the residual-Hessian contribution to zero, dispatches a trust-region step and compares actual with predicted reduction before updating. K1b1a2 records smooth nonlinear least squares with supplied first derivatives, scoped to MODEL=1, no bounds/weights/regularization. The public solve still requires a Hessian-callback argument; the supplied dummy is suitable for this selected first-order model. The default MODEL=3 is hybrid, so explicitly select MODEL=1 for this usage. Status 0 reports the selected stopping tests, not a unique/global minimum or accuracy certificate. Convergence can be on residual, gradient or step size; inspect inform fields and recompute residuals. Optional weights multiply residuals, rather than being unsquared objective coefficients. Preprocessing creates separate single/double modules. No fit or trust-region kernel/dependency audit was executed.

procedures.summary: Public solve re-exported by ral_nlls_double for the default double build. X(N) is INOUT; residual/Jacobian/Hessian callbacks take status, dimensions, assumed-size arrays and polymorphic params. Jacobian storage in the author example is column-major M-by-N flattened. INFORM contains status and stopping/evaluation details.

use ral_nlls_double, only: wp,nlls_options,nlls_inform,nlls_solve,ral_nlls_eval_hf_dummy
type(nlls_options) :: options
type(nlls_inform) :: inform
! Allocate X, define PARAMS extending params_base_type, and implement residual/Jacobian callbacks.
options%model=1
call nlls_solve(n,m,x,eval_r,eval_j,ral_nlls_eval_hf_dummy,params,options,inform)
if(inform%status/=0) error stop "RALFit did not report convergence"
! Inspect convergence flags and independently recompute the residual/gradient.

Protocol fragment with missing problem callbacks/data; the pinned exponential-fit example supplies full declarations but uses its default model unless modified. local.name: subplex
local.description: R interface to simplex optimization on subspaces for unconstrained problems.

classifications.notes: The README describes suitability for noisy or discontinuous objectives and attributes the algorithm to Tom Rowan. Such suitability is method guidance, not a guarantee for every noise model or discontinuity.

SUBPLX sorts step scales, partitions coordinates into subspaces and calls SIMPLX for derivative-free simplex minimization, repeating until its relative coordinate/step test is satisfied or a limit is returned. The nonsmooth unconstrained class records this local search, not global optimization. Unlike older comments, this fork has no MODE argument and always initializes default options through SUBOPT. COMMON and SAVE state make nested/concurrent use unsafe without isolation. This review does not establish noisy-objective performance or inspect the entire R bridge.

procedures.summary: External objective-only minimizer with DOUBLE PRECISION F(N,X). X is overwritten, FX is the resulting cost, NFE the evaluation count. Allocate WORK >= 2*N+NSMAX*(NSMAX+4)+1 and IWORK >= N+INT(N/NSMIN), with default NSMAX=MIN(5,N), NSMIN=MIN(2,N).
procedures.signature: CALL SUBPLX(F, N, TOL, MAXNFE, SCALE, X, FX, NFE, WORK, IWORK, IFLAG)
procedures.usage:
! N > 0; declare F DOUBLE PRECISION EXTERNAL and allocate documented work arrays.
scale(1) = -1.0d0  ! common initial step magnitude for every coordinate
iflag = 0
call subplx(f,n,1.0d-6,10000,scale,x,fx,nfe,work,iwork,iflag)
! IFLAG=0 tolerance; 1 machine limit; -1 evaluation budget; -2 invalid input.

local.name: TRDF

classifications.notes: The brief README identifies the algorithm and links publications on constrained minimization and convergence. A broad optimization mapping does not establish that all publication assumptions or variants apply to each routine in this snapshot.

TRDF performs a constrained derivative-free objective trust-region iteration: it dispatches a feasibility solve, builds a quadratic interpolation model, solves a constrained model subproblem, evaluates the true objective and updates radius/model geometry. Constraints can mix equalities/inequalities and bound constraints; CCODED selects whether linked constraint Jacobian/Hessian routines are supplied. This review covers outer iteration/linked-problem dispatch, not all model algebra or ALGENCAN kernels. The interface requires linked CALOBJF/CALCON and optional derivative routines via functions.f, not procedure arguments. COMMON state and compile-time dimensions in tr_params.par limit reentrancy/size. An alternate model-build path calls CALFUN with three arguments although its wrapper takes four; this mismatch needs repair/checked validation. The routine returns F/FEAS/FCNT but no termination flag, and early failure can reach output code before a valid final model point exists. No feasibility or optimizer result was run.

local.name: vc-SQNM
local.description: Stabilized quasi-Newton optimization including variable-cell-shape minimization.

classifications.notes: The README identifies Fortran, C++ and Python implementations and an extension that also optimizes lattice vectors. Reliability and speed claims remain upstream claims; detailed algorithm equivalence and physical model coverage need later review.

The reusable Fortran SQNM_OPTIMIZER takes externally computed objective values/gradients, retains displacement/gradient histories, diagonalizes history and Hessian subspaces and returns a stabilized quasi-Newton displacement. The caller applies X<-X+STEP and reevaluates; SQNM_STEP does not call a user objective or overwrite X. Initialization configures history length, step scale/floor and subspace threshold; CLOSE_SQNM releases buffers. An internal max-gradient cutoff of 1e-11 returns a zero step, but application convergence/budgets are otherwise caller responsibilities. Degenerate history/eigenvalue divisions need valid inputs; LAPACK failures STOP, with no returned status. Only this fixed-coordinate unconstrained smooth supplied-gradient optimizer is mapped, not variable-cell/atomistic wrappers or a rigorous lower-bound guarantee.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound method on SQNM_OPTIMIZER in module SQNM. X/gradient/step use REAL(C_DOUBLE); X is INTENT(IN). Initialize with INTEGER(C_INT) dimensions/history and compatible real controls first, then close explicitly. No success/error output is provided.
procedures.usage:
use iso_c_binding, only: c_int,c_double
use sqnm, only: sqnm_optimizer
type(sqnm_optimizer) :: opt
real(c_double) :: x(2),gradient(2),step(2),value
integer :: iteration
x=[2.0_c_double,-1.0_c_double]
call opt%initialize_sqnm(2_c_int,5_c_int,0.1_c_double, &
     0.001_c_double,1.0e-4_c_double)
do iteration=1,100
  value=sum(x*x); gradient=2.0_c_double*x
  if (maxval(abs(gradient)) < 1.0e-8_c_double) exit
  call opt%sqnm_step(x,value,gradient,step)
  x=x+step
end do
call opt%close_sqnm()

local.name: VTDIRECT95
local.description: Serial and distributed Fortran implementations of the DIRECT global-search algorithm.

classifications.notes: The README identifies ACM Algorithm 897, checkpointing and serial/distributed implementations. Performance studies and the word global do not certify that a finite run attains the exact global minimum of an arbitrary objective.

VTdirect normalizes the finite box, samples its center, selects potentially optimal rectangles by size/value (or the aggressive option), samples displaced centers on longest dimensions and dispatches thirds-based subdivision. The inspected serial driver scales final X back and returns the best sampled value. G2i records deterministic derivative-free global box search, not a finite-budget proof of the global minimum or an audit of parallel/checkpoint modes. OBJ_FUNC returns a value and IFLAG; undefined samples become HUGE rather than a validated feasible solution. R8=SELECTED_REAL_KIND(13), N>=2, strict finite L<U and valid callback values are required. MAX_ITER/MAX_EVL are mutable controls/results; evaluation limits are checked after a batch/iteration and can be exceeded by that batch. Normal statuses are 1..4 stopping rules, not a conventional STATUS=0 success check. Shared global box bookkeeping prevents assuming reentrancy. No DIRECT search, regression or stopping-limit behavior was executed.

procedures.summary: Public VTdirect_MOD routine with assumed-shape R8 bounds/result vectors and an explicit objective interface. STATUS encodes stopping rule/error class. Optional MAX_ITER/MAX_EVL/MIN_DIA are INOUT, so use variables. The selected sketch omits checkpointing and optional multiple-box output.

use REAL_PRECISION, only: r8
use VTdirect_MOD, only: VTdirect
real(r8) :: lower(2),upper(2),x(2),fmin
integer :: status,iterations,evaluations
! Supply explicit-interface OBJ_FUNC(C,IFLAG) returning REAL(r8).
lower=-2.0_r8; upper=2.0_r8; iterations=100; evaluations=1000
call VTdirect(2,lower,upper,obj_func,x,fmin,status, &
 MAX_ITER=iterations,MAX_EVL=evaluations)
if(status<1 .or. status>4) error stop "DIRECT error"

CSPLREP constructs piecewise-cubic coefficients by solving a tridiagonal system for second derivatives with user-supplied endpoint curvatures; CSPLEV selects an interval and evaluates its local polynomial. Zero endpoint curvatures give a natural cubic spline. Require at least four matching sorted, well-separated data nodes. Source findings: fewer nodes return uninitialized coefficients, CSPLREP uses ALLOCATED(CSP%X).AND.SIZE(CSP%X) without guaranteed short-circuit evaluation, and the interval lookup can return 0 or N for outside/upper-end queries although coefficients have N-1 columns. Those queries are not safe extrapolation. The mapping covers fitting and scalar value evaluation, not derivative/integral/root helpers or a full dependency audit.

The REAL64 root_brentq path evaluates two endpoints, accepts an endpoint zero, then alternates secant/inverse interpolation with bisection safeguards and a combined absolute/relative interval stopping rule. F1b records a derivative-free scalar root, not polynomial-specific roots or optimization. The callback is a subroutine f(x,fx), not a scalar function. Optional res carries status and counts; on a same-sign interval the early return leaves x0 undefined, so inspect res before using it. Sign checks multiply endpoint values and can overflow/underflow; finiteness, positive tolerances and valid iteration limits are not comprehensively checked. Lagrange_polynomials returns all cardinal polynomial values and their derivatives at XP via a descending-order recurrence dividing by X(j)-X(r). E3c records manipulation/evaluation of interpolation basis functions, not a black-box fit or a verified interpolation-error bound. Row 0 holds basis values, positive rows derivatives, and row -1 a polynomial antiderivative difference whose lower limit is selected by the actual MINLOC-minus-two expression; it should not be assumed to integrate from X(0) or from the nearest node. Callers combine rows with their data to form an interpolant or its derivatives. Default REAL is used. Require nonempty finite distinct nodes; no duplicate-node, conditioning or overflow status is returned. This module is separate from the repository Numerical Recipes directory, whose routines are not reviewed here. No basis identities, interpolation or derivatives were executed.

procedures.summary: Public PURE function in Lagrange_interpolation. X has dummy lower bound 0 and the result has bounds (-1:SIZE(X)-1,0:SIZE(X)-1). Retain those bounds explicitly when selecting derivative rows; an allocatable assignment can otherwise obscure the intended indexing.

use Lagrange_interpolation, only: Lagrange_polynomials

x=[0.,1.,2.]; y=x**2
basis=Lagrange_polynomials(x,0.5)

dp=sum(basis(1,:)*y)
