classifications.notes: FIT_TRANSITION_MATRIX estimates a higher-order categorical transition table from an ordered state sequence. It encodes each length-ORDER history in base N_STATES, counts the following state and normalizes each observed-history row. An entirely unseen history receives a uniform row; this is a fallback, not Laplace smoothing of all observed counts. The result has N_STATES**ORDER rows and N_STATES columns, so storage and integer exponent/index overflow grow rapidly with order. Require state labels in 1..N_STATES, positive state count/order and enough sequence entries. There is no input-validation or statistical-status output. This is categorical time-domain model estimation, not linear autoregression, and broad L10a2 is kept rather than forcing an AR estimation leaf. The separate higher-order k-step routine chooses successive MAXLOC states and is not a full probability forecast; that routine is not used by this sketch.

local.description: Rust bindings bundling Fortran PFAPACK routines for skew-symmetric matrices and Pfaffians.

classifications.notes: The short Rust-binding README is supplemented by the bundled Fortran example guide, which documents dense/banded Pfaffians and skew-symmetric decompositions. The build tag records the documented Make-based Fortran examples, not a verified Rust packaging workflow; this is a binding/distribution of PFAPACK rather than a separate algorithm.

DSKTRF computes a pivoted Parlett-Reid congruence factorization of a real skew-symmetric matrix, P*A*P^T=L*T*L^T or U*T*U^T. D2a1 is used only for this related factorization in the real nonsymmetric general-storage branch; it does not assert a solver for every nonsymmetric matrix. MODE=N fully tridiagonalizes, while MODE=P performs the partial even-order reduction used for Pfaffians. The driver chooses blocked DLASKTRF or unblocked DSKTF2 panels, propagates zero-pivot INFO and adjusts permutations. It overwrites the selected triangle with tridiagonal entries and multipliers. DSKPFA is also annotated as the public Pfaffian consumer of this reduction; it returns a Pfaffian, not a determinant, and reports zero for odd order. No new QR/SVD classification is inferred from this congruence reduction. BLAS/LAPACK-compatible support and the remaining PFAPACK kernels are required; this review inspects dispatch and Pfaffian accumulation, not all panel arithmetic.

classifications.notes: The README documents complex block-sparse tfQMR solves, multiple right-hand sides and Fortran 90/77 entry points. CUDA implements the computational backend. Convergence, GPU availability and performance require individual testing and are not implied by this broad classification.

The public TFQMRGPU_BSRSV_COMPLETE wrapper solves complex non-Hermitian sparse A*X=B using block-sparse row patterns for A, B and the allowed solution X. It delegates to a private rectangular helper that creates a GPU handle/plan, uploads block data, calls the transpose-free QMR core, downloads X and frees resources. The core performs two TFQMR half-steps with sparse multiplications and per-RHS residual/breakdown tracking. Solution sparsity is prescribed by the caller, so a restricted X pattern is not equivalent to an unrestricted dense solve. Block sizes must have been compiled into the CUDA backend. Fortran patterns are one-based; block transposition flags are n/t, not an arbitrary conjugate-transpose operator. ITERATIONS/RESIDUAL are input limits and output reports. Helper CheckError uses STOP on many failures despite an IERR argument; core completion can include breakdown-stopped RHSs, so verify the reported and independently computed residual even after a successful status. Review covers the square-block convenience API and selected recurrence/stopping paths, not all precisions or block configurations.

The public dense Cholesky factorization builds the lower factor from the symmetric positive-definite input, followed by public forward and transposed-backward substitution helpers to solve a system. A%BW limits accessed off-diagonals; use a bandwidth covering the mathematical matrix. The code uses default REAL, calls plotting helpers inside arithmetic loops, and assumes Dense_Type allocation/grid/plot state has already been initialized. It does not pivot, verify symmetry/positive definiteness, or return an INFO status: negative square-root arguments or zero pivots are not a controlled failure protocol. The outer educational Cholesky demo constructs a discretized grid system rather than consuming arbitrary caller matrices. Review covers factor/substitution source paths, not a production solver API or validated residual.

local.name: HPCSeriesCore
local.description: Fortran-backed statistical reductions, quantiles, rolling summaries and anomaly-analysis kernels.

classifications.notes: The README documents Fortran/C/C++ kernels exposed through Python tooling, including reductions, robust summaries and rolling analysis. Reported speedups and cross-backend consistency were not reproduced; this is statistical computing rather than a general-purpose physical simulator.

The public SAFE-mode HPCS_MEDIAN/MAD/QUANTILE entries provide nonparametric location, dispersion and quantile summaries. They copy inputs, select order statistics by quickselect, average middle values for even-size medians, and interpolate quantiles with h=1+(n-1)*q. MAD is the raw median absolute deviation without a Gaussian consistency multiplier. SAFE mode propagates NaN with HPCS_SUCCESS rather than omitting it; callers must check both status and finiteness. Invalid n/q/mode returns do not promise an initialized numeric output, and NaN q is not rejected by ordinary range comparisons. Very large finite values can overflow middle-value averaging or interpolation differences. Explicit SAFE selection avoids the thread-local global mode; FAST/deterministic branches are not numerically validated here. Review covers public dispatch and SAFE calculations, not performance or rounding-error certification.

classifications.notes: HPCS_ROLLING_MEDIAN applies a trailing nonlinear median filter to a one-dimensional sequence. The SAFE path fills the first WINDOW-1 outputs with quiet NaN, then copies each complete window and calls the SAFE scalar median. This is a nonlinear filter, not a symmetric linear moving average or a centered window. NaN within a window propagates into its output, and no missing-value omission or boundary padding is performed. Require 1<=WINDOW<=N and an N-element output. Inner status is not propagated after each median call; the valid-window path finally returns HPCS_SUCCESS. The implementation allocates/copies window buffers and is not an O(n) sliding-order-statistic method. Review covers SAFE dispatch/window semantics, not all rolling anomaly/MAD algorithms or performance.

DLININT1 evaluates piecewise-linear interpolation on strictly monotone coordinates, with exact sentinel handling and optional removal of missing input values. The selected sketch uses ascending coordinates, ICYCX=0 and IOPT=0: no extrapolation is performed; out-of-range outputs and intervals touching missing data stay XMSG. Provide NXI>=2, NXO>=1 and separate work arrays, conservatively NXI2>=NXI+2; supported IOPT values are 0/1, with no rejection of other values. Independently validate coordinates and retained sample count: missing-value filtering can leave fewer than two nodes while the interpolation kernel accesses a pair. Single output coordinates are treated as ascending by the validator, so decreasing inputs with a single query can be rejected. DLINMSG separately fills interior missing runs on equally spaced sample indices in place. Its length threshold applies to interior and leading gaps, but the trailing MFLAG<0 continuation branch ignores MPTCRT. All-missing input remains missing. Missing values use exact sentinel equality, not NaN semantics. Cyclic extension and the internal short-gap optimization are outside the selected calling paths.

classifications.notes: DLININT2 performs separable linear interpolation on a rectilinear two-dimensional grid: X interpolation of each input row followed by Y interpolation of the intermediate field. FI is dimensioned (NXI,NYI), FO (NXO,NYO). Require at least two nodes on each input axis, nonempty output axes, strictly monotone coordinates with matching input/output direction, finite exact missing sentinel, and supported IOPT=0/1. The reviewed calling path uses ascending complete data, ICYCX=0, IOPT=0 and separate NXI+2 work arrays. IER=1 reports dimensions, 2 X-coordinate validation and 3 Y validation. Outputs outside the coordinate ranges or lacking valid bracketing values remain missing. Filtering IOPT=1 can leave fewer than two valid nodes and must be guarded by the caller; it is not a scattered-data method, conservative remapper or missing-data extrapolator. The same direction flag is reused after both coordinate checks and passed into both interpolation stages: use axes with the same direction, as in the sketch; independently increasing X and decreasing Y is not safely supported by that implementation.

classifications.notes: COMPUTE_LANCZOS_WEIGHTS constructs an odd-length symmetric windowed-sinc FIR filter. PASS_TYPE=1 normalizes low-pass weights to unit sum; 2 forms the high-pass delta complement. CUTOFF_FREQ is in cycles per sample and must lie strictly between 0 and 0.5; NWT must be odd and >=3. IERR=1/2/3/4/5 reports short/even window, invalid cutoff, near-zero normalization or unsupported pass type; do not apply weights after failure. APPLY_FILTER_1D reflects indices once at each boundary, requiring N>1 and half-window <=N-1; larger windows can access outside DATA. APPLY_FILTER_1D_PERIODIC wraps with MODULO and requires N>0. Use separate input/output arrays, generated symmetric weights and finite complete data: there is no missing/NaN policy or application status. The routines use REAL(8), which must be matched to the compiler build, rather than a portable named kind. This classification covers symmetric linear filtering, not a spectral estimator or certified frequency-response design.

classifications.notes: COMPUTE_S_VALUE sums pairwise signs in a clean ordered scalar series to obtain the Mann-Kendall S statistic. COMPUTE_BASE_VARIANCE copies and sorts the series, then computes the conventional independent-observation variance with equal-value tie correction. Both are public components of sequence analysis: these two entries do not return a p-value, significance decision, continuity-corrected Z or serial-correlation correction, and they do not establish general stationarity. Require finite, missing-free REAL64 data and a distinct sorted workspace with at least SIZE(Y) entries. Exact equality defines ties. S accumulation is quadratic in sample count; no missing filtering or time-coordinate vector is provided at these entry points. Preserve the original time ordering for S; sorting is only on the separate variance workspace.

classifications.notes: COMPUTE_SEN_SLOPE returns the median of all pairwise slopes (Y(j)-Y(i))/(j-i), a robust simple trend-slope estimate for unit-spaced observations. It constructs reciprocal index lags and dispatches to the public precomputed-lag variant, which materializes N*(N-1)/2 slopes and uses selection rather than a full sort; even counts average the two middle values. Require clean finite REAL64 data, a separate slope workspace of that size, and sample counts whose integer products/indices fit the compiler integer kind. N<2 returns quiet NaN. This is a slope per sample interval, not a full regression result: no intercept, confidence interval, p-value, time-coordinate array or missing-value removal is returned. Removing gaps before calling changes the time spacing and therefore the problem. Memory and pair construction are quadratic; no large-series performance claim was executed.

The public ARMA_ACVF function forms theoretical autocovariances for a supplied causal ARMA model using a state transition/loading representation and fixed-point iteration of the stationary state covariance. It then propagates lag vectors to extract covariance at lags zero through MAX_LAG. These are model-implied covariances, not estimates from a sample. The sketch uses a stable AR(1), positive innovation variance and explicitly allocated empty MA coefficients. Invalid lag/variance returns an empty array; covariance iteration is capped and a failure returns HUGE-valued entries rather than a general status. A finite-value test alone does not reject that finite sentinel, and this routine does not independently prove model stability. Review covers state representation, iterative covariance and lag extraction, not the many unrelated translated time-series packages in the repository.

procedures.summary: Public theoretical ARMA autocovariance calculation returning an allocated zero-based lag array.
procedures.usage:
use kind_mod, only: dp
use itsmr_mod, only: itsmr_arma_model_t,arma_acvf
type(itsmr_arma_model_t) :: model
real(dp),allocatable :: covariance(:)
allocate(model%ar(1),model%ma(0)); model%ar=[0.5_dp]
model%innovation_variance=1._dp
covariance=arma_acvf(model,4)
if(size(covariance)/=5) error stop "invalid covariance result shape"
if(any(abs(covariance)>=huge(1._dp))) error stop "covariance iteration failed"

classifications.notes: The public BURG_FIT helper estimates univariate autoregressive coefficients by forward/backward prediction-error recursion. polynomial_arnoldi::gmres builds a Krylov basis using twice-applied modified Gram-Schmidt, applies Givens rotations to a Hessenberg least-squares problem and updates X through a triangular solve, restarting when the subspace fills. D2 records this linear-system solver implementation. The public API is hardwired to external SpecialMatrices::Poisson2D, not a general dense/sparse matrix or arbitrary operator callback, so no unrestricted matrix-storage subclass is inferred without a dependency implementation review. The tolerance is internal ATOL+RTOL*NORM(B), with no caller tolerance/status dummy. A zero RHS is normalized before an early-exit check, and the total iteration cap is tested only at outer-cycle boundaries using <=; a full cycle can exceed it. Happy-breakdown/zero rotations and triangular pivots need independent validation. It prints a final true residual but returns X even if the budget is exhausted. Polynomial-preconditioned variants/root extraction and dependency kernels are outside this review. No solve or convergence experiment was run.

local.name: QuadProg modern Fortran
local.description: Active-set solution of strictly convex dense quadratic programs, with constrained least-squares helpers.

classifications.notes: The README describes a modernization of Turlach Quadprog using BLAS/LAPACK and currently real64 arithmetic. It targets strictly convex, small to moderate dense problems; indefinite/nonconvex QP support is not inferred. Its standard-compliance and performance claims were not tested here.

The standard qp_problem constructor copies and Cholesky-factorizes a positive-definite quadratic matrix, stores its inverse triangular factor, and records linear equality/inequality rows. solve_standard_qp packs constraints and calls the private qpgen2 active-set implementation. The reviewed driver starts at the unconstrained quadratic minimizer, selects violated constraints, computes primal/dual steps, adds constraints with Givens rotations and removes constraints when a dual step requires it. G2e1 records positive-definite-Hessian quadratic programming; no indefinite or merely semidefinite extension is inferred. The objective is 0.5*x-transpose*P*x - x-transpose*q, with A*x=b and C*x>=d; sign and row orientation matter. The constructor checks dimensions but does not propagate TRTRI INFO, and its Cholesky call has no returned err argument. The unconstrained wrapper branch sets X and success but never assigns result%obj; the sketch therefore uses a constrained case. The boolean success loses detailed driver failure information, so validate returned feasibility/stationarity independently. Compact storage, least-squares/LASSO variants and external numerical kernels are not audited. No QP or author tests were executed. The linked inequality test transposes C despite the constructor row-storage interface; that example orientation needs checking and is not copied into the sketch.

The constructor stores a factorization rather than the original P; reconstruct the object when changing P and preserve originals for residual/KKT checks.

HankelJ0Transform/HankelJ1Transform evaluate fixed logarithmic digital-filter sums of a kernel callback at lambda_i=10**(a+(i-1)*s)/r, then divide the weighted sum by r. Fast variants use shorter tables. J records numerical Hankel integral transforms; the original GAMS J subtree has no dedicated Hankel child, so neither Fourier nor Laplace classification is invented. The exact convention is integral_0^infinity K(lambda)*J_order(r*lambda) d(lambda), without an additional lambda measure factor. Callers using the common lambda*d(lambda) convention must incorporate lambda into K. R must be positive and finite, with a kernel defined over the sampled positive range; extreme R can overflow/underflow sampling. No error estimate, convergence status or adaptive quadrature is returned. Ogata/Bessel-zero paths are not included in this digital-filter review. No transform or published example was run.

SKYSOLVE solves a symmetric skyline/profile-stored system by unpivoted LDL-transpose factorization, forward reduction and back substitution. MSKY locates each diagonal in the packed upper profile, and A/B are overwritten by factors/intermediate values/solutions. The selected full-system usage sets NEQ1=NEQ and IFLAG=3; other flags split phases, and NEQ1<NEQ supports reduction outside this selected sketch. The routine replaces zero or sufficiently small pivots and records corrections in DCOR, with IERR=-3 indicating singular/poor conditioning correction; positive IERR=3 flags negative factor diagonals. This is not an unrestricted pivoted indefinite solver, and a corrected system is not silently equivalent to the original. Initialize all DCOR entries before factorization: the preliminary loop resets only its first column while later negative-flag suppression can inspect other columns. Use positive EPS/SCALE and valid skyline bounds, compatible BLAS/default-integer ABI, full SAM dependencies and a valid log unit or LPU<0 to suppress diagnostics. Preserve originals and check IERR/NND plus an independently recomputed residual. Negative IFLAG suppression and reduced-system semantics are not certified by this source review.

msky=[1,3]; dcor=0.d0

The public CHOLDC/CHOLSL pair factors and solves a real symmetric positive-definite dense system. CHOLDC reads the original upper triangle, stores strict lower factors in A and diagonal factors in P, leaving the upper input triangle in place. CHOLSL performs forward/back substitution using those factors. Require 1<=N<=NP, conforming REAL64 arrays and positive definiteness; there is no pivoting or symmetry test. Nonpositive computed pivots set INFO=1 and return incomplete factors; check before solving. CHOLSL treats INFO as input/output and returns immediately only when it equals 1, so pass the factorization status, not an uninitialized integer. Source comments credit Numerical Recipes; this mapping is source inspection, not a claim about complete third-party rights or numerical stability for arbitrary matrices.

classifications.notes: MOINDRES_CARRES fits a scalar response at supplied two-coordinate sample locations using user model F and parameter-derivative DF callbacks. It periodically rebuilds the Jacobian (every ten iterations), forms normal equations, inflates each diagonal by 1.5, solves with Cholesky and applies a fixed RELAX-scaled correction to the first NB_VAR_DER parameters. This is a particular damped, periodically updated Gauss-Newton-like implementation, not a complete adaptive Levenberg-Marquardt/trust-region API. Require 0<NB_VAR_DER<=NB_VAR and compatible derivatives/design rank; callbacks must match the linked signatures and their parameter array is declared INTENT(INOUT). The relative correction stop divides by ABS(BETA) without zero guards, and there is no maximum-iteration limit or complete failed-factorization exit. INFO reports the local Cholesky state, not a convergence certificate; the same-buffer solve finding from the linear fitter applies. The commented calling contract is not recommended for unattended execution before adding termination/failure guards.

For the explicitly selected finite line element, SHAPEFUNC constructs nodal Lagrange polynomial basis functions and EVAL evaluates them at a requested reference coordinate. An interpolated value is the dot product of nodal data with returned basis values. This E1b mapping is restricted to the univariate polynomial case; it does not conflate reference-element shape functions with scattered-data mesh generation or global spline fitting. Node ordering can be permuted through NODES, so the sketch forms data from the returned COORDS instead of assuming a particular edge/interior order. SET requires a cubature object from the separate fortran_cubatures dependency; invalid setup can ERROR STOP. Review covers finite Lagrange line construction/evaluation, not every simplex/serendipity/infinite-element variant or an executed interpolation result.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound reference-element basis/value/derivative evaluator; all result arrays are required.
procedures.usage:
use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
use cubatures, only: cubature,CUB_LIN
use shapefuncs, only: shapefunc
type(cubature) :: q
type(shapefunc) :: sf
real(real64),allocatable :: nodal(:),basis(:),derv(:,:),curv(:,:,:)
real(real64) :: value,first,second
q=cubature(CUB_LIN,4)
sf=shapefunc(q,2)
allocate(nodal(sf%nnodes),basis(sf%nnodes),derv(1,sf%nnodes),curv(1,1,sf%nnodes))
nodal=sf%coords(1,:)**2
call sf%eval([0.25_real64],basis,derv,curv)
value=dot_product(nodal,basis)
first=dot_product(nodal,derv(1,:))
second=dot_product(nodal,curv(1,1,:))
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Finite line/polynomial example using the separate cubatures dependency and REAL64. classifications.notes: The broad mapping uses the README together with documented predict/update interfaces in forapollo_estimate.f90. FA_KF_PREDICT applies x=F*x and P=F*P*F-transpose+Q. FA_KF_UPDATE computes innovations, gates individual measurements by squared innovation over diagonal innovation variance, extracts the retained full covariance submatrix, solves the SPD innovation system, and applies a Joseph-form covariance update. All C-boundary matrices are flat row-major, not ordinary Fortran column-major arrays. VALIDITY is output: +1 fused, 0 skipped above 9, -1 rejected above 16 (or degenerate diagonal); if no values are fused, state/covariance remain at prediction with INFO=0. Cholesky solve failure maps to INFO=4; invalid dimensions to 3. Covariance consistency/finite values are not comprehensively checked. Some helper calls alias input/output arrays despite differing INTENTs and need compiler/alias-contract review. The sketch uses a scalar model to avoid layout ambiguity. Review covers the linear KF path and matrix-solve helper, not every EKF/UKF/particle-filter variant.

DPCG uses diagonal-preconditioned conjugate gradients for a symmetric positive-definite sparse operator. Nonzero usable diagonals and SPD of the complete operator/preconditioner are caller assumptions, not validated. The initial absolute L1 residual threshold is 1e-13, with subsequent stopping on a relative L1 residual against SOR(IFI). No zero/near-breakdown guards protect all PCG denominators. LININTERPOL searches for neighboring abscissae and evaluates an affine weighted pair, using a saved interval index for subsequent calls. The implemented interpolation is univariate piecewise linear. Despite header prose promising zero outside the table, those returns/assignments are commented out; search conditions may evaluate negative/out-of-range elements and the final formula extrapolates after clamping. The nold<1 check does not reject a one-point table. Even an in-range query on a two-point table can first read beyond the upper end because the saved-index clamp sets nold-1 then accesses ilastnum+1. Resetting ILASTVAL sets ILASTNUM=-1; a subsequent upward search can begin at -2 and read a negative index even for an in-range query. More table points do not repair this. The sketch records the interface only; the search requires repair and checked testing before use. This review does not establish flux conservation or review the spectral-resampling dispatcher.

procedures.summary: External subroutine using numeric RP=8 and IB=4 kinds from ModDataType. Table/query/output vectors use dummy lower bound zero; NOLD_VEC/NXYVALUE are explicit lengths. ILASTVAL is input/output (negative resets saved search state), ISKEEPON is output and VERBOSITY optional. An explicit interface is required.
procedures.signature:
CALL LINinterpol(XX_VALUE, YY_VALUE, NXYVALUE, XOLD_VEC, YOLD_VEC, &
     NOLD_VEC, ILASTVAL, ISKEEPON, VERBOSITY)
procedures.usage:
use ModDataType, only: rp,ib
! Supply the linked explicit interface including OPTIONAL VERBOSITY.
real(rp) :: x(0:2), y(0:2), query(0:0), value(0:0)
integer(ib) :: last,status
x=[0.0_rp,1.0_rp,2.0_rp]; y=2.0_rp*x
query=[0.5_rp]; last=-999_ib
call LINinterpol(query,value,1_ib,x,y,3_ib,last,status,0_ib)
! Inspect STATUS, but it does not certify bounds safety or accuracy.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. This is an interface sketch, not a recommended safe general interpolator. The source search/bounds findings need repair and checked testing. Saved ILASTNUM makes the core nonreentrant; resetting ILASTVAL is essential after changing tables. The public INTERP_LINEAR generic implements adjacent-point piecewise-linear interpolation for scalar/vector queries; INTERP_SPLINE builds cubic piecewise-polynomial coefficients and evaluates them. Require equal nonempty X/Y lengths, finite strictly increasing distinct X and at least two points for the spline. Linear queries outside the interval clamp to endpoint values. Spline outside queries use reflection about the endpoint and a reflected value, rather than the same constant policy; farther outside reflected arguments may themselves leave the interval. The cubic helper solves a tridiagonal coefficient system with its own endpoint conditions, not a user-selectable natural/clamped boundary API. No status argument validates sorting, duplicate nodes or model error. The defining helper source credits an earlier Godunov interpolation implementation; component provenance remains scoped.

classifications.notes: The public INTERP_BILINEAR generic selects a double-precision rectangular tensor-grid path which brackets each query on two ordered coordinate axes, linearly combines four neighboring values and preserves a missing sentinel where interpolation is unavailable. This is a source review of the gridded overload, not the separate paired-query or nearest-neighbor variants, scattered triangulation or conservative remapping.

classifications.notes: The public LOESS_SMOOTH generic regularizes an irregular series onto a uniform grid, calls the native LOWESS local-linear smoother with two robustness iterations, then linearly maps the smoothed series back. It omits Y equal to the chosen missing sentinel, uses the minimum consecutive X spacing to allocate the uniform grid, and derives F from L, DX and grid size; require sorted distinct X, at least two points and a practical minimum spacing to avoid huge allocation. L is not simply a point-count window; the code uses (2*L+1) in both its availability gate and fraction formula. It prints L/F and returns the sentinel when its point-count gate fails. The double overload explicitly casts data/window to default real before computation; its output is not a full double-precision LOWESS calculation. The same repository offers FILTER_GAUSSIAN via normalized sampled Gaussian weights and reflected boundary patches. Explicitly supply positive DX: the float path starts with SIGMAP=SIGMAP and only assigns a value when DX is present, and the double wrapper evaluates REAL(DX) without a PRESENT guard. The double Gaussian overload also reduces the field to REAL(4). Kernel width must fit the convolution implementation; its four-pass fallback is not an unlimited large-kernel remedy. These are smoothing implementations, not uncertainty estimates, missing-NaN detection or a precision guarantee.

classifications.notes: The public CONVOLVE routine accumulates weighted two-dimensional patches after reflecting each side once. Its implementation multiplies weights in their stored orientation without reversing them: for general asymmetric weights this is a correlation-style operation; symmetric Gaussian weights implement the corresponding convolution. H2/J2-style scalar integral or Fourier transform APIs are not inferred from the name. Inputs, weights and outputs are REAL(4), output must match input shape and weights should have odd extents so patches conform. Each weight extent must be strictly less than the corresponding input extent+1 (checked with an assertion that can terminate). Without MASK it is a direct weighted patch sum. With MASK, excluded centers remain unchanged and weights of excluded neighbors are redistributed equally over included neighbors; this is not a general theorem of global field conservation. The kernel is not automatically normalized and no sentinel/NaN policy is provided.

classifications.notes: HGRAD returns the magnitude of a centered finite-difference horizontal gradient, not a two-component gradient array. Its private helpers divide by 2*DX and copy neighboring interior derivatives to boundaries. Require positive finite DX and at least three points in each direction. A concrete boundary-index defect is present: D_DX assigns DU(NY,:) rather than DU(NX,:), so nonsquare grids can leave the last row wrong or address beyond the first extent. Restrict the sketch to square grids or repair this before general rectangular use. NORM=.TRUE. divides by MAXVAL(ABS(DU)) without a zero guard, so constant fields may divide by zero. Review records the local stencil and its limitations, not a general nonuniform/curvilinear gradient, convergence study or corrected implementation.

classifications.notes: The public CREATE_POLYGON and POINT_IN_POLYGON generics build a planar polygon from coordinate arrays and classify query points by parity of ray/edge intersections. The selected constructors assemble sequential edges closing the polygon; the query creates a default-real point and counts intersections over stored index pairs. Supply matching finite coordinate vectors, at least three sensible vertices and a valid simple polygon. The implementation perturbs a query Y equal to a vertex Y by a fixed EPS=1e-5, and slope/vertical-edge comparisons use floating-point thresholds. Consequently boundary/vertex inclusion, scale dependence and degenerate/self-intersecting polygons are not certified exact predicates. This is planar point containment, not spherical geometry, triangulation or polygon Boolean operations. Allocatable polygon components carry copied points/edge indices; the explicit FREE_POLYGON helper is private.

MCM returns the arithmetic mean of each column of a double-precision matrix by straightforward sequential summation and division by the number of rows. Calling with one column provides a univariate raw-data location summary; multiple columns are treated independently, not as a joint model. Require N>0, positive column count, matching storage and finite prefiltered data. There is no missing-value, overflow, compensated-summation or recoverable status policy. This records the implemented descriptive statistic, not an inferential estimate with uncertainty or a robustness guarantee.

procedures.summary: External arithmetic column-mean routine; one-column use gives a scalar mean.
procedures.usage:
double precision :: x(4,1),mean(1)
x(:,1)=[1.d0,2.d0,3.d0,4.d0]
call MCM(4,1,x,mean)
! No status or missing-data handling is returned.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Require nonempty finite columns; naive summation can lose accuracy for large offsets or cancellation.

classifications.notes: VARIAN computes sample variance as (SUM(X**2)-SUM(X)**2/N)/(N-1); VOLAT calls it and takes a square root except that variance below a fixed 1e-30 threshold is returned as zero. Both set INFO=-2 for fewer than two observations. The one-pass difference-of-squares formula is vulnerable to cancellation and can produce a negative computed variance for poorly scaled inputs; VOLAT then silently returns zero rather than reporting that loss of accuracy. Require finite data and inspect scale/conditioning independently. These routines are raw-data dispersion summaries, not confidence intervals, robust scale estimators or an accurate two-pass variance implementation.

procedures.summary: External sample variance with N-1 denominator and a cancellation-prone one-pass formula.
procedures.usage:
double precision :: x(4),variance
integer :: info
x=[1.d0,2.d0,3.d0,4.d0]
call VARIAN(4,x,variance,info)
if(info/=0) error stop "inspect variance input length"
! Independently assess cancellation for large-offset data.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Finite raw-data fragment; INFO=0 is not an accuracy check.

classifications.notes: SKEWN and KURTOS accept a raw sample plus a caller-supplied mean and variance, accumulate third/fourth central powers and apply explicit finite-sample formulas. SKEWN requires N>=3 and variance>=1e-15; KURTOS requires N>=4 and variance>1e-15. The mean/variance must describe the same sample and use a compatible convention; these are not independently estimated inside the routines. SKEWN initializes INFO=0, but KURTOS assigns INFO only on failure and leaves it unchanged on success: initialize it before calling. The header labels the kurtosis unbiased excess kurtosis, but the hand-coded expression is retained as implementation evidence rather than certifying equivalence to the usual bias-corrected estimator. Neither formula, overflow behavior nor sample distribution was numerically validated. These are descriptive shape calculations, not normality tests or confidence intervals.

classifications.notes: COVM computes column means, centers N by P observations through EMPCOV and forms the sample covariance; CORM normalizes it to a correlation matrix. Require N>=2, P>=1 and finite complete data. COVM needs DWORK(P*(N+1)); CORM actually needs P*(N+P+2), as its header states, despite a shorter conflicting workspace comment. CORM returns INFO=-5 when a variance is <=1e-30. The underlying COVR scales by 1./FLOAT(N-1), evaluated in default real before assignment, so this factor can have lower precision than the double arrays. COVCOR and CORCOV convert a supplied covariance/correlation matrix and standard deviations; COVCOR rejects diagonals <=1e-30, while CORCOV does not validate a correlation matrix or standard deviations. These are descriptive/representation operations, not hypothesis tests, missing-data estimation or certification of positive definiteness. Although some headers mention a mean vector, COVM has no separate named mean output; its first P workspace entries contain the means.

if(info/=0) error stop "inspect covariance status"

classifications.notes: TENSORK and TENSORKK calculate selected slices of third- and fourth-order empirical central co-moments from multivariate raw data. The scalar FZERO overload dispatches to NEWTON_INTERPOL, which uses two nearby initial function values and secant interpolation to solve a scalar equation without a supplied derivative. It is not a bracketing Brent solver despite other optimization routines in the toolbox. The selected cosine-minus-x example is a nonpolynomial equation and supports F1b. X is overwritten; the optional CHECK_RETURN is false on a residual-based return and true on stagnation or exhausted iterations. Shared module tolerance/iteration settings affect calls. The iteration has no interval or domain safeguard and can encounter a vanishing secant denominator; callers must supply a valid initial neighborhood and independently check the final residual. Review covers the scalar generic/implementation, not the distinct vector Broyden overload or global root isolation.

logical :: failed
x=0.5d0

if(failed) error stop "root iteration stagnated or reached its limit"
print *,x,residual(x)
contains
function residual(x) result(value)

classifications.notes: The scalar POLY_INTERPOL generic evaluates the global Lagrange interpolating polynomial through supplied univariate nodes. The implementation builds each product basis directly and sums YI times the bases; it is not piecewise interpolation, a spline or a barycentric implementation. Equal node/value counts are asserted, but duplicate nodes are not rejected before division. Distinct well-scaled nodes and modest degree are appropriate for the calling sketch; polynomial interpolation does not imply stable extrapolation or freedom from Runge oscillation. The node/value dummy arrays have lower bound zero, which is reflected in the usage fragment. Review covers scalar evaluation and generic visibility, not the separate vector-query implementation or fitted-error guarantees.

classifications.notes: LEGENDRE generates Gauss-Legendre abscissas and weights on a finite interval, selecting order from the output-array size. It uses symmetric initial root guesses, recurrence evaluation of Legendre polynomials/derivatives, Newton corrections and symmetric mapping of roots/weights to the target interval. The concrete mapping is quadrature service routine H2c: this API does not itself accept or integrate a user function, and the sketch performs the fixed-order weighted sum separately. Array-size mismatch or exhausted root iterations invokes the toolbox error handler; no numerical status is returned. The source caps root iteration at ten steps. A positive order and increasing finite endpoints are assumed by the sketch. The source explicitly identifies Numerical Recipes adaptation, which is retained as a licensing/provenance qualification rather than silently treating every component as original GPL code.

local.name: ANN Fortran interface
local.description: Fortran/C interface to the C++ ANN exact and approximate nearest-neighbor library.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly expands ANN as Approximate Nearest Neighbors, not artificial neural networks. The underlying algorithms/data structures are C++, with Fortran access provided here. Approximation guarantees, high-dimensional performance and current build compatibility were not checked.

The Fortran ANN module forwards point-cloud construction and single-query k-nearest-neighbor search to the C++ ANN kd-tree. The bridge copies a Fortran point matrix with ROWS points and COLS coordinates using input offset I+J*ROWS; QUERY has DIM coordinates, compatible with the built tree. The backend uses EPS to relax search and returns zero-based point indices with squared Euclidean distances; EPS=0 selects exact search under the native algorithm. Require 1<=K<=ROWS and nonnegative EPS. Important reviewed defects prevent treating this as a ready-to-use ownership API: NNIDX/DISTS pointers are written into but never allocated by the bridge, so callers must supply live K-entry buffers; C++ temporary arrays are freed with scalar DELETE rather than matching array deallocation; the public Fortran destroy routine only nulls its handle, with its C destroy call commented out; construction point storage ownership is not released by that public path. The C destroy declaration also passes a pointer reference while the C++ definition takes a pointer value. Native search state uses file-scope globals, so independent concurrent search is not assumed. This is a mapping of the implemented kd-tree bridge with defects recorded, not a successful build, leak-free lifecycle, numerical verification or batch-query interface.

The public NEURALNET%BACKPROP method differentiates the scalar network loss with respect to packed weights and optional biases by reverse propagation through activation derivatives and BLAS products. This is analytic chain-rule/backpropagation differentiation, not finite differences or a general source-transforming AD tool. WEIGHTS/BIAS are inout buffers: their entry values become model parameters and their returned contents become gradients. DATA uses predictor rows plus one target row and observation columns. The LOSS callback supplies derivative with respect to prediction, despite its name; the supplied MSE returns 2*(prediction-actual), with averaging performed inside BACKPROP. Activation callbacks distinguish forward value from derivative with FW. The method mutates network intermediate state and reports selected dimension failures via IERR. EVALUATE declares IERR INTENT(OUT) but does not set it on success; BACKPROP immediately tests that undefined value and likewise lacks an explicit final success assignment. Repair the success-status contract before relying on returned gradients. if(ierr/=0) error stop "network gradient failed"

classifications.notes: The public OPT_MOD::ADAM module subroutine updates an unconstrained vector using a supplied gradient callback, exponential first/second moments and bias-corrected adaptive steps. classifications.notes: NEURALNET%TRAIN defaults to MSE, which returns 2*(PRED-ACTUAL), the derivative of a squared residual. NN_TL computes a Jacobian-vector product for the configured dense network while also returning the nonlinear output; NN_AD computes the transpose-Jacobian action on a supplied output seed. They apply analytic activation derivatives and ordinary/transposed BLAS GEMM through the layer sequence, recomputing nonlinear trajectories for the reverse path. Parameters are fixed module data; these interfaces differentiate inputs, not train weights or differentiate arbitrary Fortran source. Architecture constants in YONOGWDNN fix input/output sizes, width and hidden depth. Allocate/populate INPUT/HIDDEN/OUTPUT and batch-shaped bias arrays before any call; KLON must agree with storage. PARKIND1 selects NNP=DOUB in the inspected build. No argument-shape/status validation or derivative-accuracy certificate is exposed. Review covers the input tangent/adjoint paths and author setup contract, not execution of the supplied Taylor/dot-product tests.

SVDFIT forms a weighted linear least-squares design from the built-in FUNCS1 ENTRY, divides each row and response by SIG(i), factors it through local SVDCMP, zeros singular values below 1e-14 of the maximum, and applies SVBKSB. It is linear in fitted coefficients of a permutationally invariant polynomial basis in exp(-distance), not nonlinear parameter fitting or a generic callback-based fitter. PREPOT must previously initialize saved basis tables, MPI state and COMMON model/training distances as in the application driver; FUNCS1 is an ENTRY in that initialized routine. Require positive finite weights/scales, 1<=MA<=NDATA<=MAXDATA, MA<=MAXTERM and MA<=MAXDATA for local SVD buffers, MP>=NDATA and NP>=MA, matching includes/COMMON layout and sufficient memory for U(MP,NP), V(NP,NP) and large static model arrays. The safest selected dimensions are MP=NDATA, NP=MA, matching the author call and avoiding the oversized NP dummy contract in SVBKSB. Only coefficients A are returned: CHISQ, U/V/W are local despite stale comments suggesting outputs. There is no exposed convergence/rank/error status; SVDCMP has a finite iteration loop but its nonconvergence PAUSE diagnostic is commented out. Recompute weighted residuals and assess rank independently; this is not a certified robust or converged fit.

! Only A is returned. Independently recompute weighted residuals/rank.

The public SequentialNeuralNetwork tangent-linear and adjoint bindings propagate perturbations/cotangents through sequential layers. Unlike an input-only Jacobian API, DP includes packed parameter perturbations and the adjoint returns both parameter and input cotangents. Dense layers pack biases first, followed by the reshaped weight matrix. Call APPLY_FORWARD for the same MEMBER and unchanged parameters/base input first: layer forward_input and activation state supply the linearization trajectory. APPLY_ADJOINT may overwrite the supplied DY; keep a copy for dot-product comparisons. Batch-member storage is mutable, and no automatic shape/member/status checks should be inferred. The inspected dense/tanh path supports a smooth derivative example; dropout modes and ReLU at zero need separate interpretation. Review covers sequential dispatch, dense chain-rule products and tanh derivative implementation, not the complete layer catalogue or executed consistency tests.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound state-plus-parameter tangent action after a forward trajectory has been stored.

use fnn_common, only: rk,ik
use fnn_network_sequential, only: SequentialNeuralNetwork,snn_fromfile
type(SequentialNeuralNetwork) :: network
! A valid author-format dense/tanh model file and allocated matching arrays are required.
network=snn_fromfile(1_ik,"model.txt")
! DP has network%get_num_parameters() entries; X/DX and Y/DY match input/output sizes.
call network%apply_forward(.false.,1_ik,x,y)
call network%apply_tangent_linear(1_ik,dp,dx,dy)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-allocation fragment; model.txt is a prerequisite, not supplied by this sketch. Preserve the forward trajectory per member, match fnn_common RK/IK, and avoid overwriting that state before derivative calls. No model import, layer derivative or tangent test was run.

ADAPGAUSS generates an M-point Gauss-Legendre rule and adaptively bisects a finite interval, comparing a parent rule value with the sum of child values. The callback is a SUBROUTINE FUN(X,PAR1,PAR2,VAL), despite some comments calling it a function. Use matching REAL*8 parameter arrays/callback arguments; do not infer type-safe arbitrary integer user-data passing from historical comments. M must be positive and <=100 because local node/weight arrays have 100 entries. EPS>0 is compared independently against each accepted leaf difference: it is not divided among leaves and therefore is not a guaranteed global absolute-error bound. Depth is limited to 200 and the work loop to 100000 steps; IER=8/16 indicates those respective limits and RINT can be partial. MAXREC/NUMINT describe the traversal, not proof of error control. The rule differences can miss unresolved singularities/oscillations; no special weighted-integrand or rigorous error certificate is implied.

procedures.summary: External finite-interval adaptive Gauss-Legendre integrator with local tolerance comparisons.

! With a matching subroutine FUN(X,PAR1,PAR2,VAL), REAL*8 arrays/controls,

call adapgauss(ier,a,b,fun,par1,par2,m,eps,integral,maxrec,numint)
if(ier/=0) error stop "quadrature stopped at a subdivision limit"
! Assess total error independently; EPS is used on every accepted leaf.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Post-callback-setup fragment. No integrand, error estimate or subdivision limit was executed.

classifications.notes: LEGEWHTS constructs nodes and optional weights for a fixed-order Gauss-Legendre rule on [-1,1]. It starts from cosine root approximations, uses up to ten Newton corrections and exploits symmetry; weights come from a sum-of-squared-Legendre orthogonality relation. IFWHTS=1 computes weights, 0 returns nodes alone. Choose the quadrature order yourself; no tolerance-driven integrand adaptation or error estimate is returned. Positive N and caller-owned TS/WHTS storage of at least N elements are required. The old dummy declarations TS(1)/WHTS(1) are indexed beyond their declared extent, a legacy source convention requiring attention under bounds/conformance checking. Newton termination is not reported by a separate status, so do not infer successful roots/weights for every order. The calling sketch shows how this rule would be applied to a smooth scalar integrand, not a checked polynomial-exactness test.

procedures.summary: External fixed-order Gauss-Legendre rule construction on [-1,1].
procedures.usage:
integer,parameter :: n=8
double precision :: nodes(n),weights(n),integral
call legewhts(n,nodes,weights,1)
integral=sum(weights*exp(nodes))
! This is a fixed-order rule; compare increasing orders independently.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Legacy array declarations need compatible compilation or assumed-size declaration repair before bounds-checked use. No nodes, weights, integral or Newton convergence was executed.

classifications.notes: LEGEPOL uses the Legendre three-term recurrence to return P_N(X), then computes its first derivative through N*(X*P_N-P_(N-1))/(X**2-1). Degree 0 and 1 have explicit value/derivative branches. Require N>=0; negative degree is not rejected. For N>=2, X=+/-1 gives a zero denominator and near-endpoint evaluation can lose derivative accuracy. Use interior finite arguments or separately supply mathematically appropriate endpoint limits; this pin does not implement such a special branch. This is evaluation of one Legendre polynomial and derivative, not evaluation of a whole fitted series, associated Legendre functions or a spherical-harmonic transform.

classifications.notes: The inspected executable minimizes a finite maximum of component functions, a generally nonsmooth multivariate objective. functmu builds a log-sum-exp smoothing from value-only functs callbacks, and MAINBOX performs derivative-free line searches while adapting the smoothing parameter. classifications.notes: The README documents minimum-radius coverings, polygon generation, Voronoi cells, Sutherland-Hodgman clipping and convex-polygon/circle intersections. The README documents minimum-radius coverings, polygon generation, Voronoi cells, Sutherland-Hodgman clipping and convex-polygon/circle intersections. It requires ALGENCAN, BLAS and HSL, with bundled GEOMETRY/GEOMPACK sources. These are generic geometric optimization problems; optimality, intersection degeneracies and paper results were not checked.

The main program minimizes x(n), the common ball radius, through an external bmalgencan::algencan call. evalc computes the uncovered-area constraint as total polygon area minus covered area, while evalg, evalj and evalhl supply objective gradient, geometric constraint derivatives and sparse Lagrangian-Hessian entries. The objective Hessian is explicitly zero. This establishes a specialized nonlinear constrained optimization implementation (G2h3), not a generic optimizer implemented in this repository. A smoothness-specific leaf is withheld: the geometry includes tolerances, deterministic small center perturbations, topology changes and zero-derivative fallbacks for invalid configurations. Merely exposing derivative callbacks does not establish a global C2 contract; a later review must also resolve the external solver constraint convention before selecting the equality/inequality branch. The Makefile requires external ALGENCAN 4, HSL and BLAS; its single driver and restart/initialization heuristics do not certify a global minimum. No solve, derivative formula or asymptotic bound was verified.

Public module subroutine for square nonlinear systems. Supply n residuals for n REAL(KIND=8) unknowns through evalr; x is updated and res, iter, fcnt and istop are returned. epsf controls the residual 2-norm, ndiis the acceleration interval and nhlim the history capacity. pdataptr is optional.
procedures.signature:
CALL dfsaneacc(evalr, n, x, res, epsf, maxit, ndiis, nhlim, &
               iter, fcnt, istop, pdataptr)
procedures.usage:
use bmdfsaneacc, only: dfsaneacc
! Define evalr with the rsub interface and initialize x and controls.
! Use a positive ndiis and suitable history capacity, e.g. nhlim=6.
call dfsaneacc(evalr, n, x, res, epsf, maxit, ndiis, nhlim, &
               iter, fcnt, istop)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; the optional data pointer is omitted here. If the residual callback needs data, pass a valid C_PTR as in the author example. Build bmqr and the numerical-library dependencies described in the Fortran README. Check istop and the residual norm. No new numerical execution was performed.

classifications.notes: bmdfsaneacc::dfsaneacc solves a square system: the residual callback maps x(n) to res(n), with no Jacobian callback. It combines residual-direction nonmonotone steps with QR-based sequential-secant acceleration built from iterate/residual history. Success requires dot_product(res,res)<=epsf**2, so epsf bounds the residual Euclidean norm; iteration exhaustion is a distinct return. F2 is already a GAMS leaf: there is no official derivative-free or acceleration child to add. Internal least-squares acceleration is not evidence for a general rectangular least-squares solver, and this does not enumerate all roots or certify uniqueness. The Fortran example supplies a three-variable exponential system; the reviewed Fortran path does not require running R or CUTEst. Memory/rank limits, singular cases and the author example were not tested.

local.name: Extrapolation Integration
local.description: Sampled-data quadrature with Richardson extrapolation and trapezoidal fallback.

classifications.notes: The README specifies equally spaced real/complex samples and returns the integral divided by the interval length, so callers must supply interval scaling themselves. Extrapolation requires 2^M+1 samples; other lengths use trapezoidal reduction, and a singleton is returned unchanged. Stated error orders and edge cases were not independently checked.

procedures.summary: Public generic array-reduction function. The inspected REAL(dp) binding accepts an assumed-shape vector and returns a scalar of the same kind; extrapol_rdp and its nested helpers are private implementation details. Supply equally spaced samples with 2**m+1 entries for the reviewed extrapolation path, and multiply the normalized result by the physical interval length.
procedures.usage:
use Extrapolation_Integration_Kinds, only: dp
use Extrapolation_Integration, only: extrapolation
! array is REAL(dp) with 2**m+1 equally spaced samples on [a,b].
result = (b - a) * extrapolation(array)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only. Initialize the samples and interval endpoints with compatible kinds. This function takes sampled values, not an integrand callback or error tolerance. The inspected non-dyadic fallback has the endpoint-weight discrepancy documented in the source review; the sketch deliberately uses the dyadic path. No accuracy or execution check was performed here. Other real/complex bindings are not newly certified by this interface review.

classifications.notes: The reviewed real(dp) extrapol_rdp path accepts equally spaced samples rather than an integrand callback, error tolerance or adaptive sampling request. It reorders 2^m+1 samples with endpoints first, constructs nested trapezoidal approximations and applies Richardson extrapolation. H2a1b2 is the nonautomatic finite-interval grid-quadrature leaf. The reduction is normalized to [0,1]; multiply by (b-a) for samples on [a,b], as the author sinc example does. A material fallback discrepancy was found by source inspection: non-dyadic sample counts are sent directly to trap_rdp, which half-weights array(1) and array(2), not the first and last samples in natural order. For [0,1/3,2/3,1] the displayed formula predicts 11/18 instead of the trapezoidal result 1/2; this is an arithmetic consequence of the source, not a compiled result. Singleton/two-point cases have separate branches; empty input and all accuracy claims remain unverified. No checked driver is supplied.

local.name: PowellOpt
local.description: Modern Fortran derivative-free optimization routines by M. J. D. Powell; the reviewed BOBYQA interface supports simple variable bounds.

classifications.notes: The public bobyqa_module::bobyqa minimizes a smooth real scalar function under lower/upper variable bounds without supplied derivatives. It builds quadratic interpolation models and uses a trust-region method, dispatching to private BOBYQB. The selected public interface has ten arguments: N,NPT,X,XL,XU,RHOBEG,RHOEND,IPRINT,MAXFUN,CALFUN; it allocates workspace internally. This differs from older external BOBYQA interfaces with a user workspace and from other forks with status/F outputs. N must be at least 2; N+2<=NPT<=(N+1)*(N+2)/2; NPT=2*N+1 is a suggested initial choice. Provide conforming REAL(wp) vectors X/XL/XU of length at least N. wp is REAL64 in the pinned kind_module. Require positive RHOEND<=RHOBEG and each bound interval at least 2*RHOBEG wide; scale variables appropriately. The wrapper can adjust the initial X away from bounds to construct its interpolation model. CALFUN(N,X,F) is a subroutine callback with default INTEGER N, assumed-shape REAL(wp) X(:) INTENT(IN), and scalar REAL(wp) F INTENT(OUT). X is overwritten by the best estimate; neither objective value nor convergence status is an output argument. Reevaluate the callback to obtain F and independently assess the result. Invalid NPT or insufficient bound spacing prints a diagnostic and returns; normal return alone is not a success certificate. IPRINT=0 suppresses ordinary iteration output but not those wrapper diagnostics. MAXFUN limits callback evaluations; there is no public counter/status result. This review inspects the public wrapper, callback declarations and precision selection, not every private interpolation/trust-region kernel. The illustrative calling program was not compiled or run for this independent review. The existing playground box-quadratic checked driver remains separately recorded and is not reclassified as a new independent numerical test.

procedures.summary: Public derivative-free box-constrained optimizer. Workspace is internal; X is updated, but no F, INFO or evaluation-count output is returned.
procedures.usage:
program bounded_minimum
  use kind_module, only: wp
  use bobyqa_module, only: bobyqa
  implicit none
  integer, parameter :: n=2, npt=5
  real(wp) :: x(n), xl(n), xu(n), f
  x=[0.5_wp,0.5_wp]
  xl=[0.0_wp,0.0_wp]
  xu=[1.0_wp,1.0_wp]
  call bobyqa(n,npt,x,xl,xu,0.2_wp,1.0e-8_wp,0,1000,objective)
  call objective(n,x,f)
  print *, x, f
contains
  subroutine objective(n,x,f)
    integer, intent(in) :: n
    real(wp), intent(in) :: x(:)
    real(wp), intent(out) :: f
    f=(x(1)-2.0_wp)**2+(x(2)+1.0_wp)**2
  end subroutine objective
end program bounded_minimum
procedures.usage_notes: Illustrative complete calling program only; not compiled or run for this independent review. local.name: fmin
local.description: Derivative-free minimization of a scalar function on an interval.

classifications.notes: The public FMIN function performs smooth scalar minimization without user derivatives over an initial interval. It uses safeguarded parabolic interpolation with golden-section fallback and a stopping scale SQRT(EPSILON)*ABS(X)+TOL/3. This modern package places F before AX/BX, unlike some textbook interfaces of the same name. The return is only a minimizer estimate; no convergence/status output or evaluation budget is exposed. This independent review records the public interfaces, dispatch and caller contracts, not a new numerical execution check or audit of every dependency/kernel. The existing problem-specific hosted drivers remain separate. No upstream numerical source is bundled.

procedures.summary: Scalar derivative-free minimizer combining golden-section and parabolic steps. The objective function F(X) is the first argument, followed by ordered interval endpoints AX/BX and nonnegative TOL; the result XMIN is an abscissa, not the minimum function value. Reevaluate F(XMIN) if its value is needed. Import fmin_rk to match the preprocessed real kind (REAL64 by default); callback argument and result have that kind. The source has no status, iteration-count or maximum-evaluation argument; its unbounded loop exits on an interval/machine-precision condition. Finite objective values and a suitable unimodal interval are caller responsibilities; multimodal, invalid-input and nontermination behavior are not certified by this review. The upstream source filename is case-sensitive fmin_module.F90.

procedures.summary: Simplified Levenberg-Marquardt nonlinear least squares with M residuals, N variables and a forward-difference residual Jacobian. Require M>=N>0, TOL>=0, FVEC(M), IWA(N) and real WA(LWA) with LWA>=M*N+5*N+M. X(N) is input/output. local.name: qdldl-fortran
local.description: Sparse LDL-transpose factorization, orderings and solves for quasi-definite systems.

classifications.notes: The QDLDL object separates symmetric sparse analysis, nonpivoted LDLT factorization and in-place solve. Quasi-definite and pivot-safety limitations are explicit. This is a pinned public-interface/source review, not a new numerical execution check or complete API audit. Existing hosted drivers and their verified problem scope are recorded separately.

procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(qdldl_type) :: solver from qdldl_module. Analyze a symmetric sparse pattern once, using INTEGER(QDLDL_IP) N and equal-length 1-based IROW/ICOL arrays. Entries may use either triangle; each off-diagonal entry represents its symmetric pair and duplicates are summed. Supplying both triangles with full values doubles off-diagonals; supply one value per symmetric entry (or zeros for the redundant triangle). Required default-integer ISTAT should equal QDLDL_SUCCESS before FACTOR. Optional PERM is a permutation of 1..N and selects user ordering; ORDERING chooses a public QDLDL_ORDER_* constant otherwise. Structural analysis and workspace allocation are stored in the object. The passed object ME in the linked implementation is supplied implicitly by solver%; do not pass it again.

comments.text: column indices of the entries (`1..n`, same size as `irow`)

procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(qdldl_type) :: solver from qdldl_module. Numerically factor after successful ANALYZE. VAL(:) must follow the original IROW/ICOL order and length and use QDLDL_WP (REAL64 default). Duplicate values are summed into the symmetric matrix. A new value array with the same pattern can reuse analysis. Mandatory ISTAT reports success, missing analysis, invalid sizes, nonfinite entries or a zero pivot. This LDLT implementation does not pivot; its robust intended scope is quasi-definite systems, not arbitrary symmetric-indefinite matrices. Optional regularization is configured by object components and may alter the factored matrix. The passed object ME in the linked implementation is supplied implicitly by solver%; do not pass it again.

comments.text: the values of the entries (same size as `irow`)

procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(qdldl_type) :: solver from qdldl_module. Solve after a successful FACTOR, replacing B(N) in place by X. B and the returned solution use the original matrix ordering; permutations are applied internally. Match QDLDL_WP and inspect mandatory ISTAT, including not-factored, wrong-size and nonfinite-data diagnostics. Optional integer REFINE limits refinement steps (otherwise object default MAX_REFINE applies). Preserve a copy of the right-hand side for an independent residual check; a successful return is not a bound on forward error. The passed object ME in the linked implementation is supplied implicitly by solver%; do not pass it again.

procedures.summary: Public generic PRIMES with one INTEGER(IP) upper bound returns an allocatable INTEGER(IP) list of prime VALUES in [1,LIMIT]. INTEGER(WP)=INT64 overload of public generic IS_PRIME, returning default LOGICAL. The procedure is elemental, so conforming integer arrays are allowed. N<2 is false and 2 is true; larger values use lookup, trial factors and strong probable-prime witness tests. Import the exact integer kind from PRIME_CONSTANTS or use INT64 actuals. This interface review does not establish a new proof of the witness set or verify every 64-bit input. A separate INT32 overload also exists.

procedures.summary: Double-precision scalar-query overload of generic INTERP1D. X/Y are same-length arrays on a strictly increasing grid with at least two points; XVAL and result are scalar. Match SELECTED_REAL_KIND(15,307). Optional BOUNDS_ERROR defaults true and out-of-range queries can print a diagnostic then STOP; with BOUNDS_ERROR=.FALSE., optional FILL_VALUE is returned instead (default zero). Array-query overload of generic INTERP1D. X/Y have the same grid contract as the scalar overload; XVAL(:) returns a real vector of SIZE(XVAL), using repeated scalar interpolation. procedures.summary: Double-precision generic QUADRATIC for A*X**2+B*X+C=0. Supply nonzero A and strictly positive discriminant for two real outputs X1/X2. It uses the straightforward quadratic formula and is not protected against all overflow/cancellation cases. Match SELECTED_REAL_KIND(15,307) and independently check residuals; do not present this interface as a complete robust quadratic solver.

procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(dvode_t) :: solver from dvode_module. Register derivative callback F(ME,NEQ,T,Y,YDOT), whose ME is CLASS(DVODE_T); the linked explicit interface includes this object despite older prose showing a legacy callback without it. Match DVODE_WP (REAL64 default). Optional JAC follows F_JAC for supplied dense/banded Jacobians; methods using internal finite differences can omit it. Optional DEWSET/DVNORM replace error weights/norms. Retain callbacks while the solver stores their pointers. There is no initialization status output. The passed object ME is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(dvode_t) :: solver from dvode_module. Integrate after INITIALIZE, retaining this object and caller-owned RWORK/IWORK between continuation calls. Y(NEQ) and scalar T are INOUT; RTOL/ATOL are arrays, even for scalar tolerances, selected by ITOL=1..4. Set ISTATE=1 for a new problem, ITASK=1 to return at TOUT, IOPT=0 for default controls. ISTATE=2 is successful return; negative values require diagnostic handling, and T may be short of TOUT. For nonstiff Adams MF=10 use LRW>=20+16*NEQ and LIW>=30; stiff BDF with internal dense Jacobian MF=22 requires LRW>=22+9*NEQ+2*NEQ**2 and LIW>=30+NEQ. Other MF/workspace/band controls follow the linked declarations. Match DVODE_WP, use nonnegative tolerances giving positive error weights, and do not reset continuation workspace. The passed object ME is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(fitpack_curve) :: solver from fitpack_curves. Copy data X(:), Y(:) of equal length into the curve, destroying its previous fit. Values use FP_REAL=C_DOUBLE. The wrapper sorts X and associated Y/optional positive W; supply finite, distinct abscissae and enough points for the intended degree. Default weights are one. This loads points and workspace but does not itself generate a fitted spline: call INTERPOLATE or FIT next. Empty data are invalid for its MINVAL/MAXVAL setup. The passed object THIS is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

Declare TYPE(fitpack_curve) :: solver from fitpack_curves. After NEW_POINTS, construct an interpolating spline with zero smoothing. Optional ORDER is spline degree, not degree+1; default cubic is 3, with supported degrees 1..5 and number of data points greater than the degree. FP_SIZE/FP_FLAG are INT32-compatible kinds exported by FITPACK_CORE. Optional RESET_KNOTS defaults true. This is a function returning an integer FITPACK status, so use IERR=solver%interpolate(...), not CALL; inspect the status before evaluation. Interpolation normally returns -1, while positive flags require diagnostics. The passed object THIS is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

Declare TYPE(fitpack_curve) :: solver from fitpack_curves. Scalar overload of generic EVAL with an explicit required INTEGER(FP_FLAG) IERR actual. Return one REAL(FP_REAL) spline value at X after a successful fit. Despite the implementation comment saying optional, IERR is required for this overload; a separate no-error overload exists. Inspect IERR=0 before accepting the value. Boundary behavior follows the object BC field, initially OUTSIDE_NEAREST_BND (clamping); other policies can extrapolate, return zero or report an error. The passed object THIS is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(fcn1var_helper) :: solver from nonlin_single_var. Register a PROCEDURE(FCN1VAR), POINTER actual with signature REAL64 function FCN(X,ARGS), where X is REAL64 and optional ARGS is CLASS(*), INTENT(INOUT). Declare/associate a procedure pointer before passing it; an ordinary procedure actual is not the declared POINTER dummy contract here. Keep the target alive while the helper stores it. The helper is passed to BRENT_SOLVER%SOLVE; it is not the solver object itself. The passed object THIS is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

Declare TYPE(brent_solver) :: solver from nonlin_solve. Solve a continuous scalar root problem using an initialized FCN1VAR_HELPER and VALUE_PAIR limits LIM%X1/LIM%X2 bracketing a sign change. X is a REAL64 output-through-INOUT actual; its input guess is ignored. Optional F returns the residual, IB is TYPE(ITERATION_BEHAVIOR), and ARGS is forwarded to the callback. Inspect IB%CONVERGE_ON_FCN/CONVERGE_ON_CHNG and independently check residual/bracket requirements; a small change alone need not establish a small residual. Invalid helper/limits can ERROR STOP. local.name: kissfft-f

procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(fft) :: solver from kissfft. Create a one-dimensional KISS FFT plan for positive INTEGER(C_INT) NFFT and required INTEGER(C_INT) INVERSE_FFT (0 for forward, 1 for inverse). Call once before execution and before the object is finalized; the stored C pointer is not initialized to null by default. There is no returned allocation status: inspect C_ASSOCIATED(solver%KISS_FFT_CFG) before use. Reinitialization does not free an old plan; copying this pointer-owning object can cause duplicate frees. The passed object SELF is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

Declare TYPE(fft) :: solver from kissfft. Execute the initialized one-dimensional plan with FIN(:) and FOUT(:), arrays of TYPE(KISS_FFT_CPX), not intrinsic COMPLEX. Components RE/IM are REAL(C_FLOAT). Supply contiguous arrays at least NFFT long with storage appropriate to the plan; the wrapper does not check lengths or plan association. Both arguments are declared INOUT and this wrapper applies no output normalization. Do not substitute a multidimensional plan into this method; use PERFORM_ND for INIT_ND. The passed object SELF is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

Circularly reorder a one-dimensional TYPE(KISS_FFT_CPX) array, returning a same-size array and preserving the input. The implementation uses CSHIFT with -FLOOR(SIZE(X)/2), moving a conventional unshifted FFT zero-frequency bin to the middle. This is data reordering, not a Fourier transform or scaling operation; IFFTSHIFT differs for odd lengths.

classifications.notes: Singly linked list append, logical emptying and explicit cleanup distinguish owned payload copies from retained node storage. This is a pinned public-interface/source review, not a new numerical execution check or complete API audit. Existing hosted drivers and their verified problem scope are recorded separately.

procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(sll) :: solver from sll_linked_list. Append scalar CLASS(*) DATA to an initialized/default SLL. The node allocates a SOURCE= copy, not an association to the scalar actual; normal pointer-component aliasing rules still apply. After EMPTY the list can reuse retained nodes. No allocation/status result is returned. Avoid intrinsic copying of a live list: HEAD/TAIL are pointers and copies share the same chain. The passed object SELF is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

Declare TYPE(sll) :: solver from sll_linked_list. Logically clear the list by resetting length/tail, retaining the allocated chain, payloads and capacity for reuse. This is not resource destruction and can retain data until replaced or explicitly finalized. SIZE() becomes zero; SIZE(CAPACITY=.TRUE.) describes retained capacity. Use SLL_FINALIZER to release node allocations when done. The passed object SELF is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

Explicitly traverse and free an SLL chain/payloads, nullify the tail and reset length/capacity. Despite its name, this routine is not a FINAL binding in the SLL type: CALL SLL_FINALIZER(list) yourself. Do not finalize shallow copies of the same live chain separately. No recoverable status is returned; node payloads follow their own Fortran finalization semantics.

local.name: string-utf-8
local.description: Manipulate UTF-8 strings as arrays of Unicode code points.

classifications.notes: UTF-8 byte segmentation, reassembly and code-point-array slicing document representation and validation limits. This is a pinned public-interface/source review, not a new numerical execution check or complete API audit. Existing hosted drivers and their verified problem scope are recorded separately.

procedures.summary: Split valid UTF-8 encoded default CHARACTER bytes into an allocatable CHAR_UTF array. Each element CHAR stores one code point encoded as its original byte sequence, not a UTF-32 integer or a user-perceived grapheme cluster. The implementation recognizes leading/continuation byte prefixes without full UTF-8 validation; malformed/leading-continuation input is outside this scope. No status output or Unicode normalization is performed.

Concatenate CHAR_UTF(:)%CHAR byte strings into allocated CHARACTER text. This is the inverse assembly step for a valid array from CHARS_ARRAY, not decoding to another Fortran character kind. Empty input yields empty text. Each component must be allocated; there is no validation/status channel for manually constructed invalid elements.

Return an allocatable CHAR_UTF slice using code-point-array positions. START_INDEX is one-based; negative starts count from the end. Omitted LENGTH extends toward the end, negative LENGTH selects backward but returns elements in original order. Zero/out-of-range start or zero length yields an empty slice; bounds are clipped by the linked helper. These are code-point positions, not UTF-8 byte offsets or grapheme indexes.

classifications.notes: Regex match, split and replace record fixed-length storage, no-separator behavior and aborting syntax errors. This is a pinned public-interface/source review, not a new numerical execution check or complete API audit. Existing hosted drivers and their verified problem scope are recorded separately.

procedures.summary: Return LOGICAL for the implemented regex matcher on CHARACTER RE/STR. Both pattern and subject are TRIMmed, so trailing blanks are not preserved. Empty patterns and syntax failures can abort through THROW_ERROR rather than return a status; the supported grammar is the pinned engine subset, not a PCRE/POSIX compatibility guarantee. Each call builds and frees its own NFA, with fixed parser buffers.

Split on a consuming separator pattern into an allocatable CHARACTER(LEN=fixed) OUTPUT(:). Declare an adequate element length before the call: allocation specifies the extent, not a deferred character length, and longer pieces can truncate to that length. If no separator is counted the routine returns before allocating/replacing OUTPUT; an earlier allocation may remain. Check allocation and do not infer a fresh one-element result. No status output is provided.

Return replaced text in CHARACTER(LEN=PF_BUFF_SIZE), not an automatically sized allocation. REPL is replacement text under this engine implementation; no general capture-expansion semantics are promised. Account for fixed-result truncation/padding, use bounded input/output and TRIM only when appropriate. Pattern/subject scanning trims trailing subject blanks. Invalid patterns can abort; there is no IOSTAT/error-result argument.

procedures.summary: Use a concrete extension of CONMAX_SOLVER from conmax_module. Solve the constrained minimax problem from an initial PARAM vector. CONMAX_SOLVER is ABSTRACT: extend it and implement the deferred FNSET callback with the linked FUNC declarations; use that concrete solver as the receiver. The callback sets constraint types/values and requested derivatives. IOPTN=0 requests supplied derivatives; its units digit 1 enables differences. Allocate LIWRK >= 7*NUMGR+7*NPARM+3 and LWRK >= 2*NPARM**2+4*NUMGR*NPARM+11*NUMGR+27*NPARM+13. Reset option-bearing workspace inputs between calls. This pin returns ITER=-999 for short workspace, despite older comments describing negative lengths. Check ITER and ERROR(NUMGR+1:NUMGR+3), including feasibility and the iteration limit; return does not certify an optimum. Use REAL(REAL64) via ISO_FORTRAN_ENV. The passed object ME is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

local.name: psqp

classifications.notes: SQP solve and advanced workspace entry document objective/constraint gradients, callback lifetime and termination measures. procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(psqp_class) :: solver from psqp_module. Solve a smooth constrained problem from X, allocating internal work arrays. Supply OBJ/DOBJ and CON/DCON callbacks with analytic gradients and the exact linked interfaces; constraint callbacks remain required actual arguments even when NC=0. CF has NC+1 entries. Use REAL(PSQP_WP), IPAR(6), RPAR(5) and the documented bound/constraint type codes. Only REPORT is optional. Set IPRNT=0 for quiet operation. Check ITERM, CMAX and GMAX; statuses 11-13 are budgets rather than convergence. Callback pointers are retained in the object; keep their targets alive. An omitted REPORT on a reused object does not clear an earlier reporter, so use a fresh object when changing reporter lifetimes. The passed object ME is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.
