local.name: optgra
local.description: Constrained optimization designed for nearly linear problems with many constraints.

classifications.notes: Near-linear constrained optimization setup, solve and explicit cleanup distinguish constraint and merit slots and stopping statuses. This is a pinned public-interface/source review, not a new numerical execution check or complete API audit. Existing hosted drivers and their verified problem scope are recorded separately.

procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(optgra) :: solver from optgra_module. Initialize the problem before SOLVE; every displayed argument is REQUIRED, including both value/derivative callbacks, iteration/logging settings and names. Use REAL(OPTGRA_WP) and default INT32 integers in this build. Arrays for constraints include an extra merit-function slot NUMCON+1, while variable arrays have NUMVAR entries; names have length 80. CONTYP(1:NUMCON) distinguishes >=0, <=0, equality and derived-data constraints, while CONTYP(NUMCON+1) selects maximization/minimization. VARDER chooses analytic or differenced derivatives. Callback procedure pointers are retained, so targets must outlive use. Scales must be meaningful/nonzero; no initialization status dummy is returned. The passed object ME is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(optgra) :: solver from optgra_module. Solve after INITIALIZE, taking unscaled VALVAR as the initial variables and returning updated variables and VALCON(NUMCON+1), including the merit value in the last slot. Check FINOPT: 1 matched/optimal under its stopping tests; 2 matched but not optimal; 3 not matched/not optimal; 4 infeasible/not optimal; -1 fatal singular constraints. FINITE is a separate integer result, not a LOGICAL finiteness test. Returned values and status do not certify a global optimum. Callback dimensions, scale choices and iteration settings come from initialization. The passed object ME is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

procedures.summary: INTEGER(INT64) overload of NEW_STRINT returns an initialized STRINT_TYPE, storing a signed zero-padded decimal representation. procedures.summary: Add equal-length CHARACTER binary strings, returning allocated text with the SAME width as A. Use only 0/1 characters and equal actual lengths (B has explicit LEN(A)); high carry is dropped, giving fixed-width arithmetic rather than a growing result. Invalid input allocates output without assigning characters, so ALLOCATED(result) is not a validity check and no status is returned. Validate before calling, using the helper module if desired.

Zero-fill a left shift of valid binary text, preserving its length. Optional INTEGER(INT32) AMOUNT defaults to 1; its absolute value is used, so a negative actual still shifts left. Require ABS(AMOUNT)<=LEN(A) and avoid the most-negative integer whose ABS cannot be represented. Invalid text or excessive shift allocates an uninitialized character result rather than returning a status. It is a logical string shift, not a cyclic shift or signed arithmetic shift.

Return allocated digitwise XOR of equal-width valid binary strings A/B. B is CHARACTER(LEN(A)); it is not a machine-integer XOR overload. Input remains unchanged. Invalid inputs cause allocation of uninitialized output text with no status, so ensure both operands contain only binary digits and satisfy the actual-length contract. Do not use allocation success as evidence of a valid bitstring.

procedures.summary: Solve the five-point Cartesian Helmholtz discretization on a boundary-inclusive (M+1)-by-(N+1) grid. Use REAL(WP)/INTEGER(IP) from FISHPACK, with A<B, C<D and M,N>3. F(IDIMF,N+1), IDIMF>=M+1, holds RHS and required Dirichlet boundary values on entry and is overwritten by the solution; derivative data go in BDA/BDB(N+1) and BDC/BDD(M+1). Boundary codes 0-4 distinguish periodic, value and derivative conditions. Check IERROR and PERTRB: singular Poisson cases may solve an RHS adjusted by PERTRB and have an arbitrary additive constant. Positive-lambda warning 6 is not the same as invalid-input failure. Internal workspace is allocated; no legacy W argument is accepted.

Solve the five-point Cartesian Helmholtz discretization on a STAGGERED M-by-N cell-center grid, not the boundary-inclusive HWSCRT layout. Use FISHPACK WP/IP kinds and inspect IERROR plus the compatibility adjustment PERTRB for singular Poisson problems. Do not copy centered-grid boundary values into F using HWSCRT rules. Workspace is allocated internally.

Solve the seven-point 3-D Cartesian Helmholtz discretization with boundary-inclusive grid sizes L+1,M+1,N+1. Supply F(LDIMF,MDIMF,N+1), LDIMF>=L+1 and MDIMF>=M+1, and boundary-face arrays of the linked shapes. F combines interior RHS and requested Dirichlet data, then is overwritten; derivative faces are separate actuals. Boundary codes control each pair of faces. Use FISHPACK WP/IP, check IERROR/PERTRB and account for null-space constants in singular Poisson cases. This is a finite-difference solve, not a continuous exact-solution or convergence-error guarantee.

procedures.summary: Allocate and initialize allocatable REAL(WP) WAVETABLE(:) for regular-grid scalar analysis at NLAT/NLON. Check ERROR_FLAG=0 before SHAEC. This is the allocating convenience wrapper around SHAECI, so the caller does not calculate a legacy wavetable length. An INTENT(OUT) allocatable actual is replaced on reinitialization. Reuse the resulting table only for the same grid and do not modify it. The synthesis table is initialized separately by INITIALIZE_SHSEC.

Analyze NT scalar fields on a regular latitude/longitude sphere into the package normalized real harmonic coefficients A/B. For the basic full-sphere case ISYM=0, use G(IDG,JDG,NT) with IDG>=NLAT, JDG>=NLON; theta(i)=(i-1)*pi/(NLAT-1) includes both poles, longitude has NLON distinct points without a repeated 2*pi endpoint. NLAT>=3, NLON>=4. A/B are (MDAB,NDAB,NT), NDAB>=NLAT and MDAB at least MIN(NLAT,(NLON+2)/2) for even NLON or MIN(NLAT,(NLON+1)/2) for odd NLON. Initialize WSHAEC first and check IERROR. ISYM=1/2 use different half-sphere storage. Do not substitute a Gaussian latitude grid.

Allocate and initialize a distinct REAL(WP) WAVETABLE(:) for regular-grid scalar SYNTHESIS. Check ERROR_FLAG before SHSEC, retain the table unchanged for repeated synthesis at the same NLAT/NLON, and reinitialize after grid-size changes. This initializes tables only, not harmonic coefficients or output fields. Do not assume an analysis table is interchangeable with this synthesis table.

Synthesize NT regular-grid scalar fields G from the package A/B harmonic coefficients. With ISYM=0 use the same full-sphere dimensions, grid order and coefficient normalization as SHAEC; NDAB>=NLAT and MDAB obeys the linked parity rule. G is an output array and A/B are input. Initialize WSHSEC for this grid with INITIALIZE_SHSEC and inspect IERROR before using G. Arbitrary samples need not survive an analysis/synthesis round trip exactly: unresolved harmonic content is projected away. Gaussian-grid synthesis uses a different entry point.

Return Gaussian COLATITUDES THETA(NLAT) in increasing radians in (0,pi) and Gauss-Legendre WTS(NLAT); NLAT must be positive and IERROR=0 indicates valid input. These are angular colatitudes, not latitude degrees or the uniform-grid coordinates required by SHAEC/SHSEC. Weights apply to integration in cos(theta), so they are not uniform theta-step weights. The caller allocates both output arrays; this does not initialize a harmonic transform table.

procedures.summary: Construct a FLANN_INDEX with required FLANNParameters and integer(C_INT) distance identifier, plus optional Minkowski ORDER. Declare TYPE(flann_index) :: solver from flann. Build the native index from contiguous REAL(C_FLOAT) TARGET point storage shaped (dimension,number_of_points). Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

PARAMS is required SEARCH_PARAMS; optional INTEGER(C_INT) STAT reports the native status, while omission can ERROR STOP. Euclidean DISTS are squared distances and native returned indices remain zero-based at this pin. The routine also contains diagnostic PRINTs. Require matching query dimension, 1<=KNN<=number_of_points and live backing data; this is not a shape-validating general wrapper. The passed object SELF is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. procedures.summary: Evaluate a numeric calculator expression as DOUBLE PRECISION. Supply optional default-INTEGER IERR and accept the number only when it indicates success; numerical errors also return 0.0, so value alone cannot distinguish failure from a valid zero. Store/replace a numeric named variable in the module-wide calculator dictionary. Numeric names must not start with "$". Optional IOFLAG requests formatted output, not a returned error flag. No public status argument is supplied. State persists across calls and is shared by DNUM0/SNUM0 and other evaluator entries.

procedures.summary: Encode REAL(C_FLOAT) F into at least two contiguous INTEGER(C_UINT16_T) register elements in ABCD byte order. This is an offline representation conversion, requiring native libmodbus but no device context or connection. DEST is assumed-size and no length/status is passed, so the caller guarantees enough storage. In the ordinary HAS_UNSIGNED=0 build C_UINT16_T aliases signed C_INT16_T: preserve raw register bits rather than treating each element as a nonnegative Fortran integer.

Decode at least two INTEGER(C_UINT16_T) register elements in ABCD order into REAL(C_FLOAT). Use the matching SET_FLOAT_ABCD conversion or externally documented device ordering. No context, allocation or status is involved and the assumed-size SRC actual must be long enough. This does not numerically convert two integer values to a float; it interprets their bit representation. Signed fallback register kinds retain the native 16-bit payload.

Encode REAL(C_FLOAT) F into at least two INTEGER(C_UINT16_T) register elements in DCBA order, the alternative order paired with GET_FLOAT_DCBA. No device/network operation is performed. Supply adequate contiguous storage, the build-selected register kind and a native libmodbus version exporting this symbol; no array-bound checks or recoverable error result are provided. Do not interchange ABCD/DCBA getters based on host endianness assumptions.

Decode two or more INTEGER(C_UINT16_T) elements using DCBA byte ordering and return REAL(C_FLOAT). Pair with SET_FLOAT_DCBA for a round trip; other orderings are separate functions. Buffer length and interpretation belong to the caller because SRC is assumed-size and no status is exposed. This scoped call demonstrates data conversion only, not Modbus transport, address validation or device availability.

local.name: m-process
local.description: POSIX pipes for reading and writing subprocess streams.

classifications.notes: POSIX subprocess open/read/close interfaces document shell semantics, bounded record handling and the pinned undefined-status cleanup defect. This is a pinned public-interface/source review, not a new numerical execution check or complete API audit. Existing hosted drivers and their verified problem scope are recorded separately.

procedures.summary: Open a POSIX POPEN pipe to read command stdout into TYPE(STREAMPOINTER) FP; IERR=0 only means the pipe was opened, not that the child command succeeded. CMD is a shell command string with shell quoting/expansion semantics, not an argv array. A compatible POSIX C runtime and allowed subprocesses are required; sandbox restrictions still apply. Do not reopen an already owned FP or shallow-copy its native handle. See the pinned PROCESS_CLOSE limitation before relying on cleanup or exit reporting.

Read into caller CHARACTER READFROM from an already open pipe. IERR=0 returns a record chunk; IERR=-1 combines end-of-file and read failure. This pin uses bounded FGETS and assumes newline plus NUL when trimming, so an overlong line or final unterminated line may lose data. Restrict this sketch to newline-terminated records comfortably shorter than the caller buffer (length at least two); it is not a lossless arbitrary-length record reader. The stream remains open after EOF and requires cleanup.

Intended explicit POPEN cleanup using PCLOSE and a returned integer status, but this PIN has a source defect: IERR is INTENT(OUT) and is read in IF(IERR.GE.0) before assignment, so calling with IERR=0 beforehand does not repair the undefined read and PCLOSE can be skipped. The handle is not nullified after closing either. Do not rely on this upstream routine for guaranteed cleanup, repeated-close safety or dependable child exit reporting without a corrected implementation. This review identifies the interface/limitation, not a verified resource-lifetime recipe.

Do not alias PHI and RHS or assume unsupported mixed boundary configurations produce initialized output. No IERROR/status dummy is returned.

Explicitly free this solver FFTW plans and associated real/complex work arrays via the FINALIZE generic. This is a public free subroutine CALL FINALIZE(solver), not a type-bound automatic FINAL declaration. Use it once for the owning initialized solver, avoid shallow copies and do not assume repeated cleanup or subsequent EXECUTE is safe. Native/resource state must be reconstructed before another solve.

Preconditioned steepest descent through INTEGER(C_INT) reverse-communication FLAG: begin with 0 plus objective, GRAD and GRAD_PRECO at X; when FLAG=1 recompute all required values at returned X and call again; FLAG=3 is a new-step notification to continue; 2/4 terminate by stopping test/line-search failure. local.name: dftatom
local.description: Radial Schrodinger, Dirac and Poisson solvers for atomic calculations.

classifications.notes: Radial exponential-mesh construction, mapping derivative and bound-state shooting entry document N+1 storage, atomic units and integer convergence status. This is a pinned public-interface/source review, not a new numerical execution check or complete API audit. Existing hosted drivers and their verified problem scope are recorded separately.

procedures.summary: Construct REAL(DP) radial coordinates on [R_MIN,R_MAX] with N elements and N+1 points, using DP from DFTATOM. A is the ratio of last to first element widths, not a simple adjacent-point ratio. Use increasing endpoints, positive A and positive N; for the paired mesh derivative reviewed here require N>1 and A different from one. The uniform A=1 mesh branch exists, but the companion derivative rejects it. Invalid cases can stop rather than return a status.

Return REAL(DP) Rp(N+1)=dR/dt for the same exponential-mesh parameters, with computational coordinate t=1,...,N+1 and unit index spacing. Use N>1 and A>0, A/=1: the pinned implementation STOPs at A=1 even though MESH_EXP can generate a uniform mesh. This is an analytic mapping derivative, not finite differences of R and not a physical wavefunction derivative. Preserve correspondence between R and Rp for the eigenproblem call.

Solve a radial bound-state eigenproblem with REAL(DP) R/Rp/V on the same mesh and P/Q output arrays of matching extent. Supply n>0, 0<=l<n, energy guess EIN, positive EPS/MAX_ITER and a valid energy bracket EMIN_INIT/EMAX_INIT. The scoped nonrelativistic path uses RELAT=0, atomic-unit potential/energies and integer Coulomb Z; C is the speed of light in atomic units for relativistic paths. CONVERGED is an INTEGER status, with zero success, not a logical. On failure do not interpret E or partial P/Q as a converged state. PERTURB assumes suitable Coulomb asymptotics; the alternative is bracket bisection. This is a radial boundary-value/shooting eigenproblem, not a full self-consistent atomic DFT calculation.

classifications.notes: Headless drawing output/device selection, single-precision move/line primitives and finalization document native state and raster presentation boundaries. This is a pinned public-interface/source review, not a new numerical execution check or complete API audit. Existing hosted drivers and their verified problem scope are recorded separately.

procedures.summary: Select the native drawing output filename using ordinary Fortran CHARACTER text; this wrapper converts it with S2C. Configure before VINIT with a file driver such as the hosted PPM path. This does not itself choose the driver, allocate a canvas or save a complete image. No success/status dummy is exposed.

Initialize the selected native drawing device, for example "ppm" for a headless file render. The wrapper terminates the CHARACTER device name. Configure output first and use supported native driver/coordinate/color settings before drawing. Font/interactive/X11 facilities have their own runtime requirements; compilation/linking alone does not validate those paths. Finish with VEXIT to flush/release native device state.

Move the current two-dimensional drawing position without drawing a line. X/Y are REAL(C_FLOAT),VALUE in this native binding; use that kind rather than assuming default REAL64 actuals convert through the explicit interface. Coordinates follow the active view/projection, not inherently pixel indices. Requires a live initialized device and does not itself create a file or return a status.

Draw a line from the current position to REAL(C_FLOAT) X/Y and update that position. Call MOVE2 first when beginning a new curve and set the intended coordinate mapping/color separately. These are scalar by-value C_FLOAT arguments, not vector polyline arrays. Output remains tied to the current native device until finalization; no numerical/rendering status is returned.

Finish drawing and release/flush the current native device. For the hosted PPM driver the produced raster is separately collected/converted to a browser PNG preview; VEXIT itself does not open a browser or provide that conversion. This no-argument C binding is explicit lifecycle cleanup, not an automatic finalizer on a Fortran figure object.

procedures.summary: Character-string overload of PARSE_LENGTH returns TYPE(FALLIBLE_LENGTH_T), not a real number or a bare length. Text must include an understood unit, for example "2 m"; the default candidates are PROVIDED_UNITS. Inspect FAILED before extracting LENGTH; an invalid string produces stored diagnostics rather than a successful zero measurement. Parsing does not establish physical validity of a measurement.

Declare TYPE(fallible_length_t) :: solver from quaff_length_m. Logical query reporting whether the stored parse result has errors. Call this on the result returned by PARSE_LENGTH before consuming LENGTH; it does not print errors or stop execution. A success flag is a parsing/units result, not a numerical error bound. The passed object SELF is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

Declare TYPE(fallible_length_t) :: solver from quaff_length_m. Return the stored TYPE(LENGTH_T) value after checking that FAILED is false. This accessor itself does not reject an unsuccessful parse; a failed result can retain its default zero length. Physical values are stored in meters; use the public unit operators for conversions rather than assume a raw default-real result. The passed object SELF is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

procedures.summary: VERTEX_TYPE generic constructor requires a REAL(REAL32) feature vector; optional ID sets an application identifier. Returns an owned vertex value whose feature array is copied. local.name: diffstruc
local.description: Forward and reverse automatic differentiation with array computation graphs.

classifications.notes: Tracked array initialization, value replacement, reverse differentiation and extraction document batch shape, seed semantics and pointer lifetime requirements. This is a pinned public-interface/source review, not a new numerical execution check or complete API audit. Existing hosted drivers and their verified problem scope are recorded separately.

procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(array_type) :: solver from diffstruc__types. Initialize a fresh ARRAY_TYPE with allocated values. A supported simple path is SOURCE=a REAL(REAL32) rank-two array, supplied alone; last dimension is the sample/batch dimension. Alternatively supply positive ARRAY_SHAPE and initialize its values separately. Do not pass both arguments as though SOURCE were always a harmless initializer: the implementation has branch-specific checks. Reallocating a live object or passing neither optional argument is an error. Pointer graph ownership requires library lifecycle rules, not arbitrary shallow copies. The passed object THIS is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

Declare TYPE(array_type) :: solver from diffstruc__types. Replace values on an already allocated object with REAL(REAL32) input matching the complete logical shape including batch dimension. The scoped path uses rank-two input with identical shape to VAL. The routine returns silently on its shape guard, with no status argument, so verify dimensions beforehand; it does not allocate a missing array or build a new differentiation operation. The passed object THIS is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

Declare TYPE(array_type) :: solver from diffstruc__types. Set the required logical REQUIRES_GRAD flag on an input before constructing dependent graph operations. This controls derivative tracking; it does not calculate derivatives or supply a direction vector for forward mode. Retain input objects while the result graph refers to them, following the library ownership rules. The passed object THIS is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

Declare TYPE(array_type) :: solver from diffstruc__types. Run reverse-mode propagation on a live result graph with tracked inputs. Request RESET_GRAPH=.true. for explicit reset semantics when appropriate; existing gradient state otherwise matters. A newly allocated result seed is filled with ones, corresponding to a sum of result components rather than a complete independently seeded Jacobian. Retrieve derivatives from tracked input GRAD objects after checking association. Pointer lifetimes/ownership and initialization are essential; this is not a stateless function of raw real arrays. The passed object THIS is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

Declare TYPE(array_type) :: solver from diffstruc__types. Copy values into a REAL(REAL32), ALLOCATABLE output of the matching declared rank. The simple documented path is rank two for a rank-two sample/batch input. INTENT(OUT) deallocates an existing actual on entry; the implementation allocates it by assignment. An unallocated source reports a warning and returns, so do not assume the output is then allocated. To read a derivative call the binding on an associated input%grad, not on the original input value. The passed object THIS is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

local.name: athena
local.description: Neural networks with convolutional, graph-based and physics-informed layers.

classifications.notes: Model-evaluation scoring interfaces document columnwise results and the one-minus-error convention, separate from model training/inference. This is a pinned public-interface/source review, not a new numerical execution check or complete API audit. Existing hosted drivers and their verified problem scope are recorded separately.

procedures.summary: Return REAL(REAL32) scores per column/sample from conformable rank-two PREDICTED and EXPECTED arrays. Each column is scored 1 or 0 by equality of the first MAXLOC class indices; this is not a scalar average accuracy and not a probability calibration metric. Use nonempty class axes and an intended tie policy; compute an aggregate explicitly if required.

Return a REAL(REAL32) vector, one score per sample column. Despite the name, the exact implementation is 1 - SUM(ABS(expected-predicted),DIM=1)/SIZE(expected,1), not raw mean absolute error. Inputs must be conformable with a nonempty first dimension; scores can be negative and are not clipped. No training or network evaluation is performed.

Return one REAL(REAL32) score per sample column, computed as 1 - mean squared error over the first dimension. This is not raw MSE or an R-squared coefficient and can be negative. Caller supplies conformable nonempty rank-two model/reference values and chooses how to aggregate the vector. No finite-value or shape-recovery status is supplied.

classifications.notes: network_type%train supports unweighted nonlinear least-squares regression when a compiled continuous-response model selects loss_method="mse" or set_loss("mse") and an unpenalized optimizer. set_loss selects mse_loss_type; compute_mse constructs means of squared residuals divided by two, and training differentiates the loss graph and updates model parameters internally. No user regression Jacobian is required, so this is not L8e1b2. Cross-entropy classification, robust losses, PINN composite objectives and regularization are outside this mapping. Use compatible real(real32) predictor/response arrays, an initialized and compiled network/batch configuration and positive NUM_EPOCHS. The linked author sine example uses tanh hidden layers, a sigmoid response and MSE with Adam. Its Weights & Biases wrapper is application infrastructure, not required by the base train interface; the example was not run. Existing mse_score is a reporting metric (one minus an error), not the fitting entry point. Training accuracy, convergence and uncertainty estimates were not verified.

procedures.summary: Fit an initialized, compiled regression network configured with MSE loss; parameter gradients and updates are computed internally.

procedures.summary: REAL(R64) overload of ARANGE fills a preallocated allocatable vector; it does not allocate RES. Allocate exactly N=INT((STP-START)/STEP)+1 elements, with default STEP=1, nonzero step and a valid nonnegative count. START/STP/STEP must use R64 from VARIABLEKIND for this overload. The last point follows this truncated count, not a guarantee to include an arbitrary floating endpoint. A size mismatch calls the library error handler.

REAL(R64) overload writes successive differences THIS(i+1)-THIS(i) to caller-sized RES. Allocate/declare RES with SIZE(THIS)-1 elements before calling; this is a vector difference utility, not a derivative divided by grid spacing or an allocating function. The implementation stops through its error handler for a size mismatch.

REAL(R64) overload returns logical true for nondecreasing input, allowing ties. It does not sort or return permutation indices. The implementation returns true for empty and singleton arrays; comparisons with NaN do not establish a meaningful total ordering, so handle exceptional values separately if relevant.

procedures.summary: Construct a CENTERS_TO_FACES_1D_T staggered-grid interpolation operator using default INTEGER ORDER/CELLS and default REAL DX. This pin implements only order 2 or 4 and ERROR STOPs otherwise. Use a positive adequately sized cell count for the selected boundary stencils. Declare TYPE(centers_to_faces_1D_t) :: solver from interpolator_1D_m. Apply an initialized center-to-face operator to default REAL CENTERS_EXTENDED(:) of length CELLS+2, including the two endpoint values. Return an allocatable REAL vector of length CELLS+1. These are staggered interpolation/boundary closure values, not arbitrary scattered-data interpolation. Choose enough cells for every boundary stencil and satisfy the linked assertions. Construct a FACES_TO_CENTERS_1D_T with supported ORDER 2 or 4, positive adequately sized CELLS and default REAL DX. This is the reverse staggered interpolation operator with its own endpoint closures, not an algebraic inverse of CENTERS_TO_FACES_1D_T. Unsupported orders terminate. The same private integer DX_ storage limitation applies.

Declare TYPE(faces_to_centers_1D_t) :: solver from interpolator_1D_m. Apply the initialized face-to-center operator to default REAL FACES(:) of length CELLS+1 and return an allocatable vector of length CELLS+2, with endpoint entries. Matching sizes and adequate stencil extent are caller requirements. Do not assume a round trip through both interpolation operators is identity or that this binding solves a PDE by itself. The passed object SELF is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

procedures.summary: Convert a square REAL(REAL12) dense matrix to TYPE(SPRS2_DP) coordinate storage retaining entries with ABS(A)>THRESH. RA owns newly allocated pointer targets for values/row/column arrays; pass a fresh object and release its targets according to SPTYPE ownership, since this is not an automatic deep replacement. THRESH should be nonnegative for the intended sparsification. Use constants REAL12/INT12 and SPTYPE definitions from this build, not default kinds by assumption.

Compute B=RA*X for initialized coordinate storage RA and distinct REAL(REAL12) vectors of length RA%N. B is caller-sized, overwritten, and not allocated by this routine. Row/column indices must be valid and pointer arrays consistent; the partial native bounds guard is not a general validator. This is a sparse matrix-vector product, not a linear-system solve.

Solve with the matrix stored in GLOBE_DATA%RA, not a matrix argument. Initialize consistent coordinate storage with nonzero ordered diagonal entries for the Jacobi preconditioner, supply B and an initial X of matching length, initialize ITER, and use ITOL=1 or 2, positive TOL and ITMAX. INTEGER(I4B) is build-selected and must match SPTYPE; REAL12 values use CONSTANTS. ERR/ITER need inspection, and independently check residuals: this pin has no separate convergence status, no robust breakdown checks and divides by norm(B), so zero RHS/exact-start cases are not generally safe. This does not initialize or run the complete heat-transport application.

classifications.notes: Kriging covariance assembly and packed solve interfaces document mixed precision, destructive packed storage and the intended simple/ordinary-kriging scope. procedures.summary: External legacy covariance routine used to assemble kriging systems. Coordinates, C0/CC/AA, CMAX/COVA are default REAL through implicit typing; ROTMAT(MAXROT,3,3) is REAL*8, NST/IT and index/count arguments are default INTEGER. Set IVARG=1 for a single model, populate valid nested variogram arrays and anisotropy rotations, and match MAXNST/MAXROT capacities. Exponential parameter AA is the practical range in this implementation (EXP(-3*H/AA)), despite the header language about 3a. No argument-validation/status result is returned. This assembles covariances, not kriging predictions by itself.

External legacy packed symmetric-system helper for simple/ordinary kriging; scope NRIGHT=NSB=1. A is REAL*8 packed upper triangle in column order, R/S are REAL*8 vectors of NEQ entries, and counts/ISING are default INTEGER via implicit typing. A and R are overwritten during elimination. Check ISING=0 before using S; NEQ<=1 returns -1 and a small pivot returns its position. The solver does not search for a maximal pivot, uses a fixed absolute threshold and is explicitly not recommended by its header for universal kriging. It is not a general robust symmetric-indefinite factorization.
